Privacy First: Always request consent before accessing precise location data Fallback Strategy: Implement graceful degradation when location detection fails Cache Wisely: Cache geo data appropriately to balance performance and accuracy Security: Validate and sanitize all location data inputs Compliance: Stay updated with regional privacy regulations Performance: Use CDN geo headers when available for better performance Testing: Test with VPNs and different IP ranges to ensure accuracy

This comprehensive geo-targeting implementation provides a solid foundation for building location-aware applications. The modular approach allows you to implement only the features you need while maintaining flexibility for future enhancements. Key benefits of this implementation: Multiple detection methods for maximum accuracy Privacy-compliant data handling Performance optimized with caching strategies Flexible and extensible architecture Production-ready with comprehensive error handling Start with the basic location detection and gradually add advanced features like geo-fencing and A/B testing as your application requirements grow.

Implementing GitOps for microservices deployment brings consistency, reliability, and traceability to your deployment pipeline. This practical guide walks through setting up a complete GitOps workflow for Node.js microservices on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) using Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), ArgoCD, and Kustomize. We'll build a production-ready deployment pipeline that follows infrastructure as code principles and implements security best practices for enterprise-grade applications.
documents.s: GitOps in Practice: Deploying Node.js Microservices to GCP GKE with ArgoCD and Kustomize

documents.t: GitOps transforms how we think about deployments by making Git the single source of truth for both application code and infrastructure configuration. Instead of pushing deployments to environments, GitOps pulls the desired state from Git repositories and continuously reconciles the actual state with the declared state.

Declarative Infrastructure: Everything defined as code Version Control: Full audit trail of all changes Automated Deployments: Reduced human error and faster delivery Security: No direct cluster access required for deployments Rollback Capability: Easy recovery from failed deployments Multi-Environment Management: Consistent configuration across environments

Our GitOps implementation uses a three-repository strategy: graph TD A[Application Repos] --> B[CI Pipeline] B --> C[Container Registry] B --> D[GitOps Repo Update] D --> E[ArgoCD Sync] E --> F[GKE Deployment] G[Infrastructure Repo] --> H[Terraform] H --> I[GCP Resources] J[GitOps Repo] --> K[Kustomize Overlays] K --> E
First, let's set up our GKE cluster using Terraform for infrastructure as code.

infrastructure/ ├── terraform/ │ ├── environments/ │ │ ├── dev/ │ │ ├── staging/ │ │ └── production/ │ ├── modules/ │ │ ├── gke/ │ │ ├── networking/ │ │ └── security/ │ └── shared/ └── scripts/ ├── setup.sh └── teardown.sh

# terraform/modules/gke/main.tf resource "google_container_cluster" "microservices" { name = var.cluster_name location = var.region # Remove default node pool remove_default_node_pool = true initial_node_count = 1 # Network configuration network = google_compute_network.vpc.name subnetwork = google_compute_subnetwork.subnet.name # Enable workload identity for secure pod-to-GCP service communication workload_identity_config { workload_pool = "${var.project_id}.svc.id.goog" } # Private cluster for enhanced security private_cluster_config { enable_private_nodes = true enable_private_endpoint = false master_ipv4_cidr_block = "172.16.0.0/28" } # Networking features network_policy { enabled = true } # Enable necessary APIs addons_config { horizontal_pod_autoscaling { disabled = false } network_policy_config { disabled = false } http_load_balancing { disabled = false } } # Logging and monitoring logging_service = "logging.googleapis.com/kubernetes" monitoring_service = "monitoring.googleapis.com/kubernetes" } resource "google_container_node_pool" "primary_nodes" { name = "${var.cluster_name}-nodes" location = var.region cluster = google_container_cluster.microservices.name # Auto-scaling configuration autoscaling { min_node_count = var.min_node_count max_node_count = var.max_node_count } node_config { preemptible = var.preemptible machine_type = var.machine_type disk_size_gb = var.disk_size_gb disk_type = "pd-ssd" # Service account for nodes service_account = google_service_account.gke_nodes.email oauth_scopes = [ "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/logging.write", "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/monitoring", "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/devstorage.read_only" ] # Security settings workload_metadata_config { mode = "GKE_METADATA" } labels = { environment = var.environment managed-by = "terraform" } } management { auto_repair = true auto_upgrade = true } }

Navigating the complex landscape of global privacy regulations has become increasingly challenging as countries worldwide implement comprehensive data protection laws. With over 100 countries now having privacy legislation, understanding the specific requirements for cookie consent and data collection in each jurisdiction is crucial for any business operating internationally. This comprehensive guide examines the cookie and privacy requirements across major jurisdictions, providing practical implementation guidance and compliance strategies for 2025.
documents.s: Global Cookie Privacy Compliance: A Complete Guide to Country-Specific Regulations in 2025

documents.t: The privacy regulatory environment has evolved dramatically since the GDPR's introduction in 2018. What started as a European initiative has now spread globally, with each jurisdiction adding its unique requirements and interpretations.

Convergence on Core Rights: Most laws now include rights to access, delete, and port data Consent Fatigue Solutions: Regulators seeking balance between privacy and user experience Cross-Border Transfer Restrictions: Increasing focus on data localization Enforcement Intensification: Higher fines and more aggressive enforcement Children's Privacy: Enhanced protections for minors across jurisdictions

The GDPR applies to any organization processing personal data of EU residents, regardless of where the company is located. Combined with the ePrivacy Directive (and upcoming ePrivacy Regulation), this creates the most comprehensive privacy framework globally.

interface EUCookieCompliance { beforeCookiesSet: { consentBannerDisplayed: boolean; noCookiesPlaced: boolean; // Except strictly necessary clearInformation: boolean; }; consentMechanism: { explicitConsent: boolean; // Must be opt-in granularChoices: boolean; // Per category freelyGiven: boolean; // No cookie walls withdrawable: boolean; // Easy withdrawal informed: boolean; // Clear purposes specific: boolean; // Not bundled }; technicalRequirements: { consentRecording: boolean; versionTracking: boolean; ipAnonymization: boolean; consentExpiry: string; // "12 months maximum" }; }

Germany: Strictest interpretation globally Planet49 ruling: Pre-checked boxes invalid No implied consent for any non-essential cookies Must show reject button equally prominent to accept France: CNIL guidance evolution Cookie walls forbidden (2020 ruling) Analytics cookies require consent (Google Analytics ban) Legitimate interest narrowly interpreted Netherlands: Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM) Focus on dark patterns in consent interfaces Strict enforcement on withdrawal mechanisms Regular audits of major websites Ireland: DPC as lead regulator Meta and Google enforcement actions Focus on data transfer mechanisms Consent validity for large-scale processing

class EUGDPRConsentManager { private readonly CONSENT_VERSION = '2024.1'; private readonly MAX_CONSENT_AGE = 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 1 year async displayConsentBanner(): Promise<void> { // Ensure no non-essential cookies before consent this.clearNonEssentialCookies(); const banner = new ConsentBanner({ title: 'Your Privacy Matters', description: this.getGDPRCompliantDescription(), categories: this.getCookieCategories(), buttons: { acceptAll: { text: 'Accept All', style: 'primary' }, rejectAll: { text: 'Reject All', style: 'secondary' }, // Equally prominent customize: { text: 'Manage Preferences', style: 'secondary' } }, layout: 'gdpr-compliant', // No cookie wall design withdrawalLink: '/cookie-settings' }); await banner.display(); } private getGDPRCompliantDescription(): string { return `We use cookies to enhance your experience and analyze site usage. ` + `You can choose which categories to accept. You can change your ` + `preferences at any time through our Cookie Settings.`; } private getCookieCategories(): CookieCategory[] { return [ { id: 'necessary', name: 'Strictly Necessary', description: 'Essential for website functionality', required: true, legalBasis: 'legitimate_interest' }, { id: 'analytics', name: 'Analytics', description: 'Help us understand how visitors use our site', required: false, legalBasis: 'consent', vendors: ['Google Analytics', 'Hotjar'] }, { id: 'marketing', name: 'Marketing', description: 'Used to deliver relevant advertisements', required: false, legalBasis: 'consent', vendors: ['Facebook Pixel', 'Google Ads'] } ]; } recordConsent(consent: ConsentChoices): void { const record: ConsentRecord = { timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), version: this.CONSENT_VERSION, choices: consent, method: 'banner_interaction', ipAddress: this.anonymizeIP(this.getUserIP()), userAgent: navigator.userAgent.substring(0, 200), // Truncated for privacy pageUrl: window.location.href, gdprApplies: true }; // Store locally and send to server this.storeConsentRecord(record); this.sendToConsentAPI(record); } private anonymizeIP(ip: string): string { // GDPR requires IP anonymization for consent logs const parts = ip.split('.'); return parts.length === 4 ? `${parts[0]}.${parts[1]}.${parts[2]}.0` : ip; } }
The UK operates its own version of GDPR combined with the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR), creating a unique regulatory environment.

interface UKPrivacyRequirements { ukGDPR: { similarToEU: boolean; // Largely identical icoGuidance: boolean; // UK-specific interpretations adequacyStatus: 'maintained' | 'under_review' | 'lost'; }; pecr: { electronicMarketing: boolean; // Stricter than GDPR cookieConsent: boolean; // Specific cookie rules directMarketing: boolean; // B2B exemptions }; enforcement: { maxFines: string; // "£17.5 million or 4% of turnover" recentActions: string[]; // ICO enforcement examples }; }

class UKConsentManager extends EUGDPRConsentManager { protected getUKSpecificRequirements(): UKRequirements { return { pecrCompliance: true, directMarketingConsent: true, emailMarketingOptIn: true, electronicMarketingRules: true }; } async handleDirectMarketing(consent: ConsentChoices): Promise<void> { if (consent.marketing) { // PECR requires specific consent for electronic marketing await this.recordMarketingConsent({ email: consent.emailMarketing || false, sms: consent.smsMarketing || false, phone: consent.phoneMarketing || false, post: true // Postal marketing doesn't require consent under PECR }); } } }
The US lacks comprehensive federal privacy legislation, resulting in a complex patchwork of state laws with varying requirements.

interface CaliforniaCompliance { ccpaRequirements: { doNotSellLink: boolean; // Must be visible privacyPolicy: boolean; // Detailed disclosures dataInventory: string[]; // Categories collected consumerRights: { rightToKnow: boolean; rightToDelete: boolean; rightToOptOut: boolean; rightToCorrect: boolean; // CPRA addition rightToLimit: boolean; // CPRA addition }; }; technicalRequirements: { globalPrivacyControl: boolean; // Must respect GPC signals optOutMethods: string[]; // Multiple methods required verificationProcess: boolean; // Identity verification responseTimeline: string; // "45 days" }; }

class CCPAConsentManager { private readonly CCPA_VERSION = '2024.1'; async initializeCCPACompliance(): Promise<void> { // Check for Global Privacy Control this.handleGlobalPrivacyControl(); // Display "Do Not Sell" link this.displayDoNotSellLink(); // Set up opt-out mechanisms this.setupOptOutMechanisms(); } private handleGlobalPrivacyControl(): void { if (navigator.globalPrivacyControl === true) { // Automatically honor GPC signal this.processOptOutRequest({ method: 'gpc', timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), automatic: true }); // Update user preferences this.updateDataSaleOptOut(true); // Record GPC processing this.recordGPCSignal(); } } private displayDoNotSellLink(): void { const doNotSellLink = document.createElement('a'); doNotSellLink.href = '/do-not-sell'; doNotSellLink.textContent = 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information'; doNotSellLink.className = 'ccpa-do-not-sell-link'; // Must be visible and accessible doNotSellLink.style.minHeight = '20px'; doNotSellLink.style.minWidth = '200px'; doNotSellLink.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Opt out of personal information sale'); // Add to footer or prominent location const footer = document.querySelector('footer') || document.body; footer.appendChild(doNotSellLink); } async processDataRequest(request: CCPADataRequest): Promise<void> { const { type, email, verificationCode } = request; // Verify identity (required for CCPA requests) const verified = await this.verifyIdentity(email, verificationCode); if (!verified) { throw new Error('Identity verification failed'); } switch (type) { case 'access': return this.processAccessRequest(email); case 'delete': return this.processDeletionRequest(email); case 'opt-out': return this.processOptOutRequest({ email, method: 'form' }); case 'correct': return this.processCorrectionRequest(request); } } private async verifyIdentity(email: string, code?: string): Promise<boolean> { // CCPA requires reasonable verification methods if (code) { return this.verifyTwoFactorCode(email, code); } // For low-risk requests, email verification may suffice return this.sendVerificationEmail(email); } }

interface StatePrivacyLaws { virginia: { effectiveDate: '2023-01-01'; applicabilityThreshold: '100k consumers or 25k sales'; rights: ['access', 'correct', 'delete', 'portability', 'opt-out']; sensitiveDataConsent: boolean; }; colorado: { effectiveDate: '2023-07-01'; universalOptOut: boolean; // Must respect GPC dataProtectionAssessments: boolean; rights: ['access', 'correct', 'delete', 'portability', 'opt-out']; }; connecticut: { effectiveDate: '2023-07-01'; similarToVirginia: boolean; dataMinimization: boolean; consumerRights: string[]; }; }

interface CanadianPrivacyCompliance { federal: { pipeda: { meaningfulConsent: boolean; plainLanguage: boolean; withdrawalRights: boolean; breachNotification: boolean; }; }; provincial: { quebec: { law25: { gdprLike: boolean; explicitConsent: boolean; privacyByDesign: boolean; effectiveDate: '2023-09-22'; }; }; britishColumbia: { pipa: boolean; sectorSpecific: boolean; }; alberta: { pipa: boolean; similarToBC: boolean; }; }; }

class QuebecLaw25ConsentManager { private readonly LAW25_VERSION = '2024.1'; async implementLaw25Compliance(): Promise<void> { // Similar to GDPR in requirements const consent = await this.getExplicitConsent(); // Privacy by design principles this.implementPrivacyByDesign(); // Enhanced breach notification this.setupBreachNotification(); // Data subject rights this.setupDataSubjectRights(); } private async getExplicitConsent(): Promise<ConsentRecord> { // Quebec requires explicit consent similar to GDPR return this.displayGDPRStyleBanner({ language: this.detectLanguage(), // French/English explicitConsent: true, granularOptions: true, withdrawalMechanism: true }); } private implementPrivacyByDesign(): void { // Privacy by design is mandatory under Law 25 this.configureDefaultPrivacySettings(); this.minimizeDataCollection(); this.implementDataProtectionMeasures(); } }

interface PIPLCompliance { applicability: { dataProcessingInChina: boolean; chineseNaturalPersons: boolean; crossBorderTransfers: boolean; }; keyRequirements: { explicitConsent: { informed: boolean; specific: boolean; clear: boolean; voluntary: boolean; }; dataLocalization: { criticalInformation: boolean; importantData: boolean; personalDataOver1Million: boolean; }; sensitiveData: { separateConsent: boolean; biometricData: boolean; religiousBeliefs: boolean; healthData: boolean; }; }; enforcement: { fines: string; // "Up to 50 million RMB or 5% of revenue" criminalLiability: boolean; }; }

class PIPLConsentManager { async implementPIPLCompliance(): Promise<void> { // Check if PIPL applies if (!this.isPIPLApplicable()) return; // Implement explicit consent requirements await this.getExplicitConsent(); // Handle data localization this.ensureDataLocalization(); // Manage sensitive data separately this.handleSensitiveData(); } private isPIPLApplicable(): boolean { const userLocation = this.detectUserLocation(); const dataProcessingLocation = this.getDataProcessingLocation(); return userLocation === 'CN' || dataProcessingLocation === 'CN' || this.targetingChineseUsers(); } private async getExplicitConsent(): Promise<void> { const consent = await this.displayConsentBanner({ title: '隐私政策', // Privacy Policy in Chinese explicitConsentRequired: true, separateSensitiveDataConsent: true, dataLocalizationNotice: true, minimumAge: 14, // China's minimum age for consent parentalConsentRequired: true }); this.recordPIPLConsent(consent); } }

interface DPDPCompliance { keyPrinciples: { lawfulBasis: string[]; dataMinimization: boolean; accuracy: boolean; storageLimitation: boolean; accountability: boolean; }; consentRequirements: { clear: boolean; specific: boolean; informed: boolean; freeGiven: boolean; retrievable: boolean; }; childrensData: { parentalConsent: boolean; ageThreshold: number; // 18 years verificationRequired: boolean; }; crossBorderTransfers: { governmentApproval: boolean; adequacyDecisions: boolean; contractualSafeguards: boolean; }; }

class GlobalPrivacyComplianceManager { private jurisdictionDetector: JurisdictionDetector; private complianceEngine: ComplianceEngine; private consentManager: ConsentManager; constructor() { this.jurisdictionDetector = new JurisdictionDetector(); this.complianceEngine = new ComplianceEngine(); this.consentManager = new ConsentManager(); } async initializeCompliance(): Promise<void> { // Detect user jurisdiction const jurisdiction = await this.jurisdictionDetector.detect(); // Get applicable laws const applicableLaws = this.getApplicableLaws(jurisdiction); // Generate compliance configuration const config = this.complianceEngine.generateConfig(applicableLaws); // Initialize consent management await this.consentManager.initialize(config); } private getApplicableLaws(jurisdiction: string): PrivacyLaw[] { const lawMap: Record<string, PrivacyLaw[]> = { 'EU': [PrivacyLaw.GDPR, PrivacyLaw.EPRIVACY], 'UK': [PrivacyLaw.UK_GDPR, PrivacyLaw.PECR], 'US-CA': [PrivacyLaw.CCPA, PrivacyLaw.CPRA], 'US-VA': [PrivacyLaw.VCDPA], 'US-CO': [PrivacyLaw.CPA], 'CA': [PrivacyLaw.PIPEDA], 'CA-QC': [PrivacyLaw.PIPEDA, PrivacyLaw.QUEBEC_LAW25], 'BR': [PrivacyLaw.LGPD], 'CN': [PrivacyLaw.PIPL], 'IN': [PrivacyLaw.DPDP], 'AU': [PrivacyLaw.PRIVACY_ACT], 'JP': [PrivacyLaw.JAPAN_PIPA], 'KR': [PrivacyLaw.KOREA_PIPA], 'SG': [PrivacyLaw.SINGAPORE_PDPA] }; return lawMap[jurisdiction] || [PrivacyLaw.DEFAULT]; } } class JurisdictionDetector { async detect(): Promise<string> { // Primary: User preference/explicit selection const userPreference = localStorage.getItem('jurisdiction_preference'); if (userPreference) return userPreference; // Secondary: Geo-IP location const geoLocation = await this.getGeoIPLocation(); if (geoLocation) return this.mapGeoToJurisdiction(geoLocation); // Tertiary: Browser language/locale const browserLocale = navigator.language; return this.mapLocaleToJurisdiction(browserLocale); } private async getGeoIPLocation(): Promise<string | null> { try { const response = await fetch('/api/geo-location'); const data = await response.json(); return data.country; } catch { return null; } } private mapGeoToJurisdiction(country: string): string { const euCountries = ['DE', 'FR', 'IT', 'ES', 'NL', 'PL', 'BE', 'AT', 'PT', 'CZ', 'HU', 'SE', 'GR', 'DK', 'FI', 'SK', 'IE', 'HR', 'LT', 'SI', 'LV', 'EE', 'CY', 'LU', 'MT']; if (euCountries.includes(country)) return 'EU'; if (country === 'GB') return 'UK'; if (country === 'US') return 'US'; // Will need state detection if (country === 'CA') return 'CA'; if (country === 'BR') return 'BR'; if (country === 'CN') return 'CN'; if (country === 'IN') return 'IN'; return 'DEFAULT'; } }

// Automated testing for global compliance describe('Global Privacy Compliance', () => { const jurisdictions = [ { name: 'EU', geoIP: 'DE', expectedLaws: ['GDPR', 'ePrivacy'] }, { name: 'UK', geoIP: 'GB', expectedLaws: ['UK_GDPR', 'PECR'] }, { name: 'California', geoIP: 'US', state: 'CA', expectedLaws: ['CCPA'] }, { name: 'Canada', geoIP: 'CA', expectedLaws: ['PIPEDA'] }, { name: 'Brazil', geoIP: 'BR', expectedLaws: ['LGPD'] }, { name: 'China', geoIP: 'CN', expectedLaws: ['PIPL'] } ]; jurisdictions.forEach(jurisdiction => { describe(`${jurisdiction.name} Compliance`, () => { beforeEach(async () => { // Mock geo-location await mockGeoLocation(jurisdiction.geoIP); if (jurisdiction.state) { await mockState(jurisdiction.state); } }); test('should detect correct jurisdiction', async () => { const detector = new JurisdictionDetector(); const detected = await detector.detect(); expect(detected).toBe(jurisdiction.name.replace(' ', '-')); }); test('should apply correct privacy laws', async () => { const manager = new GlobalPrivacyComplianceManager(); await manager.initializeCompliance(); const config = manager.getCurrentConfig(); expect(config.applicableLaws).toEqual( expect.arrayContaining(jurisdiction.expectedLaws) ); }); test('should display appropriate consent banner', async () => { const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.goto('/'); if (jurisdiction.expectedLaws.includes('GDPR')) { await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="gdpr-banner"]')).toBeVisible(); await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="reject-all"]')).toBeVisible(); } if (jurisdiction.expectedLaws.includes('CCPA')) { await expect(page.locator('text="Do Not Sell"')).toBeVisible(); } }); }); }); });

Harmonization Efforts: International frameworks for cross-border data transfers AI-Specific Regulations: Cookie consent for AI training data Children's Privacy: Enhanced protections becoming global standard Consent Fatigue Solutions: Regulatory push for better UX patterns Real-Time Enforcement: Automated compliance monitoring tools

interface Future PrivacyTech { consentBrokers: { centralizedConsent: boolean; crossSiteConsent: boolean; blockchainConsent: boolean; }; privacyEnhancingTechnologies: { differentialPrivacy: boolean; homomorphicEncryption: boolean; secureMultipartyComputation: boolean; }; automatedCompliance: { aiPoweredAuditing: boolean; realTimeMonitoring: boolean; predictiveCompliance: boolean; }; }
Implement GDPR-level controls globally to simplify compliance management.
Provide summary information upfront with detailed explanations available on demand.
Build privacy controls into your architecture from the beginning.
Conduct quarterly reviews of your privacy program and consent mechanisms.
Work closely with privacy attorneys familiar with each jurisdiction's nuances.
Help users understand their privacy choices through clear, jargon-free explanations.

Global privacy compliance requires a nuanced understanding of each jurisdiction's specific requirements, combined with robust technical implementation and ongoing monitoring. As the regulatory landscape continues to evolve, organizations must balance compliance obligations with user experience considerations. The key to success lies in building flexible, scalable privacy systems that can adapt to new requirements while maintaining user trust and business functionality. By understanding the specific requirements outlined in this guide and implementing comprehensive compliance strategies, organizations can navigate the complex global privacy landscape effectively. Remember that privacy regulations are continuously evolving, and this guide should be supplemented with current legal advice and regular monitoring of regulatory updates in each jurisdiction where you operate.

Prompt engineering has become one of the most crucial skills in the age of large language models (LLMs). Whether you're using ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or any other AI model, the quality of your prompts directly determines the quality of the responses you get. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore the best practices for creating effective prompts that consistently deliver high-quality results. Understanding how to craft good prompts is like learning to communicate effectively with a highly knowledgeable but literal-minded assistant. The better your instructions, the better the outcomes.
documents.s: The Art of Prompt Engineering: How to Create Effective Prompts for AI

documents.t: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and optimizing text inputs (prompts) to elicit the best possible responses from AI language models. It's both an art and a science that involves understanding how these models interpret and respond to different types of instructions. Think of it as writing clear, specific instructions for a very capable but literal assistant. The assistant can perform complex tasks, but only if you communicate your needs effectively.

The difference between a poorly crafted prompt and a well-engineered one can be dramatic: Poor prompt: "Tell me about Earth" Good prompt: "Generate a list of ways that makes Earth unique compared to other planets" The first might give you a generic encyclopedia entry, while the second will provide focused, valuable insights tailored to your specific need.

The Problem: Verbose prompts introduce unnecessary noise that can confuse the model and dilute your intent. ❌ Not Recommended: What do you think could be a good name for a flower shop that specializes in selling bouquets of dried flowers more than fresh flowers? ✅ Recommended: Suggest a name for a flower shop that sells bouquets of dried flowers Why it works: The concise version eliminates unnecessary words while preserving the core request. The model can focus on the essential task without getting distracted by conversational filler.

Vague prompts lead to vague responses. The more specific you are about what you want, the more targeted the response will be. ❌ Too Generic: Tell me about Earth ✅ Specific and Targeted: Generate a list of ways that makes Earth unique compared to other planets The difference: The specific prompt gives the model a clear framework (comparison with other planets) and a specific output format (a list), resulting in a much more useful response.

Multi-part questions often lead to incomplete or imbalanced responses where one part gets more attention than others. ❌ Multiple Tasks: What's the best method of boiling water and why is the sky blue? ✅ Single Task: What's the best method of boiling water? Then separately: Why is the sky blue? Benefits: Single-task prompts ensure each question gets the full attention it deserves and produces more thorough, focused responses.
documents.s: 3. Ask One Task at a Time

documents.t: System instructions help prevent the AI from veering off-topic or providing inappropriate responses. They act as behavioral guidelines for the entire conversation. Example Travel Chatbot System Instruction: You are an AI chatbot for a travel website. Your mission is to provide helpful queries for travelers. Before answering any question, check if it complies with your mission. If not, respond with "Sorry, I can't answer that question." This approach helps maintain focus and prevents the AI from responding to unrelated queries like cooking recipes when it should be helping with travel.

When you need more predictable, controlled outputs, convert open-ended questions into multiple-choice formats. ❌ High Variability (Generative): I'm a high school student. Recommend me a programming activity to improve my skills. ✅ Lower Variability (Classification): I'm a high school student. Which of these activities do you suggest and why: a) learn Python b) learn JavaScript c) learn Fortran Why this works: Classification tasks constrain the possible outputs, making responses more predictable and easier to process programmatically.
documents.s: Turn Generative Tasks into Classification Tasks

documents.t: Zero-shot prompting provides no examples, relying entirely on the model's training to understand the task. Example: Decide whether a Tweet's sentiment is positive, neutral, or negative. Tweet: I loved the new YouTube video you made! Sentiment:

One-shot prompting provides a single example to guide the model's understanding. Example: Decide whether a Tweet's sentiment is positive, neutral, or negative. Tweet: I loved the new YouTube video you made! Sentiment: positive Tweet: That was awful. Super boring 😠 Sentiment:

Few-shot prompting provides multiple examples to establish a clear pattern. Example: Decide whether a Tweet's sentiment is positive, neutral, or negative. Tweet: I loved the new YouTube video you made! Sentiment: positive Tweet: That was awful. Super boring 😠 Sentiment: negative Tweet: Something surprised me about this video - it was actually original. It was not the same old recycled stuff that I always see. Watch it - you will not regret it. Sentiment:

Zero-shot: When you want creative, open-ended responses One-shot: When you need to establish a basic pattern or format Few-shot: When you need consistent, predictable responses that follow a specific pattern
AI models can generate confident-sounding but factually incorrect information, known as "hallucinations." Here's how to minimize them:
❌ "What day is it today?" ✅ "What day of the week typically has the highest retail sales?"
✅ "List the major causes of World War I. If you're uncertain about any point, please indicate that."

✅ "Explain photosynthesis and indicate which parts are well-established science versus current research areas." Note: Asking for citations doesn't eliminate hallucinations, as models can fabricate sources too.
Write a Python function that [specific task]. Include: - Input validation - Error handling - Type hints - A docstring with usage examples

Write a [blog post/email/social media post] about [topic] that: - Targets [specific audience] - Has a [tone: professional/casual/friendly] - Includes [specific elements] - Is approximately [word count] words
Analyze this data and provide: 1. Key trends and patterns 2. Notable outliers or anomalies 3. Three actionable insights 4. Confidence level for each finding [Insert data]
Create variations of your prompt Test with the same input multiple times Compare outputs for consistency and quality Refine based on results

Keep track of prompt variations and their performance: v1.0: "Summarize this article" v1.1: "Summarize this article in 3 bullet points" v1.2: "Summarize this article in 3 bullet points, focusing on key actions and outcomes"
Don't make prompts unnecessarily complex. Start simple and add complexity only when needed.
AI doesn't have access to your screen, previous conversations (unless explicitly provided), or real-time information.
Each model has token limits, knowledge cutoffs, and specific strengths and weaknesses.
Test your prompts with unusual inputs to understand their robustness.
Use open-ended prompts Provide style or tone guidance Include creative constraints for more interesting outputs
Be extremely specific about format Include examples of desired output Specify technical level for the audience
Use system instructions for brand voice Include escalation paths for complex issues Test with challenging customer scenarios
Provide clear input/output format specifications Include error handling instructions Test with edge cases and malformed data

Consistency: How similar are responses to the same prompt? Accuracy: How often are factual claims correct? Relevance: How well does the output match the request? Completeness: Does the response address all parts of the prompt?
Usefulness: Does the output solve your problem? Clarity: Is the response well-structured and understandable? Tone: Does it match your desired communication style?
Keep successful prompts organized by use case Document what works and what doesn't Share effective prompts with your team
Use systematic approaches to test prompt variations Automate testing where possible Track performance over time
Join prompt engineering communities Study examples from others in your field Contribute your own successful patterns
As AI models continue to evolve, prompt engineering techniques will also advance:

Multimodal prompts: Combining text, images, and other media Chain-of-thought prompting: Breaking complex tasks into steps Role-based prompting: Having the AI adopt specific personas or expertise Meta-prompting: Using AI to help design better prompts
Understanding model capabilities and limitations Systematic testing and evaluation methods Domain expertise to create relevant examples Communication skills for clear instruction writing

Effective prompt engineering is a crucial skill in our AI-powered world. By following these best practices—being concise, specific, and strategic about examples—you can dramatically improve the quality and consistency of AI-generated responses. Remember that prompt engineering is both an art and a science. While these guidelines provide a solid foundation, the best prompts often come from experimentation, iteration, and deep understanding of your specific use case. Key takeaways: Start simple and add complexity gradually Test thoroughly with various inputs and edge cases Use examples strategically to guide model behavior Be specific about format, tone, and requirements Consider the model's limitations when designing prompts Iterate based on results rather than assuming first attempts are optimal As AI models become more sophisticated, the ability to communicate effectively with them will only become more valuable. Master these prompt engineering fundamentals, and you'll be well-equipped to leverage AI tools effectively in whatever domain you work in.

In today's web landscape, HTTPS is no longer optional—it's essential. Search engines favor HTTPS sites, browsers mark HTTP sites as "not secure," and users expect their data to be encrypted. Let's Encrypt has revolutionized SSL certificate provisioning by providing free, automated, and open certificates that are trusted by all major browsers. In this comprehensive guide, we'll walk through setting up Let's Encrypt SSL certificates with Nginx, from initial installation to automated renewal, ensuring your website stays secure without manual intervention.
documents.s: Securing Your Website with Let's Encrypt and Nginx: A Complete Guide

documents.t: Let's Encrypt is a free, automated, and open Certificate Authority (CA) run by the Internet Security Research Group (ISRG). It provides domain-validated SSL/TLS certificates at no cost, with the mission of creating a more secure and privacy-respecting web.

Free: No cost for certificates Automated: Certificates can be issued and renewed automatically Open: The protocol and software are open source Trusted: Certificates are trusted by all major browsers Domain Validated: Quick verification process 90-day Validity: Forces automation and reduces risk of compromised keys

Before we begin, ensure you have: A domain name pointing to your server Nginx installed and running Root or sudo access to your server Port 80 accessible from the internet A basic Nginx configuration for your domain
Certbot is the official Let's Encrypt client that automates certificate issuance and renewal.
sudo apt update sudo apt install snapd sudo snap install core; sudo snap refresh core sudo snap install --classic certbot sudo ln -s /snap/bin/certbot /usr/bin/certbot

sudo dnf install epel-release sudo dnf install snapd sudo systemctl enable --now snapd.socket sudo ln -s /var/lib/snapd/snap /snap sudo snap install core; sudo snap refresh core sudo snap install --classic certbot sudo ln -s /snap/bin/certbot /usr/bin/certbot
# Ubuntu/Debian sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx # CentOS/RHEL sudo yum install certbot python3-certbot-nginx

Before obtaining SSL certificates, set up a basic HTTP configuration: # /etc/nginx/sites-available/example.com server { listen 80; server_name example.com www.example.com; root /var/www/example.com; index index.html index.htm; location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; } # Let's Encrypt challenge location location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/example.com; } } Enable the site and test the configuration: sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/example.com /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl reload nginx

The easiest way is to let Certbot automatically configure Nginx: sudo certbot --nginx -d example.com -d www.example.com This command will: Verify domain ownership Obtain the certificate Automatically configure Nginx Set up HTTP to HTTPS redirects
If you prefer to configure Nginx manually: sudo certbot certonly --nginx -d example.com -d www.example.com Then manually configure Nginx with the obtained certificates.
For more control over the verification process: sudo certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/example.com -d example.com -d www.example.com

If you used the certificate-only method, here's how to configure Nginx manually: # /etc/nginx/sites-available/example.com server { listen 80; server_name example.com www.example.com; # Redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri; } server { listen 443 ssl http2; server_name example.com www.example.com; # SSL Configuration ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem; # SSL Security Configuration ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384; ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off; ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m; ssl_session_timeout 10m; # OCSP Stapling ssl_stapling on; ssl_stapling_verify on; ssl_trusted_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/chain.pem; resolver 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4 valid=300s; resolver_timeout 5s; # Security Headers add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always; add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always; add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always; add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always; root /var/www/example.com; index index.html index.htm; location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; } # Let's Encrypt renewal location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/example.com; } } Test and reload Nginx: sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl reload nginx
Generate Diffie-Hellman parameters for enhanced security: sudo openssl dhparam -out /etc/nginx/dhparam.pem 2048 Add to your Nginx configuration: ssl_dhparam /etc/nginx/dhparam.pem;

Create a reusable SSL configuration: # /etc/nginx/snippets/ssl-params.conf ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305; ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off; ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:10m; ssl_session_timeout 10m; # OCSP Stapling ssl_stapling on; ssl_stapling_verify on; resolver 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4 valid=300s; resolver_timeout 5s; # Diffie-Hellman parameter ssl_dhparam /etc/nginx/dhparam.pem; # Security Headers add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always; add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always; add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always; add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always; Include it in your server blocks: server { listen 443 ssl http2; server_name example.com; ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem; ssl_trusted_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/chain.pem; include /etc/nginx/snippets/ssl-params.conf; # Your site configuration... }
Let's Encrypt certificates expire after 90 days, so automation is crucial.

Certbot automatically installs a systemd timer. Check if it's active: sudo systemctl status snap.certbot.renew.timer If not using snap, create a cron job: sudo crontab -e Add this line to check for renewal twice daily: 0 12 * * * /usr/bin/certbot renew --quiet
Test the renewal process without actually renewing: sudo certbot renew --dry-run

Add hooks to reload Nginx after successful renewal: sudo certbot renew --deploy-hook "systemctl reload nginx" Or create a renewal configuration file: # /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-nginx.sh #!/bin/bash systemctl reload nginx # Make it executable sudo chmod +x /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/reload-nginx.sh
sudo certbot --nginx -d example.com -d www.example.com -d api.example.com -d blog.example.com

For wildcard certificates, you need DNS challenge: sudo certbot certonly --manual --preferred-challenges dns -d example.com -d *.example.com You'll need to add TXT records to your DNS for verification.

For automated wildcard certificates, use DNS plugins: # Cloudflare example sudo snap install certbot-dns-cloudflare sudo certbot certonly --dns-cloudflare --dns-cloudflare-credentials /etc/letsencrypt/cloudflare.ini -d example.com -d *.example.com

For applications behind Nginx: server { listen 443 ssl http2; server_name api.example.com; ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/api.example.com/fullchain.pem; ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/api.example.com/privkey.pem; include /etc/nginx/snippets/ssl-params.conf; location / { proxy_pass http://localhost:3000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade'; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade; # Timeouts proxy_connect_timeout 60s; proxy_send_timeout 60s; proxy_read_timeout 60s; } }
Check certificate details: sudo certbot certificates View certificate information: openssl x509 -in /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/cert.pem -text -noout

Rate Limits: Let's Encrypt has rate limits (50 certificates per domain per week) DNS Propagation: Ensure DNS records have propagated Firewall: Ensure ports 80 and 443 are open Webroot Permissions: Ensure Nginx can write to webroot directory

Create a script to monitor certificate expiry: #!/bin/bash # /usr/local/bin/check-ssl-expiry.sh DOMAIN="example.com" THRESHOLD=30 EXPIRY_DATE=$(echo | openssl s_client -servername $DOMAIN -connect $DOMAIN:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates | grep notAfter | cut -d= -f2) EXPIRY_EPOCH=$(date -d "$EXPIRY_DATE" +%s) CURRENT_EPOCH=$(date +%s) DAYS_UNTIL_EXPIRY=$(( ($EXPIRY_EPOCH - $CURRENT_EPOCH) / 86400 )) if [ $DAYS_UNTIL_EXPIRY -lt $THRESHOLD ]; then echo "SSL certificate for $DOMAIN expires in $DAYS_UNTIL_EXPIRY days!" # Send alert (email, Slack, etc.) fi
Use tools like: SSL Labs SSL Test Mozilla Observatory Security Headers
Monitor your certificates at: crt.sh Certificate Transparency logs
Submit your domain to the HSTS preload list for enhanced security.

For containerized applications: # docker-compose.yml version: '3.8' services: nginx: image: nginx:alpine ports: - "80:80" - "443:443" volumes: - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf - /etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt:ro certbot: image: certbot/certbot volumes: - /etc/letsencrypt:/etc/letsencrypt - /var/www/certbot:/var/www/certbot command: certonly --webroot -w /var/www/certbot -d example.com --email admin@example.com --agree-tos --no-eff-email

Let's Encrypt with Nginx provides a robust, free solution for securing your websites with SSL/TLS certificates. The combination of automated certificate issuance, renewal, and Nginx's high-performance SSL handling creates a powerful security setup that scales from small personal sites to large enterprise applications. Key takeaways: Always use automated renewal to prevent certificate expiry Implement proper security headers for enhanced protection Monitor certificate health and expiry dates Use strong SSL configurations following current best practices Test your SSL configuration regularly With this setup, you'll have a secure, automated SSL certificate management system that requires minimal maintenance while providing maximum security for your users.

Building secure microservices with proper authentication and authorization is one of the most critical aspects of modern application development. When deploying to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Kubernetes, we need to consider not only the application-level security patterns but also the infrastructure and container orchestration security layers. This comprehensive guide demonstrates how to implement robust authentication and authorization in a NestJS microservices architecture deployed on GCP Kubernetes, incorporating enterprise-grade security patterns including RBAC, JWT tokens, service mesh security, and cloud-native best practices.
documents.s: Building Secure Microservices: Authentication & Authorization with NestJS on GCP Kubernetes

documents.t: Authentication: Verifying who the user is (identity verification) Authorization: Determining what the authenticated user can do (access control)

RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): Users have roles, roles have permissions ReBAC (Relationship-Based Access Control): Access based on user's relationship to resources ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control): Access based on user, resource, and environment attributes

// apps/auth-service/src/auth.service.ts import { Injectable, UnauthorizedException, ConflictException } from '@nestjs/common'; import { JwtService } from '@nestjs/jwt'; import { InjectRepository } from '@nestjs/typeorm'; import { Repository } from 'typeorm'; import * as bcrypt from 'bcryptjs'; import { User } from './entities/user.entity'; import { Role } from './entities/role.entity'; import { Permission } from './entities/permission.entity'; export interface JwtPayload { sub: string; email: string; roles: string[]; permissions: string[]; companyId?: string; departmentId?: string; iat?: number; exp?: number; } @Injectable() export class AuthService { constructor( @InjectRepository(User) private readonly userRepository: Repository<User>, @InjectRepository(Role) private readonly roleRepository: Repository<Role>, private readonly jwtService: JwtService, ) {} async register(registerDto: RegisterDto): Promise<{ user: User; tokens: TokenPair }> { // Check if user already exists const existingUser = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { email: registerDto.email } }); if (existingUser) { throw new ConflictException('User with this email already exists'); } // Hash password const saltRounds = 12; const hashedPassword = await bcrypt.hash(registerDto.password, saltRounds); // Create user with default role const defaultRole = await this.roleRepository.findOne({ where: { name: 'USER' }, relations: ['permissions'] }); const user = this.userRepository.create({ ...registerDto, password: hashedPassword, roles: defaultRole ? [defaultRole] : [], isActive: true, emailVerified: false, }); const savedUser = await this.userRepository.save(user); // Generate tokens const tokens = await this.generateTokens(savedUser); // Remove password from response delete savedUser.password; return { user: savedUser, tokens }; } async login(loginDto: LoginDto): Promise<{ user: User; tokens: TokenPair }> { // Find user with roles and permissions const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { email: loginDto.email }, relations: ['roles', 'roles.permissions', 'company', 'department'] }); if (!user) { throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid credentials'); } // Check if user is active if (!user.isActive) { throw new UnauthorizedException('Account is deactivated'); } // Verify password const isPasswordValid = await bcrypt.compare(loginDto.password, user.password); if (!isPasswordValid) { throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid credentials'); } // Update last login user.lastLoginAt = new Date(); await this.userRepository.save(user); // Generate tokens const tokens = await this.generateTokens(user); // Remove password from response delete user.password; return { user, tokens }; } async generateTokens(user: User): Promise<TokenPair> { const roles = user.roles?.map(role => role.name) || []; const permissions = user.roles?.flatMap(role => role.permissions?.map(permission => permission.name) || [] ) || []; const payload: JwtPayload = { sub: user.id, email: user.email, roles, permissions, companyId: user.company?.id, departmentId: user.department?.id, }; const [accessToken, refreshToken] = await Promise.all([ this.jwtService.signAsync(payload, { secret: process.env.JWT_ACCESS_SECRET, expiresIn: process.env.JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRES_IN || '15m', }), this.jwtService.signAsync( { sub: user.id, type: 'refresh' }, { secret: process.env.JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, expiresIn: process.env.JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN || '7d', } ), ]); return { accessToken, refreshToken }; } async refreshTokens(refreshToken: string): Promise<TokenPair> { try { const payload = await this.jwtService.verifyAsync(refreshToken, { secret: process.env.JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, }); if (payload.type !== 'refresh') { throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid token type'); } const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id: payload.sub }, relations: ['roles', 'roles.permissions', 'company', 'department'] }); if (!user || !user.isActive) { throw new UnauthorizedException('User not found or inactive'); } return this.generateTokens(user); } catch (error) { throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid refresh token'); } } async validateUser(userId: string): Promise<User | null> { return this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id: userId }, relations: ['roles', 'roles.permissions', 'company', 'department'] }); } async logout(userId: string): Promise<void> { // In a production environment, you might want to blacklist the JWT // or store logout events for audit purposes await this.userRepository.update(userId, { lastLogoutAt: new Date() }); } } interface TokenPair { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string; } // DTOs export class RegisterDto { email: string; password: string; firstName: string; lastName: string; companyId?: string; departmentId?: string; } export class LoginDto { email: string; password: string; }

// apps/auth-service/src/entities/user.entity.ts import { Entity, PrimaryGeneratedColumn, Column, ManyToMany, ManyToOne, JoinTable, CreateDateColumn, UpdateDateColumn } from 'typeorm'; import { Role } from './role.entity'; import { Company } from './company.entity'; import { Department } from './department.entity'; @Entity('users') export class User { @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') id: string; @Column({ unique: true }) email: string; @Column() password: string; @Column() firstName: string; @Column() lastName: string; @Column({ default: true }) isActive: boolean; @Column({ default: false }) emailVerified: boolean; @Column({ nullable: true }) phoneNumber: string; @Column({ nullable: true }) avatarUrl: string; @Column({ nullable: true }) lastLoginAt: Date; @Column({ nullable: true }) lastLogoutAt: Date; @CreateDateColumn() createdAt: Date; @UpdateDateColumn() updatedAt: Date; @ManyToMany(() => Role, role => role.users, { eager: true }) @JoinTable({ name: 'user_roles', joinColumn: { name: 'userId', referencedColumnName: 'id' }, inverseJoinColumn: { name: 'roleId', referencedColumnName: 'id' } }) roles: Role[]; @ManyToOne(() => Company, company => company.users) company: Company; @ManyToOne(() => Department, department => department.users) department: Department; } // apps/auth-service/src/entities/role.entity.ts @Entity('roles') export class Role { @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') id: string; @Column({ unique: true }) name: string; @Column({ nullable: true }) description: string; @Column({ default: true }) isActive: boolean; @CreateDateColumn() createdAt: Date; @UpdateDateColumn() updatedAt: Date; @ManyToMany(() => User, user => user.roles) users: User[]; @ManyToMany(() => Permission, permission => permission.roles, { eager: true }) @JoinTable({ name: 'role_permissions', joinColumn: { name: 'roleId', referencedColumnName: 'id' }, inverseJoinColumn: { name: 'permissionId', referencedColumnName: 'id' } }) permissions: Permission[]; } // apps/auth-service/src/entities/permission.entity.ts @Entity('permissions') export class Permission { @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') id: string; @Column({ unique: true }) name: string; @Column({ nullable: true }) description: string; @Column() resource: string; // e.g., 'orders', 'products', 'users' @Column() action: string; // e.g., 'create', 'read', 'update', 'delete' @Column({ default: true }) isActive: boolean; @CreateDateColumn() createdAt: Date; @UpdateDateColumn() updatedAt: Date; @ManyToMany(() => Role, role => role.permissions) roles: Role[]; }

// libs/auth/src/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts import { Injectable, UnauthorizedException } from '@nestjs/common'; import { AuthGuard } from '@nestjs/passport'; import { ExecutionContext } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class JwtAuthGuard extends AuthGuard('jwt') { canActivate(context: ExecutionContext) { return super.canActivate(context); } handleRequest(err: any, user: any, info: any, context: ExecutionContext) { if (err || !user) { throw err || new UnauthorizedException('Invalid or expired token'); } return user; } } // libs/auth/src/guards/roles.guard.ts import { Injectable, CanActivate, ExecutionContext, ForbiddenException } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'; import { ROLES_KEY } from '../decorators/roles.decorator'; @Injectable() export class RolesGuard implements CanActivate { constructor(private reflector: Reflector) {} canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean { const requiredRoles = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<string[]>(ROLES_KEY, [ context.getHandler(), context.getClass(), ]); if (!requiredRoles) { return true; } const { user } = context.switchToHttp().getRequest(); if (!user) { throw new ForbiddenException('User not authenticated'); } const hasRole = requiredRoles.some(role => user.roles?.includes(role)); if (!hasRole) { throw new ForbiddenException(`Required roles: ${requiredRoles.join(', ')}`); } return true; } } // libs/auth/src/guards/permissions.guard.ts import { Injectable, CanActivate, ExecutionContext, ForbiddenException } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'; import { PERMISSIONS_KEY } from '../decorators/permissions.decorator'; @Injectable() export class PermissionsGuard implements CanActivate { constructor(private reflector: Reflector) {} canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean { const requiredPermissions = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<string[]>(PERMISSIONS_KEY, [ context.getHandler(), context.getClass(), ]); if (!requiredPermissions) { return true; } const { user } = context.switchToHttp().getRequest(); if (!user) { throw new ForbiddenException('User not authenticated'); } const hasPermission = requiredPermissions.every(permission => user.permissions?.includes(permission) ); if (!hasPermission) { throw new ForbiddenException(`Required permissions: ${requiredPermissions.join(', ')}`); } return true; } } // libs/auth/src/decorators/roles.decorator.ts import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common'; export const ROLES_KEY = 'roles'; export const Roles = (...roles: string[]) => SetMetadata(ROLES_KEY, roles); // libs/auth/src/decorators/permissions.decorator.ts import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common'; export const PERMISSIONS_KEY = 'permissions'; export const RequirePermissions = (...permissions: string[]) => SetMetadata(PERMISSIONS_KEY, permissions); // libs/auth/src/decorators/current-user.decorator.ts import { createParamDecorator, ExecutionContext } from '@nestjs/common'; export const CurrentUser = createParamDecorator( (data: unknown, ctx: ExecutionContext) => { const request = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest(); return request.user; }, );

// libs/auth/src/guards/resource-access.guard.ts import { Injectable, CanActivate, ExecutionContext, ForbiddenException } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'; import { ClientProxy } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { Inject } from '@nestjs/common'; import { firstValueFrom } from 'rxjs'; export interface ResourceAccessConfig { resource: string; action: string; ownershipField?: string; companyScoped?: boolean; departmentScoped?: boolean; } export const RESOURCE_ACCESS_KEY = 'resource_access'; export const ResourceAccess = (config: ResourceAccessConfig) => SetMetadata(RESOURCE_ACCESS_KEY, config); @Injectable() export class ResourceAccessGuard implements CanActivate { constructor( private reflector: Reflector, @Inject('USER_SERVICE') private userServiceClient: ClientProxy, ) {} async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> { const config = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<ResourceAccessConfig>( RESOURCE_ACCESS_KEY, [context.getHandler(), context.getClass()], ); if (!config) { return true; } const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest(); const user = request.user; if (!user) { throw new ForbiddenException('User not authenticated'); } // Check basic permission const hasPermission = user.permissions?.includes(`${config.resource}:${config.action}`); if (!hasPermission) { throw new ForbiddenException(`Permission denied: ${config.resource}:${config.action}`); } // Check ownership if configured if (config.ownershipField) { const resourceId = request.params.id || request.body[config.ownershipField]; if (resourceId) { const hasAccess = await this.checkResourceAccess( user, config.resource, resourceId, config ); if (!hasAccess) { throw new ForbiddenException('Access denied to this resource'); } } } return true; } private async checkResourceAccess( user: any, resource: string, resourceId: string, config: ResourceAccessConfig ): Promise<boolean> { try { const result = await firstValueFrom( this.userServiceClient.send('check_resource_access', { userId: user.sub, resource, resourceId, config, }) ); return result.hasAccess; } catch (error) { console.error('Error checking resource access:', error); return false; } } }

// apps/api-gateway/src/main.ts import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core'; import { ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common'; import { DocumentBuilder, SwaggerModule } from '@nestjs/swagger'; import helmet from 'helmet'; import * as compression from 'compression'; import * as morgan from 'morgan'; import { AppModule } from './app.module'; async function bootstrap() { const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule); // Security middleware app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"], scriptSrc: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"], styleSrc: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"], imgSrc: ["'self'", "data:", "https:"], }, }, hsts: { maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true, preload: true, }, })); app.use(compression()); app.use(morgan('combined')); // Enable CORS app.enableCors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS?.split(',') || ['http://localhost:3000'], methods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'PATCH'], allowedHeaders: ['Content-Type', 'Authorization'], credentials: true, }); // Global validation pipe app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, transform: true, })); // Swagger documentation const config = new DocumentBuilder() .setTitle('E-commerce Microservices API') .setDescription('Secure microservices API with authentication and authorization') .setVersion('1.0') .addBearerAuth( { type: 'http', scheme: 'bearer', bearerFormat: 'JWT', name: 'JWT', description: 'Enter JWT token', in: 'header', }, 'JWT-auth', ) .build(); const document = SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config); SwaggerModule.setup('api', app, document); const port = process.env.PORT || 3000; await app.listen(port, '0.0.0.0'); console.log(`API Gateway is running on: http://localhost:${port}`); } bootstrap(); // apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.controller.ts import { Controller, Post, Body, UseGuards, Get, Req } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientProxy } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { Inject } from '@nestjs/common'; import { firstValueFrom } from 'rxjs'; import { JwtAuthGuard } from '@app/auth'; import { CurrentUser } from '@app/auth'; import { ApiTags, ApiOperation, ApiBearerAuth } from '@nestjs/swagger'; @ApiTags('Authentication') @Controller('auth') export class AuthController { constructor( @Inject('AUTH_SERVICE') private authServiceClient: ClientProxy, ) {} @Post('register') @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Register a new user' }) async register(@Body() registerDto: any) { return firstValueFrom( this.authServiceClient.send('auth.register', registerDto) ); } @Post('login') @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Login user' }) async login(@Body() loginDto: any) { return firstValueFrom( this.authServiceClient.send('auth.login', loginDto) ); } @Post('refresh') @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Refresh access token' }) async refresh(@Body() refreshDto: { refreshToken: string }) { return firstValueFrom( this.authServiceClient.send('auth.refresh', refreshDto) ); } @Post('logout') @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) @ApiBearerAuth('JWT-auth') @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Logout user' }) async logout(@CurrentUser() user: any) { return firstValueFrom( this.authServiceClient.send('auth.logout', { userId: user.sub }) ); } @Get('profile') @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) @ApiBearerAuth('JWT-auth') @ApiOperation({ summary: 'Get current user profile' }) async getProfile(@CurrentUser() user: any) { return firstValueFrom( this.authServiceClient.send('auth.profile', { userId: user.sub }) ); } }

// apps/order-service/src/orders.controller.ts import { Controller, Get, Post, Body, Param, UseGuards, Query } from '@nestjs/common'; import { JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard, PermissionsGuard, ResourceAccessGuard } from '@app/auth'; import { Roles, RequirePermissions, ResourceAccess, CurrentUser } from '@app/auth'; import { ApiTags, ApiBearerAuth } from '@nestjs/swagger'; @ApiTags('Orders') @Controller('orders') @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) @ApiBearerAuth('JWT-auth') export class OrdersController { constructor(private readonly ordersService: OrdersService) {} @Post() @UseGuards(PermissionsGuard) @RequirePermissions('orders:create') async createOrder( @Body() createOrderDto: CreateOrderDto, @CurrentUser() user: any ) { return this.ordersService.create(createOrderDto, user); } @Get() @UseGuards(PermissionsGuard) @RequirePermissions('orders:read') async getOrders( @Query() query: GetOrdersDto, @CurrentUser() user: any ) { return this.ordersService.findAllForUser(query, user); } @Get(':id') @UseGuards(ResourceAccessGuard) @ResourceAccess({ resource: 'orders', action: 'read', ownershipField: 'userId', companyScoped: true }) async getOrder(@Param('id') id: string) { return this.ordersService.findOne(id); } @Post(':id/cancel') @UseGuards(ResourceAccessGuard) @ResourceAccess({ resource: 'orders', action: 'cancel', ownershipField: 'userId' }) async cancelOrder(@Param('id') id: string, @CurrentUser() user: any) { return this.ordersService.cancel(id, user); } @Get('admin/all') @UseGuards(RolesGuard) @Roles('ADMIN', 'ORDER_MANAGER') async getAllOrdersAdmin(@Query() query: AdminGetOrdersDto) { return this.ordersService.findAllAdmin(query); } } // apps/order-service/src/orders.service.ts @Injectable() export class OrdersService { constructor( @InjectRepository(Order) private orderRepository: Repository<Order>, @Inject('USER_SERVICE') private userServiceClient: ClientProxy, ) {} async create(createOrderDto: CreateOrderDto, user: any): Promise<Order> { // Verify user can create orders in their company/department const canCreate = await this.checkUserPermission( user, 'orders:create', createOrderDto.companyId ); if (!canCreate) { throw new ForbiddenException('Cannot create orders for this company'); } const order = this.orderRepository.create({ ...createOrderDto, userId: user.sub, companyId: user.companyId, status: OrderStatus.PENDING, }); return this.orderRepository.save(order); } async findAllForUser(query: GetOrdersDto, user: any): Promise<Order[]> { const queryBuilder = this.orderRepository.createQueryBuilder('order'); // Apply user-specific filters based on roles if (user.roles.includes('ADMIN')) { // Admins can see all orders } else if (user.roles.includes('COMPANY_MANAGER')) { // Company managers can see company orders queryBuilder.where('order.companyId = :companyId', { companyId: user.companyId }); } else { // Regular users can only see their own orders queryBuilder.where('order.userId = :userId', { userId: user.sub }); } // Apply additional filters if (query.status) { queryBuilder.andWhere('order.status = :status', { status: query.status }); } if (query.startDate) { queryBuilder.andWhere('order.createdAt >= :startDate', { startDate: query.startDate }); } return queryBuilder.getMany(); } private async checkUserPermission( user: any, permission: string, resourceId?: string ): Promise<boolean> { try { const result = await firstValueFrom( this.userServiceClient.send('check_permission', { userId: user.sub, permission, resourceId, context: { companyId: user.companyId, departmentId: user.departmentId, } }) ); return result.hasPermission; } catch (error) { console.error('Error checking user permission:', error); return false; } } }
