Message queues are the backbone of modern microservice architectures, enabling asynchronous communication, decoupling services, and providing fault tolerance. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore how to implement message queues in NestJS microservices and compare the most popular message queue solutions: RabbitMQ, Redis, Apache Kafka, and AWS SQS.
documents.s: Building Scalable Microservices with NestJS: Message Queues Implementation and Comparison Guide

documents.t: Decoupled Services: Services don't need to wait for synchronous responses Better Performance: Non-blocking operations improve overall system throughput Fault Tolerance: Messages persist even if consumers are temporarily unavailable Scalability: Independent scaling of producers and consumers

Message Persistence: Critical data survives service restarts and failures Retry Mechanisms: Automatic retry logic for failed message processing Dead Letter Queues: Failed messages are preserved for analysis At-Least-Once Delivery: Guarantees message delivery under normal conditions

Event-Driven Architecture: Services communicate through domain events CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation): Separate read/write operations Saga Pattern: Distributed transaction management across services Pub/Sub Pattern: One-to-many message distribution

Best For: Complex routing, guaranteed delivery, enterprise applications Pros: Advanced routing capabilities (exchanges, bindings) Strong consistency guarantees Built-in management UI Excellent NestJS integration Support for multiple messaging patterns Cons: Higher resource consumption More complex setup and configuration Not ideal for extremely high throughput scenarios Use Cases: E-commerce order processing Financial transaction systems Task queues with complex routing

Best For: High performance, simple pub/sub, caching + messaging Pros: Extremely fast (in-memory) Simple setup and configuration Multiple data structures support Built-in persistence options Great for real-time applications Cons: Limited message persistence guarantees Memory constraints for large message volumes Basic routing capabilities Use Cases: Real-time notifications Chat applications Simple event broadcasting Cache invalidation events

Best For: High throughput, event streaming, big data pipelines Pros: Exceptional throughput and scalability Event sourcing capabilities Distributed and fault-tolerant Long-term message retention Stream processing support Cons: Complex setup and operations Higher latency for small messages Steep learning curve Resource intensive Use Cases: Event sourcing systems Real-time analytics Log aggregation High-volume transaction processing

Best For: Cloud-native applications, serverless architectures Pros: Fully managed service Automatic scaling Pay-per-use pricing model Integrated with AWS ecosystem Built-in security features Cons: Vendor lock-in Limited message size (256KB) Potential latency in cross-region scenarios Less flexible than self-hosted solutions Use Cases: Serverless applications AWS-native microservices Background job processing Decoupling AWS services

Installation and Setup​ npm install @nestjs/microservices amqplib amqp-connection-manager Message Queue Configuration​ // rabbitmq.config.ts import { Transport } from '@nestjs/microservices'; export const rabbitmqConfig = { transport: Transport.RMQ, options: { urls: [process.env.RABBITMQ_URL || 'amqp://localhost:5672'], queue: 'main_queue', queueOptions: { durable: true, }, prefetchCount: 10, socketOptions: { heartbeatIntervalInSeconds: 60, reconnectTimeInSeconds: 5, }, }, }; Producer Service​ // producer.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientProxy, ClientProxyFactory } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { rabbitmqConfig } from './rabbitmq.config'; @Injectable() export class ProducerService { private client: ClientProxy; constructor() { this.client = ClientProxyFactory.create(rabbitmqConfig); } async sendOrderCreated(orderData: any) { const pattern = 'order.created'; return this.client.emit(pattern, orderData).toPromise(); } async sendPaymentRequest(paymentData: any) { const pattern = 'payment.process'; return this.client.send(pattern, paymentData).toPromise(); } async onModuleDestroy() { await this.client.close(); } } Consumer Controller​ // order.controller.ts import { Controller } from '@nestjs/common'; import { MessagePattern, Payload } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { OrderService } from './order.service'; @Controller() export class OrderController { constructor(private readonly orderService: OrderService) {} @MessagePattern('order.created') async handleOrderCreated(@Payload() data: any) { console.log('Processing order:', data); try { await this.orderService.processOrder(data); return { success: true, message: 'Order processed successfully' }; } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to process order:', error); throw error; } } @MessagePattern('order.cancelled') async handleOrderCancelled(@Payload() data: any) { console.log('Cancelling order:', data); await this.orderService.cancelOrder(data.orderId); return { success: true }; } } Microservice Bootstrap​ // main.ts import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core'; import { AppModule } from './app.module'; import { rabbitmqConfig } from './rabbitmq.config'; async function bootstrap() { const app = await NestFactory.createMicroservice(AppModule, rabbitmqConfig); await app.listen(); console.log('Order microservice is listening on RabbitMQ'); } bootstrap();

Installation and Setup​ npm install @nestjs/microservices redis Redis Configuration​ // redis.config.ts import { Transport } from '@nestjs/microservices'; export const redisConfig = { transport: Transport.REDIS, options: { host: process.env.REDIS_HOST || 'localhost', port: parseInt(process.env.REDIS_PORT) || 6379, password: process.env.REDIS_PASSWORD, retryAttempts: 5, retryDelay: 3000, }, }; Redis Producer​ // redis-producer.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientProxy, ClientProxyFactory } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { redisConfig } from './redis.config'; @Injectable() export class RedisProducerService { private client: ClientProxy; constructor() { this.client = ClientProxyFactory.create(redisConfig); } async publishNotification(notification: any) { return this.client.emit('notification.send', notification); } async publishCacheInvalidation(cacheKey: string) { return this.client.emit('cache.invalidate', { key: cacheKey }); } } Redis Consumer​ // redis-consumer.controller.ts import { Controller } from '@nestjs/common'; import { EventPattern, Payload } from '@nestjs/microservices'; @Controller() export class RedisConsumerController { @EventPattern('notification.send') async handleNotification(@Payload() data: any) { console.log('Sending notification:', data); // Implement notification logic (email, SMS, push, etc.) } @EventPattern('cache.invalidate') async handleCacheInvalidation(@Payload() data: { key: string }) { console.log('Invalidating cache:', data.key); // Implement cache invalidation logic } }

Installation and Setup​ npm install @nestjs/microservices kafkajs Kafka Configuration​ // kafka.config.ts import { Transport } from '@nestjs/microservices'; export const kafkaConfig = { transport: Transport.KAFKA, options: { client: { clientId: 'order-service', brokers: [process.env.KAFKA_BROKER || 'localhost:9092'], }, consumer: { groupId: 'order-consumer-group', allowAutoTopicCreation: true, }, producer: { allowAutoTopicCreation: true, }, }, }; Kafka Producer​ // kafka-producer.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientKafka, ClientProxyFactory } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { kafkaConfig } from './kafka.config'; @Injectable() export class KafkaProducerService { private kafka: ClientKafka; constructor() { this.kafka = ClientProxyFactory.create(kafkaConfig) as ClientKafka; } async onModuleInit() { await this.kafka.connect(); } async publishEvent(topic: string, event: any) { return this.kafka.emit(topic, { key: event.id, value: JSON.stringify(event), timestamp: Date.now().toString(), }); } async publishOrderEvent(orderEvent: any) { return this.publishEvent('order-events', orderEvent); } async onModuleDestroy() { await this.kafka.close(); } } Kafka Consumer​ // kafka-consumer.controller.ts import { Controller } from '@nestjs/common'; import { EventPattern, Payload, Ctx, KafkaContext } from '@nestjs/microservices'; @Controller() export class KafkaConsumerController { @EventPattern('order-events') async handleOrderEvent(@Payload() message: any, @Ctx() context: KafkaContext) { const { partition, offset, timestamp } = context.getMessage(); console.log('Received order event:', { value: message, partition, offset, timestamp, }); try { // Process the order event await this.processOrderEvent(JSON.parse(message.value)); // Manually commit offset (if needed) const heartbeat = context.getHeartbeat(); await heartbeat(); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to process order event:', error); throw error; } } private async processOrderEvent(event: any) { switch (event.type) { case 'ORDER_CREATED': await this.handleOrderCreated(event.data); break; case 'ORDER_UPDATED': await this.handleOrderUpdated(event.data); break; case 'ORDER_CANCELLED': await this.handleOrderCancelled(event.data); break; default: console.warn('Unknown event type:', event.type); } } }

Installation and Setup​ npm install @aws-sdk/client-sqs SQS Service Implementation​ // sqs.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { SQSClient, SendMessageCommand, ReceiveMessageCommand, DeleteMessageCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-sqs'; @Injectable() export class SQSService { private readonly sqsClient: SQSClient; private readonly queueUrl: string; constructor() { this.sqsClient = new SQSClient({ region: process.env.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1', credentials: { accessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, secretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, }, }); this.queueUrl = process.env.SQS_QUEUE_URL; } async sendMessage(messageBody: any, delaySeconds?: number) { const command = new SendMessageCommand({ QueueUrl: this.queueUrl, MessageBody: JSON.stringify(messageBody), DelaySeconds: delaySeconds || 0, MessageAttributes: { 'timestamp': { DataType: 'String', StringValue: new Date().toISOString(), }, 'service': { DataType: 'String', StringValue: 'order-service', }, }, }); return await this.sqsClient.send(command); } async receiveMessages(maxMessages: number = 10) { const command = new ReceiveMessageCommand({ QueueUrl: this.queueUrl, MaxNumberOfMessages: maxMessages, WaitTimeSeconds: 20, // Long polling MessageAttributeNames: ['All'], }); return await this.sqsClient.send(command); } async deleteMessage(receiptHandle: string) { const command = new DeleteMessageCommand({ QueueUrl: this.queueUrl, ReceiptHandle: receiptHandle, }); return await this.sqsClient.send(command); } } SQS Consumer Service​ // sqs-consumer.service.ts import { Injectable, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common'; import { SQSService } from './sqs.service'; @Injectable() export class SQSConsumerService implements OnModuleInit { private isPolling = false; constructor(private readonly sqsService: SQSService) {} onModuleInit() { this.startPolling(); } private async startPolling() { if (this.isPolling) return; this.isPolling = true; while (this.isPolling) { try { const result = await this.sqsService.receiveMessages(10); if (result.Messages && result.Messages.length > 0) { await Promise.all( result.Messages.map(message => this.processMessage(message)) ); } } catch (error) { console.error('Error polling SQS:', error); await this.sleep(5000); // Wait 5 seconds before retrying } } } private async processMessage(message: any) { try { const messageBody = JSON.parse(message.Body); console.log('Processing SQS message:', messageBody); // Process your message here await this.handleMessage(messageBody); // Delete message after successful processing await this.sqsService.deleteMessage(message.ReceiptHandle); } catch (error) { console.error('Failed to process message:', error); // Message will be returned to queue after visibility timeout } } private async handleMessage(messageBody: any) { // Implement your business logic here switch (messageBody.type) { case 'ORDER_CREATED': await this.handleOrderCreated(messageBody.data); break; case 'PAYMENT_PROCESSED': await this.handlePaymentProcessed(messageBody.data); break; default: console.warn('Unknown message type:', messageBody.type); } } private async sleep(ms: number) { return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms)); } }

// dead-letter.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class DeadLetterService { async handleFailedMessage(message: any, error: Error, retryCount: number) { if (retryCount >= 3) { // Send to dead letter queue await this.sendToDeadLetterQueue({ originalMessage: message, error: error.message, failedAt: new Date(), retryCount, }); } else { // Retry with exponential backoff const delay = Math.pow(2, retryCount) * 1000; setTimeout(() => { this.retryMessage(message, retryCount + 1); }, delay); } } private async sendToDeadLetterQueue(failedMessage: any) { // Implementation depends on your message queue choice console.log('Sending to dead letter queue:', failedMessage); } private async retryMessage(message: any, retryCount: number) { // Retry logic here } }

// deduplication.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class DeduplicationService { private readonly processedMessages = new Set<string>(); async isMessageProcessed(messageId: string): Promise<boolean> { return this.processedMessages.has(messageId); } async markMessageAsProcessed(messageId: string): Promise<void> { this.processedMessages.add(messageId); // In production, use Redis or database for persistence // await this.redis.setex(`processed:${messageId}`, 3600, 'true'); } async processMessageIdempotently<T>( messageId: string, processor: () => Promise<T> ): Promise<T | null> { if (await this.isMessageProcessed(messageId)) { console.log(`Message ${messageId} already processed, skipping`); return null; } try { const result = await processor(); await this.markMessageAsProcessed(messageId); return result; } catch (error) { console.error(`Failed to process message ${messageId}:`, error); throw error; } } }

// circuit-breaker.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; enum CircuitState { CLOSED = 'CLOSED', OPEN = 'OPEN', HALF_OPEN = 'HALF_OPEN', } @Injectable() export class CircuitBreakerService { private state = CircuitState.CLOSED; private failures = 0; private lastFailureTime: number = 0; private readonly failureThreshold = 5; private readonly timeout = 60000; // 1 minute async executeWithCircuitBreaker<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> { if (this.state === CircuitState.OPEN) { if (Date.now() - this.lastFailureTime > this.timeout) { this.state = CircuitState.HALF_OPEN; } else { throw new Error('Circuit breaker is OPEN'); } } try { const result = await operation(); this.onSuccess(); return result; } catch (error) { this.onFailure(); throw error; } } private onSuccess() { this.failures = 0; this.state = CircuitState.CLOSED; } private onFailure() { this.failures++; this.lastFailureTime = Date.now(); if (this.failures >= this.failureThreshold) { this.state = CircuitState.OPEN; } } }

// batch-processor.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class BatchProcessorService { private batch: any[] = []; private readonly batchSize = 100; private readonly batchTimeout = 5000; // 5 seconds private batchTimer: NodeJS.Timeout; async addToBatch(message: any) { this.batch.push(message); if (this.batch.length >= this.batchSize) { await this.processBatch(); } else if (!this.batchTimer) { this.batchTimer = setTimeout(() => { this.processBatch(); }, this.batchTimeout); } } private async processBatch() { if (this.batch.length === 0) return; const currentBatch = [...this.batch]; this.batch = []; if (this.batchTimer) { clearTimeout(this.batchTimer); this.batchTimer = null; } try { await this.processMessages(currentBatch); } catch (error) { console.error('Batch processing failed:', error); // Handle failed batch (retry, DLQ, etc.) } } private async processMessages(messages: any[]) { console.log(`Processing batch of ${messages.length} messages`); // Implement batch processing logic } }

// connection-pool.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class ConnectionPoolService { private readonly pool: any[] = []; private readonly maxConnections = 10; private readonly minConnections = 2; async getConnection() { if (this.pool.length > 0) { return this.pool.pop(); } if (this.getTotalConnections() < this.maxConnections) { return await this.createConnection(); } // Wait for available connection return await this.waitForConnection(); } async releaseConnection(connection: any) { if (this.pool.length < this.minConnections) { this.pool.push(connection); } else { await this.closeConnection(connection); } } private async createConnection() { // Create and return new connection } private async waitForConnection() { // Implement connection waiting logic } private getTotalConnections(): number { // Return total number of connections return this.pool.length; } }

// metrics.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class MetricsService { private metrics = { messagesProduced: 0, messagesConsumed: 0, messagesFailed: 0, averageProcessingTime: 0, }; incrementProduced() { this.metrics.messagesProduced++; } incrementConsumed() { this.metrics.messagesConsumed++; } incrementFailed() { this.metrics.messagesFailed++; } recordProcessingTime(duration: number) { // Calculate rolling average this.metrics.averageProcessingTime = (this.metrics.averageProcessingTime + duration) / 2; } getMetrics() { return { ...this.metrics, successRate: this.calculateSuccessRate(), timestamp: new Date(), }; } private calculateSuccessRate(): number { const total = this.metrics.messagesConsumed + this.metrics.messagesFailed; return total > 0 ? (this.metrics.messagesConsumed / total) * 100 : 100; } }

// health-check.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class HealthCheckService { async checkMessageQueueHealth(): Promise<boolean> { try { // Implement health check for your message queue await this.pingMessageQueue(); return true; } catch (error) { console.error('Message queue health check failed:', error); return false; } } async checkDatabaseHealth(): Promise<boolean> { try { // Implement database health check return true; } catch (error) { console.error('Database health check failed:', error); return false; } } async getHealthStatus() { const [mqHealth, dbHealth] = await Promise.all([ this.checkMessageQueueHealth(), this.checkDatabaseHealth(), ]); return { status: mqHealth && dbHealth ? 'healthy' : 'unhealthy', services: { messageQueue: mqHealth ? 'up' : 'down', database: dbHealth ? 'up' : 'down', }, timestamp: new Date(), }; } private async pingMessageQueue() { // Implement specific ping logic for your message queue } }

// order.controller.spec.ts import { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing'; import { OrderController } from './order.controller'; import { OrderService } from './order.service'; describe('OrderController', () => { let controller: OrderController; let orderService: OrderService; beforeEach(async () => { const module: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({ controllers: [OrderController], providers: [ { provide: OrderService, useValue: { processOrder: jest.fn(), cancelOrder: jest.fn(), }, }, ], }).compile(); controller = module.get<OrderController>(OrderController); orderService = module.get<OrderService>(OrderService); }); describe('handleOrderCreated', () => { it('should process order successfully', async () => { const orderData = { id: '123', amount: 100 }; jest.spyOn(orderService, 'processOrder').mockResolvedValue(undefined); const result = await controller.handleOrderCreated(orderData); expect(orderService.processOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith(orderData); expect(result).toEqual({ success: true, message: 'Order processed successfully' }); }); it('should handle processing errors', async () => { const orderData = { id: '123', amount: 100 }; const error = new Error('Processing failed'); jest.spyOn(orderService, 'processOrder').mockRejectedValue(error); await expect(controller.handleOrderCreated(orderData)).rejects.toThrow(error); }); }); });

// message-queue.integration.spec.ts import { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing'; import { ClientProxy } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { ProducerService } from './producer.service'; describe('Message Queue Integration', () => { let producerService: ProducerService; let client: ClientProxy; beforeEach(async () => { const module: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({ providers: [ ProducerService, { provide: 'MESSAGE_QUEUE_CLIENT', useValue: { emit: jest.fn(), send: jest.fn(), }, }, ], }).compile(); producerService = module.get<ProducerService>(ProducerService); client = module.get<ClientProxy>('MESSAGE_QUEUE_CLIENT'); }); it('should send order created event', async () => { const orderData = { id: '123', amount: 100 }; jest.spyOn(client, 'emit').mockReturnValue(Promise.resolve()); await producerService.sendOrderCreated(orderData); expect(client.emit).toHaveBeenCalledWith('order.created', orderData); }); });

documents.s: Decision Matrix: Choosing the Right Message Queue

documents.t: Choose RabbitMQ when: You need complex routing and message patterns Reliability and message guarantees are critical You have moderate to high throughput requirements You prefer open-source solutions Choose Redis when: You need extremely fast message processing You're already using Redis for caching You have simple pub/sub requirements Real-time performance is critical Choose Kafka when: You need to handle massive message volumes Event sourcing is part of your architecture You need long-term message retention You're building data streaming pipelines Choose AWS SQS when: You're building on AWS infrastructure You prefer managed services You need automatic scaling You want to minimize operational overhead

Implementing message queues in NestJS microservices provides the foundation for building scalable, resilient, and maintainable applications. Each message queue technology has its strengths and ideal use cases: RabbitMQ excels in enterprise applications requiring complex routing and strong guarantees Redis provides unmatched performance for real-time applications Kafka handles massive scale and supports event-driven architectures AWS SQS offers simplicity and seamless cloud integration The key to success lies in understanding your specific requirements, considering factors like throughput, persistence, complexity, and operational overhead. Start with simpler solutions like Redis or AWS SQS for basic use cases, and consider RabbitMQ or Kafka as your requirements grow in complexity and scale. Remember to implement proper error handling, monitoring, and testing strategies regardless of your chosen message queue technology. These patterns ensure your microservices remain robust and maintainable as they evolve. Ready to implement message queues in your NestJS microservices? Start with the technology that best fits your current needs, and don't hesitate to evolve your solution as your requirements change.

Rate limiting is a critical security and performance mechanism in production microservice architectures. It protects your services from abuse, ensures fair resource allocation, and maintains system stability under high load. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore how to implement robust, scalable rate limiting in NestJS applications designed for microservice environments.
documents.s: Handling Rate Limiting in NestJS for Production Microservices

documents.t: DDoS Protection: Prevents overwhelming individual services with excessive requests API Abuse Prevention: Stops malicious actors from exhausting system resources Brute Force Attack Mitigation: Limits login attempts and sensitive operations Resource Protection: Ensures no single client can monopolize service capacity

Fair Resource Allocation: Ensures all users get equitable access to services Cascade Failure Prevention: Prevents one overloaded service from affecting others Cost Control: Manages computational and bandwidth costs in cloud environments SLA Compliance: Helps maintain service level agreements under varying loads

Distributed State Management: Rate limits must work across multiple service instances Service-to-Service Communication: Internal APIs need different limits than public ones Dynamic Scaling: Rate limits must adapt to auto-scaling scenarios Cross-Service Coordination: Shared limits across multiple related services
Before implementing custom rate limiting solutions, consider these battle-tested libraries that can significantly speed up development:

documents.t: The official NestJS throttling library provides simple, decorator-based rate limiting. // Installation npm install @nestjs/throttler // Basic setup import { ThrottlerModule, ThrottlerGuard } from '@nestjs/throttler'; import { APP_GUARD } from '@nestjs/core'; @Module({ imports: [ ThrottlerModule.forRoot([ { name: 'short', ttl: 1000, // 1 second limit: 3, // 3 requests per second }, { name: 'medium', ttl: 10000, // 10 seconds limit: 20, // 20 requests per 10 seconds }, { name: 'long', ttl: 60000, // 1 minute limit: 100, // 100 requests per minute }, ]), ], providers: [ { provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: ThrottlerGuard, }, ], }) export class AppModule {} // Usage in controllers import { Throttle } from '@nestjs/throttler'; @Controller('api') export class ApiController { @Get('public') @Throttle({ default: { limit: 10, ttl: 60000 } }) getPublicData() { return { data: 'Limited to 10 requests per minute' }; } @Post('auth/login') @Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 300000 } }) // 5 attempts per 5 minutes login(@Body() credentials: any) { return { token: 'jwt-token' }; } }

A mature Express.js rate limiting middleware that works seamlessly with NestJS. // Installation npm install express-rate-limit // Global setup import rateLimit from 'express-rate-limit'; const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule); // Global rate limiting app.use( rateLimit({ windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes max: 100, // Limit each IP to 100 requests per windowMs message: { error: 'Too many requests, please try again later.', retryAfter: '15 minutes', }, standardHeaders: true, // Return rate limit info in headers legacyHeaders: false, // Redis store for distributed rate limiting store: new RedisStore({ sendCommand: (...args: string[]) => redisClient.call(...args), }), }) ); // Route-specific limiting import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express'; const loginLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes max: 5, // Limit each IP to 5 login requests per windowMs message: 'Too many login attempts, please try again later.', skipSuccessfulRequests: true, // Don't count successful requests }); @Controller('auth') export class AuthController { @Post('login') @UseInterceptors( // Apply rate limiting middleware as interceptor (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => loginLimiter(req, res, next) ) login(@Body() credentials: any) { return { token: 'jwt-token' }; } }

Advanced rate limiting with queuing, clustering, and Redis support. // Installation npm install bottleneck // Service implementation import Bottleneck from 'bottleneck'; import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class AdvancedRateLimitService { private limiters = new Map<string, Bottleneck>(); constructor() { // Create different limiters for different use cases this.setupLimiters(); } private setupLimiters() { // API rate limiter with Redis clustering this.limiters.set('api', new Bottleneck({ reservoir: 100, // Initial capacity reservoirRefreshAmount: 100, // Tokens to add reservoirRefreshInterval: 60 * 1000, // Every minute maxConcurrent: 10, // Max concurrent requests minTime: 100, // Min time between requests (100ms) // Redis clustering for distributed rate limiting datastore: 'redis', clearDatastore: false, clientOptions: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379, }, clusterNodes: [ { host: 'redis-1', port: 6379 }, { host: 'redis-2', port: 6379 }, ], })); // Premium API with higher limits this.limiters.set('premium', new Bottleneck({ reservoir: 1000, reservoirRefreshAmount: 1000, reservoirRefreshInterval: 60 * 1000, maxConcurrent: 50, minTime: 20, })); // Heavy processing limiter this.limiters.set('processing', new Bottleneck({ maxConcurrent: 3, // Only 3 heavy operations at once minTime: 2000, // 2 seconds between operations })); } async executeWithRateLimit<T>( limiterType: string, operation: () => Promise<T>, priority?: number ): Promise<T> { const limiter = this.limiters.get(limiterType); if (!limiter) { throw new Error(`Unknown limiter type: ${limiterType}`); } return limiter.schedule({ priority }, operation); } async checkRateLimit( limiterType: string, weight: number = 1 ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; msBeforeNext: number }> { const limiter = this.limiters.get(limiterType); if (!limiter) { return { allowed: false, msBeforeNext: 0 }; } try { const result = await limiter.check(weight); return { allowed: result >= 0, msBeforeNext: result < 0 ? Math.abs(result) : 0, }; } catch (error) { return { allowed: false, msBeforeNext: 1000 }; } } // Get limiter statistics getStats(limiterType: string) { const limiter = this.limiters.get(limiterType); if (!limiter) return null; return { running: limiter.running(), queued: limiter.queued(), reservoir: limiter.reservoir(), capacity: limiter.capacity, }; } } // Usage in controllers @Controller('api') export class ApiController { constructor( private readonly rateLimitService: AdvancedRateLimitService ) {} @Get('data') async getData() { return this.rateLimitService.executeWithRateLimit( 'api', async () => { // Your API logic here return { data: 'API response' }; } ); } @Post('heavy-process') async heavyProcess(@Body() data: any) { const check = await this.rateLimitService.checkRateLimit('processing'); if (!check.allowed) { throw new HttpException( { message: 'Processing queue full', retryAfter: Math.ceil(check.msBeforeNext / 1000), }, HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS ); } return this.rateLimitService.executeWithRateLimit( 'processing', async () => { // Heavy processing logic await this.performHeavyOperation(data); return { status: 'completed' }; }, 5 // High priority ); } @Get('stats') getSystemStats() { return { api: this.rateLimitService.getStats('api'), premium: this.rateLimitService.getStats('premium'), processing: this.rateLimitService.getStats('processing'), }; } }

Redis-based rate limiting with sliding window implementation. // Installation npm install ioredis-rate-limiter ioredis // Service implementation import RateLimiter from 'ioredis-rate-limiter'; import Redis from 'ioredis'; import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; @Injectable() export class RedisRateLimitService { private redis: Redis; private limiters = new Map<string, RateLimiter>(); constructor() { this.redis = new Redis({ host: 'localhost', port: 6379, retryDelayOnFailover: 100, }); this.setupLimiters(); } private setupLimiters() { // API rate limiter - 100 requests per minute this.limiters.set('api', new RateLimiter({ redis: this.redis, key: (id: string) => `rate_limit:api:${id}`, window: 60000, // 1 minute window limit: 100, // 100 requests per window })); // Login rate limiter - 5 attempts per 15 minutes this.limiters.set('login', new RateLimiter({ redis: this.redis, key: (id: string) => `rate_limit:login:${id}`, window: 15 * 60000, // 15 minutes limit: 5, // 5 attempts })); // Premium API - 1000 requests per minute this.limiters.set('premium', new RateLimiter({ redis: this.redis, key: (id: string) => `rate_limit:premium:${id}`, window: 60000, limit: 1000, })); } async checkLimit( type: string, identifier: string, cost: number = 1 ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remaining: number; resetTime: Date; totalHits: number; }> { const limiter = this.limiters.get(type); if (!limiter) { throw new Error(`Unknown rate limiter type: ${type}`); } try { const result = await limiter.check(identifier, cost); return { allowed: result.allowed, remaining: result.remaining, resetTime: new Date(result.resetTime), totalHits: result.totalHits, }; } catch (error) { // Fallback in case of Redis issues console.error('Rate limit check failed:', error); return { allowed: true, // Fail open for availability remaining: 0, resetTime: new Date(Date.now() + 60000), totalHits: 0, }; } } async getRemainingQuota(type: string, identifier: string): Promise<number> { const result = await this.checkLimit(type, identifier, 0); // Cost 0 for check only return result.remaining; } } // Guard implementation @Injectable() export class RedisRateLimitGuard implements CanActivate { constructor( private readonly rateLimitService: RedisRateLimitService, private readonly reflector: Reflector ) {} async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> { const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest(); const response = context.switchToHttp().getResponse(); // Get rate limit configuration from decorator const config = this.reflector.get<{ type: string; identifier?: (req: any) => string; cost?: number; }>('REDIS_RATE_LIMIT', context.getHandler()); if (!config) { return true; // No rate limiting configured } // Generate identifier const identifier = config.identifier ? config.identifier(request) : request.ip; // Check rate limit const result = await this.rateLimitService.checkLimit( config.type, identifier, config.cost || 1 ); // Set headers response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining); response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime.toISOString()); response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Total', result.totalHits); if (!result.allowed) { response.setHeader('Retry-After', Math.ceil((result.resetTime.getTime() - Date.now()) / 1000)); throw new HttpException( { statusCode: HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, message: 'Rate limit exceeded', retryAfter: result.resetTime.toISOString(), }, HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS ); } return true; } } // Decorator for easy usage export const RedisRateLimit = (config: { type: string; identifier?: (req: any) => string; cost?: number; }) => SetMetadata('REDIS_RATE_LIMIT', config); // Usage example @Controller('api') @UseGuards(RedisRateLimitGuard) export class ApiController { @Get('data') @RedisRateLimit({ type: 'api', identifier: (req) => req.ip, }) getData() { return { data: 'API response' }; } @Post('login') @RedisRateLimit({ type: 'login', identifier: (req) => `${req.ip}:${req.body.email}`, }) login(@Body() credentials: any) { return { token: 'jwt-token' }; } @Get('premium') @RedisRateLimit({ type: 'premium', identifier: (req) => req.user?.id || req.ip, cost: 5, // This endpoint costs 5 "points" }) getPremiumData() { return { data: 'Premium API response' }; } }

Library Pros Cons Best For @nestjs/throttler ✅ Official NestJS support ✅ Decorator-based ✅ Multiple rate limits ✅ Redis support ❌ Limited algorithms ❌ Basic queuing Simple rate limiting, Getting started express-rate-limit ✅ Mature & stable ✅ Extensive middleware ✅ Good documentation ✅ Flexible configuration ❌ Express-specific ❌ Limited queue management General web applications, Migration from Express bottleneck ✅ Advanced queuing ✅ Clustering support ✅ Priority queues ✅ Multiple algorithms ❌ Complex configuration ❌ Learning curve Complex rate limiting, Job queues, Distributed systems ioredis-rate-limiter ✅ Sliding window ✅ High performance ✅ Simple API ✅ Redis-native ❌ Redis dependency ❌ Limited to sliding window High-performance APIs, Redis-based infrastructure

If you're using custom rate limiting and want to migrate to a library: // From custom implementation @RateLimit({ algorithm: 'sliding-window', limit: 100, windowMs: 60000, }) // To @nestjs/throttler @Throttle({ default: { limit: 100, ttl: 60000 } }) // To bottleneck async method() { return this.rateLimitService.executeWithRateLimit('api', async () => { // Your logic here }); } // To ioredis-rate-limiter @RedisRateLimit({ type: 'api', identifier: (req) => req.ip, })

The token bucket algorithm is ideal for allowing bursts while maintaining average rate limits. // rate-limiting/token-bucket.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis'; interface TokenBucketConfig { capacity: number; // Maximum tokens in bucket refillRate: number; // Tokens added per second windowSize: number; // Time window in seconds } @Injectable() export class TokenBucketService { constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {} async checkRateLimit( key: string, config: TokenBucketConfig, tokensRequested: number = 1 ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remainingTokens: number; resetTime: number; retryAfter?: number; }> { const script = ` local key = KEYS[1] local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[1]) local refillRate = tonumber(ARGV[2]) local windowSize = tonumber(ARGV[3]) local tokensRequested = tonumber(ARGV[4]) local now = tonumber(ARGV[5]) -- Get current bucket state local bucket = redis.call('HMGET', key, 'tokens', 'lastRefill') local tokens = tonumber(bucket[1]) or capacity local lastRefill = tonumber(bucket[2]) or now -- Calculate tokens to add based on time elapsed local elapsed = math.max(0, now - lastRefill) local tokensToAdd = math.floor(elapsed * refillRate) tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + tokensToAdd) -- Check if request can be fulfilled local allowed = tokens >= tokensRequested local remainingTokens = tokens local retryAfter = 0 if allowed then remainingTokens = tokens - tokensRequested -- Update bucket state redis.call('HMSET', key, 'tokens', remainingTokens, 'lastRefill', now) redis.call('EXPIRE', key, windowSize * 2) else -- Calculate retry after time local tokensNeeded = tokensRequested - tokens retryAfter = math.ceil(tokensNeeded / refillRate) end return { allowed and 1 or 0, remainingTokens, now + (capacity - remainingTokens) / refillRate, retryAfter } `; const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000); const result = await this.redis.eval( script, 1, key, config.capacity, config.refillRate, config.windowSize, tokensRequested, now ) as [number, number, number, number]; return { allowed: result[0] === 1, remainingTokens: result[1], resetTime: result[2], retryAfter: result[3] > 0 ? result[3] : undefined, }; } }

Sliding window provides more accurate rate limiting by tracking requests in a rolling time window. // rate-limiting/sliding-window.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis'; interface SlidingWindowConfig { limit: number; // Maximum requests per window windowMs: number; // Window size in milliseconds precision: number; // Sub-window precision (e.g., 10 for 10 sub-windows) } @Injectable() export class SlidingWindowService { constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {} async checkRateLimit( key: string, config: SlidingWindowConfig ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remaining: number; resetTime: number; currentUsage: number; }> { const script = ` local key = KEYS[1] local limit = tonumber(ARGV[1]) local windowMs = tonumber(ARGV[2]) local precision = tonumber(ARGV[3]) local now = tonumber(ARGV[4]) -- Calculate sub-window size local subWindowMs = windowMs / precision local currentWindow = math.floor(now / subWindowMs) local windowStart = currentWindow - precision + 1 -- Clean old sub-windows redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, 0, windowStart - 1) -- Count current requests in the sliding window local currentCount = 0 local subWindows = redis.call('ZRANGE', key, 0, -1, 'WITHSCORES') for i = 1, #subWindows, 2 do local subWindow = tonumber(subWindows[i + 1]) local count = tonumber(subWindows[i]) if subWindow >= windowStart then -- Calculate overlap percentage for partial windows local overlap = 1 if subWindow == windowStart then local subWindowTime = subWindow * subWindowMs local windowTime = now - windowMs overlap = math.max(0, (subWindowTime + subWindowMs - windowTime) / subWindowMs) end currentCount = currentCount + (count * overlap) end end local allowed = currentCount < limit local remaining = math.max(0, limit - currentCount - 1) if allowed then -- Increment counter for current sub-window redis.call('ZINCRBY', key, 1, currentWindow) redis.call('EXPIRE', key, math.ceil(windowMs / 1000) * 2) end local resetTime = (currentWindow + 1) * subWindowMs return { allowed and 1 or 0, remaining, resetTime, currentCount + (allowed and 1 or 0) } `; const now = Date.now(); const result = await this.redis.eval( script, 1, key, config.limit, config.windowMs, config.precision, now ) as [number, number, number, number]; return { allowed: result[0] === 1, remaining: result[1], resetTime: result[2], currentUsage: result[3], }; } }

Create a flexible, configurable rate limiting guard that supports multiple algorithms and strategies. // guards/rate-limit.guard.ts import { Injectable, CanActivate, ExecutionContext, HttpException, HttpStatus, Inject, } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'; import { Request, Response } from 'express'; import { TokenBucketService } from '../rate-limiting/token-bucket.service'; import { SlidingWindowService } from '../rate-limiting/sliding-window.service'; import { RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS } from '../decorators/rate-limit.decorator'; export interface RateLimitOptions { algorithm: 'token-bucket' | 'sliding-window' | 'fixed-window'; keyGenerator?: (req: Request) => string; skipIf?: (req: Request) => boolean; onLimitReached?: (req: Request, res: Response) => void; // Token bucket specific capacity?: number; refillRate?: number; // Sliding/Fixed window specific limit?: number; windowMs?: number; precision?: number; // For sliding window // Common options message?: string; standardHeaders?: boolean; legacyHeaders?: boolean; skipSuccessfulRequests?: boolean; skipFailedRequests?: boolean; } @Injectable() export class RateLimitGuard implements CanActivate { constructor( private readonly reflector: Reflector, private readonly tokenBucket: TokenBucketService, private readonly slidingWindow: SlidingWindowService, @Inject('CONFIG_SERVICE') private readonly config: any ) {} async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> { const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>(); const response = context.switchToHttp().getResponse<Response>(); // Get rate limit options from decorator or global config const options = this.getRateLimitOptions(context); if (!options) { return true; // No rate limiting configured } // Check if request should be skipped if (options.skipIf && options.skipIf(request)) { return true; } // Generate rate limit key const key = this.generateKey(request, options); // Apply rate limiting based on algorithm const result = await this.applyRateLimit(key, options); // Set response headers this.setHeaders(response, result, options); if (!result.allowed) { // Execute custom handler if provided if (options.onLimitReached) { options.onLimitReached(request, response); } // Throw rate limit exceeded exception throw new HttpException( { statusCode: HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, message: options.message || 'Rate limit exceeded', error: 'Too Many Requests', retryAfter: result.retryAfter, }, HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS ); } return true; } private getRateLimitOptions(context: ExecutionContext): RateLimitOptions | null { // Check method-level decorator first const methodOptions = this.reflector.get<RateLimitOptions>( RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS, context.getHandler() ); if (methodOptions) { return methodOptions; } // Check class-level decorator const classOptions = this.reflector.get<RateLimitOptions>( RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS, context.getClass() ); if (classOptions) { return classOptions; } // Return global default options if configured return this.config.get('rateLimit.default'); } private generateKey(request: Request, options: RateLimitOptions): string { if (options.keyGenerator) { return options.keyGenerator(request); } // Default key generation strategy const ip = request.ip || request.connection.remoteAddress; const userId = (request as any).user?.id || 'anonymous'; const route = `${request.method}:${request.route?.path || request.path}`; return `rate_limit:${ip}:${userId}:${route}`; } private async applyRateLimit( key: string, options: RateLimitOptions ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remaining?: number; resetTime?: number; retryAfter?: number; currentUsage?: number; }> { switch (options.algorithm) { case 'token-bucket': return this.tokenBucket.checkRateLimit(key, { capacity: options.capacity || 10, refillRate: options.refillRate || 1, windowSize: Math.floor((options.windowMs || 60000) / 1000), }); case 'sliding-window': return this.slidingWindow.checkRateLimit(key, { limit: options.limit || 100, windowMs: options.windowMs || 60000, precision: options.precision || 10, }); case 'fixed-window': return this.applyFixedWindow(key, { limit: options.limit || 100, windowMs: options.windowMs || 60000, }); default: throw new Error(`Unknown rate limiting algorithm: ${options.algorithm}`); } } private async applyFixedWindow( key: string, config: { limit: number; windowMs: number } ): Promise<any> { // Simple fixed window implementation using Redis const window = Math.floor(Date.now() / config.windowMs); const windowKey = `${key}:${window}`; const current = await this.tokenBucket['redis'].incr(windowKey); await this.tokenBucket['redis'].expire(windowKey, Math.ceil(config.windowMs / 1000)); const allowed = current <= config.limit; const remaining = Math.max(0, config.limit - current); const resetTime = (window + 1) * config.windowMs; return { allowed, remaining, resetTime, currentUsage: current, }; } private setHeaders(response: Response, result: any, options: RateLimitOptions): void { if (options.standardHeaders !== false) { // Standard rate limit headers (draft RFC) response.setHeader('RateLimit-Limit', options.limit || options.capacity); response.setHeader('RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining || 0); response.setHeader('RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime); if (result.retryAfter) { response.setHeader('Retry-After', result.retryAfter); } } if (options.legacyHeaders) { // Legacy X-RateLimit headers for compatibility response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Limit', options.limit || options.capacity); response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining || 0); response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime); } } }

Create flexible decorators for easy application of rate limits. // decorators/rate-limit.decorator.ts import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common'; import { RateLimitOptions } from '../guards/rate-limit.guard'; export const RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS = 'RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS'; export const RateLimit = (options: RateLimitOptions) => SetMetadata(RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS, options); // Convenience decorators for common patterns export const PublicApiRateLimit = () => RateLimit({ algorithm: 'sliding-window', limit: 1000, windowMs: 60000, // 1 minute message: 'Too many requests from this IP, please try again later', standardHeaders: true, }); export const AuthRateLimit = () => RateLimit({ algorithm: 'token-bucket', capacity: 5, refillRate: 1/60, // 1 token per minute windowMs: 300000, // 5 minutes message: 'Too many authentication attempts, please try again later', keyGenerator: (req) => `auth:${req.ip}:${req.body?.email || 'unknown'}`, }); export const PremiumApiRateLimit = () => RateLimit({ algorithm: 'sliding-window', limit: 10000, windowMs: 60000, skipIf: (req) => (req as any).user?.plan === 'enterprise', keyGenerator: (req) => `premium:${(req as any).user?.id || req.ip}`, }); export const InternalServiceRateLimit = () => RateLimit({ algorithm: 'token-bucket', capacity: 1000, refillRate: 10, windowMs: 60000, skipIf: (req) => req.headers['x-service-token'] === process.env.INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, keyGenerator: (req) => `internal:${req.headers['x-service-name'] || 'unknown'}`, }); // Dynamic rate limiting based on user tier export const TieredRateLimit = () => RateLimit({ algorithm: 'sliding-window', windowMs: 60000, keyGenerator: (req) => { const user = (req as any).user; const tier = user?.plan || 'free'; return `tiered:${tier}:${user?.id || req.ip}`; }, limit: 0, // Will be dynamically set });

Implement service-specific rate limiting strategies that work across distributed systems. // services/distributed-rate-limit.service.ts import { Injectable, Inject } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientProxy } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis'; interface ServiceRateLimitConfig { serviceName: string; globalLimit: number; perInstanceLimit: number; windowMs: number; coordinationStrategy: 'redis' | 'gossip' | 'leader-election'; } @Injectable() export class DistributedRateLimitService { private instanceId: string; constructor( private readonly redis: RedisService, @Inject('MESSAGE_BROKER') private readonly messageBroker: ClientProxy ) { this.instanceId = `${process.env.POD_NAME || 'local'}-${Date.now()}`; } async checkServiceRateLimit( config: ServiceRateLimitConfig, clientKey: string ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; globalUsage: number; instanceUsage: number; recommendation: 'allow' | 'deny' | 'throttle'; }> { const script = ` local globalKey = KEYS[1] local instanceKey = KEYS[2] local globalLimit = tonumber(ARGV[1]) local perInstanceLimit = tonumber(ARGV[2]) local windowMs = tonumber(ARGV[3]) local now = tonumber(ARGV[4]) local instanceId = ARGV[5] -- Clean expired entries local cutoff = now - windowMs redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', globalKey, 0, cutoff) redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', instanceKey, 0, cutoff) -- Get current usage local globalUsage = redis.call('ZCARD', globalKey) local instanceUsage = redis.call('ZCARD', instanceKey) -- Calculate available capacity local globalAvailable = globalLimit - globalUsage local instanceAvailable = perInstanceLimit - instanceUsage -- Determine if request should be allowed local allowed = globalAvailable > 0 and instanceAvailable > 0 local recommendation = 'allow' if not allowed then recommendation = 'deny' elseif globalAvailable < globalLimit * 0.1 then recommendation = 'throttle' end if allowed then -- Record the request local requestId = instanceId .. ':' .. now .. ':' .. math.random(1000000) redis.call('ZADD', globalKey, now, requestId) redis.call('ZADD', instanceKey, now, requestId) redis.call('EXPIRE', globalKey, math.ceil(windowMs / 1000) * 2) redis.call('EXPIRE', instanceKey, math.ceil(windowMs / 1000) * 2) globalUsage = globalUsage + 1 instanceUsage = instanceUsage + 1 end return { allowed and 1 or 0, globalUsage, instanceUsage, recommendation } `; const now = Date.now(); const globalKey = `service_rate_limit:${config.serviceName}:global:${clientKey}`; const instanceKey = `service_rate_limit:${config.serviceName}:${this.instanceId}:${clientKey}`; const result = await this.redis.eval( script, 2, globalKey, instanceKey, config.globalLimit, config.perInstanceLimit, config.windowMs, now, this.instanceId ) as [number, number, number, string]; // Publish metrics for monitoring await this.publishMetrics(config.serviceName, { globalUsage: result[1], instanceUsage: result[2], recommendation: result[3], timestamp: now, }); return { allowed: result[0] === 1, globalUsage: result[1], instanceUsage: result[2], recommendation: result[3] as any, }; } private async publishMetrics(serviceName: string, metrics: any): Promise<void> { try { await this.messageBroker.emit('rate_limit.metrics', { serviceName, instanceId: this.instanceId, ...metrics, }); } catch (error) { // Metrics publishing failure shouldn't affect rate limiting console.warn('Failed to publish rate limit metrics:', error); } } async getServiceHealth(serviceName: string): Promise<{ totalInstances: number; healthyInstances: number; globalUsage: number; averageInstanceUsage: number; }> { const healthKey = `service_health:${serviceName}`; const instances = await this.redis.hgetall(healthKey); const now = Date.now(); const healthyThreshold = 30000; // 30 seconds let healthyCount = 0; let totalUsage = 0; for (const [instanceId, lastSeen] of Object.entries(instances)) { if (now - parseInt(lastSeen) < healthyThreshold) { healthyCount++; // Get instance usage const usageKey = `service_rate_limit:${serviceName}:${instanceId}:*`; const usageKeys = await this.redis.keys(usageKey); for (const key of usageKeys) { const usage = await this.redis.zcard(key); totalUsage += usage; } } } return { totalInstances: Object.keys(instances).length, healthyInstances: healthyCount, globalUsage: totalUsage, averageInstanceUsage: healthyCount > 0 ? totalUsage / healthyCount : 0, }; } }

Here's how to apply rate limiting in real microservice controllers: // controllers/api.controller.ts import { Controller, Get, Post, Body, UseGuards, Req, HttpStatus, HttpException, } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Request } from 'express'; import { RateLimitGuard } from '../guards/rate-limit.guard'; import { PublicApiRateLimit, AuthRateLimit, TieredRateLimit, InternalServiceRateLimit, } from '../decorators/rate-limit.decorator'; @Controller('api/v1') @UseGuards(RateLimitGuard) export class ApiController { @Get('public/data') @PublicApiRateLimit() async getPublicData() { return { data: 'This is public data with standard rate limiting' }; } @Post('auth/login') @AuthRateLimit() async login(@Body() credentials: any, @Req() request: Request) { // Implement authentication logic return { token: 'jwt-token' }; } @Get('user/profile') @TieredRateLimit() async getUserProfile(@Req() request: Request) { // Dynamic rate limiting based on user tier const user = (request as any).user; // This would be handled by a custom guard that sets limits based on user tier return { profile: user.profile }; } @Post('internal/sync') @InternalServiceRateLimit() async internalSync(@Body() data: any, @Req() request: Request) { // Internal service communication with special rate limiting return { status: 'synced' }; } @Get('premium/analytics') @RateLimit({ algorithm: 'sliding-window', limit: 1000, windowMs: 60000, keyGenerator: (req) => { const user = (req as any).user; const tier = user?.plan || 'free'; // Different limits for different tiers const limits = { free: 10, pro: 100, enterprise: 1000, }; return `analytics:${tier}:${user?.id || req.ip}`; }, onLimitReached: (req, res) => { // Custom handling for limit exceeded const user = (req as any).user; if (user?.plan === 'free') { // Suggest upgrade for free users res.setHeader('X-Upgrade-Suggestion', 'Consider upgrading to Pro for higher limits'); } }, }) async getPremiumAnalytics(@Req() request: Request) { const user = (request as any).user; const tierLimits = { free: 10, pro: 100, enterprise: 1000, }; const userLimit = tierLimits[user?.plan] || tierLimits.free; return { analytics: 'Advanced analytics data', currentPlan: user?.plan || 'free', apiLimit: userLimit, }; } }

Implement middleware for application-wide rate limiting with exemptions. // middleware/global-rate-limit.middleware.ts import { Injectable, NestMiddleware, HttpException, HttpStatus } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express'; import { TokenBucketService } from '../rate-limiting/token-bucket.service'; @Injectable() export class GlobalRateLimitMiddleware implements NestMiddleware { constructor(private readonly tokenBucket: TokenBucketService) {} async use(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) { // Skip rate limiting for certain paths const exemptPaths = [ '/health', '/metrics', '/api/v1/internal', ]; if (exemptPaths.some(path => req.path.startsWith(path))) { return next(); } // Skip for internal service calls if (req.headers['x-service-token'] === process.env.INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN) { return next(); } // Apply global rate limiting const clientKey = this.generateClientKey(req); const result = await this.tokenBucket.checkRateLimit(clientKey, { capacity: 10000, // 10k requests refillRate: 100, // 100 requests per second windowSize: 3600, // 1 hour window }); // Set rate limit headers res.setHeader('X-Global-RateLimit-Limit', '10000'); res.setHeader('X-Global-RateLimit-Remaining', result.remainingTokens); res.setHeader('X-Global-RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime); if (!result.allowed) { throw new HttpException( { statusCode: HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, message: 'Global rate limit exceeded', error: 'Too Many Requests', retryAfter: result.retryAfter, }, HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS ); } next(); } private generateClientKey(req: Request): string { // Prioritize API key, then user ID, then IP const apiKey = req.headers['x-api-key'] as string; const userId = (req as any).user?.id; const ip = req.ip || req.connection.remoteAddress; if (apiKey) { return `global:api:${apiKey}`; } if (userId) { return `global:user:${userId}`; } return `global:ip:${ip}`; } }

Set up the rate limiting module with proper configuration management. // modules/rate-limit.module.ts import { Module, Global } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ConfigModule, ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config'; import { RedisModule } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis'; import { TokenBucketService } from '../rate-limiting/token-bucket.service'; import { SlidingWindowService } from '../rate-limiting/sliding-window.service'; import { DistributedRateLimitService } from '../services/distributed-rate-limit.service'; import { RateLimitGuard } from '../guards/rate-limit.guard'; @Global() @Module({ imports: [ ConfigModule, RedisModule.forRootAsync({ imports: [ConfigModule], useFactory: (configService: ConfigService) => ({ config: { host: configService.get('REDIS_HOST', 'localhost'), port: configService.get('REDIS_PORT', 6379), password: configService.get('REDIS_PASSWORD'), db: configService.get('REDIS_DB', 0), keyPrefix: configService.get('REDIS_KEY_PREFIX', 'rate_limit:'), retryDelayOnFailover: 100, enableReadyCheck: true, maxRetriesPerRequest: 3, }, }), inject: [ConfigService], }), ], providers: [ TokenBucketService, SlidingWindowService, DistributedRateLimitService, RateLimitGuard, { provide: 'CONFIG_SERVICE', useFactory: (configService: ConfigService) => configService, inject: [ConfigService], }, ], exports: [ TokenBucketService, SlidingWindowService, DistributedRateLimitService, RateLimitGuard, ], }) export class RateLimitModule {} // config/rate-limit.config.ts export const rateLimitConfig = () => ({ rateLimit: { default: { algorithm: 'sliding-window', limit: 100, windowMs: 60000, standardHeaders: true, legacyHeaders: false, }, redis: { host: process.env.REDIS_HOST || 'localhost', port: parseInt(process.env.REDIS_PORT) || 6379, password: process.env.REDIS_PASSWORD, db: parseInt(process.env.REDIS_DB) || 0, keyPrefix: process.env.REDIS_KEY_PREFIX || 'rate_limit:', }, microservice: { instanceId: process.env.POD_NAME || `local-${Date.now()}`, serviceName: process.env.SERVICE_NAME || 'unknown-service', coordinationStrategy: process.env.RATE_LIMIT_COORDINATION || 'redis', }, }, });

Implement comprehensive monitoring for rate limiting performance. // monitoring/rate-limit-metrics.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Gauge, Counter, Histogram, register } from 'prom-client'; @Injectable() export class RateLimitMetricsService { private readonly requestsTotal: Counter<string>; private readonly requestsBlocked: Counter<string>; private readonly rateLimitUsage: Gauge<string>; private readonly rateLimitLatency: Histogram<string>; constructor() { this.requestsTotal = new Counter({ name: 'rate_limit_requests_total', help: 'Total number of requests processed by rate limiter', labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm', 'key_type'], registers: [register], }); this.requestsBlocked = new Counter({ name: 'rate_limit_requests_blocked_total', help: 'Total number of requests blocked by rate limiter', labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm', 'key_type', 'reason'], registers: [register], }); this.rateLimitUsage = new Gauge({ name: 'rate_limit_usage_ratio', help: 'Current usage ratio of rate limits (0-1)', labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm', 'key_type'], registers: [register], }); this.rateLimitLatency = new Histogram({ name: 'rate_limit_check_duration_seconds', help: 'Time spent checking rate limits', labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm'], buckets: [0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0], registers: [register], }); } recordRequest(service: string, algorithm: string, keyType: string): void { this.requestsTotal.inc({ service, algorithm, key_type: keyType }); } recordBlocked( service: string, algorithm: string, keyType: string, reason: string ): void { this.requestsBlocked.inc({ service, algorithm, key_type: keyType, reason }); } recordUsage( service: string, algorithm: string, keyType: string, ratio: number ): void { this.rateLimitUsage.set({ service, algorithm, key_type: keyType }, ratio); } recordLatency(service: string, algorithm: string, duration: number): void { this.rateLimitLatency.observe({ service, algorithm }, duration); } async getMetrics(): Promise<string> { return register.metrics(); } } // Health check for rate limiting system import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { HealthIndicator, HealthIndicatorResult, HealthCheckError } from '@nestjs/terminus'; import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis'; @Injectable() export class RateLimitHealthIndicator extends HealthIndicator { constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) { super(); } async isHealthy(key: string): Promise<HealthIndicatorResult> { try { // Test Redis connectivity const start = Date.now(); await this.redis.ping(); const latency = Date.now() - start; // Test rate limiting functionality const testKey = `health_check:${Date.now()}`; await this.redis.incr(testKey); await this.redis.expire(testKey, 60); const isHealthy = latency < 100; // Consider healthy if latency < 100ms const result = this.getStatus(key, isHealthy, { redis_latency: latency, redis_status: 'connected', }); if (isHealthy) { return result; } throw new HealthCheckError('Rate limiting is unhealthy', result); } catch (error) { throw new HealthCheckError('Rate limiting check failed', { [key]: { status: 'down', error: error.message, }, }); } } }

Comprehensive testing strategies for rate limiting functionality. // tests/rate-limit.integration.spec.ts import { Test, TestingModule } from '@nestjs/testing'; import { INestApplication } from '@nestjs/common'; import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis'; import * as request from 'supertest'; import { AppModule } from '../src/app.module'; describe('Rate Limiting Integration', () => { let app: INestApplication; let redis: RedisService; beforeEach(async () => { const moduleFixture: TestingModule = await Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [AppModule], }).compile(); app = moduleFixture.createNestApplication(); redis = moduleFixture.get<RedisService>(RedisService); await app.init(); // Clear Redis before each test await redis.flushdb(); }); afterEach(async () => { await app.close(); }); describe('Token Bucket Rate Limiting', () => { it('should allow requests within capacity', async () => { const endpoint = '/api/v1/auth/login'; // Should allow first 5 requests (capacity) for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { const response = await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password' }) .expect(200); expect(response.headers['ratelimit-remaining']).toBeDefined(); } }); it('should block requests exceeding capacity', async () => { const endpoint = '/api/v1/auth/login'; const email = 'test@example.com'; // Exhaust the token bucket for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email, password: 'password' }); } // Next request should be blocked const response = await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email, password: 'password' }) .expect(429); expect(response.body.message).toContain('Too many authentication attempts'); expect(response.headers['retry-after']).toBeDefined(); }); it('should refill tokens over time', async () => { const endpoint = '/api/v1/auth/login'; // Exhaust capacity for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password' }); } // Wait for token refill (mock time or use actual delay) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 60000)); // 1 minute // Should allow request after refill await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password' }) .expect(200); }); }); describe('Sliding Window Rate Limiting', () => { it('should track requests in sliding window', async () => { const endpoint = '/api/v1/public/data'; // Make requests at different times within window const responses = []; for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { const response = await request(app.getHttpServer()) .get(endpoint) .expect(200); responses.push(response); // Small delay between requests await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 100)); } // Check that remaining count decreases properly responses.forEach((response, index) => { const remaining = parseInt(response.headers['ratelimit-remaining']); expect(remaining).toBe(1000 - index - 1); // Assuming limit of 1000 }); }); }); describe('Distributed Rate Limiting', () => { it('should coordinate limits across service instances', async () => { // This would require multiple app instances for proper testing // Mock multiple instances using different instance IDs const endpoint = '/api/v1/premium/analytics'; const userId = 'test-user-123'; // Simulate requests from different instances for (let instance = 0; instance < 3; instance++) { // Mock different instance IDs process.env.POD_NAME = `test-pod-${instance}`; const response = await request(app.getHttpServer()) .get(endpoint) .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${generateJWT({ id: userId })}`) .expect(200); expect(response.headers['x-global-usage']).toBeDefined(); } }); }); describe('Rate Limit Headers', () => { it('should return correct rate limit headers', async () => { const response = await request(app.getHttpServer()) .get('/api/v1/public/data') .expect(200); expect(response.headers['ratelimit-limit']).toBeDefined(); expect(response.headers['ratelimit-remaining']).toBeDefined(); expect(response.headers['ratelimit-reset']).toBeDefined(); }); it('should return retry-after header when rate limited', async () => { const endpoint = '/api/v1/auth/login'; // Exhaust rate limit for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password' }); } const response = await request(app.getHttpServer()) .post(endpoint) .send({ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password' }) .expect(429); expect(response.headers['retry-after']).toBeDefined(); expect(parseInt(response.headers['retry-after'])).toBeGreaterThan(0); }); }); }); // Load testing for rate limiting describe('Rate Limiting Load Tests', () => { it('should handle high concurrent load', async () => { const concurrentRequests = 100; const endpoint = '/api/v1/public/data'; const promises = Array(concurrentRequests) .fill(null) .map(() => request(app.getHttpServer()) .get(endpoint) ); const results = await Promise.allSettled(promises); const successful = results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled' && r.value.status === 200 ).length; const rateLimited = results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled' && r.value.status === 429 ).length; expect(successful + rateLimited).toBe(concurrentRequests); expect(successful).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1000); // Assuming limit of 1000 }); }); function generateJWT(payload: any): string { // Mock JWT generation for testing return 'mock.jwt.token'; }

Environment-Specific Limits: Use different rate limits for development, staging, and production Dynamic Configuration: Allow runtime adjustment of rate limits without deployment Graceful Degradation: Fall back to in-memory limiting if Redis is unavailable Circuit Breakers: Implement circuit breakers for rate limiting services

Metrics Collection: Track rate limit usage, blocked requests, and system health Alerting: Set up alerts for high block rates or system failures Dashboard: Create monitoring dashboards for real-time rate limit visibility Log Analysis: Analyze logs to identify patterns and potential abuse

Redis Optimization: Use Redis clusters for high availability and performance Lua Scripts: Leverage atomic Lua scripts for consistent rate limiting Connection Pooling: Optimize Redis connection management Caching: Cache rate limit decisions for frequently accessed keys

Key Generation: Use secure, unpredictable key generation strategies API Key Management: Implement proper API key validation and rotation Bypass Protection: Secure internal service communication channels Audit Logging: Log all rate limit decisions for security auditing

Implementing robust rate limiting in NestJS microservices requires careful consideration of algorithms, distribution strategies, and production requirements. The solutions presented here provide: Multiple Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token bucket, sliding window, and fixed window implementations Distributed Coordination: Service-aware rate limiting across multiple instances Flexible Configuration: Decorator-based and middleware approaches for different use cases Production Readiness: Monitoring, health checks, and comprehensive testing Performance Optimization: Redis-based storage with efficient Lua scripts Start with simple rate limiting for critical endpoints, gradually expanding to more sophisticated distributed strategies as your microservice architecture grows. Always monitor rate limiting effectiveness and adjust limits based on actual usage patterns and business requirements. Remember that rate limiting is just one part of a comprehensive security and performance strategy. Combine it with other techniques like authentication, authorization, caching, and circuit breakers for maximum effectiveness in production environments. Ready to implement rate limiting? This comprehensive guide provides everything you need to build robust rate limiting for your NestJS microservices architecture.

Nginx (pronounced "engine-x") is one of the most popular and powerful web servers in the world, powering over 30% of all websites on the internet. Originally created by Igor Sysoev in 2004 to solve the C10K problem (handling 10,000 concurrent connections), Nginx has evolved into a versatile tool that serves as a web server, reverse proxy, load balancer, and HTTP cache. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore what makes Nginx special, its key features, common use cases, and how to get started with basic configurations.
documents.s: Nginx: The High-Performance Web Server and Reverse Proxy

documents.t: Nginx is an open-source web server that can also function as a reverse proxy, load balancer, mail proxy, and HTTP cache. Unlike traditional web servers that create a new thread or process for each request, Nginx uses an event-driven, asynchronous architecture that allows it to handle thousands of concurrent connections with minimal resource usage.

High Performance: Handles thousands of concurrent connections efficiently Low Memory Usage: Uses significantly less memory compared to Apache Event-Driven Architecture: Non-blocking I/O operations Modular Design: Extensible through modules Configuration Flexibility: Simple yet powerful configuration syntax
Nginx can serve static content (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images) extremely efficiently. Its ability to handle static files makes it an excellent choice for serving modern web applications.
Acts as an intermediary between clients and backend servers, forwarding client requests to appropriate backend services and returning responses back to clients.
Distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers to ensure optimal resource utilization and prevent any single server from becoming overwhelmed.
Handles SSL/TLS encryption and decryption, offloading this computationally intensive task from backend servers.
Provides HTTP caching capabilities to store frequently requested content, reducing load on backend servers and improving response times.

server { listen 80; server_name example.com; root /var/www/html; location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; } location ~* \.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|ico|css|js)$ { expires 1y; add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable"; } }

server { listen 80; server_name api.example.com; location / { proxy_pass http://localhost:3000; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade'; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade; } }
upstream backend { server backend1.example.com; server backend2.example.com; server backend3.example.com; } server { listen 80; server_name example.com; location / { proxy_pass http://backend; } }

server { listen 443 ssl http2; server_name example.com; ssl_certificate /path/to/certificate.crt; ssl_certificate_key /path/to/private.key; ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384; location / { root /var/www/html; index index.html; } } # Redirect HTTP to HTTPS server { listen 80; server_name example.com; return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri; }

Feature Nginx Apache Architecture Event-driven, asynchronous Process/thread-based Memory Usage Lower Higher Static Content Excellent performance Good performance Configuration Centralized config files .htaccess + main config Modules Dynamic loading Both static and dynamic Learning Curve Moderate Easier for beginners

For Apple Silicon M4 processors, you may need to install Homebrew for ARM64 architecture if not already done: # Install Homebrew (if not already installed) /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)" # Ensure you're using ARM64 architecture arch # Should output: arm64 # Install Nginx optimized for M4 brew install nginx # Verify installation and architecture file $(brew --prefix)/bin/nginx # Should show: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64 # Start Nginx with optimized settings for M4 brew services start nginx # Check if running brew services list | grep nginx M4-Optimized Configuration​ For optimal performance on M4 chips, consider these configuration adjustments: # /opt/homebrew/etc/nginx/nginx.conf (M4 optimized) user _www; worker_processes auto; # M4 has efficient cores, auto-detection works well error_log /opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/error.log; events { worker_connections 2048; # M4 can handle higher connections efficiently use kqueue; # Optimal for macOS multi_accept on; } http { include mime.types; default_type application/octet-stream; # M4 optimization settings sendfile on; tcp_nopush on; tcp_nodelay on; # Buffer sizes optimized for M4 memory bandwidth client_body_buffer_size 128k; client_max_body_size 10m; client_header_buffer_size 1k; large_client_header_buffers 4 4k; output_buffers 1 32k; postpone_output 1460; server { listen 8080; # Default Homebrew port server_name localhost; root /opt/homebrew/var/www; index index.html index.htm; location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; } } } Common M4 Considerations​ File Paths: Homebrew on M4 installs to /opt/homebrew/ instead of /usr/local/ Default Port: Homebrew Nginx typically runs on port 8080 to avoid permission issues Process Management: Use brew services for better integration with macOS Performance: M4's efficiency cores handle Nginx's event-driven architecture exceptionally well # M4-specific paths Configuration: /opt/homebrew/etc/nginx/nginx.conf Document root: /opt/homebrew/var/www Error log: /opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/error.log Access log: /opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/access.log

Nginx configuration is typically located at /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and follows a hierarchical structure: # Main context user nginx; worker_processes auto; error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log; # Events context events { worker_connections 1024; } # HTTP context http { include /etc/nginx/mime.types; default_type application/octet-stream; # Server context server { listen 80; server_name example.com; # Location context location / { root /var/www/html; index index.html; } } }
Set worker processes to match your CPU cores: worker_processes auto;
Increase worker connections for high-traffic sites: events { worker_connections 2048; use epoll; # Linux use kqueue; # macOS/BSD }

Enable compression to reduce bandwidth: gzip on; gzip_vary on; gzip_min_length 1024; gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript text/xml application/xml; # M4 optimization: Use higher compression for better CPU/bandwidth trade-off gzip_comp_level 6; # M4 can handle higher compression efficiently gzip_proxied any;
Set appropriate cache headers: location ~* \.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|ico|css|js)$ { expires 1y; add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable"; }

# Basic rate limiting by IP address limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s; # Rate limiting by user session (requires session ID) limit_req_zone $cookie_sessionid zone=session:10m rate=5r/s; # Rate limiting by server name (per domain) limit_req_zone $server_name zone=domain:10m rate=100r/s; # Rate limiting by request URI (specific endpoints) limit_req_zone $request_uri zone=endpoint:10m rate=2r/s; # Whitelist trusted IPs geo $limit { default 1; 10.0.0.0/8 0; # Internal network 192.168.0.0/16 0; # Private network 127.0.0.1/32 0; # Localhost } map $limit $limit_key { 0 ""; 1 $binary_remote_addr; } limit_req_zone $limit_key zone=trusted:10m rate=20r/s; # Different rate limits for different locations location /api/ { limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay; limit_req_status 429; limit_req_log_level warn; } location /login { # Stricter rate limiting for login attempts limit_req zone=api burst=5 nodelay; limit_req_status 429; } location /search { # Higher burst for search with delay limit_req zone=api burst=50; } location /upload { # Very strict rate limiting for uploads limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=upload:10m rate=1r/m; limit_req zone=upload burst=2; } location /public/ { # Use trusted zone for public content limit_req zone=trusted burst=100 nodelay; } Advanced Rate Limiting Configurations​ Multiple Rate Limits: # Apply multiple rate limits simultaneously location /api/critical/ { limit_req zone=api burst=10 nodelay; limit_req zone=session burst=5 nodelay; limit_req zone=endpoint burst=2 nodelay; } Dynamic Rate Limiting Based on Response Status: # Stricter limits after failed attempts map $status $loggable { ~^[23] 0; # Don't log successful requests default 1; } limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=strict:10m rate=1r/s; location /api/auth { limit_req zone=api burst=10; # Apply stricter limits if previous requests failed if ($http_x_failed_attempts) { limit_req zone=strict burst=3; } } Rate Limiting with Custom Error Pages: # Custom error page for rate limited requests error_page 429 /rate_limit.html; location = /rate_limit.html { root /var/www/error; internal; add_header Content-Type text/html; add_header Retry-After 60; } location /api/ { limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay; limit_req_status 429; } Burst Control Strategies: # No burst - strict limiting location /strict-api/ { limit_req zone=api; } # Burst with delay - smoother for users location /smooth-api/ { limit_req zone=api burst=10; } # Burst with nodelay - fast response but strict enforcement location /fast-api/ { limit_req zone=api burst=10 nodelay; }
