# retrieval/qdrant_retriever.py import asyncio from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional, Tuple import numpy as np from qdrant_client import QdrantClient from qdrant_client.http import models from qdrant_client.http.models import ( Distance, VectorParams, CreateCollection, PointStruct, Filter, FieldCondition, PayloadSchemaType ) import logging from abc import ABC, abstractmethod logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class BaseVectorRetriever(ABC): """Abstract base class for vector retrievers""" @abstractmethod async def create_collection(self, collection_name: str, vector_dimension: int) -> bool: pass @abstractmethod async def upsert_vectors(self, collection_name: str, vectors: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool: pass @abstractmethod async def search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, limit: int = 10, filters: Optional[Dict] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: pass class QdrantRetriever(BaseVectorRetriever): """Qdrant vector database retriever implementation""" def __init__(self, host: str = "localhost", port: int = 6333, api_key: Optional[str] = None): self.client = QdrantClient( host=host, port=port, api_key=api_key, timeout=30 ) self.collection_configs = {} logger.info(f"Connected to Qdrant at {host}:{port}") async def create_collection(self, collection_name: str, vector_dimension: int, distance_metric: Distance = Distance.COSINE) -> bool: """Create a new collection in Qdrant""" try: # Check if collection already exists collections = self.client.get_collections() existing_names = [col.name for col in collections.collections] if collection_name in existing_names: logger.info(f"Collection {collection_name} already exists") return True # Create collection self.client.create_collection( collection_name=collection_name, vectors_config=VectorParams( size=vector_dimension, distance=distance_metric ), optimizers_config=models.OptimizersConfig( default_segment_number=2, max_segment_size=20000, memmap_threshold=20000, indexing_threshold=20000, ), replication_factor=1, write_consistency_factor=1, ) # Create payload schema for better performance self.client.create_payload_index( collection_name=collection_name, field_name="category", field_schema=PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD ) self.client.create_payload_index( collection_name=collection_name, field_name="brand", field_schema=PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD ) self.client.create_payload_index( collection_name=collection_name, field_name="price", field_schema=PayloadSchemaType.FLOAT ) self.client.create_payload_index( collection_name=collection_name, field_name="rating", field_schema=PayloadSchemaType.FLOAT ) logger.info(f"Created collection {collection_name} with dimension {vector_dimension}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to create collection {collection_name}: {e}") return False async def upsert_vectors(self, collection_name: str, vectors: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool: """Insert or update vectors in the collection""" try: points = [] for i, vector_data in enumerate(vectors): point = PointStruct( id=vector_data.get('id', i), vector=vector_data['vector'].tolist() if isinstance(vector_data['vector'], np.ndarray) else vector_data['vector'], payload=vector_data.get('payload', {}) ) points.append(point) # Batch upsert batch_size = 100 for i in range(0, len(points), batch_size): batch = points[i:i + batch_size] operation_info = self.client.upsert( collection_name=collection_name, wait=True, points=batch ) logger.debug(f"Upserted batch {i//batch_size + 1}: {operation_info}") logger.info(f"Successfully upserted {len(vectors)} vectors to {collection_name}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to upsert vectors to {collection_name}: {e}") return False async def search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, limit: int = 10, filters: Optional[Dict] = None, score_threshold: Optional[float] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Search for similar vectors""" try: # Convert numpy array to list query_vector_list = query_vector.tolist() if isinstance(query_vector, np.ndarray) else query_vector # Build filters qdrant_filter = self._build_qdrant_filter(filters) if filters else None # Perform search search_result = self.client.search( collection_name=collection_name, query_vector=query_vector_list, limit=limit, query_filter=qdrant_filter, score_threshold=score_threshold, with_payload=True, with_vectors=False ) # Format results results = [] for scored_point in search_result: result = { 'id': scored_point.id, 'score': scored_point.score, 'payload': scored_point.payload } results.append(result) logger.debug(f"Found {len(results)} results for query in {collection_name}") return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Search failed in {collection_name}: {e}") return [] async def hybrid_search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, text_query: str, limit: int = 10, alpha: float = 0.7) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Hybrid search combining vector and text search""" try: # Vector search vector_results = await self.search( collection_name=collection_name, query_vector=query_vector, limit=limit * 2 # Get more candidates ) # Text-based filtering/scoring text_scored_results = self._score_text_relevance(vector_results, text_query) # Combine scores final_results = [] for result in text_scored_results: vector_score = result['score'] text_score = result.get('text_score', 0.0) # Weighted combination combined_score = alpha * vector_score + (1 - alpha) * text_score result['combined_score'] = combined_score result['vector_score'] = vector_score result['text_score'] = text_score final_results.append(result) # Sort by combined score and limit results final_results.sort(key=lambda x: x['combined_score'], reverse=True) return final_results[:limit] except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Hybrid search failed: {e}") return [] def _build_qdrant_filter(self, filters: Dict[str, Any]) -> Filter: """Build Qdrant filter from dictionary""" conditions = [] for field, value in filters.items(): if isinstance(value, dict): # Range filter if 'gte' in value or 'lte' in value or 'gt' in value or 'lt' in value: condition = FieldCondition( key=field, range=models.Range(**value) ) # Match any filter elif 'any' in value: condition = FieldCondition( key=field, match=models.MatchAny(any=value['any']) ) else: continue else: # Exact match condition = FieldCondition( key=field, match=models.MatchValue(value=value) ) conditions.append(condition) return Filter(must=conditions) if conditions else None def _score_text_relevance(self, results: List[Dict[str, Any]], text_query: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Score results based on text relevance""" query_terms = set(text_query.lower().split()) for result in results: text_score = 0.0 payload = result.get('payload', {}) # Score based on title match title = payload.get('title', '').lower() title_words = set(title.split()) title_overlap = len(query_terms & title_words) / max(len(query_terms), 1) text_score += title_overlap * 0.6 # Score based on description match description = payload.get('description', '').lower() desc_words = set(description.split()) desc_overlap = len(query_terms & desc_words) / max(len(query_terms), 1) text_score += desc_overlap * 0.3 # Score based on category/brand match category = payload.get('category', '').lower() brand = payload.get('brand', '').lower() if any(term in category for term in query_terms): text_score += 0.1 if any(term in brand for term in query_terms): text_score += 0.1 result['text_score'] = text_score return results async def get_collection_info(self, collection_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Get information about a collection""" try: info = self.client.get_collection(collection_name) return { 'status': info.status, 'vectors_count': info.vectors_count, 'points_count': info.points_count, 'config': info.config } except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to get collection info: {e}") return {} async def delete_collection(self, collection_name: str) -> bool: """Delete a collection""" try: self.client.delete_collection(collection_name) logger.info(f"Deleted collection {collection_name}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to delete collection {collection_name}: {e}") return False

# retrieval/pinecone_retriever.py import pinecone import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import logging import asyncio from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class PineconeRetriever(BaseVectorRetriever): """Pinecone vector database retriever implementation""" def __init__(self, api_key: str, environment: str): pinecone.init(api_key=api_key, environment=environment) self.api_key = api_key self.environment = environment self.indexes = {} self.executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=10) logger.info(f"Initialized Pinecone in environment: {environment}") async def create_collection(self, collection_name: str, vector_dimension: int, metric: str = "cosine", pods: int = 1, pod_type: str = "p1.x1") -> bool: """Create a new index in Pinecone""" try: # Check if index exists if collection_name in pinecone.list_indexes(): logger.info(f"Index {collection_name} already exists") self.indexes[collection_name] = pinecone.Index(collection_name) return True # Create index pinecone.create_index( name=collection_name, dimension=vector_dimension, metric=metric, pods=pods, pod_type=pod_type ) # Wait for index to be ready await asyncio.sleep(10) # Pinecone needs time to initialize self.indexes[collection_name] = pinecone.Index(collection_name) logger.info(f"Created Pinecone index {collection_name}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to create Pinecone index {collection_name}: {e}") return False async def upsert_vectors(self, collection_name: str, vectors: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool: """Insert or update vectors in Pinecone""" try: if collection_name not in self.indexes: self.indexes[collection_name] = pinecone.Index(collection_name) index = self.indexes[collection_name] # Prepare vectors for Pinecone format pinecone_vectors = [] for vector_data in vectors: vector_id = str(vector_data.get('id')) vector_values = vector_data['vector'].tolist() if isinstance(vector_data['vector'], np.ndarray) else vector_data['vector'] metadata = vector_data.get('payload', {}) pinecone_vectors.append((vector_id, vector_values, metadata)) # Batch upsert batch_size = 100 for i in range(0, len(pinecone_vectors), batch_size): batch = pinecone_vectors[i:i + batch_size] # Run in executor to avoid blocking await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor( self.executor, lambda: index.upsert(vectors=batch) ) logger.info(f"Upserted {len(vectors)} vectors to Pinecone index {collection_name}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to upsert vectors to Pinecone: {e}") return False async def search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, limit: int = 10, filters: Optional[Dict] = None, include_metadata: bool = True) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Search for similar vectors in Pinecone""" try: if collection_name not in self.indexes: self.indexes[collection_name] = pinecone.Index(collection_name) index = self.indexes[collection_name] # Convert numpy array to list query_vector_list = query_vector.tolist() if isinstance(query_vector, np.ndarray) else query_vector # Perform search search_response = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor( self.executor, lambda: index.query( vector=query_vector_list, top_k=limit, filter=filters, include_metadata=include_metadata ) ) # Format results results = [] for match in search_response.matches: result = { 'id': match.id, 'score': match.score, 'payload': match.metadata if include_metadata else {} } results.append(result) logger.debug(f"Found {len(results)} results in Pinecone index {collection_name}") return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Pinecone search failed: {e}") return [] async def delete_collection(self, collection_name: str) -> bool: """Delete a Pinecone index""" try: pinecone.delete_index(collection_name) if collection_name in self.indexes: del self.indexes[collection_name] logger.info(f"Deleted Pinecone index {collection_name}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to delete Pinecone index {collection_name}: {e}") return False async def get_collection_info(self, collection_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Get information about a Pinecone index""" try: index_stats = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor( self.executor, lambda: pinecone.Index(collection_name).describe_index_stats() ) return { 'total_vector_count': index_stats.total_vector_count, 'dimension': index_stats.dimension, 'index_fullness': index_stats.index_fullness } except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to get Pinecone index info: {e}") return {}

# retrieval/hybrid_retriever.py import asyncio from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional, Tuple import numpy as np from elasticsearch import AsyncElasticsearch import logging from collections import defaultdict logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class HybridRetriever: """Combines vector search with traditional text search""" def __init__(self, vector_retriever: BaseVectorRetriever, elasticsearch_client: Optional[AsyncElasticsearch] = None): self.vector_retriever = vector_retriever self.elasticsearch_client = elasticsearch_client self.fusion_methods = { 'rrf': self._reciprocal_rank_fusion, 'weighted': self._weighted_fusion, 'linear': self._linear_combination } async def hybrid_search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, text_query: str, limit: int = 10, vector_weight: float = 0.7, fusion_method: str = 'rrf', filters: Optional[Dict] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Perform hybrid search combining vector and text search""" # Run searches in parallel vector_task = self._vector_search(collection_name, query_vector, limit * 2, filters) text_task = self._text_search(collection_name, text_query, limit * 2, filters) vector_results, text_results = await asyncio.gather(vector_task, text_task) # Fuse results fusion_func = self.fusion_methods.get(fusion_method, self._reciprocal_rank_fusion) fused_results = fusion_func(vector_results, text_results, vector_weight) # Limit and return results return fused_results[:limit] async def _vector_search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, limit: int, filters: Optional[Dict] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Perform vector similarity search""" try: results = await self.vector_retriever.search( collection_name=collection_name, query_vector=query_vector, limit=limit, filters=filters ) # Add search type and normalize scores for i, result in enumerate(results): result['search_type'] = 'vector' result['rank'] = i + 1 result['normalized_score'] = result['score'] # Assumes cosine similarity [0,1] return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Vector search failed: {e}") return [] async def _text_search(self, collection_name: str, text_query: str, limit: int, filters: Optional[Dict] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Perform full-text search using Elasticsearch""" if not self.elasticsearch_client: logger.warning("Elasticsearch client not configured, skipping text search") return [] try: # Build Elasticsearch query es_query = { "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "multi_match": { "query": text_query, "fields": ["title^3", "description^2", "category", "brand"], "type": "best_fields", "fuzziness": "AUTO" } } ] } }, "size": limit } # Add filters if provided if filters: es_filters = self._build_elasticsearch_filters(filters) es_query["query"]["bool"]["filter"] = es_filters # Execute search response = await self.elasticsearch_client.search( index=collection_name, body=es_query ) # Format results results = [] for i, hit in enumerate(response['hits']['hits']): result = { 'id': hit['_id'], 'score': hit['_score'], 'payload': hit['_source'], 'search_type': 'text', 'rank': i + 1, 'normalized_score': hit['_score'] / response['hits']['max_score'] if response['hits']['max_score'] > 0 else 0 } results.append(result) return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Text search failed: {e}") return [] def _reciprocal_rank_fusion(self, vector_results: List[Dict[str, Any]], text_results: List[Dict[str, Any]], vector_weight: float = 0.7, k: int = 60) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Combine results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion""" # Create score maps vector_scores = {result['id']: 1 / (k + result['rank']) for result in vector_results} text_scores = {result['id']: 1 / (k + result['rank']) for result in text_results} # Get all unique IDs all_ids = set(vector_scores.keys()) | set(text_scores.keys()) # Calculate combined scores combined_results = [] item_map = {} # Create item lookup for result in vector_results + text_results: if result['id'] not in item_map: item_map[result['id']] = result for item_id in all_ids: vector_score = vector_scores.get(item_id, 0) text_score = text_scores.get(item_id, 0) # Weighted RRF score combined_score = (vector_weight * vector_score + (1 - vector_weight) * text_score) if item_id in item_map: result = item_map[item_id].copy() result['rrf_score'] = combined_score result['vector_rrf'] = vector_score result['text_rrf'] = text_score combined_results.append(result) # Sort by combined score combined_results.sort(key=lambda x: x['rrf_score'], reverse=True) return combined_results def _weighted_fusion(self, vector_results: List[Dict[str, Any]], text_results: List[Dict[str, Any]], vector_weight: float = 0.7) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Combine results using weighted score fusion""" # Create score maps vector_scores = {result['id']: result['normalized_score'] for result in vector_results} text_scores = {result['id']: result['normalized_score'] for result in text_results} # Get all unique IDs all_ids = set(vector_scores.keys()) | set(text_scores.keys()) # Calculate combined scores combined_results = [] item_map = {} # Create item lookup for result in vector_results + text_results: if result['id'] not in item_map: item_map[result['id']] = result for item_id in all_ids: vector_score = vector_scores.get(item_id, 0) text_score = text_scores.get(item_id, 0) # Weighted combination combined_score = (vector_weight * vector_score + (1 - vector_weight) * text_score) if item_id in item_map: result = item_map[item_id].copy() result['combined_score'] = combined_score result['vector_score'] = vector_score result['text_score'] = text_score combined_results.append(result) # Sort by combined score combined_results.sort(key=lambda x: x['combined_score'], reverse=True) return combined_results def _linear_combination(self, vector_results: List[Dict[str, Any]], text_results: List[Dict[str, Any]], vector_weight: float = 0.7) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Simple linear combination of normalized scores""" return self._weighted_fusion(vector_results, text_results, vector_weight) def _build_elasticsearch_filters(self, filters: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Convert filters to Elasticsearch format""" es_filters = [] for field, value in filters.items(): if isinstance(value, dict): if 'gte' in value or 'lte' in value: es_filters.append({ "range": { field: value } }) elif 'any' in value: es_filters.append({ "terms": { field: value['any'] } }) else: es_filters.append({ "term": { field: value } }) return es_filters

# retrieval/contextual_search.py from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import numpy as np from datetime import datetime, timedelta import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class ContextualSearchEngine: """Advanced search engine with context awareness""" def __init__(self, retriever: BaseVectorRetriever): self.retriever = retriever self.context_weights = { 'seasonal': 0.1, 'trending': 0.15, 'personal': 0.3, 'behavioral': 0.25, 'collaborative': 0.2 } async def contextual_search(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, user_context: Dict[str, Any], limit: int = 10) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Perform context-aware search""" # Get base search results base_results = await self.retriever.search( collection_name=collection_name, query_vector=query_vector, limit=limit * 3 # Get more candidates for reranking ) # Apply contextual reranking reranked_results = await self._apply_contextual_reranking( base_results, user_context ) # Apply diversity filtering diverse_results = self._apply_diversity_filtering(reranked_results, limit) return diverse_results async def _apply_contextual_reranking(self, results: List[Dict[str, Any]], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Rerank results based on context""" for result in results: payload = result.get('payload', {}) base_score = result['score'] # Calculate context-based adjustments seasonal_boost = self._calculate_seasonal_boost(payload, context) trending_boost = self._calculate_trending_boost(payload, context) personal_boost = self._calculate_personal_boost(payload, context) behavioral_boost = self._calculate_behavioral_boost(payload, context) collaborative_boost = self._calculate_collaborative_boost(payload, context) # Apply weighted boosts context_score = ( self.context_weights['seasonal'] * seasonal_boost + self.context_weights['trending'] * trending_boost + self.context_weights['personal'] * personal_boost + self.context_weights['behavioral'] * behavioral_boost + self.context_weights['collaborative'] * collaborative_boost ) # Combine base score with context score result['contextual_score'] = base_score * (1 + context_score) result['context_breakdown'] = { 'seasonal': seasonal_boost, 'trending': trending_boost, 'personal': personal_boost, 'behavioral': behavioral_boost, 'collaborative': collaborative_boost } # Sort by contextual score results.sort(key=lambda x: x['contextual_score'], reverse=True) return results def _calculate_seasonal_boost(self, product: Dict[str, Any], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate seasonal relevance boost""" current_month = datetime.now().month product_category = product.get('category', '').lower() # Define seasonal categories seasonal_categories = { 'winter': ['coats', 'sweaters', 'boots', 'heating'], 'spring': ['flowers', 'gardening', 'light_clothing'], 'summer': ['swimwear', 'shorts', 'cooling', 'outdoor'], 'fall': ['jackets', 'school_supplies', 'warm_drinks'] } # Determine current season season_map = { 12: 'winter', 1: 'winter', 2: 'winter', 3: 'spring', 4: 'spring', 5: 'spring', 6: 'summer', 7: 'summer', 8: 'summer', 9: 'fall', 10: 'fall', 11: 'fall' } current_season = season_map.get(current_month, 'spring') seasonal_items = seasonal_categories.get(current_season, []) # Check if product matches current season for item in seasonal_items: if item in product_category or item in product.get('title', '').lower(): return 0.2 # 20% boost for seasonal items return 0.0 def _calculate_trending_boost(self, product: Dict[str, Any], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate trending boost based on recent popularity""" popularity_score = product.get('popularity_score', 0) recent_views = product.get('recent_views', 0) # Boost based on popularity and recent activity trending_score = 0.0 if popularity_score > 0.8: trending_score += 0.15 elif popularity_score > 0.6: trending_score += 0.1 if recent_views > 1000: # High recent activity trending_score += 0.1 return trending_score def _calculate_personal_boost(self, product: Dict[str, Any], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate personal preference boost""" user_preferences = context.get('preferences', {}) personal_score = 0.0 # Category preference preferred_categories = user_preferences.get('preferred_categories', []) if product.get('category') in preferred_categories: personal_score += 0.3 # Brand preference preferred_brands = user_preferences.get('preferred_brands', []) if product.get('brand') in preferred_brands: personal_score += 0.2 # Price preference price_sensitivity = user_preferences.get('price_sensitivity', 0.5) product_price = product.get('price', 0) user_avg_price = context.get('avg_order_value', 100) if price_sensitivity < 0.3: # Price-conscious user if product_price <= user_avg_price * 0.8: personal_score += 0.1 elif price_sensitivity > 0.7: # Premium-oriented user if product_price >= user_avg_price * 1.2: personal_score += 0.1 return personal_score def _calculate_behavioral_boost(self, product: Dict[str, Any], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate behavioral pattern boost""" user_behavior = context.get('behavioral_features', {}) behavioral_score = 0.0 # Time-based patterns current_hour = datetime.now().hour user_peak_hour = context.get('peak_hour', 12) # Boost items typically purchased at current time if abs(current_hour - user_peak_hour) <= 2: behavioral_score += 0.1 # Purchase frequency patterns purchase_frequency = user_behavior.get('purchase_frequency', 0) if purchase_frequency > 10: # Frequent buyer # Boost consumable/replenishable items if any(keyword in product.get('title', '').lower() for keyword in ['refill', 'pack', 'bulk']): behavioral_score += 0.15 return behavioral_score def _calculate_collaborative_boost(self, product: Dict[str, Any], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate collaborative filtering boost""" # This would typically use precomputed user similarity scores # For now, we'll use simplified logic similar_users_preferences = context.get('similar_users_bought', []) if product.get('id') in similar_users_preferences: return 0.2 return 0.0 def _apply_diversity_filtering(self, results: List[Dict[str, Any]], limit: int, diversity_threshold: float = 0.3) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Apply diversity filtering to avoid too similar items""" if not results: return results diverse_results = [results[0]] # Always include top result for result in results[1:]: if len(diverse_results) >= limit: break # Check diversity against already selected items is_diverse = True result_category = result.get('payload', {}).get('category', '') result_brand = result.get('payload', {}).get('brand', '') category_count = sum(1 for r in diverse_results if r.get('payload', {}).get('category', '') == result_category) brand_count = sum(1 for r in diverse_results if r.get('payload', {}).get('brand', '') == result_brand) # Avoid too many items from same category/brand if (category_count >= limit * diversity_threshold or brand_count >= limit * diversity_threshold): is_diverse = False if is_diverse: diverse_results.append(result) return diverse_results

# retrieval/performance_optimizer.py import asyncio from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import numpy as np import redis import json import hashlib from datetime import datetime, timedelta import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class SearchPerformanceOptimizer: """Optimize search performance through caching and query optimization""" def __init__(self, redis_client: Optional[redis.Redis] = None): self.redis_client = redis_client self.cache_ttl = { 'search_results': 3600, # 1 hour 'user_embeddings': 86400, # 24 hours 'popular_queries': 7200, # 2 hours } self.query_stats = {} async def optimized_search(self, search_func, cache_key: str, ttl: int = 3600, *args, **kwargs) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Wrapper for optimized search with caching""" # Try cache first cached_result = await self._get_cached_result(cache_key) if cached_result is not None: logger.debug(f"Cache hit for key: {cache_key}") return cached_result # Execute search start_time = datetime.now() results = await search_func(*args, **kwargs) execution_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds() # Cache results await self._cache_result(cache_key, results, ttl) # Update query statistics self._update_query_stats(cache_key, execution_time, len(results)) logger.debug(f"Search executed in {execution_time:.3f}s, {len(results)} results") return results async def _get_cached_result(self, cache_key: str) -> Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]]: """Retrieve cached search results""" if not self.redis_client: return None try: cached_data = self.redis_client.get(cache_key) if cached_data: return json.loads(cached_data) except Exception as e: logger.warning(f"Cache retrieval failed: {e}") return None async def _cache_result(self, cache_key: str, results: List[Dict[str, Any]], ttl: int) -> None: """Cache search results""" if not self.redis_client: return try: # Serialize results (handle numpy arrays) serializable_results = self._make_serializable(results) cached_data = json.dumps(serializable_results) self.redis_client.setex(cache_key, ttl, cached_data) logger.debug(f"Cached results for key: {cache_key}") except Exception as e: logger.warning(f"Caching failed: {e}") def _make_serializable(self, results: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Convert results to JSON-serializable format""" serializable_results = [] for result in results: serializable_result = {} for key, value in result.items(): if isinstance(value, np.ndarray): serializable_result[key] = value.tolist() elif isinstance(value, (np.int64, np.int32)): serializable_result[key] = int(value) elif isinstance(value, (np.float64, np.float32)): serializable_result[key] = float(value) else: serializable_result[key] = value serializable_results.append(serializable_result) return serializable_results def _update_query_stats(self, cache_key: str, execution_time: float, result_count: int) -> None: """Update query performance statistics""" if cache_key not in self.query_stats: self.query_stats[cache_key] = { 'count': 0, 'total_time': 0.0, 'total_results': 0, 'avg_time': 0.0, 'avg_results': 0.0 } stats = self.query_stats[cache_key] stats['count'] += 1 stats['total_time'] += execution_time stats['total_results'] += result_count stats['avg_time'] = stats['total_time'] / stats['count'] stats['avg_results'] = stats['total_results'] / stats['count'] def generate_cache_key(self, *args, **kwargs) -> str: """Generate cache key from search parameters""" # Create deterministic key from parameters key_data = { 'args': args, 'kwargs': kwargs } key_string = json.dumps(key_data, sort_keys=True, default=str) return hashlib.md5(key_string.encode()).hexdigest() async def warm_cache(self, collection_name: str, popular_queries: List[str], retriever: BaseVectorRetriever, embedding_generator) -> None: """Pre-warm cache with popular queries""" logger.info(f"Warming cache with {len(popular_queries)} popular queries") for query in popular_queries: try: # Generate query embedding query_embedding = await embedding_generator.generate_query_embedding(query) # Generate cache key cache_key = self.generate_cache_key( 'search', collection_name, query, limit=20 ) # Execute search if not cached cached_result = await self._get_cached_result(cache_key) if cached_result is None: results = await retriever.search( collection_name=collection_name, query_vector=query_embedding, limit=20 ) await self._cache_result(cache_key, results, self.cache_ttl['search_results']) # Rate limiting to avoid overwhelming the system await asyncio.sleep(0.1) except Exception as e: logger.warning(f"Failed to warm cache for query '{query}': {e}") logger.info("Cache warming completed") def get_performance_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Get performance statistics""" total_queries = sum(stats['count'] for stats in self.query_stats.values()) avg_execution_time = np.mean([stats['avg_time'] for stats in self.query_stats.values()]) if self.query_stats else 0 return { 'total_queries': total_queries, 'unique_query_patterns': len(self.query_stats), 'avg_execution_time': avg_execution_time, 'query_breakdown': self.query_stats }

# tests/test_retrieval_system.py import pytest import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict, Any import asyncio import time from retrieval.qdrant_retriever import QdrantRetriever from retrieval.hybrid_retriever import HybridRetriever class RetrievalSystemTester: """Comprehensive testing for retrieval system""" def __init__(self, retriever: BaseVectorRetriever): self.retriever = retriever self.test_collection = "test_products" self.test_data = self._generate_test_data() async def run_all_tests(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Run comprehensive test suite""" results = { 'accuracy_tests': await self._test_search_accuracy(), 'performance_tests': await self._test_search_performance(), 'scalability_tests': await self._test_scalability(), 'relevance_tests': await self._test_relevance_ranking() } return results async def _test_search_accuracy(self) -> Dict[str, float]: """Test search accuracy using ground truth data""" # Set up test collection await self.retriever.create_collection(self.test_collection, 384) await self.retriever.upsert_vectors(self.test_collection, self.test_data) accuracy_scores = [] # Test with known similar items for test_case in self._get_accuracy_test_cases(): query_vector = test_case['query_vector'] expected_ids = set(test_case['expected_ids']) results = await self.retriever.search( collection_name=self.test_collection, query_vector=query_vector, limit=len(expected_ids) * 2 ) # Calculate accuracy metrics retrieved_ids = set([r['id'] for r in results[:len(expected_ids)]]) precision = len(retrieved_ids & expected_ids) / len(retrieved_ids) if retrieved_ids else 0 recall = len(retrieved_ids & expected_ids) / len(expected_ids) if expected_ids else 0 f1_score = 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0 accuracy_scores.append({ 'precision': precision, 'recall': recall, 'f1_score': f1_score }) # Calculate average metrics avg_precision = np.mean([s['precision'] for s in accuracy_scores]) avg_recall = np.mean([s['recall'] for s in accuracy_scores]) avg_f1 = np.mean([s['f1_score'] for s in accuracy_scores]) return { 'precision': avg_precision, 'recall': avg_recall, 'f1_score': avg_f1 } async def _test_search_performance(self) -> Dict[str, float]: """Test search performance and latency""" query_vector = np.random.rand(384) # Warm up await self.retriever.search(self.test_collection, query_vector, limit=10) # Performance test latencies = [] for _ in range(50): start_time = time.time() await self.retriever.search(self.test_collection, query_vector, limit=10) latency = time.time() - start_time latencies.append(latency) return { 'avg_latency': np.mean(latencies), 'p95_latency': np.percentile(latencies, 95), 'p99_latency': np.percentile(latencies, 99), 'min_latency': np.min(latencies), 'max_latency': np.max(latencies) } async def _test_scalability(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Test system scalability with increasing load""" results = {} # Test concurrent queries for concurrency in [1, 5, 10, 20]: query_vector = np.random.rand(384) start_time = time.time() tasks = [] for _ in range(concurrency): task = self.retriever.search(self.test_collection, query_vector, limit=10) tasks.append(task) await asyncio.gather(*tasks) total_time = time.time() - start_time results[f'concurrency_{concurrency}'] = { 'total_time': total_time, 'avg_time_per_query': total_time / concurrency, 'queries_per_second': concurrency / total_time } return results async def _test_relevance_ranking(self) -> Dict[str, float]: """Test relevance ranking quality""" # This would test if more relevant items appear higher in results # For now, we'll implement a simplified version relevance_scores = [] for test_case in self._get_relevance_test_cases(): query_vector = test_case['query_vector'] relevance_map = test_case['relevance_map'] # id -> relevance_score results = await self.retriever.search( collection_name=self.test_collection, query_vector=query_vector, limit=10 ) # Calculate NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) dcg = 0.0 ideal_dcg = 0.0 # Calculate DCG for retrieved results for i, result in enumerate(results): relevance = relevance_map.get(result['id'], 0) dcg += relevance / np.log2(i + 2) # Calculate ideal DCG ideal_relevances = sorted(relevance_map.values(), reverse=True) for i, relevance in enumerate(ideal_relevances[:len(results)]): ideal_dcg += relevance / np.log2(i + 2) ndcg = dcg / ideal_dcg if ideal_dcg > 0 else 0 relevance_scores.append(ndcg) return { 'avg_ndcg': np.mean(relevance_scores), 'min_ndcg': np.min(relevance_scores), 'max_ndcg': np.max(relevance_scores) } def _generate_test_data(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Generate test data for evaluation""" test_data = [] # Generate synthetic product vectors and metadata for i in range(1000): vector = np.random.rand(384) payload = { 'id': f'product_{i}', 'title': f'Test Product {i}', 'category': ['electronics', 'clothing', 'books'][i % 3], 'brand': ['BrandA', 'BrandB', 'BrandC'][i % 3], 'price': 10 + (i % 200), 'rating': 3.0 + (i % 3) } test_data.append({ 'id': f'product_{i}', 'vector': vector, 'payload': payload }) return test_data def _get_accuracy_test_cases(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Get test cases for accuracy evaluation""" # Create test cases where we know which items should be similar test_cases = [] # Electronics category test electronics_vector = np.random.rand(384) electronics_ids = [f'product_{i}' for i in range(0, 334, 3)] # Every 3rd electronics item test_cases.append({ 'query_vector': electronics_vector, 'expected_ids': electronics_ids[:10] # Top 10 expected }) return test_cases def _get_relevance_test_cases(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Get test cases for relevance evaluation""" test_cases = [] # Create relevance maps for test queries query_vector = np.random.rand(384) relevance_map = {} # Assign higher relevance to certain products for i in range(100): if i % 10 == 0: # High relevance relevance_map[f'product_{i}'] = 3 elif i % 5 == 0: # Medium relevance relevance_map[f'product_{i}'] = 2 else: # Low relevance relevance_map[f'product_{i}'] = 1 test_cases.append({ 'query_vector': query_vector, 'relevance_map': relevance_map }) return test_cases

In Part 4 of this series, we'll implement the generation and personalization engine that transforms retrieved products into intelligent, personalized recommendations. We'll cover: LLM Integration: Connecting with OpenAI, Anthropic, and local models Prompt Engineering: Crafting effective prompts for recommendation generation Personalization Algorithms: Advanced techniques for user-specific recommendations A/B Testing Framework: Measuring and optimizing recommendation quality

In this post, we've built a sophisticated retrieval system: ✅ Multi-Database Support: Implementations for Qdrant, Pinecone, and hybrid approaches ✅ Advanced Search Strategies: Semantic, keyword, and hybrid search with fusion algorithms ✅ Contextual Intelligence: Context-aware search with seasonal, behavioral, and collaborative signals ✅ Performance Optimization: Caching, query optimization, and scalability testing ✅ Comprehensive Testing: Accuracy, performance, and relevance evaluation frameworks

Ensure you have: Set up your chosen vector database Indexed your product catalog with embeddings Implemented and tested basic search functionality Prepared for LLM integration (API keys, model selection) The retrieval system is the engine that finds relevant products. Next, we'll build the intelligence layer that transforms these results into personalized recommendations!

Welcome to Part 4 of our RAG-powered e-commerce recommendation series! We've built our data pipeline, generated embeddings, and implemented sophisticated retrieval systems. Now we'll create the crown jewel: an intelligent generation and personalization engine that transforms raw product matches into compelling, personalized recommendations that drive engagement and conversions. This generation engine leverages large language models to understand context, craft personalized explanations, and create recommendations that feel natural and relevant to each individual user. We'll explore advanced prompt engineering, personalization algorithms, and A/B testing frameworks.

documents.t: Let's start by implementing a flexible LLM integration layer that supports multiple providers: # generation/llm_client.py import asyncio import openai import anthropic from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional, Union import json import logging from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from dataclasses import dataclass from enum import Enum import time logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class ModelProvider(Enum): OPENAI = "openai" ANTHROPIC = "anthropic" LOCAL = "local" AZURE_OPENAI = "azure_openai" @dataclass class GenerationConfig: temperature: float = 0.7 max_tokens: int = 1000 top_p: float = 0.9 frequency_penalty: float = 0.0 presence_penalty: float = 0.0 stop_sequences: Optional[List[str]] = None @dataclass class GenerationRequest: prompt: str config: GenerationConfig model: str system_prompt: Optional[str] = None context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None @dataclass class GenerationResponse: content: str model: str provider: ModelProvider token_usage: Dict[str, int] latency: float cost: float class BaseLLMClient(ABC): """Abstract base class for LLM clients""" @abstractmethod async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: pass @abstractmethod def calculate_cost(self, token_usage: Dict[str, int], model: str) -> float: pass class OpenAIClient(BaseLLMClient): """OpenAI API client implementation""" def __init__(self, api_key: str, organization: Optional[str] = None): self.client = openai.AsyncOpenAI( api_key=api_key, organization=organization ) self.pricing = { "gpt-4": {"input": 0.03, "output": 0.06}, "gpt-4-turbo": {"input": 0.01, "output": 0.03}, "gpt-3.5-turbo": {"input": 0.001, "output": 0.002}, "gpt-3.5-turbo-16k": {"input": 0.003, "output": 0.004} } async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: """Generate response using OpenAI API""" start_time = time.time() try: messages = [] # Add system prompt if provided if request.system_prompt: messages.append({ "role": "system", "content": request.system_prompt }) # Add main prompt messages.append({ "role": "user", "content": request.prompt }) # Make API call response = await self.client.chat.completions.create( model=request.model, messages=messages, temperature=request.config.temperature, max_tokens=request.config.max_tokens, top_p=request.config.top_p, frequency_penalty=request.config.frequency_penalty, presence_penalty=request.config.presence_penalty, stop=request.config.stop_sequences ) latency = time.time() - start_time token_usage = { "prompt_tokens": response.usage.prompt_tokens, "completion_tokens": response.usage.completion_tokens, "total_tokens": response.usage.total_tokens } cost = self.calculate_cost(token_usage, request.model) return GenerationResponse( content=response.choices[0].message.content, model=request.model, provider=ModelProvider.OPENAI, token_usage=token_usage, latency=latency, cost=cost ) except Exception as e: logger.error(f"OpenAI generation failed: {e}") raise def calculate_cost(self, token_usage: Dict[str, int], model: str) -> float: """Calculate cost based on token usage""" pricing = self.pricing.get(model, self.pricing["gpt-3.5-turbo"]) input_cost = token_usage["prompt_tokens"] * pricing["input"] / 1000 output_cost = token_usage["completion_tokens"] * pricing["output"] / 1000 return input_cost + output_cost class AnthropicClient(BaseLLMClient): """Anthropic Claude API client implementation""" def __init__(self, api_key: str): self.client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic(api_key=api_key) self.pricing = { "claude-3-opus-20240229": {"input": 0.015, "output": 0.075}, "claude-3-sonnet-20240229": {"input": 0.003, "output": 0.015}, "claude-3-haiku-20240307": {"input": 0.00025, "output": 0.00125} } async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: """Generate response using Anthropic API""" start_time = time.time() try: # Prepare prompt for Claude full_prompt = request.prompt if request.system_prompt: full_prompt = f"{request.system_prompt}\n\n{request.prompt}" # Make API call response = await self.client.messages.create( model=request.model, max_tokens=request.config.max_tokens, temperature=request.config.temperature, top_p=request.config.top_p, stop_sequences=request.config.stop_sequences or [], messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": full_prompt} ] ) latency = time.time() - start_time token_usage = { "prompt_tokens": response.usage.input_tokens, "completion_tokens": response.usage.output_tokens, "total_tokens": response.usage.input_tokens + response.usage.output_tokens } cost = self.calculate_cost(token_usage, request.model) return GenerationResponse( content=response.content[0].text, model=request.model, provider=ModelProvider.ANTHROPIC, token_usage=token_usage, latency=latency, cost=cost ) except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Anthropic generation failed: {e}") raise def calculate_cost(self, token_usage: Dict[str, int], model: str) -> float: """Calculate cost based on token usage""" pricing = self.pricing.get(model, self.pricing["claude-3-haiku-20240307"]) input_cost = token_usage["prompt_tokens"] * pricing["input"] / 1000 output_cost = token_usage["completion_tokens"] * pricing["output"] / 1000 return input_cost + output_cost class LLMClientManager: """Manages multiple LLM clients with fallback and load balancing""" def __init__(self): self.clients: Dict[ModelProvider, BaseLLMClient] = {} self.model_mapping: Dict[str, ModelProvider] = {} self.fallback_order = [ModelProvider.OPENAI, ModelProvider.ANTHROPIC] def register_client(self, provider: ModelProvider, client: BaseLLMClient): """Register an LLM client""" self.clients[provider] = client logger.info(f"Registered {provider.value} client") def register_model(self, model_name: str, provider: ModelProvider): """Register a model with its provider""" self.model_mapping[model_name] = provider async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: """Generate response with fallback support""" provider = self.model_mapping.get(request.model) if not provider: raise ValueError(f"Unknown model: {request.model}") # Try primary provider if provider in self.clients: try: return await self.clients[provider].generate(request) except Exception as e: logger.warning(f"Primary provider {provider.value} failed: {e}") # Try fallback providers for fallback_provider in self.fallback_order: if fallback_provider != provider and fallback_provider in self.clients: try: logger.info(f"Trying fallback provider: {fallback_provider.value}") fallback_request = self._adapt_request_for_provider(request, fallback_provider) return await self.clients[fallback_provider].generate(fallback_request) except Exception as e: logger.warning(f"Fallback provider {fallback_provider.value} failed: {e}") continue raise Exception("All LLM providers failed") def _adapt_request_for_provider(self, request: GenerationRequest, provider: ModelProvider) -> GenerationRequest: """Adapt request for different provider""" # Map models between providers model_mappings = { ModelProvider.OPENAI: { "claude-3-opus-20240229": "gpt-4", "claude-3-sonnet-20240229": "gpt-3.5-turbo-16k", "claude-3-haiku-20240307": "gpt-3.5-turbo" }, ModelProvider.ANTHROPIC: { "gpt-4": "claude-3-opus-20240229", "gpt-3.5-turbo": "claude-3-haiku-20240307", "gpt-3.5-turbo-16k": "claude-3-sonnet-20240229" } } adapted_model = model_mappings.get(provider, {}).get(request.model, request.model) return GenerationRequest( prompt=request.prompt, config=request.config, model=adapted_model, system_prompt=request.system_prompt, context=request.context )

# generation/prompt_engineer.py from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional from dataclasses import dataclass from enum import Enum import json import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class RecommendationType(Enum): PRODUCT_DISCOVERY = "product_discovery" SIMILAR_PRODUCTS = "similar_products" PERSONALIZED_SUGGESTIONS = "personalized_suggestions" TRENDING_ITEMS = "trending_items" BUNDLE_RECOMMENDATIONS = "bundle_recommendations" REORDER_SUGGESTIONS = "reorder_suggestions" class PersonalityType(Enum): PROFESSIONAL = "professional" FRIENDLY = "friendly" ENTHUSIASTIC = "enthusiastic" MINIMALIST = "minimalist" EXPERT = "expert" @dataclass class PromptTemplate: template: str required_variables: List[str] optional_variables: List[str] output_format: str personality: PersonalityType class PromptEngineer: """Advanced prompt engineering for e-commerce recommendations""" def __init__(self): self.templates = self._initialize_templates() self.personality_traits = self._initialize_personalities() def create_recommendation_prompt(self, recommendation_type: RecommendationType, user_context: Dict[str, Any], products: List[Dict[str, Any]], personality: PersonalityType = PersonalityType.FRIENDLY, additional_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> str: """Create a comprehensive recommendation prompt""" template = self.templates[recommendation_type][personality] personality_traits = self.personality_traits[personality] # In this post, we've built an intelligent generation and personalization engine: ✅ Flexible LLM Integration: Support for OpenAI, Anthropic, and local models with fallback ✅ Advanced Prompt Engineering: Sophisticated prompts for different personalities and use cases ✅ Comprehensive Personalization: Multi-factor personalization with confidence scoring ✅ Explainable Recommendations: Clear reasoning and human-readable explanations ✅ Diversification Logic: Preventing echo chambers and ensuring variety

In our final post, we'll make it production-ready and continuously improving!

Docusaurus blogging features are powered by the blog plugin. Here are a few tips you might find useful. Simply add Markdown files (or folders) to the blog directory. Regular blog authors can be added to authors.yml. The blog post date can be extracted from filenames, such as: 2019-05-30-welcome.md 2019-05-30-welcome/index.md A blog post folder can be convenient to co-locate blog post images: The blog supports tags as well! And if you don't want a blog: just delete this directory, and use blog: false in your Docusaurus config.

This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know about using Google's Vertex AI platform with Gemini models for enterprise AI applications. Learn how to integrate powerful generative AI capabilities into your applications using the Google Gen AI SDK.
documents.s: Getting Started with Vertex AI and Gemini Models

documents.t: The Google Gen AI SDK provides a unified interface to Google's generative AI API services, including the powerful Gemini models. This SDK simplifies the process of integrating generative AI capabilities into applications and services, enabling developers to leverage Google's advanced AI models for various tasks.

Scalability: Built for production workloads with enterprise-grade infrastructure Security: Advanced security controls and compliance certifications Integration: Seamless integration with Google Cloud services Cost Efficiency: Flexible pricing models including batch processing options

Multimodal: Process text, images, audio, video, and PDFs in a single request Advanced Reasoning: State-of-the-art language understanding and generation Function Calling: Integrate with external APIs and tools Context Caching: Optimize costs for frequently used content Controlled Generation: Enforce structured output formats

Before you begin, ensure you have: Google Cloud Project: Create a project if you don't have one Vertex AI API: Enable the Vertex AI API Authentication: Set up Application Default Credentials Python Environment: Python 3.8 or higher
Install the required packages: pip install --upgrade google-genai pandas pillow requests

import datetime import os from google import genai from google.genai.types import ( CreateBatchJobConfig, CreateCachedContentConfig, EmbedContentConfig, FunctionDeclaration, GenerateContentConfig, HarmBlockThreshold, HarmCategory, Part, SafetySetting, Tool, )

# Set your Google Cloud project information PROJECT_ID = "your-project-id" LOCATION = "us-central1" # or your preferred region # Initialize the client for Vertex AI client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=PROJECT_ID, location=LOCATION) # Choose your model MODEL_ID = "gemini-2.5-flash" # Latest Gemini model

Generate responses to text prompts with simple API calls: def generate_text_response(prompt): """Generate a text response from Gemini.""" response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt ) return response.text # Example usage prompt = "Explain the benefits of using Vertex AI for enterprise applications." response = generate_text_response(prompt) print(response)

Process images, documents, and other media alongside text: from PIL import Image import requests def analyze_image_with_text(image_url, prompt): """Analyze an image with accompanying text prompt.""" # Load image from URL image = Image.open(requests.get(image_url, stream=True).raw) response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=[ image, prompt ] ) return response.text # Example: Analyze a business document image_url = "https://example.com/business-chart.png" prompt = "Analyze this business chart and provide key insights." analysis = analyze_image_with_text(image_url, prompt) print(analysis)

For production applications, process files directly from Google Cloud Storage: def process_cloud_storage_file(file_uri, mime_type, prompt): """Process files stored in Google Cloud Storage.""" response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=[ Part.from_uri( file_uri=file_uri, mime_type=mime_type ), prompt ] ) return response.text # Example: Process a PDF document file_uri = "gs://your-bucket/document.pdf" prompt = "Summarize the key points from this document." summary = process_cloud_storage_file(file_uri, "application/pdf", prompt) print(summary)

Guide model behavior with system instructions for consistent responses: def create_specialized_assistant(system_instruction, user_prompt): """Create a specialized AI assistant with specific instructions.""" response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=user_prompt, config=GenerateContentConfig( system_instruction=system_instruction, ) ) return response.text # Example: Create a code review assistant system_instruction = """ You are an expert software architect and code reviewer. Analyze code for: - Security vulnerabilities - Performance issues - Best practices compliance - Maintainability concerns Provide specific, actionable recommendations. """ user_prompt = "Review this Python function for potential issues: [code here]" review = create_specialized_assistant(system_instruction, user_prompt) print(review)

Fine-tune model behavior with generation parameters: def generate_with_parameters(prompt, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, top_k=40): """Generate content with specific parameters for control.""" response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt, config=GenerateContentConfig( temperature=temperature, # Creativity (0.0-1.0) top_p=top_p, # Nucleus sampling top_k=top_k, # Top-k sampling candidate_count=1, # Number of responses max_output_tokens=1024, # Response length limit ) ) return response.text # Example: Generate creative content creative_prompt = "Write a story about AI in the future." story = generate_with_parameters(creative_prompt, temperature=0.9) # Example: Generate factual content factual_prompt = "List the steps to implement OAuth 2.0." steps = generate_with_parameters(factual_prompt, temperature=0.1)

Configure safety settings for enterprise applications: def generate_with_safety_controls(prompt): """Generate content with enterprise-grade safety controls.""" safety_settings = [ SafetySetting( category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT, threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE, ), SafetySetting( category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT, threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE, ), SafetySetting( category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH, threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE, ), SafetySetting( category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT, threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE, ), ] response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt, config=GenerateContentConfig( safety_settings=safety_settings, ) ) # Check safety ratings safety_ratings = response.candidates[0].safety_ratings print(f"Safety ratings: {safety_ratings}") return response.text

Create interactive chat experiences: class GeminiChatBot: def __init__(self, system_instruction="You are a helpful AI assistant."): self.chat = client.chats.create( model=MODEL_ID, config=GenerateContentConfig( system_instruction=system_instruction, temperature=0.7, ) ) def send_message(self, message): """Send a message and get response.""" response = self.chat.send_message(message) return response.text def get_history(self): """Get conversation history.""" return self.chat.history # Example: Create a coding assistant coding_assistant = GeminiChatBot( "You are an expert software developer specializing in cloud applications." ) response1 = coding_assistant.send_message("How do I deploy a Python app to Google Cloud Run?") response2 = coding_assistant.send_message("What about environment variables?") response3 = coding_assistant.send_message("Show me a Dockerfile example.")

Force the model to return structured data: from pydantic import BaseModel import json class ProductAnalysis(BaseModel): product_name: str category: str pros: list[str] cons: list[str] rating: float recommendation: str def analyze_product_structured(product_description): """Analyze a product and return structured data.""" response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=f"Analyze this product: {product_description}", config=GenerateContentConfig( response_mime_type="application/json", response_schema=ProductAnalysis, ) ) # Parse JSON response return json.loads(response.text) # Example usage product = "iPhone 15 Pro - Latest smartphone with advanced camera system" analysis = analyze_product_structured(product) print(json.dumps(analysis, indent=2))

Integrate external APIs and tools: # Define a function for the model to call def create_weather_function(): """Create a function declaration for weather data.""" return FunctionDeclaration( name="get_weather", description="Get current weather information for a location", parameters={ "type": "OBJECT", "properties": { "location": { "type": "STRING", "description": "City and country/state", }, "unit": { "type": "STRING", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "description": "Temperature unit", } }, "required": ["location"] }, ) def handle_function_calling(user_request): """Handle requests that might need function calling.""" weather_tool = Tool(function_declarations=[create_weather_function()]) response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=user_request, config=GenerateContentConfig( tools=[weather_tool], temperature=0, ) ) # Check if model wants to call a function if response.candidates[0].content.parts[0].function_call: function_call = response.candidates[0].content.parts[0].function_call print(f"Model wants to call: {function_call.name}") print(f"With arguments: {function_call.args}") # Here you would implement the actual API call # For this example, we'll simulate the response weather_data = { "temperature": 22, "condition": "sunny", "humidity": 65 } return weather_data return response.text # Example usage request = "What's the weather like in San Francisco?" result = handle_function_calling(request)

Optimize costs by caching frequently used content: def create_document_cache(documents): """Create a cache for frequently referenced documents.""" # Prepare document parts pdf_parts = [ Part.from_uri( file_uri=doc_uri, mime_type="application/pdf" ) for doc_uri in documents ] # Create cache cached_content = client.caches.create( model="gemini-2.5-flash", config=CreateCachedContentConfig( system_instruction="You are an expert document analyst.", contents=pdf_parts, ttl="3600s", # 1 hour cache ) ) return cached_content def query_cached_documents(cached_content, query): """Query documents using cached content.""" response = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-2.5-flash", contents=query, config=GenerateContentConfig( cached_content=cached_content.name, ) ) return response.text # Example: Cache and query company documents documents = [ "gs://your-bucket/policy-doc1.pdf", "gs://your-bucket/policy-doc2.pdf" ] cache = create_document_cache(documents) answer = query_cached_documents(cache, "What is our remote work policy?") # Clean up cache when done client.caches.delete(name=cache.name)

Process large volumes of requests efficiently: import time def create_batch_job(input_data_uri, output_bucket): """Create a batch processing job for large-scale inference.""" batch_job = client.batches.create( model=MODEL_ID, src=input_data_uri, # JSONL file in Cloud Storage config=CreateBatchJobConfig(dest=output_bucket), ) return batch_job def wait_for_batch_completion(batch_job): """Wait for batch job to complete.""" while batch_job.state == "JOB_STATE_RUNNING": print("Batch job still running...") time.sleep(30) batch_job = client.batches.get(name=batch_job.name) if batch_job.state == "JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED": print("Batch job completed successfully!") return batch_job.dest.gcs_uri else: print(f"Batch job failed: {batch_job.error}") return None # Example: Process thousands of customer reviews input_data = "gs://your-bucket/customer-reviews.jsonl" output_bucket = "gs://your-bucket/batch-results/" batch_job = create_batch_job(input_data, output_bucket) results_location = wait_for_batch_completion(batch_job)

Generate embeddings for semantic search and retrieval: def generate_embeddings(texts, output_dim=768): """Generate embeddings for a list of texts.""" response = client.models.embed_content( model="gemini-embedding-001", contents=texts, config=EmbedContentConfig(output_dimensionality=output_dim) ) return response.embeddings def build_knowledge_base(documents): """Build a searchable knowledge base using embeddings.""" # Generate embeddings for all documents embeddings = generate_embeddings(documents) # Store embeddings with metadata knowledge_base = [] for i, (doc, embedding) in enumerate(zip(documents, embeddings)): knowledge_base.append({ "id": i, "text": doc, "embedding": embedding.values }) return knowledge_base # Example: Create a FAQ search system faq_documents = [ "How do I reset my password?", "What are your business hours?", "How do I contact customer support?", "What is your return policy?" ] knowledge_base = build_knowledge_base(faq_documents)

import time from google.api_core import exceptions def resilient_generate_content(prompt, max_retries=3): """Generate content with error handling and retries.""" for attempt in range(max_retries): try: response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt ) return response.text except exceptions.ResourceExhausted: # Rate limit exceeded wait_time = (2 ** attempt) + 1 print(f"Rate limit hit. Waiting {wait_time}s before retry...") time.sleep(wait_time) except exceptions.InvalidArgument as e: print(f"Invalid request: {e}") break except Exception as e: print(f"Unexpected error on attempt {attempt + 1}: {e}") if attempt == max_retries - 1: raise return None

def cost_efficient_generation(prompt, use_cache=True): """Generate content with cost optimization strategies.""" config = GenerateContentConfig( # Use lower cost settings for non-critical tasks temperature=0.3, max_output_tokens=512, # Limit output length candidate_count=1, # Single response ) if use_cache: # Implement your caching logic here pass response = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-2.5-flash", # Use cost-effective model contents=prompt, config=config ) return response.text

import logging from datetime import datetime # Configure logging logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) def monitored_generation(prompt, user_id=None): """Generate content with monitoring and logging.""" start_time = datetime.now() try: response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt ) # Log successful request duration = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds() logger.info(f"Generation successful - User: {user_id}, Duration: {duration}s") return response.text except Exception as e: # Log error logger.error(f"Generation failed - User: {user_id}, Error: {str(e)}") raise

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify app = Flask(__name__) @app.route('/api/generate', methods=['POST']) def api_generate(): """API endpoint for text generation.""" try: data = request.json prompt = data.get('prompt') if not prompt: return jsonify({'error': 'Prompt is required'}), 400 response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt ) return jsonify({ 'response': response.text, 'model': MODEL_ID, 'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat() }) except Exception as e: return jsonify({'error': str(e)}), 500 if __name__ == '__main__': app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080)

class GeminiService: """Service class for Gemini operations.""" def __init__(self, project_id, location="us-central1"): self.client = genai.Client( vertexai=True, project=project_id, location=location ) self.model_id = "gemini-2.5-flash" async def generate_async(self, prompt): """Asynchronous content generation.""" # Implement async generation logic pass def generate_with_validation(self, prompt, expected_format=None): """Generate content with output validation.""" response = self.client.models.generate_content( model=self.model_id, contents=prompt ) # Validate response format if specified if expected_format: # Implement validation logic pass return response.text def health_check(self): """Service health check.""" try: self.client.models.generate_content( model=self.model_id, contents="Health check" ) return True except: return False

def secure_generation(prompt, user_id): """Generate content with privacy safeguards.""" # Remove or mask PII from prompts cleaned_prompt = remove_pii(prompt) response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=cleaned_prompt, config=GenerateContentConfig( # Enable safety filters safety_settings=[ SafetySetting( category=HarmCategory.HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT, threshold=HarmBlockThreshold.BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE, ) ] ) ) # Log access for audit trail log_api_access(user_id, "generation", datetime.now()) return response.text def remove_pii(text): """Remove personally identifiable information.""" # Implement PII detection and removal return text def log_api_access(user_id, action, timestamp): """Log API access for compliance.""" # Implement audit logging pass

from functools import wraps def require_auth(f): """Decorator for API authentication.""" @wraps(f) def decorated_function(*args, **kwargs): # Implement authentication logic token = request.headers.get('Authorization') if not validate_token(token): return jsonify({'error': 'Unauthorized'}), 401 return f(*args, **kwargs) return decorated_function def validate_token(token): """Validate authentication token.""" # Implement token validation return True @app.route('/api/secure-generate', methods=['POST']) @require_auth def secure_generate_endpoint(): """Secured generation endpoint.""" # Implementation here pass

import threading class GeminiClientPool: """Connection pool for Gemini clients.""" def __init__(self, project_id, location, pool_size=5): self.clients = [] self.lock = threading.Lock() for _ in range(pool_size): client = genai.Client( vertexai=True, project=project_id, location=location ) self.clients.append(client) def get_client(self): """Get an available client from the pool.""" with self.lock: if self.clients: return self.clients.pop() else: # Create new client if pool is empty return genai.Client(vertexai=True) def return_client(self, client): """Return client to the pool.""" with self.lock: self.clients.append(client)

import redis import json import hashlib class ResponseCache: """Redis-based cache for API responses.""" def __init__(self, redis_host='localhost', redis_port=6379): self.redis_client = redis.Redis(host=redis_host, port=redis_port) self.ttl = 3600 # 1 hour def get_cache_key(self, prompt, model_id): """Generate cache key for prompt.""" content = f"{prompt}:{model_id}" return hashlib.md5(content.encode()).hexdigest() def get(self, prompt, model_id): """Get cached response.""" key = self.get_cache_key(prompt, model_id) cached = self.redis_client.get(key) return json.loads(cached) if cached else None def set(self, prompt, model_id, response): """Cache response.""" key = self.get_cache_key(prompt, model_id) self.redis_client.setex( key, self.ttl, json.dumps(response) ) # Usage with cache cache = ResponseCache() def cached_generation(prompt): """Generate content with caching.""" # Check cache first cached_response = cache.get(prompt, MODEL_ID) if cached_response: return cached_response['text'] # Generate new response response = client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents=prompt ) # Cache the response cache.set(prompt, MODEL_ID, {'text': response.text}) return response.text

# Dockerfile FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app # Install dependencies COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt # Copy application code COPY . . # Set environment variables ENV PYTHONPATH=/app ENV GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-project-id # Health check HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \ CMD python health_check.py EXPOSE 8080 CMD ["python", "main.py"]

# k8s/deployment.yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: gemini-service spec: replicas: 3 selector: matchLabels: app: gemini-service template: metadata: labels: app: gemini-service spec: containers: - name: gemini-service image: gcr.io/your-project/gemini-service:latest ports: - containerPort: 8080 env: - name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT value: "your-project-id" - name: LOCATION value: "us-central1" resources: requests: memory: "512Mi" cpu: "250m" limits: memory: "1Gi" cpu: "500m" livenessProbe: httpGet: path: /health port: 8080 initialDelaySeconds: 30 periodSeconds: 10 readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /ready port: 8080 initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 5

# terraform/main.tf resource "google_project_service" "vertex_ai" { project = var.project_id service = "aiplatform.googleapis.com" } resource "google_service_account" "gemini_service" { account_id = "gemini-service" display_name = "Gemini Service Account" project = var.project_id } resource "google_project_iam_member" "gemini_ai_user" { project = var.project_id role = "roles/aiplatform.user" member = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.gemini_service.email}" } resource "google_cloud_run_service" "gemini_api" { name = "gemini-api" location = var.region project = var.project_id template { spec { containers { image = "gcr.io/${var.project_id}/gemini-service:latest" env { name = "GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT" value = var.project_id } resources { limits = { cpu = "2000m" memory = "2Gi" } } } service_account_name = google_service_account.gemini_service.email } } traffic { percent = 100 latest_revision = true } }

from google.cloud import monitoring_v3 from google.cloud import logging def setup_monitoring(): """Set up monitoring and logging.""" # Initialize Cloud Monitoring monitoring_client = monitoring_v3.MetricServiceClient() # Initialize Cloud Logging logging_client = logging.Client() logging_client.setup_logging() return monitoring_client, logging_client def track_generation_metrics(duration, tokens_used, model_id): """Track generation metrics.""" # Send custom metrics to Cloud Monitoring monitoring_client, _ = setup_monitoring() # Create metric data series = monitoring_v3.TimeSeries() series.metric.type = "custom.googleapis.com/gemini/generation_duration" series.resource.type = "global" point = monitoring_v3.Point() point.value.double_value = duration point.interval.end_time.seconds = int(time.time()) series.points = [point] # Send to monitoring project_name = f"projects/{PROJECT_ID}" monitoring_client.create_time_series( name=project_name, time_series=[series] )

def health_check(): """Comprehensive health check.""" checks = { "vertex_ai": check_vertex_ai_connection(), "model_availability": check_model_availability(), "cache": check_cache_connection(), "dependencies": check_dependencies() } all_healthy = all(checks.values()) return { "status": "healthy" if all_healthy else "unhealthy", "checks": checks, "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat() } def check_vertex_ai_connection(): """Check Vertex AI connectivity.""" try: client.models.generate_content( model=MODEL_ID, contents="health check" ) return True except: return False

Vertex AI with Gemini models provides a powerful platform for building enterprise AI applications. Key benefits include: Unified API: Single interface for all AI capabilities Multimodal Processing: Handle text, images, audio, and video Enterprise Features: Security, compliance, and scalability Cost Optimization: Caching, batching, and efficient processing Production Ready: Monitoring, logging, and deployment tools

Explore Advanced Features: Dive deeper into function calling and agent patterns Build Production Applications: Implement monitoring and security best practices Optimize Performance: Use caching and batch processing for scale Integrate with Workflows: Connect with existing business processes Stay Updated: Follow Google Cloud AI documentation for latest features For more examples and advanced use cases, visit the Google Cloud Generative AI GitHub repository.

Get list of users (Admin only). Query Parameters: page (number): Page number (default: 1) limit (number): Items per page (default: 10) search (string): Search query Response: { "users": [ { "id": "uuid", "email": "user@example.com", "name": "User Name", "role": "user", "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" } ], "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 100, "totalPages": 10 } }

Get calendar events. Query Parameters: start (string): Start date (ISO 8601) end (string): End date (ISO 8601) category (string): Event category filter Response: { "events": [ { "id": "uuid", "title": "Meeting", "description": "Team sync", "start": "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z", "end": "2024-01-01T11:00:00Z", "category": "meeting", "recurring": { "type": "weekly", "interval": 1, "end_date": "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z" } } ] }

Get library books with search and filtering. Query Parameters: q (string): Search query author (string): Filter by author category (string): Filter by category page (number): Page number limit (number): Items per page Response: { "books": [ { "id": "uuid", "title": "Book Title", "author": "Author Name", "isbn": "978-0000000000", "category": "Technology", "description": "Book description", "cover_url": "https://example.com/cover.jpg", "available": true, "rating": 4.5, "reviews_count": 10 } ], "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 100, "totalPages": 10 }, "facets": { "categories": [ {"name": "Technology", "count": 25}, {"name": "Science", "count": 15} ], "authors": [ {"name": "Author Name", "count": 5} ] } }

Global search across all content types. Query Parameters: q (string): Search query (required) types (string): Comma-separated content types (books,events,users) page (number): Page number limit (number): Items per page Response: { "results": [ { "type": "book", "id": "uuid", "title": "Matching Book", "highlight": "Highlighted text...", "score": 0.95 }, { "type": "event", "id": "uuid", "title": "Matching Event", "highlight": "Highlighted text...", "score": 0.87 } ], "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 25, "totalPages": 3 }, "facets": { "types": [ {"name": "books", "count": 15}, {"name": "events", "count": 10} ] } }

Get search suggestions for auto-complete. Query Parameters: q (string): Partial search query limit (number): Number of suggestions (default: 5) Response: { "suggestions": [ "JavaScript fundamentals", "JavaScript frameworks", "JavaScript testing" ] }

Response: { "status": "ok", "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "services": { "supabase": { "status": "ok", "response_time": 45, "last_check": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }, "elasticsearch": { "status": "ok", "response_time": 23, "last_check": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }, "redis": { "status": "ok", "response_time": 12, "last_check": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" } } }
All APIs return consistent error responses:

APIs are rate-limited to prevent abuse: Authentication endpoints: 5 requests per minute per IP Search endpoints: 100 requests per minute per user General APIs: 1000 requests per hour per user Rate limit headers are included in responses: X-RateLimit-Limit: 100 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1640995200

Most endpoints require authentication via Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token> Some endpoints require specific roles: Admin only: User management, system configuration Moderator: Content moderation, user support User: Personal data access, content creation

List endpoints support pagination with consistent parameters: page: Page number (1-based, default: 1) limit: Items per page (max: 100, default: 10) Pagination info is included in responses: { "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 150, "totalPages": 15, "hasNext": true, "hasPrev": false } }
Real-time updates are available via WebSocket connection at /api/ws.

This document provides a comprehensive overview of the Next.js for Production application architecture, following modern best practices and design patterns.

src/ ├── app/ # Next.js App Router pages and layouts ├── components/ # UI Components (Atomic Design) │ ├── atoms/ # Basic building blocks (Button, Input, Label) │ ├── molecules/ # Grouped atoms (SearchBox, FormField) │ ├── organisms/ # Complex UI structures (Header, Sidebar) │ └── templates/ # Page layouts (AuthLayout, DashboardLayout) ├── entities/ # Business entities and domain models ├── features/ # Feature-based modules ├── hooks/ # Custom React hooks ├── i18n/ # Internationalization configuration ├── shared/ # Shared utilities and components ├── types/ # TypeScript type definitions └── utils/ # Utility functions and helpers

We follow Brad Frost's Atomic Design methodology: Atoms: Basic HTML elements and fundamental UI components Molecules: Groups of atoms that work together as functional units Organisms: Complex UI components composed of molecules and atoms Templates: Page-level objects that provide context for organisms Pages: Specific instances of templates with real content

Each major feature is organized as a self-contained module: features/ ├── auth/ │ ├── components/ │ ├── hooks/ │ ├── services/ │ └── types/ ├── calendar/ │ ├── components/ │ ├── hooks/ │ ├── services/ │ └── types/ └── library/ ├── components/ ├── hooks/ ├── services/ └── types/
