// tools/roadmap/roadmap-planner.ts import * as fs from 'fs'; import * as path from 'path'; import { parse } from 'yaml'; export interface RoadmapItem { id: string; title: string; description: string; category: 'infrastructure' | 'platform' | 'application' | 'security' | 'performance'; priority: 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'; effort: 'small' | 'medium' | 'large' | 'epic'; timeline: { startDate: Date; endDate: Date; milestones: Milestone[]; }; dependencies: string[]; risks: Risk[]; outcomes: string[]; owner: string; stakeholders: string[]; status: 'planned' | 'in-progress' | 'blocked' | 'completed' | 'cancelled'; technologies: string[]; impactAreas: string[]; } export interface Milestone { id: string; name: string; description: string; targetDate: Date; deliverables: string[]; successCriteria: string[]; dependencies: string[]; status: 'pending' | 'in-progress' | 'completed' | 'at-risk'; } export interface Risk { id: string; description: string; probability: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; impact: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; mitigation: string; owner: string; status: 'open' | 'mitigated' | 'closed'; } export interface Dependency { id: string; type: 'technical' | 'resource' | 'external' | 'business'; description: string; provider: string; status: 'pending' | 'in-progress' | 'resolved' | 'blocked'; criticalPath: boolean; } export class ArchitectureRoadmapManager { private roadmapItems: Map<string, RoadmapItem> = new Map(); private dependencies: Map<string, Dependency> = new Map(); constructor(private configPath: string = './config/roadmap.yaml') { this.loadRoadmap(); } async createRoadmapItem(item: Omit<RoadmapItem, 'id'>): Promise<string> { const id = this.generateItemId(item.category, item.title); const roadmapItem: RoadmapItem = { ...item, id, }; this.roadmapItems.set(id, roadmapItem); await this.saveRoadmap(); await this.validateDependencies(roadmapItem); return id; } async updateItemStatus(itemId: string, status: RoadmapItem['status'], notes?: string): Promise<void> { const item = this.roadmapItems.get(itemId); if (!item) { throw new Error(`Roadmap item ${itemId} not found`); } item.status = status; // Log status change await this.logStatusChange(itemId, status, notes); // Check for dependent items if (status === 'completed') { await this.checkDependentItems(itemId); } await this.saveRoadmap(); } async generateRoadmapReport(): Promise<{ summary: any; timeline: any[]; risks: Risk[]; dependencies: Dependency[]; }> { const items = Array.from(this.roadmapItems.values()); const summary = { totalItems: items.length, byStatus: this.groupByStatus(items), byPriority: this.groupByPriority(items), byCategory: this.groupByCategory(items), completionRate: this.calculateCompletionRate(items), }; const timeline = this.generateTimeline(items); const risks = this.aggregateRisks(items); const dependencies = Array.from(this.dependencies.values()); return { summary, timeline, risks, dependencies, }; } async identifyBottlenecks(): Promise<{ criticalPath: string[]; resourceConstraints: any[]; dependencyBlocks: string[]; }> { const items = Array.from(this.roadmapItems.values()); // Identify critical path const criticalPath = this.calculateCriticalPath(items); // Identify resource constraints const resourceConstraints = this.analyzeResourceConstraints(items); // Identify dependency blocks const dependencyBlocks = this.findDependencyBlocks(); return { criticalPath, resourceConstraints, dependencyBlocks, }; } private generateItemId(category: string, title: string): string { const sanitized = title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '-'); return `${category}-${sanitized}-${Date.now()}`; } private async validateDependencies(item: RoadmapItem): Promise<void> { for (const depId of item.dependencies) { const dependency = this.roadmapItems.get(depId); if (!dependency) { console.warn(`Dependency ${depId} not found for item ${item.id}`); } else if (dependency.timeline.endDate > item.timeline.startDate) { console.warn(`Potential timeline conflict: ${depId} ends after ${item.id} starts`); } } } private groupByStatus(items: RoadmapItem[]) { return items.reduce((acc, item) => { acc[item.status] = (acc[item.status] || 0) + 1; return acc; }, {} as Record<string, number>); } private groupByPriority(items: RoadmapItem[]) { return items.reduce((acc, item) => { acc[item.priority] = (acc[item.priority] || 0) + 1; return acc; }, {} as Record<string, number>); } private groupByCategory(items: RoadmapItem[]) { return items.reduce((acc, item) => { acc[item.category] = (acc[item.category] || 0) + 1; return acc; }, {} as Record<string, number>); } private calculateCompletionRate(items: RoadmapItem[]): number { const completed = items.filter(item => item.status === 'completed').length; return items.length > 0 ? (completed / items.length) * 100 : 0; } private generateTimeline(items: RoadmapItem[]): any[] { return items .sort((a, b) => a.timeline.startDate.getTime() - b.timeline.startDate.getTime()) .map(item => ({ id: item.id, title: item.title, start: item.timeline.startDate, end: item.timeline.endDate, status: item.status, priority: item.priority, milestones: item.timeline.milestones, })); } private aggregateRisks(items: RoadmapItem[]): Risk[] { const allRisks: Risk[] = []; for (const item of items) { allRisks.push(...item.risks); } // Sort by impact and probability return allRisks.sort((a, b) => { const impactWeight = { high: 3, medium: 2, low: 1 }; const probWeight = { high: 3, medium: 2, low: 1 }; const aScore = impactWeight[a.impact] * probWeight[a.probability]; const bScore = impactWeight[b.impact] * probWeight[b.probability]; return bScore - aScore; }); } private calculateCriticalPath(items: RoadmapItem[]): string[] { // Simplified critical path calculation const sortedItems = items .filter(item => item.status !== 'completed' && item.status !== 'cancelled') .sort((a, b) => { // Sort by priority and dependencies const priorityWeight = { critical: 4, high: 3, medium: 2, low: 1 }; return priorityWeight[b.priority] - priorityWeight[a.priority]; }); return sortedItems.slice(0, 5).map(item => item.id); } private analyzeResourceConstraints(items: RoadmapItem[]): any[] { const resourceMap = new Map<string, string[]>(); for (const item of items) { if (item.status === 'in-progress' || item.status === 'planned') { if (!resourceMap.has(item.owner)) { resourceMap.set(item.owner, []); } resourceMap.get(item.owner)!.push(item.id); } } return Array.from(resourceMap.entries()) .filter(([_, itemIds]) => itemIds.length > 2) .map(([owner, itemIds]) => ({ owner, overcommitedItems: itemIds })); } private findDependencyBlocks(): string[] { const blockedItems: string[] = []; for (const [itemId, item] of this.roadmapItems) { if (item.status === 'blocked') { blockedItems.push(itemId); } } return blockedItems; } private async logStatusChange(itemId: string, status: string, notes?: string): Promise<void> { const logEntry = { timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), itemId, status, notes, }; // Log to file or monitoring system console.log(`Roadmap item ${itemId} status changed to ${status}`); } private async checkDependentItems(completedItemId: string): Promise<void> { for (const [itemId, item] of this.roadmapItems) { if (item.dependencies.includes(completedItemId) && item.status === 'planned') { const allDependenciesCompleted = item.dependencies.every(depId => { const dep = this.roadmapItems.get(depId); return dep?.status === 'completed'; }); if (allDependenciesCompleted) { console.log(`Item ${itemId} is ready to start - all dependencies completed`); } } } } private async loadRoadmap(): Promise<void> { try { const content = fs.readFileSync(this.configPath, 'utf8'); const data = parse(content); if (data.roadmapItems) { for (const item of data.roadmapItems) { this.roadmapItems.set(item.id, { ...item, timeline: { ...item.timeline, startDate: new Date(item.timeline.startDate), endDate: new Date(item.timeline.endDate), }, }); } } } catch (error) { console.log('No existing roadmap found, starting fresh'); } } private async saveRoadmap(): Promise<void> { const data = { roadmapItems: Array.from(this.roadmapItems.values()), dependencies: Array.from(this.dependencies.values()), lastUpdated: new Date().toISOString(), }; const dir = path.dirname(this.configPath); if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) { fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); } fs.writeFileSync(this.configPath, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)); } }

This guide provides comprehensive strategies for managing technical debt in software development projects.
Technical debt refers to the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy (limited) solution now instead of using a better approach that would take longer.

Code Quality Issues: Legacy code, poor documentation, lack of tests Architecture Issues: Outdated frameworks, tight coupling, poor scalability Infrastructure Issues: Manual processes, outdated dependencies, security vulnerabilities Process Issues: Lack of automation, poor deployment processes

Technical Debt Ratio: Technical Debt / Total Development Cost Code Quality Metrics: Cyclomatic complexity, code coverage, duplication Maintenance Effort: Time spent on bug fixes vs. new features Performance Metrics: Response times, resource utilization

High Impact, High Effort: Plan for major refactoring initiatives High Impact, Low Effort: Address immediately in upcoming sprints Low Impact, High Effort: Consider for long-term roadmap Low Impact, Low Effort: Include in regular maintenance

Boy Scout Rule: Always leave code better than you found it Dedicated Debt Sprints: Allocate specific time for debt reduction Incremental Refactoring: Small, continuous improvements Architecture Evolution: Gradual migration to better patterns
SonarQube: Code quality and security analysis ESLint: JavaScript/TypeScript linting Prettier: Code formatting consistency Jest: Unit testing framework

Technical Debt Register: Centralized tracking of known issues Regular Architecture Reviews: Quarterly assessments Metrics Dashboard: Continuous monitoring of quality metrics Debt Burn-down Charts: Visual tracking of debt reduction

Make Debt Visible: Track and communicate debt regularly Set Quality Gates: Prevent new debt from being introduced Allocate Time: Dedicate percentage of capacity to debt reduction Document Decisions: Record architectural decisions and trade-offs Regular Refactoring: Include refactoring in development process
Conduct comprehensive code audit Identify and catalog technical debt Establish baseline metrics Create technical debt register
Implement code quality tools Set up monitoring dashboards Establish quality gates in CI/CD Train team on new processes
Allocate 20% of sprint capacity to debt reduction Conduct monthly debt review meetings Update technical debt register Monitor progress and adjust strategy

Reduced Bug Count: 30% reduction in production bugs Improved Velocity: 20% increase in feature delivery speed Better Maintainability: Reduced time for code changes Enhanced Code Quality: Improved SonarQube ratings

Architecture & Coding Guidance​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance SETUP 1 The SCM (Source Control Management) policy is defined and documented ...des branch strategy, naming conventions, commit message rules, PR policies, and merge processes How to achieve: Create a comprehensive SCM policy document covering: main branches (main, develop, feature/, hotfix/), branch naming conventions, commit message format (e.g., "feat: add user authentication"), PR templates, code review requirements, and merge strategies. Document in README.md, wiki, or shared documentation platform. 📖 Detailed Guide: SCM Policy for NestJS & Next.js SETUP 1 ... local environment are documented Complete list of required software, tools, and versions for developer environment setup How to achieve: Create a developer setup guide listing: Node.js version, package managers (npm/yarn/pnpm), IDE requirements, browser versions, database tools, CLI tools, and any custom scripts. Include installation instructions and troubleshooting steps. Use tools like .nvmrc, package.json engines field. 📖 Detailed Guide: Development Environment Setup SETUP 1 Coding practices, coding conventions are documented, explained and followed Comprehensive coding standards including unit testing practices and code examples How to achieve: Establish coding standards document with: naming conventions, file structure, design patterns, code formatting rules, unit testing guidelines, and practical examples. Use tools like ESLint, Prettier, SonarQube for enforcement. Provide code snippets and templates. 📖 Detailed Guide: Coding Standards & Conventions SETUP 1 There is a guide for special development use-cases Step-by-step guides for environment setup, custom tools, and configuration How to achieve: Create detailed guides for: local environment setup, environment variable configuration, custom tool usage, debugging procedures, and common troubleshooting. Include scripts for automation where possible. SETUP 1 There are tools for code style checking Automated code style verification tools integrated into development workflow How to achieve: Implement tools like ESLint (JavaScript), Prettier (formatting), SonarQube (quality), and integrate with git hooks using Husky. Configure pre-commit hooks to prevent non-compliant code from being committed. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Application architecture foundation is defined and documented Complete architecture documentation including layers, frameworks, and key mechanisms How to achieve: Create architecture documentation using C4 model or similar: Context diagrams, Container diagrams, Component diagrams. Document application layers (presentation, business, data), logging mechanisms, error handling, transaction control. Schedule architecture review sessions. 📖 Complete Implementation Guide: Application Architecture Foundation PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Backup/restore strategy for Production environment is documented Comprehensive backup and disaster recovery plan for production systems How to achieve: Document backup strategies for: databases (automated backups, point-in-time recovery), file systems, configuration data. Include RTO/RPO targets, restore procedures, testing schedules, and responsibilities. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Important 3rd party APIs, libraries, frameworks are documented Comprehensive inventory of external dependencies How to achieve: Maintain a dependency matrix listing: external APIs (authentication, payment, analytics), libraries and their versions, licensing information, support contacts, and integration patterns. Use tools like npm audit, OWASP dependency check. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 All user input data is validated in code Comprehensive input validation covering all data entry points How to achieve: Implement validation at multiple layers: client-side (UI feedback), server-side (security), database constraints. Handle null/empty values, validate data types, sanitize inputs, implement rate limiting. Use validation libraries like Joi, Yup, or built-in framework validators. SETUP 2 The rollback strategy is described in the SCM plan Detailed procedures for code and deployment rollbacks How to achieve: Extend SCM policy to include: rollback procedures for different environments, database rollback strategies, feature flag usage for quick disabling, automated rollback triggers, and communication protocols during rollbacks. Communication & Alignment​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance SETUP 1 All necessary KT meetings are planned with stakeholders Knowledge transfer sessions with third parties and stakeholders How to achieve: Schedule and plan: initial stakeholder meetings, third-party integration sessions, technical knowledge transfer meetings. Create agendas, invite all relevant technical and business stakeholders, document outcomes and action items. SETUP 1 Business & Technical communication channels are facilitated Effective communication channels for all project stakeholders How to achieve: Establish clear communication channels: Slack/Teams for daily communication, email for formal communications, video calls for complex discussions. Create dedicated channels for different purposes (alerts, general discussion, releases). DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 All development policies are communicated to the team Comprehensive communication of all technical standards and processes How to achieve: Conduct team meetings to present: SCM policies, coding standards, backup procedures, NFR targets, testing processes. Use multiple communication methods (meetings, documentation, chat), ensure acknowledgment and understanding. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Big technical solutions are communicated to stakeholders Architecture changes and major technical decisions are properly communicated How to achieve: Schedule stakeholder review meetings for major changes, use architecture diagrams for explanation, provide impact analysis, document decisions and rationale, follow up with written summaries. SETUP 1 Overall Architecture diagram is shared with all stakeholders Architecture visualization shared and explained to all project participants How to achieve: Create comprehensive architecture diagrams using C4 model, schedule presentation meetings with all stakeholders (development, business, third parties), maintain up-to-date documentation, establish change communication process. Non-functional Requirements​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance SETUP 1 All NFRs are mapped and collected Comprehensive identification and documentation of non-functional requirements How to achieve: Conduct NFR workshops with stakeholders, document requirements for: performance (response times, throughput), security (authentication, authorization), reliability (uptime, error rates), scalability (user load, data volume), usability. Get stakeholder approval. SETUP 2 NFRs are documented using standardized template Consistent NFR documentation format across the organization How to achieve: Use company-standard NFR template including: requirement ID, priority, measurable criteria, testing approach, acceptance criteria. If no template exists, create one covering all NFR categories. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 NFRs are approved by stakeholders Official stakeholder approval for all non-functional requirements How to achieve: Present NFRs to stakeholders in formal review sessions, document approvals with signatures/confirmations, maintain approval audit trail, communicate scope implications of approved NFRs. SETUP 4 There are targets for NFR metrics Specific, measurable targets defined for all NFR areas How to achieve: Define SMART targets: response time < 2 seconds, 99.9% uptime, support for 10,000 concurrent users. Establish baselines, set improvement targets, align with business objectives. Technical Refinement & Design​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Business stories are split into small testable features User stories broken down into manageable, deployable components How to achieve: Apply story splitting techniques: split by data, operations, user roles, or acceptance criteria. Ensure each story is independently testable and deployable. Use INVEST criteria (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable). SETUP 1 Technologies are well-established and supported Use of mature, widely-adopted technologies with proper support How to achieve: Evaluate technologies based on: community adoption, long-term support, documentation quality, enterprise support availability. Avoid alpha/beta versions unless widely adopted. Consult with architecture team for decisions. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Technical documentation is updated during development Keep technical documentation current with code changes How to achieve: Include documentation updates in definition of done, assign documentation reviews as part of PR process, use automated documentation generation where possible, schedule regular documentation review sessions. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Technical refinement finishes on time following Heijunka Technical preparation completed one sprint ahead using leveling principles How to achieve: Plan technical refinement sessions one sprint ahead, create detailed technical guidance documents, involve PO/PPO in refinement, apply workload leveling to avoid bottlenecks, track refinement completion metrics. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 4 Technical refinement is well-structured and understood High-quality technical guidance with minimal blocking issues How to achieve: Develop standardized refinement templates, gather feedback from development team, apply continuous improvement based on blocking incidents, include detailed technical specifications and decision rationale.

Continuous Deployment​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Artifact versions are trackable across environments Clear versioning and tracking of deployments How to achieve: Implement semantic versioning (semver), use build numbers, tag releases in git, maintain deployment logs showing version deployments to each environment, use tools like GitOps for tracking. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Environment-specific configurations are externalized Configuration managed outside deployment packages How to achieve: Use environment variables for all environment-specific settings (API endpoints, database connections, feature flags), implement configuration management tools (Kubernetes ConfigMaps, AWS Parameter Store), never hard-code environment-specific values. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Deployment to dev/test environments is automated Automated deployment pipelines for non-production environments How to achieve: Set up CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Actions, implement automated deployment triggers on successful builds, ensure zero-manual-step deployments to dev/test environments. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Database changes are deployable via scripts Automated database schema and data migration How to achieve: Use database migration tools (Flyway, Liquibase, Entity Framework migrations), version control all database changes, implement rollback capabilities, test migrations in non-production environments first. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Code and database rollback is possible Comprehensive rollback strategy for both application and data How to achieve: Implement blue-green or canary deployment strategies, maintain database backup points before deployments, create automated rollback scripts, test rollback procedures regularly. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 Pre-production deployment is automated Full automation for staging/UAT environment deployments How to achieve: Extend CI/CD pipelines to include pre-production environments, implement approval gates where needed, ensure consistent deployment process across all environments. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 Production deployment is single-click Simplified production deployment process How to achieve: Implement one-click deployment with proper approval workflows, use deployment automation tools, ensure all manual steps are eliminated or automated, maintain audit trails. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 Production rollback is single-click Simplified production rollback capability How to achieve: Implement automated rollback procedures, maintain previous version availability, use feature flags for quick disabling, ensure rollback testing is part of deployment strategy. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 4 Deployment status verifiable via smoke tests Automated verification of deployment success How to achieve: Create automated smoke test suites covering critical user journeys, integrate smoke tests into deployment pipeline, implement health check endpoints, set up monitoring alerts for deployment verification. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Same package promoted across environments Build once, deploy anywhere principle How to achieve: Use immutable artifacts (Docker images, compiled packages), promote same binary across environments, use configuration injection for environment differences, implement artifact repositories. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Lead time is no longer than one sprint Fast delivery from development to production How to achieve: Optimize CI/CD pipeline performance, implement continuous deployment practices, reduce approval bottlenecks, automate testing and quality gates, measure and improve deployment frequency. Continuous Integration​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Source control tool is used efficiently Effective use of version control systems How to achieve: Train team on Git best practices, establish branching strategies (GitFlow, GitHub Flow), implement code review processes, use meaningful commit messages, avoid direct commits to main branches. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Commit messages contain ticket information Traceability between code changes and business requirements How to achieve: Establish commit message standards including ticket numbers, use commit message templates, implement git hooks to enforce format, integrate with issue tracking systems (JIRA, GitHub Issues). DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Merge requests contain informative descriptions Clear context for code review and change tracking How to achieve: Create PR templates including: description of changes, related tickets, testing performed, breaking changes. Require reviewer approval, link to relevant documentation. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Separated environments for dev/test/production Proper environment isolation and management How to achieve: Set up dedicated environments with separate databases, implement environment-specific configurations, ensure proper access controls, document environment purposes and promotion paths. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Local environment setup is not complicated Simplified developer onboarding and environment setup How to achieve: Create setup scripts, use containerization (Docker), provide one-command setup, document troubleshooting steps, consider development environment as code (Dev Containers, Vagrant). PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Dependency management tools are used Proper management of third-party libraries How to achieve: Use package managers (npm, Maven, NuGet), version control dependency files (package.json, pom.xml), implement dependency scanning, exclude node_modules/vendor folders from source control. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Build process is automated Elimination of manual build steps How to achieve: Create automated build scripts, use build tools (webpack, Maven, MSBuild), implement CI/CD pipelines, ensure builds are reproducible and environment-independent. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Branches are synchronized regularly Frequent integration to prevent merge conflicts How to achieve: Establish branch synchronization practices, merge main branch regularly, use feature flags for incomplete features, encourage frequent small commits rather than large changes. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Team commits runnable code frequently Regular integration of working code How to achieve: Encourage daily commits of working code, implement local testing before commits, use feature flags for incomplete features, establish "definition of done" for commits. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Complex merges are avoided Prevention of large, complex code integrations How to achieve: Break large features into smaller increments, encourage frequent merging, use pair programming for complex changes, implement branch policies to limit change size. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Database schema is versioned Version control for database structure How to achieve: Use database migration tools, store schema files in version control, implement schema versioning strategy, automate schema deployments, maintain schema documentation. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 2 Database rollback is possible Capability to revert database changes How to achieve: Implement database backup strategies before deployments, create rollback scripts for migrations, test rollback procedures, use database versioning tools with rollback support. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Build status is visible and notifications are sent Team awareness of build health How to achieve: Set up build status dashboards, configure email/chat notifications for build failures, use status badges in repositories, ensure immediate feedback on build issues. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Build artifacts are generated from CI/CD server Centralized and automated build generation How to achieve: Set up CI/CD servers (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps), eliminate local builds for deployments, implement artifact repositories, ensure build reproducibility. 📖 Detailed Guide: CI/CD Pipeline Setup PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Build time is acceptable (< 15 minutes) Optimized build performance How to achieve: Optimize build scripts, implement parallel builds, use build caching, optimize dependencies, separate unit tests from build process if needed for time optimization. 📖 Detailed Guide: CI/CD Pipeline Optimization PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Build scripts use pipeline approach Infrastructure as code for build processes How to achieve: Use pipeline definition files (Jenkinsfile, GitHub Actions workflows, Azure Pipelines YAML), version control pipeline configurations, implement reusable pipeline components. 📖 Detailed Guide: Pipeline as Code PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 2 Merges trigger automated builds and tests Automated quality gates on code integration How to achieve: Configure webhooks for automatic build triggers, implement branch protection rules, run unit tests as part of build process, prevent merges if builds fail. 📖 Detailed Guide: Automated Testing Integration PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 GitOps - infrastructure as code is versioned Infrastructure configuration managed as code How to achieve: Use tools like Terraform, CloudFormation, or Kubernetes manifests, version control all infrastructure definitions, implement infrastructure change approval processes. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 Logs are centralized for all environments Unified logging and monitoring solution How to achieve: Implement centralized logging (ELK stack, Splunk, CloudWatch), ensure all applications and infrastructure log to central system, implement log retention policies. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 4 Server configuration changes use scripts Automated configuration management How to achieve: Use configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet, Chef), eliminate manual configuration changes, implement infrastructure as code practices, use immutable infrastructure where possible. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 New environment creation is automated Fully automated environment provisioning How to achieve: Create environment provisioning scripts, use cloud automation tools, implement environment templates, ensure consistent environment configurations. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 4 Auto-scaling capabilities are implemented Automatic resource scaling based on demand How to achieve: Configure auto-scaling groups, implement horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA) in Kubernetes, set up monitoring-based scaling triggers, test scaling scenarios. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Immutable infrastructure - environments are never changed Complete automation of environment lifecycle How to achieve: Implement immutable infrastructure patterns, use containerization, recreate rather than modify environments, automate entire environment lifecycle through pipelines. Continuous Monitoring​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance RELEASE 1 Production infrastructure monitoring with responsible team Basic infrastructure health monitoring How to achieve: Implement monitoring for CPU, memory, disk usage, network performance. Set up alerting for threshold breaches. Assign responsibility to specific team members for monitoring and response. Use tools like Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch. RELEASE 1 Production application monitoring with responsible team Application-level health and performance monitoring How to achieve: Monitor critical business flows, API response times, error rates, user authentication, registration processes. Set up application performance monitoring (APM) tools like New Relic, Datadog, or Application Insights. RELEASE 2 Infrastructure metrics monitoring with notifications Enhanced infrastructure monitoring with alerting How to achieve: Expand monitoring to include response times, detailed performance metrics. Implement intelligent alerting to reduce noise. Ensure proper escalation procedures and response time SLAs. RELEASE 4 Infrastructure monitoring is visible to everyone Team-wide visibility of infrastructure health How to achieve: Create shared dashboards accessible to all team members, implement real-time monitoring displays, provide training on reading and interpreting metrics, ensure monitoring data is always current. RELEASE 4 Team can fix infrastructure monitoring issues Empowered team for infrastructure problem resolution How to achieve: Train development team on infrastructure components, provide access to infrastructure tools, implement runbooks for common issues, promote DevOps culture where developers handle operational concerns. RELEASE 4 Team can fix application monitoring issues Team ownership of application health and performance How to achieve: Ensure development team has access to production monitoring, create incident response procedures, implement automated remediation where possible, establish on-call rotations if needed. RELEASE 4 Business monitoring tools with responsible team Business metrics monitoring and tracking How to achieve: Implement business KPI monitoring (conversion rates, user activity, sales metrics), create business-focused dashboards, establish business metric SLAs, assign business stakeholder responsibility. RELEASE 4 Business monitoring is visible to everyone Team-wide visibility of business performance How to achieve: Share business metrics dashboards with entire team, correlate business metrics with technical metrics, provide context for how code changes affect business outcomes. RELEASE 5 Automated infrastructure issue resolution Self-healing infrastructure capabilities How to achieve: Implement auto-scaling for resource issues, automated restart procedures for failed services, intelligent alerting with automatic response capabilities, self-healing mechanisms for common infrastructure problems. RELEASE 5 Automated application issue resolution Self-healing application capabilities How to achieve: Implement circuit breakers for API failures, automated service restart for application issues, intelligent routing around failed services, automated rollback triggers for performance degradation.

People & Technical Skills Development​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance SETUP 1 Knowledge map of team technical skills exists Documented inventory of team capabilities and skill gaps How to achieve: Create skills assessment matrix covering: programming languages, frameworks, tools, methodologies, domain knowledge. Update quarterly, identify training needs, plan skill development activities, track skill progression over time. Project Plan & Architecture Roadmap​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance SETUP 1 Architecture roadmap with technical milestones exists Strategic plan for technical deliverables and milestones How to achieve: Create comprehensive roadmap including: major technical milestones, PoC timelines, security and performance testing schedules, deployment dates, technology upgrades. Align with business roadmap, update regularly. Risks & Blocks Management​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Architecture maturity PDCA meetings conducted monthly Regular architecture review and improvement meetings How to achieve: Schedule monthly PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) meetings, review maturity checklist progress, identify improvement actions, track action item completion, involve relevant stakeholders. RELEASE 1 Solution Review meetings for significant technical issues Collaborative technical problem-solving with peer architects How to achieve: Organize solution review meetings for complex technical decisions, invite architects from other projects, document solutions and decisions, create knowledge sharing culture. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 3 PDCA action plans are tracked in ticket system Systematic tracking of architecture improvement initiatives How to achieve: Create tickets in JIRA/Azure DevOps for all PDCA action items, assign owners and due dates, track progress in subsequent meetings, maintain improvement backlog. Technical Backlog Management​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Architecture backlog is managed with bi-weekly prioritization Systematic management of technical debt and improvements How to achieve: Maintain separate technical backlog for architectural tasks, prioritize bi-weekly, allocate architect time (50% refinement, 50% backlog), track technical debt metrics, plan technical tasks across sprints. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 4 Technical debts are monitored with improvement plans Proactive technical debt management How to achieve: Implement technical debt tracking tools (SonarQube), establish technical debt metrics, create regular debt review sessions, plan debt reduction sprints, communicate debt impact to stakeholders. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Team's architecture maturity is known company-wide Organization-wide knowledge sharing and scaling How to achieve: Share success stories through internal presentations, conduct architecture maturity workshops for other teams, create best practice documentation, mentor other projects, establish architecture community of practice.

Architecture Evaluation​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Code quality followed through documented code reviews Systematic code review process with quality standards How to achieve: Create code review checklist covering: security, performance, design patterns, coding standards. Train team on review process, establish review requirements for all PRs, use review tools integrated with source control. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 3 Code quality is visible with immediate feedback Real-time code quality monitoring and alerts How to achieve: Integrate quality gates in CI/CD pipeline, set up SonarQube or similar tools, configure quality alerts, make quality metrics visible to entire team via dashboards. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 3 Build fails if code quality goals not met Automated quality enforcement How to achieve: Configure build pipelines to fail on quality gate violations, set quality thresholds (code coverage, complexity, duplication), ensure no code can be deployed without meeting quality standards. Continuous Testing​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Application validated across different browsers/devices Cross-platform compatibility testing How to achieve: Define supported browser/device matrix, implement cross-browser testing protocols, use automated testing tools (Selenium, Playwright), establish device testing procedures, include compatibility testing in definition of done. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 3 Code coverage maintained without decreases Preventing regression in test coverage How to achieve: Set minimum code coverage thresholds (80%+), configure builds to fail on coverage decreases, require architect approval for coverage reductions, implement coverage reporting in CI/CD pipeline. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 3 Test cases updated with business logic changes Maintaining test relevance and accuracy How to achieve: Include test case review in story definition of done, update test cases as part of business logic changes, maintain traceability between requirements and tests, conduct regular test review sessions. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 3 Test coverage gaps converted to tracked defects Systematic approach to improving test coverage How to achieve: Regular coverage gap analysis, create improvement tasks in backlog, prioritize coverage improvements, assign ownership for coverage areas, track progress toward coverage targets. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 3 Automated testing integrated with failing builds Quality gates preventing deployment of untested code How to achieve: Integrate unit tests, integration tests into build pipeline, set minimum coverage requirements (80%+), ensure builds fail on test failures or insufficient coverage, implement automated test reporting. Non-functional Requirements Validation​ Phase Maturity Level Criteria Help Text Implementation Guidance DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Web forms protected with anti-spam mechanisms Security measures against automated abuse How to achieve: Implement CAPTCHA or equivalent anti-bot measures on all public forms, use rate limiting, implement form validation, consider honeypot techniques, monitor for spam patterns. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 CSS/JS files are compressed and images optimized Performance optimization for bandwidth usage How to achieve: Implement build-time minification for CSS/JS files, use image optimization tools, implement responsive images with multiple resolutions, use CDN for static assets, compress images for web delivery. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 1 Response headers for caching are implemented Proper HTTP caching strategies How to achieve: Implement appropriate cache-control headers, set proper ETags, configure browser caching policies, implement cache invalidation strategies, test caching behavior across different resource types. PREPARATION (Sprint 0) 1 Non-production environments are protected Security for development and testing environments How to achieve: Implement basic authentication, IP whitelisting, or VPN access for non-production environments, configure robots.txt to prevent search engine indexing, monitor access to non-production systems. RELEASE 1 Critical performance areas covered by performance testing Comprehensive performance validation How to achieve: Identify critical user journeys and business flows, implement performance testing for login, registration, core business processes, establish performance baselines, set performance targets. RELEASE 1 Performance tests executed periodically Regular performance validation How to achieve: Schedule performance tests for major releases, automate performance testing where possible, establish performance regression testing, document performance test results and trends. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 3 Solution Review meetings for complex architectures Peer review for architectural decisions How to achieve: Schedule architecture review sessions with external architects, document complex architectural decisions, seek input on challenging technical problems, create knowledge sharing opportunities. RELEASE 3 Performance test issues tracked as defects Systematic performance issue management How to achieve: Convert performance issues to trackable tickets, prioritize performance improvements, assign ownership for performance issues, track resolution progress and impact. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Developers deliver security test scripts as part of stories Integrated security testing approach How to achieve: Include security testing tasks in user story definitions, train developers on security testing, provide security testing tools and frameworks, establish security testing standards. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Security satisfaction recognized by stakeholders Transparent security metrics and reporting How to achieve: Implement automated security testing, create security dashboards, share security metrics with stakeholders, conduct regular security assessments, provide executive security reports. DEVELOPMENT (Sprint 1-N) 5 Developers deliver performance test scripts as part of stories Integrated performance testing approach How to achieve: Include performance testing in story definitions, provide performance testing tools (JMeter, LoadRunner), train developers on performance testing, establish performance testing standards. RELEASE 5 Performance satisfaction recognized by stakeholders Transparent performance metrics and reporting How to achieve: Implement automated performance monitoring, create performance dashboards, share performance metrics with stakeholders, conduct regular performance reviews, provide executive performance reports.

Documentation Coverage: % of required documentation completed Automation Level: % of manual processes automated Quality Metrics: Code coverage, defect rates, performance benchmarks Team Efficiency: Lead time, deployment frequency, recovery time Stakeholder Satisfaction: Regular feedback and approval ratings

Regular assessment and improvement through: Monthly PDCA meetings Quarterly maturity assessments Annual architecture reviews Continuous feedback collection Knowledge sharing sessions This assessment guide should be reviewed and updated regularly to reflect evolving best practices and organizational needs.
This document provides detailed action plans for achieving each architecture maturity criteria, specifically tailored for NestJS/Next.js projects deployed on GCP Kubernetes.
documents.s: Architecture Maturity Assessment - Comprehensive Action Plans

documents.t: Maturity Level 1 (Foundation)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan SETUP The SCM (Source Control Management) policy is defined and documented Complete Source Control Management policy covering branch strategy, naming conventions, commit rules, and PR policies 🎯 Action Plan: • Create SCM policy document covering: - Main branches: main, develop, feature/*, hotfix/* - Commit format: type(scope): description (e.g., feat(auth): add JWT authentication) - PR template with description, testing checklist, breaking changes - Code review requirements (minimum 2 approvals) • Set up branch protection rules in GitHub/GitLab • Configure conventional commits with commitlint • Document merge strategies (squash for features, merge for releases) • Store in README.md or dedicated CONTRIBUTING.md 📦 Tools: GitHub branch protection, commitlint, PR templates ⏱️ Timeline: 1-2 days 👥 Responsible: Technical Lead + DevOps Engineer SETUP All needed software and tools (include versions) for local environment are documented Complete developer environment setup guide with all required tools and versions 🎯 Action Plan: • Create comprehensive setup guide including: - Node.js version (use .nvmrc file) - Package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) with lock files - Database tools (Docker Compose for local DBs) - IDE extensions (ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript) - CLI tools (gcloud, kubectl, docker) • Create setup scripts for one-command installation • Use Dev Containers or Docker for consistent environments • Document troubleshooting common issues • Include environment variable templates 📦 Tools: .nvmrc, package.json engines, Docker Compose, Dev Containers ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: Senior Developer + DevOps Engineer SETUP Coding practices and conventions are documented and followed Comprehensive coding standards with unit testing guidelines and examples 🎯 Action Plan: • Establish coding standards document covering: - TypeScript/JavaScript style guide - Naming conventions (camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case) - File structure and organization - Design patterns (Repository, Factory, Strategy) - Unit testing guidelines with Jest/Vitest • Configure automated enforcement: - ESLint with TypeScript rules - Prettier for code formatting - Husky for pre-commit hooks • Create code snippets and templates • Provide practical examples for common patterns 📦 Tools: ESLint, Prettier, Husky, SonarQube ⏱️ Timeline: 3-4 days 👥 Responsible: Technical Lead + Senior Developers SETUP Guide for special development use-cases exists Step-by-step guides for environment setup, custom tools, and configurations 🎯 Action Plan: • Create detailed guides for: - Local environment setup with Docker - Environment variable configuration - Database setup and migrations - Custom tool usage (code generators, scripts) - Debugging procedures (VS Code, Chrome DevTools) - Troubleshooting common issues • Include automation scripts where possible • Create video tutorials for complex setups • Maintain FAQ section with solutions 📦 Tools: Documentation platform, screen recording tools ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: Senior Developer + Technical Writer SETUP Tools for code style checking are implemented Automated code quality and style verification integrated into workflow 🎯 Action Plan: • Set up code quality toolchain: - ESLint with TypeScript and React rules - Prettier for consistent formatting - SonarQube for code quality metrics - Husky for git hooks enforcement • Configure pre-commit hooks to prevent non-compliant code • Integrate with CI/CD pipeline for automated checks • Set up IDE integration for real-time feedback • Configure quality gates in build process 📦 Tools: ESLint, Prettier, SonarQube, Husky, GitHub Actions ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer + Senior Developer PREPARATION Application architecture foundation is defined and documented Complete architecture documentation using C4 model or equivalent 🎯 Action Plan: • Create comprehensive architecture documentation: - System context diagram (C4 Level 1) - Container diagram showing NestJS/Next.js separation (C4 Level 2) - Component diagrams for each service (C4 Level 3) - Application layers (Presentation, Business, Data Access) - Logging strategy (Winston, structured logging) - Error handling mechanisms (global filters, interceptors) - Transaction control (database transactions, saga pattern) • Schedule architecture review sessions with team • Maintain documentation with architecture decision records (ADRs) 📦 Tools: Draw.io, Mermaid, Architecture Decision Records ⏱️ Timeline: 1 week 👥 Responsible: Software Architect + Technical Lead PREPARATION Backup/restore strategy for Production environment is documented Comprehensive backup and disaster recovery plan 🎯 Action Plan: • Design backup strategy covering: - Database backups (automated daily/hourly snapshots) - File system backups (persistent volumes) - Configuration backups (Kubernetes manifests) - Application secrets and certificates • Define Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) • Create automated backup scripts for GCP • Document restore procedures with step-by-step instructions • Test backup/restore procedures monthly • Set up monitoring for backup success/failure 📦 Tools: GCP Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Scheduler ⏱️ Timeline: 3-4 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer + Database Administrator PREPARATION Important 3rd party APIs, libraries, frameworks are documented Comprehensive inventory of external dependencies 🎯 Action Plan: • Create dependency inventory including: - External APIs (authentication providers, payment gateways) - NPM packages with versions and licenses - Cloud services (GCP services, monitoring tools) - Integration patterns and data flows • Implement dependency scanning: - npm audit for security vulnerabilities - OWASP dependency check - License compliance checking • Document API contracts and SLAs • Create contingency plans for service failures 📦 Tools: npm audit, OWASP dependency check, Snyk ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: Technical Lead + Security Engineer DEVELOPMENT All user input data is validated in code Comprehensive input validation at all application layers 🎯 Action Plan: • Implement multi-layer validation: - Client-side validation (React Hook Form, Formik) - API-level validation (NestJS ValidationPipe, class-validator) - Database constraints and triggers • Handle edge cases: - Null/undefined values - Empty arrays and objects - Type coercion and sanitization • Implement rate limiting and CSRF protection • Use validation libraries (Joi, Yup, Zod) • Create reusable validation decorators • Add comprehensive error handling and user feedback 📦 Tools: class-validator, Joi, React Hook Form, express-rate-limit ⏱️ Timeline: 3-5 days 👥 Responsible: Full-stack Developers Maturity Level 2 (Managed)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan SETUP Rollback strategy is described in SCM plan Detailed procedures for code and deployment rollbacks 🎯 Action Plan: • Extend SCM policy with rollback procedures: - Git revert strategies for different scenarios - Database rollback procedures using migrations - Feature flag usage for quick disabling - Deployment rollback using Kubernetes rolling updates • Create rollback playbooks with step-by-step instructions • Implement automated rollback triggers based on metrics • Set up communication protocols during rollbacks • Practice rollback procedures in staging environment 📦 Tools: Git, Kubernetes, Feature flags, Monitoring alerts ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer + Technical Lead SETUP PR creation and protected branches details in SCM plan Comprehensive pull request and branch protection strategy 🎯 Action Plan: • Enhance SCM policy with detailed PR workflows: - PR template with required sections - Branch protection rules (require reviews, status checks) - Protected branches: main, develop, release/* - Required status checks (CI, tests, security scans) • Configure automated PR checks: - Code quality gates (SonarQube) - Security vulnerability scanning - Test coverage requirements • Set up PR assignment and review policies 📦 Tools: GitHub/GitLab branch protection, CI/CD pipelines ⏱️ Timeline: 1-2 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer + Technical Lead PREPARATION Backup/restore strategy for pre-production environments Extended backup strategy covering all environments 🎯 Action Plan: • Extend backup strategy to cover: - Development environment data snapshots - Staging environment regular backups - Test data management and restoration - Configuration synchronization across environments • Implement environment-specific backup schedules • Create automated environment refresh procedures • Document data masking for sensitive information • Set up monitoring for backup health across all environments 📦 Tools: GCP Cloud SQL, Terraform, Kubernetes CronJobs ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer 📋 Implementation Guide: Pre-Production Backup/Restore Strategy PREPARATION Unit testing process is clearly defined and documented Comprehensive unit testing guidelines and processes 🎯 Action Plan: • Create detailed unit testing guide covering: - Testing framework setup (Jest for both NestJS and Next.js) - Test structure and naming conventions - Mocking strategies for dependencies - Test coverage requirements (80% minimum) - Testing patterns for different layers • Provide practical examples and templates • Set up testing utilities and shared mocks • Configure test coverage reporting • Integrate testing requirements into Definition of Done 📦 Tools: Jest, Supertest, React Testing Library, Coverage reports ⏱️ Timeline: 3-4 days 👥 Responsible: Senior Developers + QA Engineer

Maturity Level 1 (Foundation)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan SETUP All necessary KT meetings are planned Knowledge transfer sessions with stakeholders and partners 🎯 Action Plan: • Plan comprehensive knowledge transfer program: - Initial stakeholder alignment meetings - Technical architecture presentations - Third-party integration knowledge sessions - Business process understanding workshops • Create meeting templates and agendas • Schedule regular follow-up sessions • Document all knowledge transfer outcomes • Create knowledge base from sessions 📦 Tools: Meeting scheduling tools, Documentation platform ⏱️ Timeline: 1 week 👥 Responsible: Project Manager + Technical Lead SETUP Business & Technical communication channels are established Effective communication infrastructure for all stakeholders 🎯 Action Plan: • Set up comprehensive communication strategy: - Slack/Teams channels for different purposes (general, alerts, releases) - Email distribution lists for formal communications - Video conferencing setup for technical discussions - Documentation sharing platforms (Confluence, Notion) • Define communication protocols and escalation paths • Create channel guidelines and etiquette • Set up integration between tools (Slack-JIRA, Teams-Azure DevOps) 📦 Tools: Slack/Teams, Email, Video conferencing, Documentation platforms ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: Project Manager + Communication Lead DEVELOPMENT Development policies are communicated to team Comprehensive communication of all technical standards 🎯 Action Plan: • Organize comprehensive communication sessions: - Team meetings to present all policies and standards - Hands-on workshops for practical implementation - Q&A sessions for clarification - Regular check-ins to ensure understanding • Create multiple communication channels: - Formal presentations with slides - Written documentation with examples - Video recordings for reference - Interactive workshops and demos • Implement acknowledgment and feedback mechanisms 📦 Tools: Presentation software, Video recording, Documentation platform ⏱️ Timeline: 1 week 👥 Responsible: Technical Lead + All team members DEVELOPMENT Big technical solutions are communicated to stakeholders Architecture changes and decisions properly communicated 🎯 Action Plan: • Establish formal communication process for major changes: - Regular architecture review meetings with stakeholders - Impact analysis documentation for changes - Visual presentations using architecture diagrams - Written summaries with decision rationale • Create stakeholder communication templates • Set up change approval workflows • Maintain architecture decision records (ADRs) • Schedule follow-up sessions to ensure understanding 📦 Tools: Architecture diagramming tools, Presentation software, ADR templates ⏱️ Timeline: Ongoing process 👥 Responsible: Software Architect + Stakeholder Relations SETUP Overall Architecture diagram is shared with stakeholders Architecture visualization presented to all project participants 🎯 Action Plan: • Create comprehensive architecture presentation: - System overview using C4 model - Technology stack explanation - Integration points and data flows - Deployment architecture on GCP Kubernetes • Schedule presentation meetings with all stakeholder groups • Create different levels of detail for different audiences • Make diagrams easily accessible and up-to-date • Establish process for communicating architecture changes 📦 Tools: Draw.io, Mermaid, Presentation software, Documentation platform ⏱️ Timeline: 3-4 days 👥 Responsible: Software Architect + Technical Lead

Maturity Level 1 (Foundation)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan SETUP All NFRs are mapped and collected Comprehensive identification of non-functional requirements 🎯 Action Plan: • Conduct comprehensive NFR workshops: - Performance requirements (response times, throughput) - Security requirements (authentication, authorization, encryption) - Reliability requirements (uptime, error rates, failover) - Scalability requirements (user load, data volume) - Usability requirements (accessibility, user experience) • Document requirements with measurable criteria • Get formal stakeholder approval and sign-off • Create traceability matrix linking NFRs to implementation • Regular review and update process 📦 Tools: Requirements management tools, Documentation platform ⏱️ Timeline: 1 week 👥 Responsible: Business Analyst + Software Architect + Stakeholders Maturity Level 2 (Managed)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan SETUP NFRs documented using standardized template Consistent NFR documentation format 🎯 Action Plan: • Create standardized NFR template including: - Requirement ID and priority classification - Measurable acceptance criteria - Testing approach and validation methods - Dependencies and constraints - Success metrics and monitoring approach • Convert all existing NFRs to standard format • Train team on template usage • Implement template compliance checking • Create NFR review and approval process 📦 Tools: Template documents, Requirements management system ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: Business Analyst + Quality Assurance DEVELOPMENT NFRs are approved by stakeholders Formal stakeholder approval process for requirements 🎯 Action Plan: • Establish formal NFR approval process: - Stakeholder review sessions for each NFR category - Written approval with signatures/confirmations - Impact analysis for scope and timeline - Change management process for NFR updates • Document approval audit trail • Communicate approved NFRs to development team • Set up monitoring for NFR compliance • Regular stakeholder reviews for NFR satisfaction 📦 Tools: Approval workflow tools, Digital signature platform ⏱️ Timeline: 1 week 👥 Responsible: Project Manager + Business Stakeholders Maturity Level 4 (Quantitatively Managed)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan SETUP Targets for NFR metrics are defined Specific, measurable targets for all NFR areas 🎯 Action Plan: • Define SMART targets for each NFR category: - Performance: API response time < 200ms, page load < 2s - Availability: 99.9% uptime (8.77 hours downtime/year) - Scalability: Support 10,000 concurrent users - Security: Zero critical vulnerabilities, 2FA enabled - Reliability: Error rate < 0.1%, MTTR < 30 minutes • Establish baseline measurements using current system • Set up monitoring and alerting for all metrics • Create dashboards for real-time NFR tracking • Define improvement targets and timelines 📦 Tools: Monitoring platforms, Dashboard tools, Analytics systems ⏱️ Timeline: 1 week 👥 Responsible: Software Architect + DevOps Engineer + Stakeholders

Maturity Level 1 (Foundation)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan DEVELOPMENT Artifact versions are trackable across environments Clear versioning and deployment tracking 🎯 Action Plan: • Implement comprehensive version tracking: - Semantic versioning (major.minor.patch) for releases - Build numbers with timestamp and commit hash - Git tags for all releases - Docker image tags with version information • Set up deployment logging and tracking: - Kubernetes deployment annotations with version info - Deployment dashboard showing current versions per environment - GitOps approach with ArgoCD for deployment tracking • Create version comparison and rollback capabilities 📦 Tools: Git tags, Docker registry, Kubernetes, ArgoCD, Deployment dashboards ⏱️ Timeline: 2-3 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer + Release Manager Maturity Level 2 (Managed)​ Phase Criteria Help Text Action Plan DEVELOPMENT Environment-specific configurations externalized Configuration managed outside deployment packages 🎯 Action Plan: • Implement external configuration management: - Kubernetes ConfigMaps for application settings - Kubernetes Secrets for sensitive information - GCP Secret Manager for critical secrets - Environment variables for all environment-specific values • Never hard-code environment-specific values in code • Create configuration templates for each environment • Implement configuration validation and testing • Set up configuration change tracking and auditing 📦 Tools: Kubernetes ConfigMaps/Secrets, GCP Secret Manager, Helm charts ⏱️ Timeline: 3-4 days 👥 Responsible: DevOps Engineer + Security Engineer PREPARATION Deployment to dev/test environments is automated Automated deployment pipelines for non-production 🎯 Action Plan: • Set up comprehensive CI/CD pipelines: - GitHub Actions or Cloud Build for automation - Automated testing before deployment - Zero-manual-step deployments to dev/test - Automated database migrations • Configure deployment triggers: - Automatic deployment on main branch merge - import { ArchitecturalRulesEngine } from './architectural-rules'; export interface AnalysisResult { file: string; issues: Issue[]; metrics: CodeMetrics; violations: ArchitecturalViolation[]; score: number; } export interface Issue { type: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info'; rule: string; message: string; line: number; column: number; severity: number; } export interface CodeMetrics { complexity: number; maintainability: number; testCoverage: number; technicalDebt: string; duplicatedLines: number; linesOfCode: number; } export interface ArchitecturalViolation { type: 'dependency' | 'layering' | 'pattern' | 'naming'; severity: 'critical' | 'major' | 'minor'; description: string; suggestion: string; file: string; line?: number; } export class ArchitectureAnalyzer { private eslint: ESLint; private sonarqube: SonarQubeAnalyzer; private codeclimate: CodeClimateAnalyzer; private rulesEngine: ArchitecturalRulesEngine; constructor() { this.eslint = new ESLint({ configFile: '.eslintrc.js', extensions: ['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx'], }); this.sonarqube = new SonarQubeAnalyzer(); this.codeclimate = new CodeClimateAnalyzer(); this.rulesEngine = new ArchitecturalRulesEngine(); } async analyzeProject(projectPath: string): Promise<AnalysisResult[]> { const files = await this.getSourceFiles(projectPath); const results: AnalysisResult[] = []; for (const file of files) { const result = await this.analyzeFile(file); results.push(result); } return results; } async analyzeFile(filePath: string): Promise<AnalysisResult> { const [eslintResults, metrics, violations] = await Promise.all([ this.runESLintAnalysis(filePath), this.analyzeCodeMetrics(filePath), this.checkArchitecturalRules(filePath), ]); const issues = this.convertESLintResults(eslintResults); const score = this.calculateQualityScore(issues, metrics, violations); return { file: filePath, issues, metrics, violations, score, }; } private async runESLintAnalysis(filePath: string) { const results = await this.eslint.lintFiles([filePath]); return results[0] || { messages: [] }; } private async analyzeCodeMetrics(filePath: string): Promise<CodeMetrics> { const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8'); // Use multiple analysis tools const [sonarMetrics, codeClimateMetrics] = await Promise.all([ this.sonarqube.analyzeFile(filePath, content), this.codeclimate.analyzeFile(filePath, content), ]); return { complexity: sonarMetrics.complexity, maintainability: codeClimateMetrics.maintainability, testCoverage: sonarMetrics.testCoverage, technicalDebt: sonarMetrics.technicalDebt, duplicatedLines: sonarMetrics.duplicatedLines, linesOfCode: this.countLinesOfCode(content), }; } private async checkArchitecturalRules(filePath: string): Promise<ArchitecturalViolation[]> { const content = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8'); return this.rulesEngine.validateFile(filePath, content); } private convertESLintResults(eslintResult: any): Issue[] { return eslintResult.messages.map((message: any) => ({ type: message.severity === 2 ? 'error' : 'warning', rule: message.ruleId, message: message.message, line: message.line, column: message.column, severity: message.severity, })); } private calculateQualityScore( issues: Issue[], metrics: CodeMetrics, violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] ): number { let score = 100; // Deduct for issues const errorCount = issues.filter(i => i.type === 'error').length; const warningCount = issues.filter(i => i.type === 'warning').length; score -= errorCount * 10 + warningCount * 5; // Deduct for violations const criticalViolations = violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'critical').length; const majorViolations = violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'major').length; const minorViolations = violations.filter(v => v.severity === 'minor').length; score -= criticalViolations * 15 + majorViolations * 10 + minorViolations * 5; // Factor in metrics if (metrics.complexity > 10) score -= 5; if (metrics.maintainability < 60) score -= 10; if (metrics.testCoverage < 80) score -= 15; return Math.max(0, score); } private async getSourceFiles(projectPath: string): Promise<string[]> { const files: string[] = []; const extensions = ['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx']; function walkDir(dir: string) { const items = fs.readdirSync(dir); for (const item of items) { const fullPath = path.join(dir, item); const stat = fs.statSync(fullPath); if (stat.isDirectory() && !item.startsWith('.') && item !== 'node_modules') { walkDir(fullPath); } else if (stat.isFile() && extensions.some(ext => item.endsWith(ext))) { files.push(fullPath); } } } walkDir(projectPath); return files; } private countLinesOfCode(content: string): number { return content.split('\n').filter(line => line.trim().length > 0).length; } }

// tools/architecture-analysis/architectural-rules.ts import * as fs from 'fs'; import * as path from 'path'; import { ArchitecturalViolation } from './static-analyzer'; export interface ArchitecturalRule { name: string; description: string; severity: 'critical' | 'major' | 'minor'; check: (filePath: string, content: string) => ArchitecturalViolation[]; } export class ArchitecturalRulesEngine { private rules: ArchitecturalRule[] = [ // NestJS specific rules { name: 'nestjs-service-naming', description: 'Service files should end with .service.ts', severity: 'minor', check: this.checkServiceNaming.bind(this), }, { name: 'nestjs-controller-naming', description: 'Controller files should end with .controller.ts', severity: 'minor', check: this.checkControllerNaming.bind(this), }, { name: 'nestjs-dependency-injection', description: 'Services should use proper dependency injection', severity: 'major', check: this.checkDependencyInjection.bind(this), }, { name: 'nestjs-module-structure', description: 'Modules should follow proper structure', severity: 'major', check: this.checkModuleStructure.bind(this), }, // Next.js specific rules { name: 'nextjs-page-structure', description: 'Pages should be in pages/ or app/ directory', severity: 'critical', check: this.checkPageStructure.bind(this), }, { name: 'nextjs-api-routes', description: 'API routes should be in proper directory structure', severity: 'major', check: this.checkApiRoutes.bind(this), }, { name: 'nextjs-component-naming', description: 'Components should use PascalCase naming', severity: 'minor', check: this.checkComponentNaming.bind(this), }, // General architectural rules { name: 'circular-dependencies', description: 'Circular dependencies should be avoided', severity: 'critical', check: this.checkCircularDependencies.bind(this), }, { name: 'layer-separation', description: 'Business logic should not depend on infrastructure', severity: 'major', check: this.checkLayerSeparation.bind(this), }, { name: 'single-responsibility', description: 'Classes should have single responsibility', severity: 'major', check: this.checkSingleResponsibility.bind(this), }, ]; validateFile(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; for (const rule of this.rules) { try { const ruleViolations = rule.check(filePath, content); violations.push(...ruleViolations); } catch (error) { console.error(`Error checking rule ${rule.name}:`, error); } } return violations; } private checkServiceNaming(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const fileName = path.basename(filePath); const isService = content.includes('@Injectable()') && (content.includes('Service') || fileName.includes('service')); if (isService && !fileName.endsWith('.service.ts')) { return [{ type: 'naming', severity: 'minor', description: `Service file ${fileName} should end with .service.ts`, suggestion: `Rename file to ${fileName.replace('.ts', '.service.ts')}`, file: filePath, }]; } return []; } private checkControllerNaming(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const fileName = path.basename(filePath); const isController = content.includes('@Controller(') && (content.includes('Controller') || fileName.includes('controller')); if (isController && !fileName.endsWith('.controller.ts')) { return [{ type: 'naming', severity: 'minor', description: `Controller file ${fileName} should end with .controller.ts`, suggestion: `Rename file to ${fileName.replace('.ts', '.controller.ts')}`, file: filePath, }]; } return []; } private checkDependencyInjection(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; // Check for direct instantiation of services const directInstantiation = /new\s+[A-Z]\w*Service\s*\(/g; const matches = [...content.matchAll(directInstantiation)]; for (const match of matches) { violations.push({ type: 'dependency', severity: 'major', description: 'Direct service instantiation found, use dependency injection instead', suggestion: 'Inject the service through constructor parameters', file: filePath, line: this.getLineNumber(content, match.index!), }); } return violations; } private checkModuleStructure(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; if (content.includes('@Module(') && !filePath.endsWith('.module.ts')) { violations.push({ type: 'pattern', severity: 'major', description: 'Module files should end with .module.ts', suggestion: `Rename file to ${path.basename(filePath).replace('.ts', '.module.ts')}`, file: filePath, }); } return violations; } private checkPageStructure(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; // Check if it's a Next.js page component const isPageComponent = content.includes('export default') && (filePath.includes('/pages/') || filePath.includes('/app/')) && (content.includes('NextPage') || content.includes('Page')); if (isPageComponent) { const properPageDir = filePath.includes('/pages/') || filePath.includes('/app/'); if (!properPageDir) { violations.push({ type: 'pattern', severity: 'critical', description: 'Page components should be in pages/ or app/ directory', suggestion: 'Move page component to appropriate directory structure', file: filePath, }); } } return violations; } private checkApiRoutes(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; const isApiRoute = filePath.includes('/api/') && (content.includes('export default') || content.includes('export async function')); if (isApiRoute && !filePath.match(/\/api\/.*\.(ts|js)$/)) { violations.push({ type: 'pattern', severity: 'major', description: 'API routes should follow Next.js API directory structure', suggestion: 'Place API routes in pages/api/ or app/api/ directory', file: filePath, }); } return violations; } private checkComponentNaming(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; const fileName = path.basename(filePath, path.extname(filePath)); const isComponent = content.includes('export default') && (content.includes('function') || content.includes('const')) && content.includes('return') && content.includes('<'); if (isComponent && !fileName.match(/^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/)) { violations.push({ type: 'naming', severity: 'minor', description: 'Component files should use PascalCase naming', suggestion: `Rename file to use PascalCase (e.g., ${this.toPascalCase(fileName)})`, file: filePath, }); } return violations; } private checkCircularDependencies(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { // This is a simplified check - full circular dependency detection requires graph analysis const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; const imports = this.extractImports(content); const fileName = path.basename(filePath, path.extname(filePath)); for (const importPath of imports) { if (importPath.includes(fileName)) { violations.push({ type: 'dependency', severity: 'critical', description: 'Potential circular dependency detected', suggestion: 'Refactor to remove circular dependency, consider using dependency inversion', file: filePath, }); } } return violations; } private checkLayerSeparation(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; // Check if domain/business logic imports infrastructure concerns const isDomainLayer = filePath.includes('/domain/') || filePath.includes('/entities/') || filePath.includes('/use-cases/'); if (isDomainLayer) { const infrastructureImports = [ 'typeorm', 'mongoose', 'redis', 'axios', 'fetch', '@nestjs/typeorm', 'prisma', ]; for (const infraImport of infrastructureImports) { if (content.includes(`from '${infraImport}'`) || content.includes(`from "${infraImport}"`)) { violations.push({ type: 'layering', severity: 'major', description: `Domain layer should not depend on infrastructure layer (${infraImport})`, suggestion: 'Use dependency inversion principle and inject abstractions', file: filePath, }); } } } return violations; } private checkSingleResponsibility(filePath: string, content: string): ArchitecturalViolation[] { const violations: ArchitecturalViolation[] = []; // Simple heuristic: if a class has too many public methods, it might violate SRP const publicMethods = content.match(/^\s*(public\s+)?(?:async\s+)?[a-zA-Z_]\w*\s*\(/gm); if (publicMethods && publicMethods.length > 10) { violations.push({ type: 'pattern', severity: 'major', description: `Class has ${publicMethods.length} public methods, might violate Single Responsibility Principle`, suggestion: 'Consider splitting the class into smaller, more focused classes', file: filePath, }); } return violations; } private extractImports(content: string): string[] { const importRegex = /import.*from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g; const imports: string[] = []; let match; while ((match = importRegex.exec(content)) !== null) { imports.push(match[1]); } return imports; } private getLineNumber(content: string, index: number): number { return content.substring(0, index).split('\n').length; } private toPascalCase(str: string): string { return str.replace(/(?:^|[-_])(\w)/g, (_, char) => char.toUpperCase()); } }
