// tools/review-system/review-assignment.ts import { Octokit } from '@octokit/rest'; import * as core from '@actions/core'; export interface ReviewRequirement { minReviewers: number; requiredExperts: string[]; skipConditions: string[]; autoAssign: boolean; } export interface Developer { username: string; expertise: string[]; workload: number; timezone: string; availability: boolean; } export class ReviewAssignmentSystem { private octokit: Octokit; private developers: Developer[] = [ { username: 'senior-backend-dev', expertise: ['nestjs', 'microservices', 'database', 'security'], workload: 3, timezone: 'UTC', availability: true, }, { username: 'senior-frontend-dev', expertise: ['nextjs', 'react', 'typescript', 'ui-ux'], workload: 2, timezone: 'UTC', availability: true, }, { username: 'architect', expertise: ['architecture', 'patterns', 'performance', 'scalability'], workload: 1, timezone: 'UTC', availability: true, }, { username: 'security-expert', expertise: ['security', 'compliance', 'vulnerabilities'], workload: 2, timezone: 'UTC', availability: true, }, ]; constructor(token: string) { this.octokit = new Octokit({ auth: token }); } async assignReviewers( owner: string, repo: string, pullNumber: number, changedFiles: string[] ): Promise<void> { const requirements = this.determineReviewRequirements(changedFiles); const assignees = await this.selectReviewers(requirements, changedFiles); if (assignees.length > 0) { await this.octokit.pulls.requestReviewers({ owner, repo, pull_number: pullNumber, reviewers: assignees, }); core.info(`Assigned reviewers: ${assignees.join(', ')}`); } } private determineReviewRequirements(changedFiles: string[]): ReviewRequirement { let minReviewers = 1; const requiredExperts: string[] = []; // Analyze changed files to determine requirements const hasBackendChanges = changedFiles.some(file => file.includes('/src/') && file.endsWith('.ts') && !file.includes('.spec.ts') && !file.includes('.test.ts') ); const hasFrontendChanges = changedFiles.some(file => file.includes('/components/') || file.includes('/pages/') || file.includes('/hooks/') || file.endsWith('.tsx') ); const hasArchitecturalChanges = changedFiles.some(file => file.includes('module.ts') || file.includes('config') || file.includes('infrastructure') || file.includes('architecture') ); const hasSecurityChanges = changedFiles.some(file => file.includes('auth') || file.includes('security') || file.includes('guard') || file.includes('middleware') ); const hasDatabaseChanges = changedFiles.some(file => file.includes('migration') || file.includes('entity') || file.includes('repository') || file.includes('schema') ); // Determine required expertise if (hasBackendChanges) requiredExperts.push('nestjs', 'microservices'); if (hasFrontendChanges) requiredExperts.push('nextjs', 'react'); if (hasArchitecturalChanges) requiredExperts.push('architecture'); if (hasSecurityChanges) requiredExperts.push('security'); if (hasDatabaseChanges) requiredExperts.push('database'); // Increase minimum reviewers for complex changes if (requiredExperts.length > 2) minReviewers = 2; if (hasArchitecturalChanges || hasSecurityChanges) minReviewers = Math.max(minReviewers, 2); return { minReviewers, requiredExperts, skipConditions: ['docs-only', 'test-only'], autoAssign: true, }; } private async selectReviewers( requirements: ReviewRequirement, changedFiles: string[] ): Promise<string[]> { // Filter available developers const availableDevelopers = this.developers.filter(dev => dev.availability && dev.workload < 5 ); // Find experts for required expertise const expertCandidates = availableDevelopers.filter(dev => requirements.requiredExperts.some(expertise => dev.expertise.includes(expertise) ) ); // Sort by expertise match and workload const sortedCandidates = expertCandidates.sort((a, b) => { const aExpertiseMatch = requirements.requiredExperts.filter(exp => a.expertise.includes(exp) ).length; const bExpertiseMatch = requirements.requiredExperts.filter(exp => b.expertise.includes(exp) ).length; if (aExpertiseMatch !== bExpertiseMatch) { return bExpertiseMatch - aExpertiseMatch; } return a.workload - b.workload; }); // Select reviewers const selectedReviewers: string[] = []; const coverageMap = new Set<string>(); for (const candidate of sortedCandidates) { if (selectedReviewers.length >= requirements.minReviewers) { break; } const candidateExpertise = candidate.expertise.filter(exp => requirements.requiredExperts.includes(exp) ); const addsCoverage = candidateExpertise.some(exp => !coverageMap.has(exp)); if (addsCoverage || selectedReviewers.length < requirements.minReviewers) { selectedReviewers.push(candidate.username); candidateExpertise.forEach(exp => coverageMap.add(exp)); } } return selectedReviewers; } }

// tools/review-system/architecture-review-board.ts export interface ArchitectureDecision { id: string; title: string; context: string; decision: string; consequences: string[]; status: 'proposed' | 'accepted' | 'rejected' | 'superseded'; author: string; reviewers: string[]; dateCreated: Date; dateDecided?: Date; relatedDecisions: string[]; } export interface ReviewCriteria { alignment: number; // 1-5 scale impact: number; // 1-5 scale complexity: number; // 1-5 scale risk: number; // 1-5 scale innovation: number; // 1-5 scale } export class ArchitectureReviewBoard { private decisions: Map<string, ArchitectureDecision> = new Map(); private boardMembers: string[] = [ 'chief-architect', 'senior-architect', 'tech-lead-backend', 'tech-lead-frontend', 'security-architect', ]; async submitDecision(decision: Omit<ArchitectureDecision, 'id' | 'status' | 'dateCreated'>): Promise<string> { const id = this.generateDecisionId(); const fullDecision: ArchitectureDecision = { ...decision, id, status: 'proposed', dateCreated: new Date(), }; this.decisions.set(id, fullDecision); await this.notifyReviewers(fullDecision); return id; } async reviewDecision( decisionId: string, reviewer: string, criteria: ReviewCriteria, comments: string, recommendation: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'request-changes' ): Promise<void> { const decision = this.decisions.get(decisionId); if (!decision) { throw new Error(`Decision ${decisionId} not found`); } // Store review await this.storeReview(decisionId, reviewer, criteria, comments, recommendation); // Check if all required reviews are complete const reviews = await this.getReviews(decisionId); const requiredReviewers = this.determineRequiredReviewers(decision); const completedReviews = reviews.filter(r => requiredReviewers.includes(r.reviewer) ); if (completedReviews.length >= requiredReviewers.length) { await this.makeDecision(decisionId); } } private async makeDecision(decisionId: string): Promise<void> { const decision = this.decisions.get(decisionId)!; const reviews = await this.getReviews(decisionId); const approvals = reviews.filter(r => r.recommendation === 'approve').length; const rejections = reviews.filter(r => r.recommendation === 'reject').length; const totalReviews = reviews.length; // Require 2/3 majority for approval const approvalThreshold = Math.ceil(totalReviews * 0.67); if (approvals >= approvalThreshold) { decision.status = 'accepted'; decision.dateDecided = new Date(); await this.notifyDecisionAccepted(decision); await this.updateArchitectureDocumentation(decision); } else if (rejections > totalReviews - approvalThreshold) { decision.status = 'rejected'; decision.dateDecided = new Date(); await this.notifyDecisionRejected(decision); } this.decisions.set(decisionId, decision); } private determineRequiredReviewers(decision: ArchitectureDecision): string[] { const requiredReviewers = ['chief-architect']; // Add specific expertise based on decision content if (decision.context.includes('security') || decision.decision.includes('security')) { requiredReviewers.push('security-architect'); } if (decision.context.includes('backend') || decision.decision.includes('nestjs')) { requiredReviewers.push('tech-lead-backend'); } if (decision.context.includes('frontend') || decision.decision.includes('nextjs')) { requiredReviewers.push('tech-lead-frontend'); } // For high-impact decisions, require senior architect if (this.isHighImpactDecision(decision)) { requiredReviewers.push('senior-architect'); } return [...new Set(requiredReviewers)]; } private isHighImpactDecision(decision: ArchitectureDecision): boolean { const highImpactKeywords = [ 'migration', 'refactor', 'architecture change', 'breaking change', 'new technology', 'framework change', 'security model', 'data model' ]; const content = `${decision.title} ${decision.context} ${decision.decision}`.toLowerCase(); return highImpactKeywords.some(keyword => content.includes(keyword)); } private generateDecisionId(): string { return `ADR-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 9)}`; } private async notifyReviewers(decision: ArchitectureDecision): Promise<void> { const requiredReviewers = this.determineRequiredReviewers(decision); // Send notifications (email, Slack, etc.) console.log(`Notifying reviewers for decision ${decision.id}: ${requiredReviewers.join(', ')}`); } private async storeReview( decisionId: string, reviewer: string, criteria: ReviewCriteria, comments: string, recommendation: string ): Promise<void> { // Store in database or file system console.log(`Review stored for decision ${decisionId} by ${reviewer}: ${recommendation}`); } private async getReviews(decisionId: string): Promise<any[]> { // Retrieve reviews from storage return []; } private async notifyDecisionAccepted(decision: ArchitectureDecision): Promise<void> { console.log(`Decision ${decision.id} has been accepted`); } private async notifyDecisionRejected(decision: ArchitectureDecision): Promise<void> { console.log(`Decision ${decision.id} has been rejected`); } private async updateArchitectureDocumentation(decision: ArchitectureDecision): Promise<void> { // Update ADR documentation console.log(`Updating architecture documentation for decision ${decision.id}`); } }

// tools/monitoring/architecture-dashboard.ts export interface ArchitectureMetrics { codeQuality: { maintainabilityIndex: number; cyclomaticComplexity: number; technicalDebt: string; codeSmells: number; }; testCoverage: { linesCovered: number; branchesCovered: number; functionsCovered: number; statementsCovered: number; }; dependencies: { outdatedPackages: number; vulnerabilities: number; licenseIssues: number; circularDependencies: number; }; performance: { buildTime: number; bundleSize: number; loadTime: number; memoryUsage: number; }; architecture: { complianceScore: number; patternViolations: number; layerViolations: number; couplingMetrics: number; }; } export class ArchitectureDashboard { async generateReport(): Promise<ArchitectureMetrics> { const [codeQuality, testCoverage, dependencies, performance, architecture] = await Promise.all([ this.analyzeCodeQuality(), this.analyzeTestCoverage(), this.analyzeDependencies(), this.analyzePerformance(), this.analyzeArchitecture(), ]); return { codeQuality, testCoverage, dependencies, performance, architecture, }; } private async analyzeCodeQuality() { // Implementation for code quality analysis return { maintainabilityIndex: 85, cyclomaticComplexity: 6.2, technicalDebt: '2h 15m', codeSmells: 3, }; } private async analyzeTestCoverage() { // Implementation for test coverage analysis return { linesCovered: 87.5, branchesCovered: 82.3, functionsCovered: 89.1, statementsCovered: 88.7, }; } private async analyzeDependencies() { // Implementation for dependency analysis return { outdatedPackages: 5, vulnerabilities: 1, licenseIssues: 0, circularDependencies: 0, }; } private async analyzePerformance() { // Implementation for performance analysis return { buildTime: 45.2, bundleSize: 1.2, loadTime: 850, memoryUsage: 128, }; } private async analyzeArchitecture() { // Implementation for architecture analysis return { complianceScore: 92, patternViolations: 2, layerViolations: 0, couplingMetrics: 7.8, }; } }

Continuous Testing - Automated testing frameworks Code Review Process - Manual review protocols Non-functional Requirements Validation - Specialized validation This architecture evaluation guide should be regularly updated to incorporate new tools and best practices.
This guide establishes a comprehensive code review process for NestJS microservices and Next.js microfrontend development teams, focusing on quality, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

Code reviews are essential for maintaining code quality, sharing knowledge, catching bugs early, and ensuring adherence to architectural standards. This process is specifically designed for distributed microservices and microfrontend architectures.

Standard Code Reviews​ Pull Request Reviews: All code changes must go through peer review No direct commits to main/develop branches Minimum of 2 approvals required for production code Automated checks must pass before review Review Stages: graph TD A[Create PR] --> B[Automated Checks] B --> C{Checks Pass?} C -->|No| D[Fix Issues] D --> A C -->|Yes| E[Assign Reviewers] E --> F[Peer Review] F --> G{Approved?} G -->|No| H[Address Feedback] H --> F G -->|Yes| I[Final Approval] I --> J[Merge to Target Branch] Architecture Reviews​ High-Impact Changes: New service creation API contract modifications Database schema changes Cross-service integration changes Security implementation changes Review Committee: Senior developers from affected teams Architecture team representative DevOps/Platform team member Product owner (for business logic changes)

// Correct DI usage errorHandling: boolean; // Comprehensive error handling logging: boolean; // Appropriate logging levels }; codeQuality: { typeScript: boolean; // Proper TypeScript usage naming: boolean; // Clear, descriptive names complexity: boolean; // Functions under 20 lines documentation: boolean; // JSDoc for public APIs }; testing: { unitTests: boolean; // All business logic covered integrationTests: boolean; // API endpoints tested mockStrategy: boolean; // Proper mocking approach coverage: boolean; // >80% coverage maintained }; security: { inputValidation: boolean; // All inputs validated authentication: boolean; // Proper auth implementation authorization: boolean; // Correct permission checks dataProtection: boolean; // Sensitive data handling }; performance: { queryOptimization: boolean; // Efficient database queries caching: boolean; // Appropriate caching strategy resourceUsage: boolean; // Memory and CPU efficiency asyncPatterns: boolean; // Proper async/await usage }; } Next.js Microfrontend Review Criteria: // Code Review Checklist for Next.js Applications interface NextJSReviewCriteria { architecture: { componentStructure: boolean; // Logical component organization stateManagement: boolean; // Appropriate state patterns routingStrategy: boolean; // Correct routing implementation apiIntegration: boolean; // Proper API client usage }; Reviewer Responsibilities​ Primary Reviewer Duties: // Primary Reviewer Checklist class PrimaryReviewerDuties { async reviewPullRequest(pr: PullRequest): Promise<ReviewResult> { const checks = { functionalCorrectness: await this.verifyFunctionality(pr), architecturalCompliance: await this.checkArchitecture(pr), codeQuality: await this.assessCodeQuality(pr), testingAdequacy: await this.validateTesting(pr), documentationCompleteness: await this.checkDocumentation(pr), securityConsiderations: await this.reviewSecurity(pr), performanceImpact: await this.assessPerformance(pr), }; return this.generateReview(checks); } private async verifyFunctionality(pr: PullRequest): Promise<boolean> { // Check if the code does what it's supposed to do // Verify business logic implementation // Test edge cases and error scenarios return true; } private async checkArchitecture(pr: PullRequest): Promise<boolean> { // Ensure adherence to architectural patterns // Verify service boundaries are respected // Check for proper abstraction layers return true; } } Secondary Reviewer Duties: Focus on alternative approaches and optimizations Verify test coverage and quality Check for potential edge cases Ensure consistency with team standards Author Responsibilities​ Pre-Review Preparation: // Author Pre-Review Checklist class AuthorPreReviewChecklist { async preparePullRequest(): Promise<void> { await this.selfReview(); await this.runAllTests(); await this.updateDocumentation(); await this.verifyBuildSuccess(); await this.writeDescriptiveCommits(); await this.fillPRTemplate(); } private async selfReview(): Promise<void> { // Review own code with fresh eyes // Check for obvious issues // Ensure proper formatting // Verify no debug code remains } private async writeDescriptiveCommits(): Promise<void> { // Use conventional commit format // Example: "feat(auth): add JWT token validation" // Include ticket references where applicable } }

Standard PR Template​ <!-- .github/pull_request_template.md --> ## Description Brief description of the changes made. ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes) - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Security enhancement ## Testing - [ ] Unit tests pass - [ ] Integration tests pass - [ ] E2E tests pass (if applicable) - [ ] Manual testing completed - [ ] New tests added for new functionality ## Architecture Impact - [ ] No architecture changes - [ ] Service interface changes (requires architecture review) - [ ] Database schema changes (requires migration) - [ ] New external dependencies - [ ] Security implications - [ ] Performance implications ## Checklist - [ ] Code follows team style guidelines - [ ] Self-review of code completed - [ ] Code is commented, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [ ] Changes generate no new warnings - [ ] Dependent changes merged and published ## Screenshots (if applicable) Include screenshots for UI changes. ## Additional Notes Any additional information that would be helpful for reviewers. Microservice-Specific PR Template​ <!-- .github/microservice_pr_template.md --> ## Service Information - **Service Name**: - **Service Type**: [API Gateway, Business Service, Data Service] - **Dependencies**: List affected services ## API Changes - [ ] No API changes - [ ] New endpoints added - [ ] Existing endpoints modified - [ ] Endpoints deprecated - [ ] Breaking changes (requires version bump) ## Database Changes - [ ] No database changes - [ ] New tables/collections - [ ] Schema modifications - [ ] Data migrations required - [ ] Index changes ## Message Queue Changes - [ ] No messaging changes - [ ] New message types - [ ] Modified message contracts - [ ] New queues/topics - [ ] Consumer changes ## Configuration Changes - [ ] Environment variables added/modified - [ ] Service discovery changes - [ ] Security configuration updates - [ ] Monitoring configuration changes ## Deployment Considerations - [ ] Standard deployment - [ ] Rolling deployment required - [ ] Blue-green deployment required - [ ] Database migration during deployment - [ ] Service dependencies must be deployed first

GitHub Actions Integration​ # .github/workflows/code-review.yml name: Automated Code Review on: pull_request: branches: [main, develop] jobs: automated-review: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout code uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 - name: Setup Node.js uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: '20' cache: 'npm' - name: Install dependencies run: npm ci - name: Run ESLint run: npm run lint -- --format=json --output-file=eslint-report.json continue-on-error: true - name: Run Tests with Coverage run: npm run test:coverage -- --coverage --coverageReporters=json continue-on-error: true - name: Security Audit run: npm audit --json > security-audit.json continue-on-error: true - name: Type Check run: npm run type-check - name: SonarCloud Scan uses: SonarSource/sonarcloud-github-action@master env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }} - name: Comment PR with Review uses: actions/github-script@v7 with: script: | const fs = require('fs'); // Read analysis results const eslintReport = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('eslint-report.json', 'utf8')); const coverageReport = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('coverage/coverage-summary.json', 'utf8')); // Generate review comment const comment = `## Automated Code Review ### ESLint Results - Total issues: ${eslintReport.reduce((acc, file) => acc + file.errorCount + file.warningCount, 0)} - Errors: ${eslintReport.reduce((acc, file) => acc + file.errorCount, 0)} - Warnings: ${eslintReport.reduce((acc, file) => acc + file.warningCount, 0)} ### Test Coverage - Lines: ${coverageReport.total.lines.pct}% - Functions: ${coverageReport.total.functions.pct}% - Branches: ${coverageReport.total.branches.pct}% - Statements: ${coverageReport.total.statements.pct}% ### Recommendations ${eslintReport.reduce((acc, file) => acc + file.errorCount, 0) > 0 ? '- ❌ Fix ESLint errors before merge' : '- ✅ No ESLint errors'} ${coverageReport.total.lines.pct < 80 ? '- ❌ Increase test coverage above 80%' : '- ✅ Test coverage looks good'} `; github.rest.issues.createComment({ issue_number: context.issue.number, owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, body: comment }); Code Quality Bot Integration​ // scripts/review-bot.ts import { Octokit } from '@octokit/rest'; import { PullRequest, Review } from '@octokit/webhooks-types'; class CodeReviewBot { private octokit: Octokit; constructor(token: string) { this.octokit = new Octokit({ auth: token }); } async analyzePullRequest(pr: PullRequest): Promise<void> { const analysis = await this.performCodeAnalysis(pr); const review = this.generateReview(analysis); await this.postReview(pr, review); } private async performCodeAnalysis(pr: PullRequest): Promise<AnalysisResult> { const files = await this.octokit.pulls.listFiles({ owner: pr.base.repo.owner.login, repo: pr.base.repo.name, pull_number: pr.number, }); return { complexity: this.analyzeComplexity(files.data), patterns: this.analyzePatterns(files.data), security: this.analyzeSecurityIssues(files.data), performance: this.analyzePerformanceIssues(files.data), }; } private generateReview(analysis: AnalysisResult): ReviewComment[] { const comments: ReviewComment[] = []; // Generate specific line comments based on analysis if (analysis.complexity.highComplexityFunctions.length > 0) { comments.push({ path: analysis.complexity.highComplexityFunctions[0].file, line: analysis.complexity.highComplexityFunctions[0].line, body: "Consider breaking down this function - it has high cyclomatic complexity.", }); } if (analysis.security.vulnerabilities.length > 0) { analysis.security.vulnerabilities.forEach(vuln => { comments.push({ path: vuln.file, line: vuln.line, body: `Security issue detected: ${vuln.description}`, }); }); } return comments; } }

Code Review Process - Manual code quality validation CI/CD Pipeline - Automated test execution Performance Testing - Specialized performance validation This continuous testing guide should be regularly updated to incorporate new testing tools and methodologies.

This guide establishes comprehensive validation frameworks for non-functional requirements in NestJS microservices and Next.js microfrontend applications, covering performance testing, security validation, scalability assessment, and compliance verification through automated testing and monitoring strategies.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs) define system quality attributes such as performance, security, scalability, reliability, and usability. This validation framework ensures that applications meet these critical requirements through systematic testing, monitoring, and validation processes.

// tests/performance/load-tests/user-management.k6.js import http from 'k6/http'; import { check, sleep } from 'k6'; import { Rate, Trend } from 'k6/metrics'; // Custom metrics const errorRate = new Rate('errors'); const responseTimeThreshold = new Trend('response_time_threshold'); // Test configuration export const options = { stages: [ { duration: '5m', target: 100 }, // Ramp up to 100 users { duration: '10m', target: 100 }, // Stay at 100 users { duration: '5m', target: 200 }, // Ramp up to 200 users { duration: '10m', target: 200 }, // Stay at 200 users { duration: '5m', target: 0 }, // Ramp down ], thresholds: { http_req_duration: ['p(95)<500'], // 95% of requests under 500ms http_req_failed: ['rate<0.05'], // Error rate under 5% errors: ['rate<0.05'], response_time_threshold: ['p(99)<1000'], // 99% under 1s }, ext: { loadimpact: { distribution: { 'amazon:us:ashburn': { loadZone: 'amazon:us:ashburn', percent: 50 }, 'amazon:ie:dublin': { loadZone: 'amazon:ie:dublin', percent: 50 }, }, }, }, }; const BASE_URL = __ENV.BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:3000'; let authToken; export function setup() { // Authenticate and get token const loginResponse = http.post(`${BASE_URL}/auth/login`, { email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password123', }); check(loginResponse, { 'login successful': (r) => r.status === 200, }); const token = loginResponse.json('access_token'); return { authToken: token }; } export default function (data) { authToken = data.authToken; // Test user list endpoint testUsersList(); sleep(1); // Test user creation testUserCreation(); sleep(1); // Test user update testUserUpdate(); sleep(2); } function testUsersList() { const response = http.get(`${BASE_URL}/api/users`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', }, }); const success = check(response, { 'users list status is 200': (r) => r.status === 200, 'users list response time < 200ms': (r) => r.timings.duration < 200, 'users list returns array': (r) => Array.isArray(r.json()), }); errorRate.add(!success); responseTimeThreshold.add(response.timings.duration); } function testUserCreation() { const userData = { name: `Test User ${__VU}-${__ITER}`, email: `user-${__VU}-${__ITER}@example.com`, password: 'password123', }; const response = http.post(`${BASE_URL}/api/users`, JSON.stringify(userData), { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', }, }); const success = check(response, { 'user creation status is 201': (r) => r.status === 201, 'user creation response time < 300ms': (r) => r.timings.duration < 300, 'user creation returns user id': (r) => r.json('id') !== undefined, }); errorRate.add(!success); responseTimeThreshold.add(response.timings.duration); return response.json('id'); } function testUserUpdate() { const userId = Math.floor(Math.random() * 100) + 1; const updateData = { name: `Updated User ${__VU}-${__ITER}`, }; const response = http.patch(`${BASE_URL}/api/users/${userId}`, JSON.stringify(updateData), { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', }, }); const success = check(response, { 'user update status is 200 or 404': (r) => r.status === 200 || r.status === 404, 'user update response time < 250ms': (r) => r.timings.duration < 250, }); errorRate.add(!success && response.status !== 404); responseTimeThreshold.add(response.timings.duration); } export function teardown(data) { console.log('Load test completed'); }

// tests/performance/frontend/lighthouse-performance.ts import lighthouse from 'lighthouse'; import * as chromeLauncher from 'chrome-launcher'; import * as fs from 'fs'; import * as path from 'path'; export interface PerformanceThresholds { performance: number; accessibility: number; bestPractices: number; seo: number; firstContentfulPaint: number; largestContentfulPaint: number; firstInputDelay: number; cumulativeLayoutShift: number; } export class FrontendPerformanceTester { private defaultThresholds: PerformanceThresholds = { performance: 90, accessibility: 95, bestPractices: 90, seo: 90, firstContentfulPaint: 1500, largestContentfulPaint: 2500, firstInputDelay: 100, cumulativeLayoutShift: 0.1, }; async runPerformanceTests( urls: string[], thresholds: Partial<PerformanceThresholds> = {} ): Promise<boolean> { const finalThresholds = { ...this.defaultThresholds, ...thresholds }; let allTestsPassed = true; for (const url of urls) { console.log(`Testing performance for: ${url}`); const chrome = await chromeLauncher.launch({ chromeFlags: ['--headless'] }); try { const options = { logLevel: 'info' as const, output: 'json' as const, onlyCategories: ['performance', 'accessibility', 'best-practices', 'seo'], port: chrome.port, }; const runnerResult = await lighthouse(url, options); if (!runnerResult || !runnerResult.report) { console.error(`Failed to run Lighthouse for ${url}`); allTestsPassed = false; continue; } const report = JSON.parse(runnerResult.report); const testResult = this.validatePerformanceResults(report, finalThresholds); if (!testResult.passed) { console.error(`Performance test failed for ${url}:`); testResult.failures.forEach(failure => console.error(` - ${failure}`)); allTestsPassed = false; } else { console.log(`✅ Performance test passed for ${url}`); } // Save detailed report await this.saveDetailedReport(url, report); } finally { await chrome.kill(); } } return allTestsPassed; } private validatePerformanceResults( report: any, thresholds: PerformanceThresholds ): { passed: boolean; failures: string[] } { const failures: string[] = []; const categories = report.categories; const audits = report.audits; // Check category scores if (categories.performance.score * 100 < thresholds.performance) { failures.push(`Performance score: ${Math.round(categories.performance.score * 100)} < ${thresholds.performance}`); } if (categories.accessibility.score * 100 < thresholds.accessibility) { failures.push(`Accessibility score: ${Math.round(categories.accessibility.score * 100)} < ${thresholds.accessibility}`); } if (categories['best-practices'].score * 100 < thresholds.bestPractices) { failures.push(`Best practices score: ${Math.round(categories['best-practices'].score * 100)} < ${thresholds.bestPractices}`); } if (categories.seo.score * 100 < thresholds.seo) { failures.push(`SEO score: ${Math.round(categories.seo.score * 100)} < ${thresholds.seo}`); } // Check Core Web Vitals const fcp = audits['first-contentful-paint'].numericValue; if (fcp > thresholds.firstContentfulPaint) { failures.push(`First Contentful Paint: ${Math.round(fcp)}ms > ${thresholds.firstContentfulPaint}ms`); } const lcp = audits['largest-contentful-paint'].numericValue; if (lcp > thresholds.largestContentfulPaint) { failures.push(`Largest Contentful Paint: ${Math.round(lcp)}ms > ${thresholds.largestContentfulPaint}ms`); } const cls = audits['cumulative-layout-shift'].numericValue; if (cls > thresholds.cumulativeLayoutShift) { failures.push(`Cumulative Layout Shift: ${cls.toFixed(3)} > ${thresholds.cumulativeLayoutShift}`); } return { passed: failures.length === 0, failures, }; } private async saveDetailedReport(url: string, report: any): Promise<void> { const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-'); const filename = `performance-${url.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '_')}-${timestamp}.json`; const filepath = path.join('reports', 'performance', filename); // Ensure directory exists const dir = path.dirname(filepath); if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) { fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); } fs.writeFileSync(filepath, JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)); console.log(`Detailed performance report saved to: ${filepath}`); } } // Usage example async function runTests() { const tester = new FrontendPerformanceTester(); const urls = [ 'http://localhost:3000', 'http://localhost:3000/users', 'http://localhost:3000/dashboard', ]; const customThresholds = { performance: 85, // Slightly lower threshold for complex pages largestContentfulPaint: 3000, // Allow 3s for LCP }; const passed = await tester.runPerformanceTests(urls, customThresholds); // tests/security/security-scanner.ts import { ZAPClient } from 'zaproxy'; import axios from 'axios'; import * as fs from 'fs'; import * as path from 'path'; export interface SecurityTestConfig { targetUrl: string; apiEndpoints: string[]; authToken?: string; excludeUrls: string[]; scanPolicies: string[]; } export interface SecurityVulnerability { name: string; risk: 'High' | 'Medium' | 'Low' | 'Informational'; confidence: 'High' | 'Medium' | 'Low'; const status = await this.zap.ascan.status(scanId); progress = parseInt(status); console.log(`Active scan progress: ${progress}%`); } } private async getVulnerabilities(): Promise { const alerts = await this.zap.core.alerts(); return acc; }, {} as Record); } } // API Security Testing export class APISecurityTester { async testAPIEndpoints(baseUrl: string, endpoints: string[], authToken?: string): Promise { const headers = authToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}` } : {}; for (const endpoint of endpoints) { await this.testSQLInjection(baseUrl + endpoint, headers); await this.testXSSVulnerabilities(baseUrl + endpoint, headers); await this.testAuthentication(baseUrl + endpoint); await this.testAuthorization(baseUrl + endpoint, headers); await this.testRateLimiting(baseUrl + endpoint, headers); } } private async testSQLInjection(url: string, headers: any): Promise { const sqlPayloads = [ "' OR '1'='1", "'; DROP TABLE users; --", "' UNION SELECT * FROM users --", "1' AND 1=1 --", ]; for (const payload of sqlPayloads) { try { const response = await axios.get(url, { params: { q: payload }, headers, timeout: 5000, }); // Check for SQL error messages if (response.data.includes('SQL') || response.data.includes('mysql') || response.data.includes('postgres')) { console.warn(`⚠️ Potential SQL injection vulnerability in ${url}`); } } catch (error) { // Expected for malformed requests } } } private async testXSSVulnerabilities(url: string, headers: any): Promise { const xssPayloads = [ "", "javascript:alert('XSS')", "", "';alert('XSS');//", ]; for (const payload of xssPayloads) { try { const response = await axios.post(url, { data: payload }, { headers }); if (response.data.includes(payload)) { console.warn(`⚠️ Potential XSS vulnerability in ${url}`); } } catch (error) { // Expected for malformed requests } } } private async testAuthentication(url: string): Promise { try { const response = await axios.get(url); if (response.status === 200) { console.warn(`⚠️ Endpoint ${url} accessible without authentication`); } } catch (error) { // Expected - endpoint should require authentication } } private async testAuthorization(url: string, headers: any): Promise { // Test with modified/expired token const modifiedHeaders = { ...headers, Authorization: headers.Authorization?.replace(/.$/, 'X'), // Modify last character }; try { const response = await axios.get(url, { headers: modifiedHeaders }); if (response.status === 200) { console.warn(`⚠️ Endpoint ${url} accessible with invalid token`); } } catch (error) { // Expected - should reject invalid tokens } } private async testRateLimiting(url: string, headers: any): Promise { const requests = Array.from({ length: 100 }, () => axios.get(url, { headers, timeout: 1000 }).catch(() => null) ); const responses = await Promise.all(requests); const successfulRequests = responses.filter(r => r && r.status === 200).length; if (successfulRequests > 50) { console.warn(`⚠️ Potential rate limiting issue in ${url}: ${successfulRequests}/100 requests succeeded`); // tests/scalability/auto-scaling-test.ts import { execSync } from 'child_process'; import axios from 'axios'; import * as k8s from '@kubernetes/client-node'; export interface ScalabilityTest { name: string; targetLoad: number; expectedScaling: { minReplicas: number; maxReplicas: number; targetCPU: number; targetMemory: number; }; duration: number; } export class ScalabilityValidator { private k8sApi: k8s.AppsV1Api; private metricsApi: k8s.Metrics; constructor() { const kc = new k8s.KubeConfig(); kc.loadFromDefault(); this.k8sApi = kc.makeApiClient(k8s.AppsV1Api); this.metricsApi = new k8s.Metrics(kc); } async runScalabilityTest(test: ScalabilityTest): Promise<boolean> { console.log(`Starting scalability test: ${test.name}`); try { // Record initial state const initialMetrics = await this.getCurrentMetrics(); // Generate load await this.generateLoad(test.targetLoad, test.duration); // Monitor scaling behavior const scalingResults = await this.monitorScaling(test); // Validate results const passed = this.validateScalingBehavior(scalingResults, test.expectedScaling); // Generate report await this.generateScalabilityReport(test, initialMetrics, scalingResults, passed); return passed; } catch (error) { console.error(`Scalability test failed: ${error}`); return false; } } private async generateLoad(targetRPS: number, duration: number): Promise<void> { const k6Script = ` import http from 'k6/http'; import { check } from 'k6'; export let options = { stages: [ { duration: '30s', target: ${targetRPS} }, { duration: '${duration}s', target: ${targetRPS} }, { duration: '30s', target: 0 }, ], }; export default function() { let response = http.get('${process.env.TARGET_URL || 'http://localhost:3000'}/api/health'); check(response, { 'status is 200': (r) => r.status === 200, }); } `; // Write temporary K6 script require('fs').writeFileSync('/tmp/load-test.js', k6Script); // Run load test in background const loadTestProcess = execSync('k6 run /tmp/load-test.js', { stdio: 'pipe', timeout: (duration + 120) * 1000, }); console.log('Load test completed'); } private async monitorScaling(test: ScalabilityTest): Promise<any> { const metrics: any[] = []; const startTime = Date.now(); const monitorDuration = (test.duration + 120) * 1000; // Monitor for test duration + buffer while (Date.now() - startTime < monitorDuration) { try { const currentMetrics = await this.getCurrentMetrics(); metrics.push({ timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), ...currentMetrics, }); console.log(`Replicas: ${currentMetrics.replicas}, CPU: ${currentMetrics.avgCPU}%, Memory: ${currentMetrics.avgMemory}%`); // Wait 30 seconds before next measurement await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 30000)); } catch (error) { console.error('Error collecting metrics:', error); } } return metrics; } private async getCurrentMetrics(): Promise<any> { // Get deployment info const deployment = await this.k8sApi.readNamespacedDeployment('app-backend', 'default'); const replicas = deployment.body.status?.replicas || 0; // Get pod metrics const podMetrics = await this.metricsApi.getPodMetrics('default'); let totalCPU = 0; let totalMemory = 0; let podCount = 0; for (const pod of podMetrics.body.items) { if (pod.metadata?.name?.startsWith('app-backend')) { podCount++; for (const container of pod.containers) { // Parse CPU usage (convert from nano cores) const cpuUsage = parseInt(container.usage.cpu.replace('n', '')) / 1000000; // Convert to millicores totalCPU += cpuUsage; // Parse memory usage (convert from Ki to MB) const memoryUsage = parseInt(container.usage.memory.replace('Ki', '')) / 1024; totalMemory += memoryUsage; } } } return { replicas, avgCPU: podCount > 0 ? totalCPU / podCount : 0, avgMemory: podCount > 0 ? totalMemory / podCount : 0, podCount, }; } private validateScalingBehavior(metrics: any[], expected: any): boolean { if (metrics.length === 0) { console.error('No metrics collected'); return false; } // Find peak metrics const peakReplicas = Math.max(...metrics.map(m => m.replicas)); const peakCPU = Math.max(...metrics.map(m => m.avgCPU)); const peakMemory = Math.max(...metrics.map(m => m.avgMemory)); console.log(`Peak metrics - Replicas: ${peakReplicas}, CPU: ${peakCPU}%, Memory: ${peakMemory}%`); // Validate scaling behavior const scalingValidation = { replicasInRange: peakReplicas >= expected.minReplicas && peakReplicas <= expected.maxReplicas, cpuUnderLimit: peakCPU <= expected.targetCPU * 1.2, // Allow 20% buffer memoryUnderLimit: peakMemory <= expected.targetMemory * 1.2, scalingOccurred: peakReplicas > expected.minReplicas, }; const passed = Object.values(scalingValidation).every(v => v); if (!passed) { console.error('Scaling validation failed:', scalingValidation); } return passed; } private async generateScalabilityReport( test: ScalabilityTest, initialMetrics: any, scalingResults: any[], passed: boolean ): Promise<void> { const report = { testName: test.name, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), passed, initialMetrics, scalingResults, summary: { maxReplicas: Math.max(...scalingResults.map(m => m.replicas)), maxCPU: Math.max(...scalingResults.map(m => m.avgCPU)), maxMemory: Math.max(...scalingResults.map(m => m.avgMemory)), averageReplicas: scalingResults.reduce((sum, m) => sum + m.replicas, 0) / scalingResults.length, }, }; const reportPath = `reports/scalability/scalability-${test.name}-${Date.now()}.json`; require('fs').writeFileSync(reportPath, JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)); console.log(`Scalability report saved to: ${reportPath}`); } }

// tests/accessibility/accessibility-validator.ts import { AxePuppeteer } from '@axe-core/puppeteer'; import puppeteer from 'puppeteer'; import * as fs from 'fs'; import * as path from 'path'; export interface AccessibilityTest { url: string; name: string; tags?: string[]; rules?: string[]; disableRules?: string[]; } export interface AccessibilityViolation { id: string; impact: 'minor' | 'moderate' | 'serious' | 'critical'; description: string; help: string; helpUrl: string; nodes: Array<{ html: string; target: string[]; failureSummary: string; }>; } export class AccessibilityValidator { async runAccessibilityTests(tests: AccessibilityTest[]): Promise<boolean> { console.log('Starting accessibility validation...'); const browser = await puppeteer.launch({ headless: true, args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-setuid-sandbox'], }); let allTestsPassed = true; try { for (const test of tests) { console.log(`Testing accessibility for: ${test.name}`); const page = await browser.newPage(); try { // Navigate to page await page.goto(test.url, { waitUntil: 'networkidle0' }); // Wait for dynamic content await page.waitForTimeout(2000); // Configure axe const axe = new AxePuppeteer(page); if (test.tags) { axe.withTags(test.tags); } if (test.rules) { axe.withRules(test.rules); } if (test.disableRules) { axe.disableRules(test.disableRules); } // Run accessibility scan const results = await axe.analyze(); // Process results const testPassed = this.processResults(test, results); if (!testPassed) { allTestsPassed = false; } } finally { await page.close(); } } } finally { await browser.close(); } return allTestsPassed; } private processResults(test: AccessibilityTest, results: any): boolean { const violations: AccessibilityViolation[] = results.violations.map((violation: any) => ({ id: violation.id, impact: violation.impact, description: violation.description, help: violation.help, helpUrl: violation.helpUrl, nodes: violation.nodes.map((node: any) => ({ html: node.html, target: node.target, failureSummary: node.failureSummary, })), })); // Log results if (violations.length === 0) { console.log(`✅ ${test.name}: No accessibility violations found`); return true; } else { console.error(`❌ ${test.name}: ${violations.length} accessibility violations found`); // Group violations by impact const violationsByImpact = violations.reduce((acc, violation) => { acc[violation.impact] = (acc[violation.impact] || 0) + 1; return acc; }, {} as Record<string, number>); console.error('Violations by impact:', violationsByImpact); // Save detailed report this.saveAccessibilityReport(test, violations); // Determine if test should fail based on impact const criticalViolations = violations.filter(v => v.impact === 'critical').length; const seriousViolations = violations.filter(v => v.impact === 'serious').length; // Fail test if there are critical or more than 5 serious violations return criticalViolations === 0 && seriousViolations <= 5; } } private saveAccessibilityReport(test: AccessibilityTest, violations: AccessibilityViolation[]): void { const report = { testName: test.name, url: test.url, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), violationCount: violations.length, violations, }; const reportPath = path.join('reports', 'accessibility', `a11y-${test.name.replace(/\s+/g, '-')}-${Date.now()}.json`); // Ensure directory exists const dir = path.dirname(reportPath); if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) { fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }); } fs.writeFileSync(reportPath, JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)); console.log(`Accessibility report saved to: ${reportPath}`); } } // Specific accessibility tests for common scenarios export class AccessibilityTestSuite { private validator = new AccessibilityValidator(); async runFullSuite(baseUrl: string): Promise<boolean> { const tests: AccessibilityTest[] = [ { name: 'Homepage', url: `${baseUrl}/`, tags: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'], }, { name: 'Login Page', url: `${baseUrl}/login`, tags: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'], }, { name: 'User Dashboard', url: `${baseUrl}/dashboard`, tags: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'], }, { name: 'Forms - User Registration', url: `${baseUrl}/register`, tags: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'], rules: ['label', 'color-contrast', 'keyboard-navigation'], }, { name: 'Navigation and Menus', url: `${baseUrl}/`, tags: ['wcag2a'], rules: ['focus-order-semantics', 'link-purpose', 'skip-link'], }, { name: 'Data Tables', url: `${baseUrl}/users`, tags: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'], rules: ['table-headers', 'table-caption'], }, ]; return await this.validator.runAccessibilityTests(tests); } }

// tests/compliance/gdpr-validator.ts import axios from 'axios'; import * as puppeteer from 'puppeteer'; export interface GDPRComplianceCheck { name: string; endpoint?: string; pageUrl?: string; expected: { cookieConsent: boolean; privacyPolicy: boolean; dataPortability: boolean; rightToErasure: boolean; consentWithdrawal: boolean; }; } export class GDPRComplianceValidator { async validateGDPRCompliance(baseUrl: string): Promise<boolean> { console.log('Starting GDPR compliance validation...'); const checks: GDPRComplianceCheck[] = [ { name: 'Cookie Consent Banner', pageUrl: `${baseUrl}/`, expected: { cookieConsent: true, privacyPolicy: false, dataPortability: false, rightToErasure: false, consentWithdrawal: false, }, }, { name: 'Privacy Policy Accessibility', pageUrl: `${baseUrl}/privacy`, expected: { cookieConsent: false, privacyPolicy: true, dataPortability: false, rightToErasure: false, consentWithdrawal: false, }, }, { name: 'Data Export Functionality', endpoint: `${baseUrl}/api/users/me/export`, expected: { cookieConsent: false, privacyPolicy: false, dataPortability: true, rightToErasure: false, consentWithdrawal: false, }, }, { name: 'Account Deletion', endpoint: `${baseUrl}/api/users/me`, expected: { cookieConsent: false, privacyPolicy: false, dataPortability: false, rightToErasure: true, consentWithdrawal: false, }, }, { name: 'Consent Management', pageUrl: `${baseUrl}/settings/privacy`, expected: { cookieConsent: false, privacyPolicy: false, dataPortability: false, rightToErasure: false, consentWithdrawal: true, }, }, ]; let allChecksPassed = true; for (const check of checks) { try { const result = await this.performGDPRCheck(check); if (!result) { console.error(`❌ GDPR check failed: ${check.name}`); allChecksPassed = false; } else { console.log(`✅ GDPR check passed: ${check.name}`); } } catch (error) { console.error(`❌ GDPR check error for ${check.name}:`, error); allChecksPassed = false; } } return allChecksPassed; } private async performGDPRCheck(check: GDPRComplianceCheck): Promise<boolean> { if (check.pageUrl) { return this.checkPageCompliance(check); } else if (check.endpoint) { return this.checkAPICompliance(check); } return false; } private async checkPageCompliance(check: GDPRComplianceCheck): Promise<boolean> { const browser = await puppeteer.launch({ headless: true }); try { const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.goto(check.pageUrl!, { waitUntil: 'networkidle0' }); let checksPassed = true; if (check.expected.cookieConsent) { const cookieBanner = await page.$('[data-testid="cookie-consent"], .cookie-banner, .cookie-notice'); if (!cookieBanner) { console.error('Cookie consent banner not found'); checksPassed = false; } // Check for reject option const rejectButton = await page.$('[data-testid="reject-cookies"], button:contains("Reject"), button:contains("Decline")'); if (!rejectButton) { console.error('Cookie rejection option not found'); checksPassed = false; } } if (check.expected.privacyPolicy) { const privacyContent = await page.$('[data-testid="privacy-policy"], .privacy-policy'); if (!privacyContent) { console.error('Privacy policy content not found'); checksPassed = false; } // Check for required GDPR elements const pageContent = await page.content(); const requiredTerms = [ 'data controller', 'legal basis', 'data retention', 'right to access', 'right to rectification', 'right to erasure', 'right to portability', ]; for (const term of requiredTerms) { if (!pageContent.toLowerCase().includes(term)) { console.error(`Privacy policy missing required term: ${term}`); checksPassed = false; } } } if (check.expected.consentWithdrawal) { const consentSettings = await page.$('[data-testid="consent-settings"], .consent-management'); if (!consentSettings) { console.error('Consent management interface not found'); checksPassed = false; } } return checksPassed; } finally { await browser.close(); } } private async checkAPICompliance(check: GDPRComplianceCheck): Promise<boolean> { // This would require authentication in real scenarios const authToken = process.env.TEST_AUTH_TOKEN; if (!authToken) { console.warn('No auth token provided for API compliance check'); return true; // Skip if no auth available } const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${authToken}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', }; if (check.expected.dataPortability) { try { const response = await axios.get(check.endpoint!, { headers }); if (response.status !== 200) { console.error('Data export endpoint not accessible'); return false; } // Check if response contains user data in structured format const data = response.data; if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') { console.error('Data export does not return structured data'); return false; } // Check for personal data fields const expectedFields = ['email', 'name', 'created_at']; for (const field of expectedFields) { if (!(field in data)) { console.error(`Data export missing field: ${field}`); return false; } } } catch (error) { console.error('Data export endpoint failed:', error); return false; } } if (check.expected.rightToErasure) { try { // Check if DELETE method is supported const response = await axios.delete(check.endpoint!, { headers, validateStatus: () => true, // Don't throw on any status }); if (response.status !== 200 && response.status !== 204) { console.error('Account deletion endpoint not properly implemented'); return false; } } catch (error) { console.error('Account deletion endpoint failed:', error); return false; } } return true; } }

// tools/monitoring/nfr-monitor.ts export interface NFRMetrics { performance: { responseTime: number; throughput: number; errorRate: number; availability: number; }; security: { vulnerabilityCount: number; lastScanDate: Date; securityScore: number; }; scalability: { currentReplicas: number; cpuUtilization: number; memoryUtilization: number; autoScalingEvents: number; }; reliability: { uptime: number; mtbf: number; // Mean Time Between Failures mttr: number; // Mean Time To Recovery }; usability: { accessibilityScore: number; performanceScore: number; lastAuditDate: Date; }; } export class NFRMonitor { async collectMetrics(): Promise<NFRMetrics> { const [performance, security, scalability, reliability, usability] = await Promise.all([ this.collectPerformanceMetrics(), this.collectSecurityMetrics(), this.collectScalabilityMetrics(), this.collectReliabilityMetrics(), this.collectUsabilityMetrics(), ]); return { performance, security, scalability, reliability, usability, }; } private async collectPerformanceMetrics() { // Implementation would integrate with monitoring tools like Prometheus return { responseTime: 150, // ms throughput: 1200, // requests/second errorRate: 0.5, // percentage availability: 99.9, // percentage }; } private async collectSecurityMetrics() { return { vulnerabilityCount: 2, lastScanDate: new Date(), securityScore: 85, }; } private async collectScalabilityMetrics() { return { currentReplicas: 3, cpuUtilization: 65, memoryUtilization: 70, autoScalingEvents: 5, }; } private async collectReliabilityMetrics() { return { uptime: 99.95, mtbf: 720, // hours mttr: 15, // minutes }; } private async collectUsabilityMetrics() { return { accessibilityScore: 92, performanceScore: 88, lastAuditDate: new Date(), }; } async validateNFRThresholds(metrics: NFRMetrics): Promise<boolean> { const thresholds = { performance: { responseTime: 500, errorRate: 1.0, availability: 99.5, }, security: { maxVulnerabilities: 5, minSecurityScore: 80, }, scalability: { maxCpuUtilization: 80, maxMemoryUtilization: 85, }, reliability: { minUptime: 99.0, maxMttr: 30, }, usability: { minAccessibilityScore: 90, minPerformanceScore: 85, }, }; const violations: string[] = []; // Check performance thresholds if (metrics.performance.responseTime > thresholds.performance.responseTime) { violations.push(`Response time: ${metrics.performance.responseTime}ms > ${thresholds.performance.responseTime}ms`); } if (metrics.performance.errorRate > thresholds.performance.errorRate) { violations.push(`Error rate: ${metrics.performance.errorRate}% > ${thresholds.performance.errorRate}%`); } if (metrics.performance.availability < thresholds.performance.availability) { violations.push(`Availability: ${metrics.performance.availability}% < ${thresholds.performance.availability}%`); } // Check security thresholds if (metrics.security.vulnerabilityCount > thresholds.security.maxVulnerabilities) { violations.push(`Vulnerabilities: ${metrics.security.vulnerabilityCount} > ${thresholds.security.maxVulnerabilities}`); } if (metrics.security.securityScore < thresholds.security.minSecurityScore) { violations.push(`Security score: ${metrics.security.securityScore} < ${thresholds.security.minSecurityScore}`); } // Check scalability thresholds if (metrics.scalability.cpuUtilization > thresholds.scalability.maxCpuUtilization) { violations.push(`CPU utilization: ${metrics.scalability.cpuUtilization}% > ${thresholds.scalability.maxCpuUtilization}%`); } if (metrics.scalability.memoryUtilization > thresholds.scalability.maxMemoryUtilization) { violations.push(`Memory utilization: ${metrics.scalability.memoryUtilization}% > ${thresholds.scalability.maxMemoryUtilization}%`); } // Check reliability thresholds if (metrics.reliability.uptime < thresholds.reliability.minUptime) { violations.push(`Uptime: ${metrics.reliability.uptime}% < ${thresholds.reliability.minUptime}%`); } if (metrics.reliability.mttr > thresholds.reliability.maxMttr) { violations.push(`MTTR: ${metrics.reliability.mttr}min > ${thresholds.reliability.maxMttr}min`); } // Check usability thresholds if (metrics.usability.accessibilityScore < thresholds.usability.minAccessibilityScore) { violations.push(`Accessibility score: ${metrics.usability.accessibilityScore} < ${thresholds.usability.minAccessibilityScore}`); } if (metrics.usability.performanceScore < thresholds.usability.minPerformanceScore) { violations.push(`Performance score: ${metrics.usability.performanceScore} < ${thresholds.usability.minPerformanceScore}`); } if (violations.length > 0) { console.error('NFR threshold violations:', violations); return false; } console.log('✅ All NFR thresholds met'); return true; } }

Effective communication is the backbone of successful software development projects. This document provides comprehensive guidelines for establishing, maintaining, and optimizing communication channels between development teams, clients, stakeholders, and third parties.

The primary purpose of this guideline is to ensure that: Communication flows seamlessly across all project participants Information is accessible, timely, and accurate Teams continuously evaluate and improve their communication practices Business and technical discussions are properly facilitated and documented

Instant Messaging Platforms​ Slack: Team collaboration, quick updates, file sharing Microsoft Teams: Enterprise communication, video calls, document collaboration Google Chat: Real-time messaging, integration with Google Workspace Discord: Community-style communication for larger teams Best Practices: Use threaded conversations for complex discussions Establish clear channel naming conventions Set appropriate notification levels Use status indicators effectively Archive inactive channels regularly Video Conferencing​ Zoom: Client meetings, presentations, screen sharing Google Meet: Quick team sync-ups, daily standups Microsoft Teams: Enterprise meetings with recording capabilities Slack Huddles: Informal team discussions Best Practices: Always have an agenda for meetings Record important client meetings Use screen sharing for technical discussions Provide meeting summaries and action items

Email Communication​ Client Updates: Formal project status reports Stakeholder Communication: High-level project summaries Documentation Sharing: Contracts, specifications, compliance documents Best Practices: Use clear, descriptive subject lines Include relevant stakeholders in CC Follow up on action items Maintain professional tone and formatting Project Management Tools​ Jira: Issue tracking, sprint planning, technical discussions Trello: Visual project management, task assignments Asana: Project planning, milestone tracking Monday.com: Workflow management, status updates Best Practices: Link related issues and conversations Use consistent labeling and tagging Update status regularly Maintain clear issue descriptions

Knowledge Management​ Confluence: Project documentation, meeting notes, decisions Notion: Team wikis, process documentation GitBook: Technical documentation, API guides SharePoint: Document storage and collaboration Best Practices: Maintain version control for documents Use templates for consistency Implement search-friendly organization Regular content reviews and updates

By following these guidelines, teams can ensure that information flows smoothly, stakeholders stay informed, and communication processes continuously improve. Regular assessment and optimization of communication practices will lead to better project outcomes and stakeholder satisfaction. DORA metrics are four key indicators used to measure DevOps performance: Deployment Frequency: How often code is deployed to production. Lead Time for Changes: The time it takes for a code change to reach production. Change Failure Rate: The percentage of deployments that cause a failure in production. Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR): How quickly teams recover from a failure in production. These metrics help organizations assess and improve their software delivery and operational performance.

DORA metrics (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, Mean Time to Recovery) help measure DevOps performance. Datadog provides native support for DORA metrics and integrates with CI/CD, source control, and incident management tools.

To integrate your source control and CI/CD pipeline for DORA metrics collection: a. Connect GitHub to Datadog​ Go to Datadog Integrations and search for "GitHub". Follow the instructions to connect your repository. This enables Datadog to ingest commit, PR, and deployment data. Reference: Datadog GitHub Integration b. Enable CI Visibility for GitHub Actions​ In Datadog, enable CI Visibility for your organization. In your GitHub Actions workflow, add the Datadog CI Visibility Action: - name: Datadog CI Visibility uses: DataDog/ci-visibility-github-actions@v1 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.DATADOG_API_KEY }} datadog-site: datadoghq.com This will send pipeline, job, and test data to Datadog for analysis. Reference: Datadog CI Visibility c. Track Deployment Events​ In your deployment workflow, send deployment events to Datadog: - name: Notify Datadog of Deployment uses: DataDog/datadog-actions@v1 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.DATADOG_API_KEY }} datadog-site: datadoghq.com event-title: 'Deployment to production' event-text: 'Deployed commit ${{ github.sha }}' tags: 'env:production,service:api-gateway' This enables Datadog to correlate deployments with incidents and performance data for DORA metrics.

Use Datadog's Deployment Tracking to send deployment events from GitHub Actions or ArgoCD. Example GitHub Actions step: - name: Notify Datadog of Deployment uses: DataDog/datadog-actions@v1 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.DATADOG_API_KEY }} datadog-site: datadoghq.com event-title: 'Deployment to production' event-text: 'Deployed commit ${{ github.sha }}' tags: 'env:production,service:api-gateway'
Integrate incident management (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or Datadog monitors) to track change failure rate and MTTR. Use Datadog monitors to alert on failed deployments or service outages.
Use the DORA Metrics dashboard in Datadog to view and analyze metrics. Customize dashboards to filter by service, environment, or deployment type.

Add the following to your CI/CD pipeline to send deployment events: jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: # ... your build & deploy steps ... - name: Notify Datadog of Deployment uses: DataDog/datadog-actions@v1 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.DATADOG_API_KEY }} datadog-site: datadoghq.com event-title: 'Deployment to production' event-text: 'Deployed commit ${{ github.sha }}' tags: 'env:production,service:api-gateway'

You can automate DORA metric collection and visualization using GitHub Actions for data collection, BigQuery for storage and analysis, and Looker for dashboards.

documents.t: Add steps to your workflow to log deployment events and failures. Example: jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: # ... your build & deploy steps ... - name: Log deployment event run: | echo '{"timestamp": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)", "commit": "${GITHUB_SHA}", "status": "success", "workflow": "deploy"}' >> dora_metrics.json - name: Upload metrics to artifact uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3 with: name: dora_metrics path: dora_metrics.json For failures, add a similar step in the error handling section.
documents.s: Step 1: Collect DORA Data in GitHub Actions

documents.t: Use a scheduled workflow or post-deployment job to upload the metrics file to Google Cloud Storage. Example: jobs: export_metrics: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Download metrics artifact uses: actions/download-artifact@v3 with: name: dora_metrics - name: Upload to Google Cloud Storage uses: google-github-actions/upload-cloud-storage@v1 with: path: dora_metrics.json destination: gs://your-bucket/dora_metrics/ You can later import or query this data from BigQuery, or connect Looker directly to BigQuery after loading the data from Cloud Storage. You can later import or query this data from BigQuery, or connect Looker directly to BigQuery after loading the data from Cloud Storage. (Optional) Load Data from Google Cloud Storage to BigQuery​ After uploading your metrics file to Google Cloud Storage, you can load it into BigQuery using the bq CLI or a scheduled job: jobs: load_to_bigquery: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Load metrics from GCS to BigQuery run: | bq load --source_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON your_dataset.dora_metrics gs://your-bucket/dora_metrics/dora_metrics.json This step makes your metrics available for SQL analysis and Looker dashboards.​

Write SQL queries to calculate each metric: Deployment Frequency SELECT COUNT(*) AS deployments, DATE(timestamp) AS day FROM `your_dataset.dora_metrics` WHERE status = 'success' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC Lead Time for Changes SELECT AVG(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(deploy_time, commit_time, HOUR)) AS avg_lead_time FROM ( SELECT commit_time, MIN(deploy_time) AS deploy_time FROM `your_dataset.dora_metrics` GROUP BY commit_time ) Change Failure Rate SELECT COUNTIF(status = 'failure') / COUNT(*) AS failure_rate FROM `your_dataset.dora_metrics` MTTR SELECT AVG(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(recovery_time, failure_time, MINUTE)) AS avg_mttr FROM `your_dataset.incidents`

documents.t: Connect Looker to your BigQuery dataset. Create Looks and dashboards using the above queries. Use filters and charts to visualize trends over time. Notes: Enrich your metrics file with commit timestamps, deployment timestamps, and incident data as needed. Automate the workflow to run after every deployment or on a schedule. Ensure your GitHub Actions runner has access to Google Cloud credentials. Let me know if you want ready-to-use workflow YAMLs, BigQuery schema definitions, or Looker dashboard templates!

// Basic performance monitoring service @Injectable() export class BasicPerformanceMonitor { private readonly logger = new Logger(BasicPerformanceMonitor.name); constructor(private readonly datadogService: DatadogService, private readonly configService: ConfigService) {} // Infrastructure monitoring async collectInfrastructureMetrics(): Promise<InfrastructureMetrics> { return { cpu: await this.getCPUUsage(), memory: await this.getMemoryUsage(), disk: await this.getDiskUsage(), network: await this.getNetworkMetrics(), timestamp: new Date(), }; } // Application performance monitoring async collectApplicationMetrics(): Promise<ApplicationMetrics> { return { responseTime: await this.getAverageResponseTime(), throughput: await this.getRequestThroughput(), errorRate: await this.getErrorRate(), availability: await this.getAvailability(), timestamp: new Date(), }; } // Basic alerting async checkPerformanceThresholds(metrics: PerformanceMetrics): Promise<void> { const thresholds = this.configService.get('performance.thresholds'); if (metrics.responseTime > thresholds.maxResponseTime) { await this.sendAlert('HIGH_RESPONSE_TIME', metrics); } if (metrics.errorRate > thresholds.maxErrorRate) { await this.sendAlert('HIGH_ERROR_RATE', metrics); } if (metrics.availability < thresholds.minAvailability) { await this.sendAlert('LOW_AVAILABILITY', metrics); } } }

// Advanced performance monitoring with SLI/SLO @Injectable() export class AdvancedPerformanceMonitor { private readonly performanceAnalyzer: PerformanceAnalyzer; constructor( private readonly datadogService: DatadogService, private readonly performanceBudgetService: PerformanceBudgetService, ) { this.performanceAnalyzer = new PerformanceAnalyzer(); } // SLI/SLO monitoring async monitorServiceLevelIndicators(): Promise<SLIReport> { const slis = await Promise.all([ this.measureAvailability(), this.measureLatency(), this.measureThroughput(), this.measureErrorRate(), ]); return { availability: slis[0], latency: slis[1], throughput: slis[2], errorRate: slis[3], sloCompliance: await this.calculateSLOCompliance(slis), timestamp: new Date(), }; } // Performance budget monitoring async validatePerformanceBudgets(): Promise<BudgetValidationResult> { const currentMetrics = await this.collectCurrentMetrics(); const budgets = await this.performanceBudgetService.getBudgets(); const violations = budgets.filter((budget) => currentMetrics[budget.metric] > budget.threshold); if (violations.length > 0) { await this.handleBudgetViolations(violations); } return { budgets, violations, compliance: ((budgets.length - violations.length) / budgets.length) * 100, }; } // Performance trend analysis async analyzePerformanceTrends(): Promise<TrendAnalysis> { const historicalData = await this.getHistoricalMetrics(30); // 30 days return this.performanceAnalyzer.analyzeTrends(historicalData); } }

// Real-time performance analytics with distributed tracing @Injectable() export class RealTimePerformanceAnalytics { private readonly tracingService: DistributedTracingService; private readonly chaosEngineeringService: ChaosEngineeringService; constructor( private readonly openTelemetryService: OpenTelemetryService, private readonly performanceOptimizer: PerformanceOptimizer, ) {} // Distributed tracing analysis async analyzeDistributedTrace(traceId: string): Promise<TraceAnalysis> { const trace = await this.tracingService.getTrace(traceId); return { totalDuration: trace.duration, spans: trace.spans.map((span) => ({ serviceName: span.serviceName, operationName: span.operationName, duration: span.duration, errors: span.errors, })), bottlenecks: this.identifyBottlenecks(trace), recommendations: await this.generateOptimizationRecommendations(trace), }; } // Performance chaos engineering async runChaosExperiments(): Promise<ChaosExperimentResults> { const experiments = [ { name: 'database_latency', type: 'latency_injection' }, { name: 'service_failure', type: 'service_kill' }, { name: 'network_partition', type: 'network_failure' }, ]; const results = await Promise.all(experiments.map((exp) => this.chaosEngineeringService.runExperiment(exp))); return { experiments: results, performanceImpact: await this.assessPerformanceImpact(results), recommendations: await this.generateResilienceRecommendations(results), }; } // Real-time performance optimization async optimizePerformanceRealTime(): Promise<OptimizationResults> { const currentMetrics = await this.collectRealTimeMetrics(); const optimizations = await this.performanceOptimizer.suggest(currentMetrics); // Auto-apply safe optimizations const safeOptimizations = optimizations.filter((opt) => opt.risk === 'low'); const results = await Promise.all(safeOptimizations.map((opt) => this.applyOptimization(opt))); return { applied: safeOptimizations, pending: optimizations.filter((opt) => opt.risk !== 'low'), results, }; } }

// AI-powered performance prediction and optimization @Injectable() export class PredictivePerformanceManager { private readonly mlService: MachineLearningService; private readonly businessCorrelationService: BusinessCorrelationService; constructor( private readonly performancePredictor: PerformancePredictor, private readonly autoRemediationService: AutoRemediationService, ) {} // Performance prediction using ML async predictPerformanceTrends(): Promise<PerformancePrediction> { const historicalData = await this.getHistoricalPerformanceData(); const businessData = await this.businessCorrelationService.getBusinessMetrics(); const prediction = await this.mlService.predict({ features: this.extractFeatures(historicalData, businessData), model: 'performance_prediction_v2', horizon: '7d', // 7-day prediction }); return { predictedMetrics: prediction.metrics, confidence: prediction.confidence, anomalies: prediction.anomalies, recommendations: await this.generatePredictiveRecommendations(prediction), }; } // Business impact correlation async correlateBusiness​PerformanceImpact(): Promise<BusinessImpactAnalysis> { const performanceMetrics = await this.collectPerformanceMetrics(); const businessMetrics = await this.businessCorrelationService.getBusinessMetrics(); const correlations = await this.mlService.correlate({ performance: performanceMetrics, business: businessMetrics, }); return { correlations, revenueImpact: this.calculateRevenueImpact(correlations), customerExperienceImpact: this.calculateCXImpact(correlations), optimizationPriorities: this.prioritizeOptimizations(correlations), }; } // Automated performance remediation async autoRemediate(): Promise<RemediationResults> { const issues = await this.detectPerformanceIssues(); const remediationPlans = await this.generateRemediationPlans(issues); const results = await Promise.all( remediationPlans.map(plan => this.autoRemediationService.execute(plan)) ); return { issues, remediationPlans, results, successRate: this.calculateSuccessRate(results), }; } }

// Performance testing orchestrator @Injectable() export class PerformanceTestOrchestrator { private readonly loadTester: LoadTestService; private readonly stressTester: StressTestService; private readonly spikeTester: SpikeTestService; constructor(private readonly k6Service: K6TestService, private readonly artilleryService: ArtilleryTestService) {} // Comprehensive performance test suite async runPerformanceTestSuite(): Promise<PerformanceTestResults> { const testSuite = [ this.runLoadTests(), this.runStressTests(), this.runSpikeTests(), this.runVolumeTests(), this.runEnduranceTests(), ]; const results = await Promise.allSettled(testSuite); return { loadTest: results[0].status === 'fulfilled' ? results[0].value : null, stressTest: results[1].status === 'fulfilled' ? results[1].value : null, spikeTest: results[2].status === 'fulfilled' ? results[2].value : null, volumeTest: results[3].status === 'fulfilled' ? results[3].value : null, enduranceTest: results[4].status === 'fulfilled' ? results[4].value : null, summary: this.generateTestSummary(results), }; } // Load testing implementation async runLoadTests(): Promise<LoadTestResult> { const testConfig = { stages: [ { duration: '2m', target: 100 }, // Ramp up { duration: '5m', target: 100 }, // Stay at 100 users { duration: '2m', target: 200 }, // Ramp up to 200 { duration: '5m', target: 200 }, // Stay at 200 users { duration: '2m', target: 0 }, // Ramp down ], scenarios: { browse_products: { weight: 40, exec: 'browseProducts' }, add_to_cart: { weight: 30, exec: 'addToCart' }, checkout: { weight: 20, exec: 'checkout' }, user_profile: { weight: 10, exec: 'userProfile' }, }, }; return await this.k6Service.runTest('load-test', testConfig); } // Stress testing implementation async runStressTests(): Promise<StressTestResult> { const testConfig = { stages: [ { duration: '2m', target: 100 }, // Normal load { duration: '5m', target: 100 }, { duration: '2m', target: 200 }, // Around normal load { duration: '5m', target: 200 }, { duration: '2m', target: 300 }, // Around the breaking point { duration: '5m', target: 300 }, { duration: '2m', target: 400 }, // Beyond the breaking point { duration: '5m', target: 400 }, { duration: '10m', target: 0 }, // Scale down. Recovery stage. ], thresholds: { http_req_duration: ['p(99)<1500'], // 99% of requests under 1.5s http_req_failed: ['rate<0.1'], // Error rate under 10% }, }; return await this.k6Service.runTest('stress-test', testConfig); } }

// E-commerce specific performance test scenarios export class EcommercePerformanceScenarios { // Product browsing scenario async browseProducts(session: K6Session): Promise<void> { // Home page let response = await session.get('/'); session.check(response, { 'home page status': (r) => r.status === 200, 'home page duration': (r) => r.timings.duration < 2000, }); session.sleep(1); // Category page response = await session.get('/category/electronics'); session.check(response, { 'category page status': (r) => r.status === 200, 'category page duration': (r) => r.timings.duration < 1500, }); session.sleep(2); // Product detail page const productId = this.getRandomProductId(); response = await session.get(`/product/${productId}`); session.check(response, { 'product page status': (r) => r.status === 200, 'product page duration': (r) => r.timings.duration < 1000, }); } // Shopping cart scenario async addToCart(session: K6Session): Promise<void> { // Login first await this.loginUser(session); // Add product to cart const productId = this.getRandomProductId(); const response = await session.post('/api/cart/add', { productId, quantity: Math.floor(Math.random() * 3) + 1, }); session.check(response, { 'add to cart status': (r) => r.status === 200, 'add to cart duration': (r) => r.timings.duration < 500, }); // View cart const cartResponse = await session.get('/cart'); session.check(cartResponse, { 'cart view status': (r) => r.status === 200, 'cart view duration': (r) => r.timings.duration < 800, }); } // Checkout scenario async checkout(session: K6Session): Promise<void> { await this.loginUser(session); await this.addToCart(session); // Checkout process let response = await session.get('/checkout'); session.check(response, { 'checkout page status': (r) => r.status === 200, }); // Submit order response = await session.post('/api/orders', { shippingAddress: this.getTestAddress(), paymentMethod: 'credit_card', paymentDetails: this.getTestPaymentDetails(), }); session.check(response, { 'order creation status': (r) => r.status === 201, 'order creation duration': (r) => r.timings.duration < 2000, }); } }
