// Custom metrics for auto-scaling decisions @Injectable() export class CustomScalingMetrics { private readonly prometheusService: PrometheusService; constructor(private readonly businessMetricsService: BusinessMetricsService) {} // Business-driven scaling metrics async collectBusinessScalingMetrics(): Promise<BusinessScalingMetrics> { const metrics = await Promise.all([ this.getActiveShoppingSessions(), this.getCartAbandonmentRate(), this.getCheckoutCompletionRate(), this.getSearchRequestsPerSecond(), ]); return { activeShoppingSessions: metrics[0], cartAbandonmentRate: metrics[1], checkoutCompletionRate: metrics[2], searchRequestsPerSecond: metrics[3], scalingRecommendation: this.calculateScalingRecommendation(metrics), }; } // Predictive scaling based on historical patterns async predictiveScaling(): Promise<PredictiveScalingDecision> { const historicalData = await this.getHistoricalLoadPatterns(); const upcomingEvents = await this.getUpcomingBusinessEvents(); const prediction = this.analyzeLoadPatterns(historicalData, upcomingEvents); return { predictedLoad: prediction.load, recommendedReplicas: prediction.replicas, confidence: prediction.confidence, timeframe: prediction.timeframe, triggers: prediction.triggers, }; } // Queue-based scaling for background processes async queueBasedScaling(): Promise<QueueScalingDecision> { const queueMetrics = await Promise.all([ this.getMessageQueueDepth('order-processing'), this.getMessageQueueDepth('email-notifications'), this.getMessageQueueDepth('inventory-updates'), this.getMessageQueueDepth('search-indexing'), ]); return { queues: queueMetrics, scalingDecisions: this.calculateQueueScaling(queueMetrics), priorityQueues: this.identifyPriorityQueues(queueMetrics), }; } }

// Next.js performance optimization service @Injectable() export class FrontendPerformanceOptimizer { // Bundle optimization async optimizeBundles(): Promise<BundleOptimizationResult> { const currentBundleSize = await this.getCurrentBundleSize(); const optimizations = [ this.implementCodeSplitting(), this.optimizeImages(), this.implementTreeShaking(), this.enableCompressiont(), ]; const results = await Promise.all(optimizations); return { originalSize: currentBundleSize, optimizedSize: await this.getCurrentBundleSize(), improvements: results, performanceGain: this.calculatePerformanceGain(results), }; } // Core Web Vitals optimization async optimizeCoreWebVitals(): Promise<CoreWebVitalsOptimization> { const currentMetrics = await this.measureCoreWebVitals(); const optimizations = { LCP: await this.optimizeLargestContentfulPaint(), FID: await this.optimizeFirstInputDelay(), CLS: await this.optimizeCumulativeLayoutShift(), TTFB: await this.optimizeTimeToFirstByte(), }; return { before: currentMetrics, optimizations, after: await this.measureCoreWebVitals(), improvements: this.calculateImprovements(currentMetrics, optimizations), }; } // Caching strategy optimization async optimizeCachingStrategy(): Promise<CachingOptimizationResult> { const cacheAnalysis = await this.analyzeCachePerformance(); return { browserCache: await this.optimizeBrowserCaching(), cdnCache: await this.optimizeCDNCaching(), serviceWorker: await this.optimizeServiceWorkerCaching(), analysis: cacheAnalysis, }; } }

// NestJS microservices performance optimization @Injectable() export class BackendPerformanceOptimizer { // Database query optimization async optimizeDatabaseQueries(): Promise<DatabaseOptimizationResult> { const slowQueries = await this.identifySlowQueries(); const optimizations = await Promise.all(slowQueries.map((query) => this.optimizeQuery(query))); return { slowQueries, optimizations, performanceGain: await this.measureQueryPerformanceGain(), recommendations: this.generateDatabaseRecommendations(), }; } // Microservice communication optimization async optimizeMicroserviceCommunication(): Promise<CommunicationOptimizationResult> { return { grpc: await this.optimizeGRPCCommunication(), messageQueue: await this.optimizeMessageQueues(), circuitBreaker: await this.optimizeCircuitBreakers(), loadBalancing: await this.optimizeLoadBalancing(), }; } // Memory and CPU optimization async optimizeResourceUsage(): Promise<ResourceOptimizationResult> { const currentUsage = await this.getCurrentResourceUsage(); const optimizations = { memoryOptimization: await this.optimizeMemoryUsage(), cpuOptimization: await this.optimizeCPUUsage(), garbageCollection: await this.optimizeGarbageCollection(), }; return { before: currentUsage, optimizations, after: await this.getCurrentResourceUsage(), recommendations: this.generateResourceRecommendations(), }; } }

// Business performance correlation service @Injectable() export class BusinessPerformanceCorrelationService { // Revenue impact analysis async analyzeRevenueImpact(): Promise<RevenueImpactAnalysis> { const performanceMetrics = await this.getPerformanceMetrics(); const revenueMetrics = await this.getRevenueMetrics(); const correlations = this.calculateCorrelations(performanceMetrics, revenueMetrics); return { pageLoadTimeImpact: correlations.pageLoadTime, checkoutPerformanceImpact: correlations.checkoutPerformance, searchPerformanceImpact: correlations.searchPerformance, mobilePerformanceImpact: correlations.mobilePerformance, totalRevenueAtRisk: this.calculateRevenueAtRisk(correlations), optimizationPriorities: this.prioritizeByRevenueImpact(correlations), }; } // Customer experience metrics async measureCustomerExperience(): Promise<CustomerExperienceMetrics> { return { customerSatisfactionScore: await this.getCSAT(), netPromoterScore: await this.getNPS(), taskCompletionRate: await this.getTaskCompletionRate(), userEngagementMetrics: await this.getUserEngagement(), conversionRateByPerformance: await this.getConversionRateCorrelation(), }; } // Performance ROI calculation async calculatePerformanceROI(): Promise<PerformanceROIAnalysis> { const investments = await this.getPerformanceInvestments(); const benefits = await this.getPerformanceBenefits(); return { investments, benefits, roi: this.calculateROI(investments, benefits), paybackPeriod: this.calculatePaybackPeriod(investments, benefits), npv: this.calculateNPV(investments, benefits), }; } }

// Performance KPI dashboard service @Injectable() export class PerformanceKPIDashboard { // Executive performance dashboard async generateExecutiveDashboard(): Promise<ExecutivePerformanceDashboard> { return { performanceHealth: await this.getPerformanceHealthScore(), businessImpact: await this.getBusinessImpactMetrics(), userExperience: await this.getUserExperienceMetrics(), technicalMetrics: await this.getTechnicalMetrics(), trends: await this.getPerformanceTrends(), alerts: await this.getActivePerformanceAlerts(), recommendations: await this.getPerformanceRecommendations(), }; } // Technical performance dashboard async generateTechnicalDashboard(): Promise<TechnicalPerformanceDashboard> { return { applicationPerformance: await this.getApplicationMetrics(), infrastructurePerformance: await this.getInfrastructureMetrics(), databasePerformance: await this.getDatabaseMetrics(), networkPerformance: await this.getNetworkMetrics(), cachingPerformance: await this.getCachingMetrics(), scalingMetrics: await this.getScalingMetrics(), }; } // Real-time performance monitoring async getRealtimeMetrics(): Promise<RealtimePerformanceMetrics> { return { currentLoad: await this.getCurrentLoad(), responseTime: await this.getCurrentResponseTime(), errorRate: await this.getCurrentErrorRate(), throughput: await this.getCurrentThroughput(), activeUsers: await this.getActiveUsers(), systemHealth: await this.getSystemHealth(), }; } }

// Performance maturity assessment service @Injectable() export class PerformanceMaturityAssessment { // Comprehensive maturity assessment async assessMaturityLevel(): Promise<MaturityAssessmentResult> { const assessments = await Promise.all([ this.assessMonitoringMaturity(), this.assessTestingMaturity(), this.assessOptimizationMaturity(), this.assessAutomationMaturity(), this.assessCultureMaturity(), ]); return { overallMaturity: this.calculateOverallMaturity(assessments), areaAssessments: assessments, recommendations: this.generateMaturityRecommendations(assessments), roadmap: this.generateMaturityRoadmap(assessments), }; } // Monitoring maturity assessment async assessMonitoringMaturity(): Promise<MonitoringMaturityAssessment> { const criteria = { level1: { infrastructureMonitoring: await this.hasInfrastructureMonitoring(), applicationMonitoring: await this.hasApplicationMonitoring(), basicAlerting: await this.hasBasicAlerting(), }, level2: { performanceBudgets: await this.hasPerformanceBudgets(), sliSlo: await this.hasSLISLO(), trendAnalysis: await this.hasTrendAnalysis(), }, level3: { distributedTracing: await this.hasDistributedTracing(), realTimeAnalytics: await this.hasRealTimeAnalytics(), customMetrics: await this.hasCustomMetrics(), }, level4: { predictiveAnalytics: await this.hasPredictiveAnalytics(), businessCorrelation: await this.hasBusinessCorrelation(), mlBasedMonitoring: await this.hasMLBasedMonitoring(), }, level5: { innovativeMonitoring: await this.hasInnovativeMonitoring(), industryLeadership: await this.hasIndustryLeadership(), researchContribution: await this.hasResearchContribution(), }, }; return { currentLevel: this.calculateMonitoringLevel(criteria), criteria, gaps: this.identifyMonitoringGaps(criteria), recommendations: this.generateMonitoringRecommendations(criteria), }; } }

The system is designed to: Scale with your business growth Provide measurable business value Enable data-driven performance decisions Foster a performance-focused culture Drive continuous improvement Regular assessment against the maturity framework ensures continuous evolution and optimization of your performance capabilities. Handling an idempotency key in a REST API involves the client generating a unique key for each operation and sending it in an HTTP header. The server then uses this key to recognize and de-duplicate subsequent retries of the same request, ensuring that a sensitive operation is executed only once. This prevents common issues like accidental double payments or duplicate resource creation caused by network failures.
documents.s: Handling Idempotency Keys in a REST API

documents.t: In the context of APIs, idempotency means that making the same API call multiple times will produce the same result as making it just once. While methods like GET, PUT, and DELETE are naturally idempotent, POST is not. An idempotency key is a technique to make POST requests safe to retry. Think of it like an elevator button. Pushing it once calls the elevator. Pushing it ten more times while you wait doesn't call ten more elevators; the result is the same. An idempotency key brings this same "push-once" behavior to sensitive API calls.

The implementation involves a handshake between the client and the server. The most common header used is Idempotency-Key. Client-Side Responsibilities​ Generate a Unique Key: Before sending a request for a new operation, the client must generate a unique key. A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is the best choice for this. Send the Key in a Header: The client includes this key in the request header. Retry with the Same Key: If the client does not receive a response (e.g., due to a network timeout) and needs to retry, it must send the exact same request with the exact same Idempotency-Key. Server-Side Responsibilities​ The server's logic is the core of the implementation. Check for the Key: When a request with an Idempotency-Key arrives, the server checks its storage (e.g., a cache like Redis or a database table) to see if it has ever processed this key before. Handle Scenarios: Case 1: Key is New. If the key has not been seen before, the server processes the request as usual. Crucially, before sending the response, it saves the idempotency key and the resulting HTTP status code and body to its storage. Case 2: Key is Found. If the key exists in storage, the server does not re-process the request. Instead, it immediately returns the saved response (the same status code and body) from the original request. Case 3: Race Condition. If a request arrives with a key that is currently being processed by another request, the server should return an error, such as 409 Conflict, to indicate that the client should wait and try again.
documents.s: ## How to Implement an Idempotency Key

documents.t: Imagine a client wants to make a $100 transfer. 1. First Attempt (Successful) The client generates a unique key and sends the request. POST /transfers HTTP/1.1 Host: api.example.com Content-Type: application/json Idempotency-Key: a9a2f3a4-b1c4-4c8e-a9d2-3b2a8d3b7c4e { "amount": 100, "currency": "USD", "destination_account": "123456789" }

// shared/kafka/src/config/kafka.config.ts import { Transport } from '@nestjs/microservices'; export interface KafkaServiceConfig { clientId: string; groupId: string; brokers: string[]; } export const createKafkaConfig = (serviceConfig: KafkaServiceConfig) => ({ transport: Transport.KAFKA, options: { client: { clientId: serviceConfig.clientId, brokers: serviceConfig.brokers, retry: { initialRetryTime: 100, retries: 8, }, connectionTimeout: 3000, requestTimeout: 30000, }, consumer: { groupId: serviceConfig.groupId, allowAutoTopicCreation: false, sessionTimeout: 30000, heartbeatInterval: 3000, maxWaitTimeInMs: 5000, retry: { retries: 5, }, }, producer: { allowAutoTopicCreation: false, transactionTimeout: 30000, retry: { retries: 5, }, }, }, }); export const kafkaTopics = { USER_EVENTS: 'user-events', ORDER_EVENTS: 'order-events', PAYMENT_EVENTS: 'payment-events', PRODUCT_EVENTS: 'product-events', NOTIFICATION_EVENTS: 'notification-events', ANALYTICS_EVENTS: 'analytics-events', } as const;

// shared/kafka/src/services/kafka-producer.service.ts import { Injectable, Logger, OnModuleDestroy, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientKafka } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { BaseEvent } from '@ecommerce/types'; @Injectable() export abstract class KafkaProducerService implements OnModuleInit, OnModuleDestroy { protected readonly logger = new Logger(this.constructor.name); protected abstract kafkaClient: ClientKafka; async onModuleInit() { await this.kafkaClient.connect(); this.logger.log('Kafka producer connected'); } async onModuleDestroy() { await this.kafkaClient.close(); this.logger.log('Kafka producer disconnected'); } async publishEvent<T extends BaseEvent>(topic: string, event: T): Promise<void> { try { await this.kafkaClient.emit(topic, { key: event.aggregateId, value: JSON.stringify(event), headers: { eventType: event.type, version: event.version.toString(), timestamp: event.timestamp.toISOString(), }, }); this.logger.debug(`Event published to ${topic}:`, event.type); } catch (error) { this.logger.error(`Failed to publish event to ${topic}:`, error); throw error; } } } // shared/kafka/src/services/kafka-consumer.service.ts import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common'; import { KafkaContext } from '@nestjs/microservices'; export abstract class KafkaConsumerService { protected readonly logger = new Logger(this.constructor.name); protected async handleMessage<T>( payload: any, context: KafkaContext, processor: (event: T) => Promise<void>, ): Promise<void> { const message = context.getMessage(); const { partition, offset } = message; try { const event = this.parseEvent<T>(payload); await processor(event); this.logger.debug(`Processed message from partition ${partition}, offset ${offset}`); } catch (error) { this.logger.error(`Failed to process message:`, error); throw error; } } private parseEvent<T>(payload: any): T { try { return typeof payload === 'string' ? JSON.parse(payload) : payload; } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Invalid event format: ${error.message}`); } } }

// services/order-service/src/kafka/order-producer.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientKafka, ClientProxyFactory } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { KafkaProducerService, kafkaTopics, createKafkaConfig } from '@ecommerce/kafka'; import { OrderEvents } from '@ecommerce/types'; @Injectable() export class OrderProducerService extends KafkaProducerService { protected kafkaClient: ClientKafka; constructor() { super(); this.kafkaClient = ClientProxyFactory.create( createKafkaConfig({ clientId: 'order-service-producer', groupId: 'order-service-group', brokers: [process.env.KAFKA_BROKER || 'localhost:9092'], }), ) as ClientKafka; } async publishOrderCreated(event: OrderEvents['ORDER_CREATED']): Promise<void> { await this.publishEvent(kafkaTopics.ORDER_EVENTS, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), type: 'ORDER_CREATED', aggregateId: event.orderId, version: 1, timestamp: new Date(), ...event, }); } async publishOrderConfirmed(event: OrderEvents['ORDER_CONFIRMED']): Promise<void> { await this.publishEvent(kafkaTopics.ORDER_EVENTS, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), type: 'ORDER_CONFIRMED', aggregateId: event.orderId, version: 1, timestamp: new Date(), ...event, }); } async publishOrderShipped(event: OrderEvents['ORDER_SHIPPED']): Promise<void> { await this.publishEvent(kafkaTopics.ORDER_EVENTS, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), type: 'ORDER_SHIPPED', aggregateId: event.orderId, version: 1, timestamp: new Date(), ...event, }); } }

Validate order data // 2. Check inventory availability // 3. Calculate totals const order = await this.orderRepository.save({ ...createOrderDto, userId, status: 'PENDING', createdAt: new Date(), }); // Publish order created event await this.orderProducer.publishOrderCreated({ orderId: order.id, userId: order.userId, items: order.items, totalAmount: order.totalAmount, shippingAddress: order.shippingAddress, }); return order; } async confirmOrder(orderId: string): Promise<void> { const order = await this.orderRepository.findOne({ where: { id: orderId } }); if (!order) { throw new NotFoundException('Order not found'); } order.status = 'CONFIRMED'; order.estimatedDelivery = this.calculateDeliveryDate(); await this.orderRepository.save(order); await this.orderProducer.publishOrderConfirmed({ orderId: order.id, userId: order.userId, estimatedDelivery: order.estimatedDelivery, }); } }

// services/notification-service/src/kafka/notification-consumer.controller.ts import { Controller } from '@nestjs/common'; import { EventPattern, Payload, Ctx, KafkaContext } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { KafkaConsumerService, kafkaTopics } from '@ecommerce/kafka'; import { OrderEvents, PaymentEvents, UserEvents } from '@ecommerce/types'; import { NotificationService } from '../services/notification.service'; @Controller() export class NotificationConsumerController extends KafkaConsumerService { constructor(private readonly notificationService: NotificationService) { super(); } @EventPattern(kafkaTopics.ORDER_EVENTS) async handleOrderEvent(@Payload() payload: any, @Ctx() context: KafkaContext): Promise<void> { await this.handleMessage(payload, context, async (event: any) => { switch (event.type) { case 'ORDER_CREATED': await this.notificationService.sendOrderConfirmation(event); break; case 'ORDER_SHIPPED': await this.notificationService.sendShippingNotification(event); break; case 'ORDER_DELIVERED': await this.notificationService.sendDeliveryNotification(event); break; } }); } @EventPattern(kafkaTopics.PAYMENT_EVENTS) async handlePaymentEvent(@Payload() payload: any, @Ctx() context: KafkaContext): Promise<void> { await this.handleMessage(payload, context, async (event: any) => { switch (event.type) { case 'PAYMENT_COMPLETED': await this.notificationService.sendPaymentConfirmation(event); break; case 'PAYMENT_FAILED': await this.notificationService.sendPaymentFailure(event); break; } }); } }

// services/product-service/src/kafka/inventory-consumer.controller.ts import { Controller } from '@nestjs/common'; import { EventPattern, Payload, Ctx, KafkaContext } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { KafkaConsumerService, kafkaTopics } from '@ecommerce/kafka'; import { OrderEvents } from '@ecommerce/types'; import { InventoryService } from '../services/inventory.service'; import { ProductProducerService } from './product-producer.service'; @Controller() export class InventoryConsumerController extends KafkaConsumerService { constructor( private readonly inventoryService: InventoryService, private readonly productProducer: ProductProducerService, ) { super(); } @EventPattern(kafkaTopics.ORDER_EVENTS) async handleOrderEvent(@Payload() payload: any, @Ctx() context: KafkaContext): Promise<void> { await this.handleMessage(payload, context, async (event: any) => { switch (event.type) { case 'ORDER_CREATED': await this.reserveInventory(event); break; case 'ORDER_CANCELLED': await this.releaseInventory(event); break; } }); } private async reserveInventory(event: OrderEvents['ORDER_CREATED']): Promise<void> { for (const item of event.items) { const updated = await this.inventoryService.reserveQuantity(item.productId, item.quantity); if (updated) { await this.productProducer.publishInventoryUpdated({ productId: item.productId, quantity: -item.quantity, operation: 'subtract', }); } } } private async releaseInventory(event: OrderEvents['ORDER_CANCELLED']): Promise<void> { // Implementation for releasing reserved inventory for (const item of event.items) { await this.inventoryService.releaseReservedQuantity(item.productId, item.quantity); await this.productProducer.publishInventoryUpdated({ productId: item.productId, quantity: item.quantity, operation: 'add', }); } } }

// shared/monitoring/src/kafka-metrics.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Counter, Histogram, Gauge, register } from 'prom-client'; @Injectable() export class KafkaMetricsService { private readonly messageCounter = new Counter({ name: 'kafka_messages_total', help: 'Total number of Kafka messages processed', labelNames: ['topic', 'status', 'service'], }); private readonly messageProcessingDuration = new Histogram({ name: 'kafka_message_processing_duration_seconds', help: 'Duration of message processing in seconds', labelNames: ['topic', 'service'], buckets: [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10], }); private readonly messageSize = new Histogram({ name: 'kafka_message_size_bytes', help: 'Size of Kafka messages in bytes', labelNames: ['topic', 'service'], buckets: [100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000], }); private readonly connectionGauge = new Gauge({ name: 'kafka_connections_active', help: 'Number of active Kafka connections', labelNames: ['service', 'type'], // type: producer or consumer }); constructor() { register.registerMetric(this.messageCounter); register.registerMetric(this.messageProcessingDuration); register.registerMetric(this.messageSize); register.registerMetric(this.connectionGauge); } recordMessageProcessed(topic: string, service: string, status: 'success' | 'error'): void { this.messageCounter.inc({ topic, status, service }); } recordProcessingDuration(topic: string, service: string, duration: number): void { this.messageProcessingDuration.observe({ topic, service }, duration); } recordMessageSize(topic: string, service: string, size: number): void { this.messageSize.observe({ topic, service }, size); } setActiveConnections(service: string, type: 'producer' | 'consumer', count: number): void { this.connectionGauge.set({ service, type }, count); } }

// shared/monitoring/src/datadog-kafka.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { StatsD } from 'node-statsd'; @Injectable() export class DatadogKafkaService { private statsd: StatsD; constructor() { this.statsd = new StatsD({ host: process.env.DATADOG_AGENT_HOST || 'localhost', port: parseInt(process.env.DATADOG_AGENT_PORT || '8125'), prefix: 'ecommerce.kafka.', }); } recordMessagePublished(topic: string, service: string): void { this.statsd.increment('message.published', 1, [`topic:${topic}`, `service:${service}`]); } recordMessageConsumed(topic: string, service: string, processingTime: number): void { this.statsd.increment('message.consumed', 1, [`topic:${topic}`, `service:${service}`]); this.statsd.timing('message.processing_time', processingTime, [`topic:${topic}`, `service:${service}`]); } recordError(topic: string, service: string, errorType: string): void { this.statsd.increment('message.error', 1, [`topic:${topic}`, `service:${service}`, `error_type:${errorType}`]); } }

// shared/kafka/src/decorators/retry.decorator.ts import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common'; export function KafkaRetry(maxRetries: number = 3, backoffMs: number = 1000) { return function (target: any, propertyName: string, descriptor: PropertyDescriptor) { const method = descriptor.value; const logger = new Logger(`${target.constructor.name}:${propertyName}`); descriptor.value = async function (...args: any[]) { let lastError: Error; for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) { try { return await method.apply(this, args); } catch (error) { lastError = error; logger.warn(`Attempt ${attempt}/${maxRetries} failed:`, error.message); if (attempt < maxRetries) { const delay = backoffMs * Math.pow(2, attempt - 1); // Exponential backoff await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay)); } } } logger.error(`All ${maxRetries} attempts failed. Last error:`, lastError); throw lastError; }; }; }

// shared/kafka/src/services/dead-letter-queue.service.ts import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common'; import { ClientKafka } from '@nestjs/microservices'; @Injectable() export class DeadLetterQueueService { private readonly logger = new Logger(DeadLetterQueueService.name); constructor(private readonly kafkaClient: ClientKafka) {} async sendToDeadLetterQueue( originalTopic: string, message: any, error: Error, retryCount: number = 0, ): Promise<void> { const dlqTopic = `${originalTopic}.dlq`; try { await this.kafkaClient.emit(dlqTopic, { ...message, metadata: { ...message.metadata, originalTopic, error: error.message, retryCount, failedAt: new Date().toISOString(), }, }); this.logger.error(`Message sent to DLQ: ${dlqTopic}`, { originalTopic, error: error.message, retryCount, }); } catch (dlqError) { this.logger.error(`Failed to send message to DLQ: ${dlqTopic}`, dlqError); } } }

// shared/kafka/src/services/enhanced-kafka-consumer.service.ts import { Logger } from '@nestjs/common'; import { KafkaContext } from '@nestjs/microservices'; import { KafkaMetricsService } from '@ecommerce/monitoring'; import { DeadLetterQueueService } from './dead-letter-queue.service'; export abstract class EnhancedKafkaConsumerService { protected readonly logger = new Logger(this.constructor.name); constructor( protected readonly metricsService: KafkaMetricsService, protected readonly dlqService: DeadLetterQueueService, ) {} protected async handleMessageWithRetry<T>( payload: any, context: KafkaContext, processor: (event: T) => Promise<void>, maxRetries: number = 3, ): Promise<void> { const message = context.getMessage(); const topic = context.getTopic(); const { partition, offset } = message; const startTime = Date.now(); try { const event = this.parseEvent<T>(payload); await processor(event); const processingTime = Date.now() - startTime; this.metricsService.recordMessageProcessed(topic, this.constructor.name, 'success'); this.metricsService.recordProcessingDuration(topic, this.constructor.name, processingTime / 1000); this.logger.debug(`Successfully processed message from ${topic}, partition ${partition}, offset ${offset}`); } catch (error) { const processingTime = Date.now() - startTime; this.metricsService.recordMessageProcessed(topic, this.constructor.name, 'error'); this.metricsService.recordProcessingDuration(topic, this.constructor.name, processingTime / 1000); const retryCount = this.getRetryCount(message); if (retryCount < maxRetries) { this.logger.warn(`Retrying message processing. Attempt ${retryCount + 1}/${maxRetries}`, error); // Implement retry logic here (could be immediate retry or scheduled) throw error; // Let Kafka handle the retry } else { this.logger.error(`Max retries exceeded. Sending to DLQ`, error); await this.dlqService.sendToDeadLetterQueue(topic, payload, error, retryCount); } } } private parseEvent<T>(payload: any): T { try { return typeof payload === 'string' ? JSON.parse(payload) : payload; } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Invalid event format: ${error.message}`); } } private getRetryCount(message: any): number { return message.headers?.retryCount ? parseInt(message.headers.retryCount) : 0; } }

#!/bin/bash # scripts/manage-topics.sh KAFKA_BROKER="kafka-service.kafka.svc.cluster.local:9092" KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n kafka -l app=kafka-broker -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') function list_topics() { echo "📋 Listing Kafka topics..." kubectl exec -n kafka $KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD -- kafka-topics --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER --list } function create_topic() { local topic_name=$1 local partitions=${2:-3} local replication_factor=${3:-1} echo "➕ Creating topic: $topic_name (partitions: $partitions, replication: $replication_factor)" kubectl exec -n kafka $KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD -- kafka-topics \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --create \ --topic $topic_name \ --partitions $partitions \ --replication-factor $replication_factor \ --if-not-exists } function delete_topic() { local topic_name=$1 echo "🗑️ Deleting topic: $topic_name" kubectl exec -n kafka $KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD -- kafka-topics \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --delete \ --topic $topic_name } function describe_topic() { local topic_name=$1 echo "🔍 Describing topic: $topic_name" kubectl exec -n kafka $KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD -- kafka-topics \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --describe \ --topic $topic_name } function consumer_groups() { echo "👥 Listing consumer groups..." kubectl exec -n kafka $KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD -- kafka-consumer-groups \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --list } function group_info() { local group_name=$1 echo "📊 Consumer group info: $group_name" kubectl exec -n kafka $KUBECTL_KAFKA_POD -- kafka-consumer-groups \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --describe \ --group $group_name } case "$1" in list) list_topics ;; #!/bin/bash # scripts/backup-kafka-topics.sh KAFKA_BROKER="kafka-service:9092" BACKUP_DIR="/tmp/kafka-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" KAFKA_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n kafka -l app=kafka-broker -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') mkdir -p $BACKUP_DIR echo "📦 Starting Kafka backup process..." # Get list of topics TOPICS=$(kubectl exec -n kafka $KAFKA_POD -- kafka-topics --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER --list) for topic in $TOPICS; do echo "💾 Backing up topic: $topic" # Export topic data kubectl exec -n kafka $KAFKA_POD -- kafka-console-consumer \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --topic $topic \ --from-beginning \ --timeout-ms 10000 > "$BACKUP_DIR/$topic.json" 2>/dev/null # Export topic configuration kubectl exec -n kafka $KAFKA_POD -- kafka-configs \ --bootstrap-server $KAFKA_BROKER \ --describe \ --entity-type topics \ --entity-name $topic > "$BACKUP_DIR/$topic.config" echo "✅ Backed up topic: $topic" done # Create archive tar -czf "kafka-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz" -C $(dirname $BACKUP_DIR) $(basename $BACKUP_DIR) echo "🎉 Backup completed: kafka-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz"

// Data sanitization utilities export class DataSanitizer { private static readonly PII_PATTERNS = { email: /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b/g, phone: /\b\d{3}-?\d{3}-?\d{4}\b/g, ssn: /\b\d{3}-?\d{2}-?\d{4}\b/g, creditCard: /\b\d{4}[\s-]?\d{4}[\s-]?\d{4}[\s-]?\d{4}\b/g, }; static sanitizeForTracing(data: any): any { if (typeof data === 'string') { let sanitized = data; Object.entries(this.PII_PATTERNS).forEach(([type, pattern]) => { sanitized = sanitized.replace(pattern, `[REDACTED_${type.toUpperCase()}]`); }); return sanitized; } if (typeof data === 'object' && data !== null) { const sanitized = {}; Object.entries(data).forEach(([key, value]) => { if (this.isSensitiveField(key)) { sanitized[key] = '[REDACTED]'; } else { sanitized[key] = this.sanitizeForTracing(value); } }); return sanitized; } return data; } private static isSensitiveField(fieldName: string): boolean { const sensitiveFields = [ 'password', 'token', 'secret', 'key', 'ssn', 'credit_card', 'cvv', 'pin', 'bank_account', 'routing_number', ]; return sensitiveFields.some((field) => fieldName.toLowerCase().includes(field)); } } // Secure span decorator export function SecureTrace(operationName?: string) { return function (target: any, propertyKey: string, descriptor: PropertyDescriptor) { const originalMethod = descriptor.value; const tracer = trace.getTracer('secure-service'); descriptor.value = async function (...args: any[]) { const spanName = operationName || `${target.constructor.name}.${propertyKey}`; return tracer.startActiveSpan(spanName, async (span) => { try { // Sanitize arguments before logging const sanitizedArgs = args.map((arg) => DataSanitizer.sanitizeForTracing(arg)); span.setAttributes({ 'code.function': propertyKey, 'code.namespace': target.constructor.name, 'operation.args.count': args.length, // Don't log actual argument values for security }); const result = await originalMethod.apply(this, args); span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK }); return result; } catch (error) { // Sanitize error messages const sanitizedError = DataSanitizer.sanitizeForTracing(error.message); span.recordException(new Error(sanitizedError)); span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR, message: sanitizedError }); throw error; } finally { span.end(); } }); }; return descriptor; }; }

export class ResourceAwareSampler implements Sampler { private readonly systemMetrics = new SystemMetrics(); shouldSample(context: Context, traceId: string, spanName: string): SamplingResult { const { cpuUsage, memoryUsage, diskIO } = this.systemMetrics.getCurrentMetrics(); // Reduce sampling under high load let samplingRate = 0.1; // Default 10% if (cpuUsage > 0.8 || memoryUsage > 0.8) { samplingRate = 0.01; // Reduce to 1% } else if (cpuUsage > 0.6 || memoryUsage > 0.6) { samplingRate = 0.05; // Reduce to 5% } // Always sample errors and critical operations if (spanName.includes('error') || spanName.includes('checkout')) { samplingRate = 1.0; } return { decision: Math.random() < samplingRate ? SamplingDecision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLED : SamplingDecision.NOT_RECORD, }; } }

Traefik is a modern, cloud-native edge router and reverse proxy that is well-suited for dynamic microservices environments. In this e-commerce platform, Traefik can be used as the primary ingress controller to manage external traffic, provide SSL termination, load balancing, and advanced routing for both frontend and backend services running on Kubernetes (GKE).

Dynamic Service Discovery: Automatically detects new services and routes traffic without manual configuration. Kubernetes Native: Integrates seamlessly with Kubernetes Ingress resources and CRDs. SSL/TLS Automation: Supports Let's Encrypt for automatic certificate management. Observability: Built-in dashboard, metrics, and tracing support. Advanced Routing: Path, host, header, and method-based routing. Security: Middleware for rate limiting, authentication, and IP whitelisting.

[Internet] | [Cloud Armor (WAF)] | [Global Load Balancer] | [Traefik Ingress Controller] | | | [Next.js] [API Gateway] [Microservices] Traefik sits behind the global load balancer and Cloud Armor, acting as the entry point for all HTTP(S) traffic into the GKE cluster. It routes requests to frontend (Next.js), API Gateway, and individual microservices based on Ingress rules.

Ingress Routing: Define Kubernetes Ingress or Traefik IngressRoute CRDs for each service. Automatic HTTPS: Enable Let's Encrypt for all domains/subdomains. Load Balancing: Distributes traffic across service pods. Middleware: Use for rate limiting, authentication, CORS, and more. Observability: Enable Traefik dashboard and Prometheus metrics.

Install Traefik via Helm helm repo add traefik https://traefik.github.io/charts helm repo update helm install traefik traefik/traefik \ --namespace traefik --create-namespace \ --set service.type=LoadBalancer \ --set ingressClass.enabled=true \ --set ingressClass.isDefaultClass=true Configure Ingress for Next.js Frontend apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Ingress metadata: name: nextjs-ingress namespace: frontend annotations: kubernetes.io/ingress.class: traefik spec: rules: - host: shop.example.com http: paths: - path: / pathType: Prefix backend: service: name: nextjs-service port: number: 80 tls: - hosts: - shop.example.com secretName: nextjs-tls Configure Ingress for API Gateway apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Ingress metadata: name: api-gateway-ingress namespace: backend annotations: kubernetes.io/ingress.class: traefik spec: rules: - host: api.shop.example.com http: paths: - path: / pathType: Prefix backend: service: name: api-gateway-service port: number: 80 tls: - hosts: - api.shop.example.com secretName: api-gateway-tls Enable Let's Encrypt (values.yaml) additionalArguments: - '--certificatesresolvers.le.acme.email=admin@example.com' - '--certificatesresolvers.le.acme.storage=/data/acme.json' - '--certificatesresolvers.le.acme.tlschallenge=true' - '--entrypoints.websecure.http.tls.certresolver=le' Observability Enable Traefik dashboard and metrics for monitoring traffic and health.

Use separate namespaces for Traefik, frontend, and backend. Restrict access to the Traefik dashboard. Use middleware for security (rate limiting, IP whitelisting, authentication). Regularly update Traefik for security patches.

-- Good: Normalized design for transactional data CREATE TABLE users ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL, first_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, last_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ); CREATE TABLE user_profiles ( user_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, bio TEXT, avatar_url VARCHAR(500), date_of_birth DATE, phone_number VARCHAR(20), created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ); CREATE TABLE addresses ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('billing', 'shipping', 'home', 'work')), street_line_1 VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, street_line_2 VARCHAR(255), city VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, state_province VARCHAR(100), postal_code VARCHAR(20), country_code CHAR(2) NOT NULL, is_default BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE(user_id, type, is_default) WHERE is_default = TRUE ); -- Strategic denormalization for read-heavy analytics CREATE TABLE order_analytics ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), order_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), user_id UUID NOT NULL, user_email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, -- Denormalized for faster queries order_total DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL, order_date DATE NOT NULL, customer_segment VARCHAR(50), product_categories TEXT[], -- Array for faster filtering order_month DATE GENERATED ALWAYS AS (DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) STORED, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP );

-- Foreign key constraints with appropriate actions CREATE TABLE orders ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'confirmed', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled')), total_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL CHECK (total_amount >= 0), currency_code CHAR(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD', shipping_address_id UUID REFERENCES addresses(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, billing_address_id UUID REFERENCES addresses(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, -- Ensure billing address belongs to the user CONSTRAINT fk_billing_address_user FOREIGN KEY (billing_address_id, user_id) REFERENCES addresses(id, user_id), -- Ensure shipping address belongs to the user CONSTRAINT fk_shipping_address_user FOREIGN KEY (shipping_address_id, user_id) REFERENCES addresses(id, user_id) ); -- Check constraints for business rules CREATE TABLE products ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), sku VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, description TEXT, price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL CHECK (price > 0), cost DECIMAL(10,2) CHECK (cost >= 0 AND cost <= price), weight_kg DECIMAL(8,3) CHECK (weight_kg > 0), stock_quantity INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (stock_quantity >= 0), min_stock_level INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (min_stock_level >= 0), max_stock_level INTEGER CHECK (max_stock_level IS NULL OR max_stock_level >= min_stock_level), is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE, category_id UUID REFERENCES categories(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, -- Ensure logical stock levels CONSTRAINT check_stock_levels CHECK (max_stock_level IS NULL OR stock_quantity <= max_stock_level) );

-- Good: Clear, consistent naming conventions -- Tables: plural nouns, snake_case CREATE TABLE user_sessions ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, session_token VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL, expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, last_accessed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, ip_address INET, user_agent TEXT ); -- Junction tables: combine table names CREATE TABLE user_roles ( user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, assigned_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, assigned_by UUID REFERENCES users(id), PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role_id) ); -- Audit tables: prefix with original table name CREATE TABLE order_audit_log ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), order_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, action VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('CREATE', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')), old_values JSONB, new_values JSONB, changed_by UUID REFERENCES users(id), changed_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, change_reason TEXT );

-- Index naming convention: idx_[table]_[columns]_[type] CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_id_status ON orders(user_id, status); CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at_btree ON orders(created_at); CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_gin ON products USING gin(to_tsvector('english', name)); -- Unique index naming: uniq_[table]_[columns] CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_users_email_active ON users(email) WHERE is_active = TRUE; -- Partial index naming: idx_[table]_[columns]_[condition] CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_amount_large ON orders(total_amount) WHERE total_amount > 1000; -- Functional index naming: idx_[table]_[function]_[columns] CREATE INDEX idx_users_email_lower ON users(lower(email));

-- Soft delete implementation CREATE TABLE categories ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, description TEXT, parent_category_id UUID REFERENCES categories(id), display_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0, is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, deleted_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, -- Unique constraint that ignores soft-deleted records UNIQUE(name, parent_category_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ); -- View for active records only CREATE VIEW active_categories AS SELECT id, name, description, parent_category_id, display_order, created_at, updated_at FROM categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL; -- Function to soft delete with cascade CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION soft_delete_category(category_id UUID) RETURNS VOID AS $$ BEGIN -- Soft delete the category UPDATE categories SET deleted_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = category_id AND deleted_at IS NULL; -- Soft delete all child categories UPDATE categories SET deleted_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE parent_category_id = category_id AND deleted_at IS NULL; -- Update products to remove category reference UPDATE products SET category_id = NULL, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE category_id = category_id; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Generic audit trail implementation CREATE TABLE audit_log ( id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, table_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, record_id UUID NOT NULL, operation VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (operation IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')), old_values JSONB, new_values JSONB, changed_fields TEXT[], user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id), session_id UUID, ip_address INET, user_agent TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, -- Index for common queries INDEX idx_audit_log_table_record (table_name, record_id), INDEX idx_audit_log_timestamp (timestamp), INDEX idx_audit_log_user_id (user_id) ); -- Trigger function for automatic audit logging CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION create_audit_log() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ DECLARE old_data JSONB; new_data JSONB; changed_fields TEXT[] = '{}'; field_name TEXT; BEGIN -- Determine operation type IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN old_data = to_jsonb(OLD); new_data = NULL; ELSIF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN old_data = NULL; new_data = to_jsonb(NEW); ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN old_data = to_jsonb(OLD); new_data = to_jsonb(NEW); -- Identify changed fields FOR field_name IN SELECT key FROM jsonb_each(new_data) LOOP IF old_data->field_name IS DISTINCT FROM new_data->field_name THEN changed_fields = array_append(changed_fields, field_name); END IF; END LOOP; END IF; -- Insert audit record INSERT INTO audit_log ( table_name, record_id, operation, old_values, new_values, changed_fields, user_id, session_id, ip_address ) VALUES ( TG_TABLE_NAME, COALESCE(NEW.id, OLD.id), TG_OP, old_data, new_data, changed_fields, current_setting('app.current_user_id', TRUE)::UUID, current_setting('app.current_session_id', TRUE)::UUID, current_setting('app.current_ip_address', TRUE)::INET ); RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD); END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql; -- Apply audit trigger to tables CREATE TRIGGER audit_trigger_users AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON users FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION create_audit_log();

-- Document versioning system CREATE TABLE documents ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), current_version_id UUID, title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, created_by UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ); CREATE TABLE document_versions ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), document_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, version_number INTEGER NOT NULL, title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, content_type VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'text/plain', change_summary TEXT, created_by UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE(document_id, version_number) ); -- Add foreign key after both tables are created ALTER TABLE documents ADD CONSTRAINT fk_documents_current_version FOREIGN KEY (current_version_id) REFERENCES document_versions(id); -- Function to create new document version CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION create_document_version( p_document_id UUID, p_title VARCHAR(255), p_content TEXT, p_change_summary TEXT, p_user_id UUID ) RETURNS UUID AS $$ DECLARE next_version INTEGER; version_id UUID; BEGIN -- Get next version number SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version_number), 0) + 1 INTO next_version FROM document_versions WHERE document_id = p_document_id; -- Create new version INSERT INTO document_versions ( document_id, version_number, title, content, change_summary, created_by ) VALUES ( p_document_id, next_version, p_title, p_content, p_change_summary, p_user_id ) RETURNING id INTO version_id; -- Update document to point to new version UPDATE documents SET current_version_id = version_id, title = p_title, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = p_document_id; RETURN version_id; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Order of columns in composite indexes matters -- Most selective column first, then by query patterns -- Good: Status is selective, created_at for range queries CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status_created_at ON orders(status, created_at); -- Query this index supports efficiently: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND created_at >= '2024-01-01' ORDER BY created_at DESC; -- Multi-column index for complex queries CREATE INDEX idx_products_category_active_price ON products(category_id, is_active, price) WHERE is_active = TRUE; -- Supports queries like: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category_id = 'uuid-here' AND is_active = TRUE AND price BETWEEN 10.00 AND 100.00;

-- Partial indexes for specific conditions CREATE INDEX idx_orders_pending_created_at ON orders(created_at) WHERE status = 'pending'; CREATE INDEX idx_users_active_email ON users(email) WHERE is_active = TRUE AND deleted_at IS NULL; -- Functional indexes for case-insensitive searches CREATE INDEX idx_users_email_lower ON users(lower(email)); CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_lower ON products(lower(name)); -- GIN indexes for array and JSON columns CREATE INDEX idx_order_analytics_categories_gin ON order_analytics USING gin(product_categories); CREATE INDEX idx_user_preferences_gin ON user_profiles USING gin(preferences) WHERE preferences IS NOT NULL; -- Full-text search indexes CREATE INDEX idx_products_search_text ON products USING gin(to_tsvector('english', name || ' ' || COALESCE(description, ''))); -- Usage example for full-text search: SELECT id, name, description, ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', name || ' ' || COALESCE(description, '')), plainto_tsquery('english', 'search term')) as rank FROM products WHERE to_tsvector('english', name || ' ' || COALESCE(description, '')) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'search term') ORDER BY rank DESC;

-- Monitor index usage SELECT schemaname, tablename, indexname, idx_scan as index_scans, idx_tup_read as tuples_read, idx_tup_fetch as tuples_fetched FROM pg_stat_user_indexes ORDER BY idx_scan DESC; -- Find unused indexes SELECT schemaname, tablename, indexname, idx_scan FROM pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE idx_scan = 0 AND indexname NOT LIKE '%_pkey'; -- Index bloat monitoring SELECT schemaname, tablename, indexname, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) as index_size, idx_scan, round(100 * idx_scan::numeric / NULLIF(seq_scan + idx_scan, 0), 2) as index_usage_pct FROM pg_stat_user_indexes JOIN pg_stat_user_tables USING (schemaname, tablename) ORDER BY pg_relation_size(indexrelid) DESC;

-- Good: Use appropriate join types and conditions SELECT u.id, u.email, u.first_name, u.last_name, p.bio, COUNT(o.id) as order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_spent FROM users u LEFT JOIN user_profiles p ON u.id = p.user_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id AND o.status = 'delivered' WHERE u.is_active = TRUE GROUP BY u.id, u.email, u.first_name, u.last_name, p.bio HAVING COUNT(o.id) > 0 ORDER BY total_spent DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 100; -- Use EXISTS instead of IN for better performance with large datasets SELECT p.id, p.name, p.price FROM products p WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.id AND oi.created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days' ) AND p.is_active = TRUE; -- Window functions for analytics SELECT user_id, order_date, total_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY order_date) as order_sequence, LAG(total_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY order_date) as previous_order_amount, SUM(total_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY order_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as running_total FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' ORDER BY user_id, order_date;

-- Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to understand query performance EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) SELECT u.email, COUNT(o.id) as order_count, AVG(o.total_amount) as avg_order_value FROM users u JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id WHERE o.created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days' GROUP BY u.id, u.email HAVING COUNT(o.id) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC; -- Optimize with CTEs for complex queries WITH recent_orders AS ( SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as order_count, AVG(total_amount) as avg_order_value, MAX(created_at) as last_order_date FROM orders WHERE created_at >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days' AND status = 'delivered' GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ), user_segments AS ( SELECT user_id, order_count, avg_order_value, last_order_date, CASE WHEN avg_order_value >= 500 THEN 'premium' WHEN avg_order_value >= 100 THEN 'standard' ELSE 'budget' END as customer_segment FROM recent_orders ) SELECT u.email, u.first_name, u.last_name, us.customer_segment, us.order_count, us.avg_order_value, us.last_order_date FROM users u JOIN user_segments us ON u.id = us.user_id ORDER BY us.avg_order_value DESC;

-- Cursor-based pagination for large datasets -- Instead of OFFSET which becomes slow with large offsets CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_orders_cursor( cursor_id UUID DEFAULT NULL, page_size INTEGER DEFAULT 20, order_direction TEXT DEFAULT 'ASC' ) RETURNS TABLE ( id UUID, user_id UUID, total_amount DECIMAL(10,2), created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, has_next_page BOOLEAN ) AS $$ DECLARE direction_operator TEXT; order_clause TEXT; BEGIN -- Determine comparison operator based on direction direction_operator := CASE WHEN order_direction = 'DESC' THEN '<' ELSE '>' END; order_clause := 'ORDER BY created_at ' || order_direction || ', id ' || order_direction; RETURN QUERY EXECUTE format(' WITH page_data AS ( SELECT o.id, o.user_id, o.total_amount, o.created_at FROM orders o WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR o.created_at %s $2 OR (o.created_at = $2 AND o.id %s $1)) %s LIMIT $3 + 1 ) SELECT pd.id, pd.user_id, pd.total_amount, pd.created_at, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM page_data) > $3 as has_next_page FROM page_data pd LIMIT $3', direction_operator, direction_operator, order_clause ) USING cursor_id, CASE WHEN cursor_id IS NOT NULL THEN (SELECT created_at FROM orders WHERE id = cursor_id) END, page_size; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Migration script template with rollback capability -- Migration: add_user_email_verification_fields -- Date: 2024-01-15 -- Description: Add email verification fields to users table BEGIN; -- Store migration info INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version, description, applied_at) VALUES ('20240115001', 'add_user_email_verification_fields', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP); -- Add new columns with safe defaults ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, ADD COLUMN email_verification_token VARCHAR(255), ADD COLUMN email_verification_sent_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, ADD COLUMN email_verification_expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE; -- Create index for verification tokens CREATE INDEX idx_users_email_verification_token ON users(email_verification_token) WHERE email_verification_token IS NOT NULL; -- Update existing users to be verified (existing users are trusted) UPDATE users SET email_verified = TRUE WHERE created_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '1 day'; -- Add constraint to ensure token expiry is after sent time ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT check_email_verification_expiry CHECK (email_verification_expires_at IS NULL OR email_verification_sent_at IS NULL OR email_verification_expires_at > email_verification_sent_at); COMMIT; -- Rollback script (run separately if needed) /* BEGIN; -- Remove constraint ALTER TABLE users DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS check_email_verification_expiry; -- Remove index DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_users_email_verification_token; -- Remove columns ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS email_verified, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS email_verification_token, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS email_verification_sent_at, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS email_verification_expires_at; -- Remove migration record DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version = '20240115001'; COMMIT; */

-- Complex data transformation with backup -- Migration: normalize_user_names BEGIN; -- Create backup table CREATE TABLE users_backup_20240115 AS SELECT * FROM users; -- Add temporary columns for normalized data ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN first_name_normalized VARCHAR(100), ADD COLUMN last_name_normalized VARCHAR(100); -- Normalize existing data UPDATE users SET first_name_normalized = TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(first_name, '\s+', ' ', 'g')), last_name_normalized = TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(last_name, '\s+', ' ', 'g')) WHERE first_name IS NOT NULL OR last_name IS NOT NULL; -- Validate data transformation DO $$ DECLARE invalid_count INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT COUNT(*) INTO invalid_count FROM users WHERE (first_name IS NOT NULL AND first_name_normalized IS NULL) OR (last_name IS NOT NULL AND last_name_normalized IS NULL); IF invalid_count > 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Data transformation validation failed: % invalid records', invalid_count; END IF; END $$; -- Replace original columns ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN first_name, DROP COLUMN last_name; ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN first_name_normalized TO first_name; ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN last_name_normalized TO last_name; -- Add constraints to new columns ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN first_name SET NOT NULL, ALTER COLUMN last_name SET NOT NULL; INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version, description, applied_at) VALUES ('20240115002', 'normalize_user_names', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP); COMMIT;

-- Enable RLS on sensitive tables ALTER TABLE orders ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE user_profiles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE addresses ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; -- Policy for users to see only their own orders CREATE POLICY user_orders_policy ON orders FOR ALL TO app_user USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::UUID); -- Policy for admins to see all orders CREATE POLICY admin_orders_policy ON orders FOR ALL TO app_admin USING (true); -- Policy for users to manage their own profile CREATE POLICY user_profile_policy ON user_profiles FOR ALL TO app_user USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::UUID) WITH CHECK (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::UUID); -- Read-only policy for public product information CREATE POLICY products_public_read ON products FOR SELECT TO app_user, app_guest USING (is_active = TRUE AND deleted_at IS NULL);

-- Store sensitive data encrypted CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto; CREATE TABLE payment_methods ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('credit_card', 'debit_card', 'bank_account')), encrypted_number BYTEA NOT NULL, -- Encrypted card/account number last_four CHAR(4) NOT NULL, -- Last 4 digits for display encrypted_expiry BYTEA, -- Encrypted expiry date cardholder_name VARCHAR(255), is_default BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, UNIQUE(user_id, is_default) WHERE is_default = TRUE ); -- Function to encrypt sensitive data CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION encrypt_payment_data( card_number TEXT, expiry_date TEXT, encryption_key TEXT ) RETURNS TABLE ( encrypted_number BYTEA, encrypted_expiry BYTEA, last_four CHAR(4) ) AS $$ BEGIN RETURN QUERY SELECT pgp_sym_encrypt(card_number, encryption_key)::BYTEA, pgp_sym_encrypt(expiry_date, encryption_key)::BYTEA, RIGHT(card_number, 4)::CHAR(4); END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql; -- View for displaying masked payment methods CREATE VIEW user_payment_methods_view AS SELECT id, user_id, type, CASE WHEN type = 'credit_card' THEN '**** **** **** ' || last_four WHEN type = 'bank_account' THEN '****' || last_four ELSE '**** **** **** ****' END as masked_number, cardholder_name, is_default, created_at FROM payment_methods;

-- Use parameterized queries and proper escaping -- Example of secure dynamic query building CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION search_products( search_term TEXT, category_filter UUID DEFAULT NULL, min_price DECIMAL DEFAULT NULL, max_price DECIMAL DEFAULT NULL, sort_by TEXT DEFAULT 'name', sort_order TEXT DEFAULT 'ASC' ) RETURNS TABLE ( id UUID, name VARCHAR(255), price DECIMAL(10,2), category_name VARCHAR(100) ) AS $$ DECLARE query_text TEXT; sort_column TEXT; BEGIN -- Validate and sanitize sort parameters CASE sort_by WHEN 'name' THEN sort_column := 'p.name'; WHEN 'price' THEN sort_column := 'p.price'; WHEN 'created_at' THEN sort_column := 'p.created_at'; ELSE sort_column := 'p.name'; END CASE; IF sort_order NOT IN ('ASC', 'DESC') THEN sort_order := 'ASC'; END IF; -- Build query with proper parameterization query_text := ' SELECT p.id, p.name, p.price, c.name as category_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id WHERE p.is_active = TRUE AND p.deleted_at IS NULL AND ($1 IS NULL OR to_tsvector(''english'', p.name || '' '' || COALESCE(p.description, '''')) @@ plainto_tsquery(''english'', $1)) AND ($2 IS NULL OR p.category_id = $2) AND ($3 IS NULL OR p.price >= $3) AND ($4 IS NULL OR p.price <= $4) ORDER BY ' || sort_column || ' ' || sort_order; RETURN QUERY EXECUTE query_text USING search_term, category_filter, min_price, max_price; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER; -- Grant execute permission to specific roles GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION search_products TO app_user;

-- Enable query statistics collection -- Add to postgresql.conf: -- shared_preload_libraries = 'pg_stat_statements' -- pg_stat_statements.track = all -- pg_stat_statements.max = 10000 -- Query to find slow queries SELECT query, calls, total_time, total_time/calls as avg_time, stddev_time, rows, 100.0 * shared_blks_hit / nullif(shared_blks_hit + shared_blks_read, 0) AS hit_percent FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE calls > 100 ORDER BY total_time DESC LIMIT 20; -- Find queries with high I/O SELECT query, calls, shared_blks_read, shared_blks_written, shared_blks_dirtied, shared_blks_hit, temp_blks_read, temp_blks_written FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE shared_blks_read > 1000 OR temp_blks_read > 100 ORDER BY shared_blks_read + temp_blks_read DESC;

-- Create monitoring views for database health CREATE VIEW database_health_summary AS SELECT 'connections' as metric, current_setting('max_connections')::INTEGER as max_value, COUNT(*) as current_value, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / current_setting('max_connections')::INTEGER, 2) as usage_percent FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 'database_size' as metric, NULL as max_value, pg_database_size(current_database()) as current_value, NULL as usage_percent UNION ALL SELECT 'cache_hit_ratio' as metric, NULL as max_value, ROUND(100.0 * sum(blks_hit) / nullif(sum(blks_hit + blks_read), 0), 2)::BIGINT as current_value, NULL as usage_percent FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database(); -- Monitor table bloat CREATE VIEW table_bloat_summary AS SELECT schemaname, tablename, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) as total_size, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) as table_size, n_tup_ins as inserts, n_tup_upd as updates, n_tup_del as deletes, n_dead_tup as dead_tuples, CASE WHEN n_live_tup > 0 THEN ROUND(100.0 * n_dead_tup / n_live_tup, 2) ELSE 0 END as dead_tuple_percent FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE n_live_tup > 1000 ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC; -- Automated maintenance tasks CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION run_maintenance_tasks() RETURNS TEXT AS $$ DECLARE result TEXT := ''; table_rec RECORD; BEGIN -- Auto-vacuum tables with high dead tuple percentage FOR table_rec IN SELECT schemaname, tablename, dead_tuple_percent FROM table_bloat_summary WHERE dead_tuple_percent > 10 LOOP EXECUTE 'VACUUM ANALYZE ' || quote_ident(table_rec.schemaname) || '.' || quote_ident(table_rec.tablename); result := result || 'Vacuumed ' || table_rec.schemaname || '.' || table_rec.tablename || E'\n'; END LOOP; -- Update table statistics ANALYZE; result := result || 'Updated table statistics' || E'\n'; RETURN result; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

import { Repository } from 'typeorm'; import { User } from './entities/user.entity'; import { CreateUserDto, UpdateUserDto, UserResponseDto } from './dto'; import { PaginationDto } from '../../common/dto/pagination.dto'; import { LoggerService } from '../../shared/logger/logger.service'; @Injectable() export class UsersService { constructor( @InjectRepository(User) private readonly userRepository: Repository<User>, @Inject('PASSWORD_HASHER') private readonly passwordHasher: any, private readonly logger: LoggerService, ) {} async create(createUserDto: CreateUserDto): Promise<UserResponseDto> { this.logger.log('Creating new user', { email: createUserDto.email }); // Check if user already exists const existingUser = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { email: createUserDto.email }, }); if (existingUser) { throw new ConflictException('User with this email already exists'); } // Hash password const hashedPassword = await this.passwordHasher.hash(createUserDto.password); // Create user entity const user = this.userRepository.create({ ...createUserDto, password: hashedPassword, }); // Save to database const savedUser = await this.userRepository.save(user); this.logger.log('User created successfully', { userId: savedUser.id }); return new UserResponseDto(savedUser); } async findAll(paginationDto: PaginationDto) { const { page = 1, limit = 10 } = paginationDto; const skip = (page - 1) * limit; const [users, total] = await this.userRepository.findAndCount({ skip, take: limit, order: { createdAt: 'DESC' }, }); return { data: users.map(user => new UserResponseDto(user)), pagination: { page, limit, total, totalPages: Math.ceil(total / limit), }, }; } async findByEmail(email: string): Promise<User | null> { return this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { email } }); } async update( id: string, updateUserDto: UpdateUserDto, currentUser: any, ): Promise<UserResponseDto> { // Check if user exists const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id } }); if (!user) { throw new NotFoundException(`User with ID ${id} not found`); } // Check permissions (users can only update their own profile) if (currentUser.role !== 'admin' && currentUser.id !== id) { throw new ForbiddenException('You can only update your own profile'); } // Update user Object.assign(user, updateUserDto); const updatedUser = await this.userRepository.save(user); this.logger.log('User updated successfully', { userId: id }); return new UserResponseDto(updatedUser); } async delete(id: string): Promise<void> { const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id } }); if (!user) { throw new NotFoundException(`User with ID ${id} not found`); } await this.userRepository.remove(user); this.logger.log('User deleted successfully', { userId: id }); } async validateUser(email: string, password: string): Promise<User | null> { const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { email } }); // src/modules/orders/orders.service.ts import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'; import { InjectRepository } from '@nestjs/typeorm'; import { Repository, DataSource } from 'typeorm'; import { Order } from './entities/order.entity'; import { OrderItem } from './entities/order-item.entity'; import { User } from '../users/entities/user.entity'; import { Product } from '../products/entities/product.entity'; @Injectable() export class OrdersService { constructor( @InjectRepository(Order) private readonly orderRepository: Repository<Order>, @InjectRepository(OrderItem) private readonly orderItemRepository: Repository<OrderItem>, private readonly dataSource: DataSource, ) {} async createOrder(userId: string, orderItems: CreateOrderItemDto[]): Promise<Order> { return this.dataSource.transaction(async manager => { // Create order const order = manager.create(Order, { userId, status: 'pending', total: 0, }); const savedOrder = await manager.save(order); let total = 0; // Create order items for (const item of orderItems) { // Check product availability const product = await manager.findOne(Product, { where: { id: item.productId }, }); if (!product) { throw new NotFoundException(`Product ${item.productId} not found`); } if (product.stock < item.quantity) { throw new BadRequestException( `Insufficient stock for product ${product.name}`, ); } // Create order item const orderItem = manager.create(OrderItem, { orderId: savedOrder.id, productId: item.productId, quantity: item.quantity, price: product.price, }); await manager.save(orderItem); // Update product stock product.stock -= item.quantity; await manager.save(product); total += product.price * item.quantity; } // Update order total savedOrder.total = total; await manager.save(savedOrder); return savedOrder; }); } }

// src/common/pipes/parse-object-id.pipe.ts import { PipeTransform, Injectable, ArgumentMetadata, BadRequestException, } from '@nestjs/common'; import { isUUID } from 'class-validator'; @Injectable() export class ParseObjectIdPipe implements PipeTransform<string, string> { transform(value: string, metadata: ArgumentMetadata): string { if (!isUUID(value)) { throw new BadRequestException('Invalid UUID format'); } return value; } } // src/common/pipes/validation.pipe.ts import { PipeTransform, Injectable, ArgumentMetadata, BadRequestException, } from '@nestjs/common'; import { validate } from 'class-validator'; import { plainToClass } from 'class-transformer'; @Injectable() export class ValidationPipe implements PipeTransform<any> { async transform(value: any, { metatype }: ArgumentMetadata) { if (!metatype || !this.toValidate(metatype)) { return value; } const object = plainToClass(metatype, value); const errors = await validate(object); if (errors.length > 0) { const messages = errors.map(error => { return { field: error.property, constraints: Object.values(error.constraints || {}), }; }); throw new BadRequestException({ message: 'Validation failed', errors: messages, }); } return object; } private toValidate(metatype: Function): boolean { const types: Function[] = [String, Boolean, Number, Array, Object]; return !types.includes(metatype); } }

// src/common/guards/rate-limit.guard.ts import { Injectable, CanActivate, ExecutionContext, HttpException, HttpStatus, } from '@nestjs/common'; import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'; import { RATE_LIMIT_KEY } from '../decorators/rate-limit.decorator'; interface RateLimitOptions { points: number; duration: number; } @Injectable() export class RateLimitGuard implements CanActivate { private requests = new Map<string, { count: number; resetTime: number }>(); constructor(private reflector: Reflector) {} canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean { const rateLimitOptions = this.reflector.get<RateLimitOptions>( RATE_LIMIT_KEY, context.getHandler(), ); if (!rateLimitOptions) { return true; } const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest(); const key = this.generateKey(request); const now = Date.now(); let requestInfo = this.requests.get(key); if (!requestInfo || now > requestInfo.resetTime) { requestInfo = { count: 1, resetTime: now + rateLimitOptions.duration * 1000, }; this.requests.set(key, requestInfo); return true; } if (requestInfo.count >= rateLimitOptions.points) { throw new HttpException( 'Too Many Requests', HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, ); } requestInfo.count++; return true; } private generateKey(request: any): string { return `${request.ip}:${request.route?.path || request.url}`; } } // src/common/decorators/rate-limit.decorator.ts import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common'; export const RATE_LIMIT_KEY = 'rateLimit'; export const RateLimit = (points: number, duration: number) => SetMetadata(RATE_LIMIT_KEY, { points, duration }); // Usage @Controller('auth') export class AuthController { @Post('login') @RateLimit(5, 60) // 5 requests per minute async login(@Body() loginDto: LoginDto) { return this.authService.login(loginDto); } }
