Proactive Response: Allows the PO and team to investigate and react to significant business trend changes quickly, rather than waiting for manual report reviews. Data-Driven Culture: Reinforces the importance of business metrics across the team.

Identify Alert-Worthy KPIs and Thresholds: Collaborate with PO/Stakeholders: Review the primary KPIs defined in Item 104. Discuss: Which KPIs are critical enough that a sudden, significant change warrants an immediate alert? Define "Significant Change": Determine what constitutes an anomaly worth alerting on. This requires understanding normal fluctuations. Examples: Threshold Breach: "Conversion rate drops below 2% for > 1 hour." Sudden Drop (Absolute): "Hourly signups drop by > 100 compared to the previous hour." Sudden Drop (Percentage): "Daily Active Users (DAU) drops by > 20% compared to the same day last week." Spike (Errors/Negative Metrics): "Payment failure rate exceeds 5% for > 30 minutes." Absence of Data: "No new signups recorded in the last hour" (could indicate tracking failure). Start Conservatively: Begin with alerts on only the most critical KPIs and set thresholds that avoid excessive noise from normal variations. You can tune them later. Choose the Alerting Tool: Alerting capabilities depend on your business monitoring setup (Item 104): BI Tools (Looker Studio, Tableau, Power BI, Looker): Many BI tools have built-in alerting features that allow you to set rules on dashboard metrics (e.g., "Alert if 'Sales' drops below X"). Product Analytics (Mixpanel, Amplitude): These platforms often have sophisticated anomaly detection and alerting features based on event data. Backend Monitoring (Datadog, etc.): If KPIs are derived from metrics already in your backend monitoring system (e.g., number of orders processed), you can set up alerts there. Custom Scripts: Querying underlying data (e.g., in BigQuery from Firebase Analytics export) with scheduled scripts that trigger alerts if thresholds are met. Configure the Alerts: Using the chosen tool, create alert rules based on the defined KPIs and thresholds. Target Audience: Configure the alert notifications to go to the Product Owner and Tech Lead(s) as the primary recipients. Consider a dedicated chat channel (e.g., #proj-mobile-biz-alerts) or email distribution list. Avoid sending these directly to the main developer or general alert channels initially, as they require business context for interpretation. Notification Content: Ensure the alert message clearly states: Which KPI is affected. The threshold that was breached or the detected anomaly. The current value vs. the expected value/threshold. A direct link to the relevant dashboard or chart for investigation. Document the Alerts: On your project wiki (e.g., on the "Monitoring & Alerting" or "Business KPIs" page), list the configured business alerts. Include the KPI, the trigger condition/threshold, and who gets notified. Establish Triage Process: Define who is responsible for acknowledging and initially investigating a business alert (usually the PO or Data Analyst). The first step is typically to check the dashboard for context (is it a blip? a real trend? correlated with a release or external event?). If a technical cause is suspected, the PO/Analyst should loop in the Tech Lead via the appropriate channel (e.g., #proj-mobile-biz-tech) with details and a link to the alert/dashboard. Tune and Iterate: Monitor the alerts for frequency and relevance. Adjust thresholds to reduce noise (false positives) or increase sensitivity (if real issues were missed). Add alerts for new KPIs as they become important. Review the alerting setup periodically (e.g., quarterly) with the PO. Alerting on business KPIs provides a crucial layer of monitoring focused directly on the application's outcomes and value delivery.

Item: 150 | Architecture Validation | Architecture Evaluation | RELEASE | 5 | "The PO and stakeholders recognize that the code quality is satisfactory through the metrics
and goals that are shared with them." | Share the SonarQube "Maintainability" rating and Firebase "Crash-free users" metric with the PO and stakeholders regularly. | | This guide covers the advanced practice (Maturity Level 5) of ensuring that the Product Owner (PO) and key stakeholders understand and recognize that the application's code quality is satisfactory, primarily by sharing relevant, understandable metrics.
documents.s: Completing Item 150: Ensure PO/Stakeholder Recognition of Code Quality

documents.t: Builds Trust: Demonstrates to non-technical stakeholders that the team is proactively managing the technical health and quality of the product, not just delivering features. Justifies Investment in Quality: Helps stakeholders understand the value of allocating time/resources to testing, refactoring, and process improvements (Item 138) by showing the resulting quality outcomes. Aligns Priorities: Facilitates discussions about balancing feature velocity with maintaining quality targets. If stakeholders see quality metrics are good, they might be more comfortable prioritizing features; if metrics are poor, it strengthens the case for dedicating time to improvements. Shared Definition of "Good": Moves beyond subjective feelings about quality towards a shared understanding based on agreed-upon metrics. Transparency: Provides visibility into an aspect of the product (internal quality) that is often invisible to non-technical stakeholders.

Stakeholders typically don't need (or want) deep technical details like Cyclomatic Complexity. Focus on metrics that represent user-facing impact or long-term product health: Reliability Metrics (User Impact): Crash-Free User Rate / Crash-Free Session Rate (from Firebase Crashlytics): This is highly relevant as it directly impacts user experience. "Our app is experienced as crash-free by 99.95% of users." [Image of Firebase Crashlytics stability chart] Production Bug Rate: Number of critical/major bugs reported in production per release or per time period. (Tracked via Jira). Performance Metrics (User Impact): App Start Time: (If a key NFR - from Firebase Performance). "We are meeting our goal of starting under 2 seconds for 90% of users." Key Screen Load Times: (If relevant - from Firebase Performance). Maintainability Metrics (Long-Term Health / Velocity Impact - Explain Clearly): SonarQube Maintainability Rating (A-E) or Technical Debt Ratio: Explain this as an indicator of how easy/fast it is to make changes and fix bugs. "Our 'A' rating means the codebase is healthy, allowing us to add features efficiently." or "Our Tech Debt Ratio is low (e.g., smaller than 5%), meaning we spend less time fighting old issues." [Image of SonarQube project overview] Test Coverage Percentage: Explain this as a measure of our safety net against regressions. "Our 80%+ test coverage gives us confidence to make changes quickly without breaking existing functionality." Avoid: Sharing raw numbers of code smells, vulnerabilities (unless critical and needing stakeholder awareness), duplication percentages, or complexity scores unless you can clearly translate them into business impact.
documents.s: What Metrics to Share? (Focus on Impact)

documents.t: Identify Key Metrics and Goals: Select 2-4 key metrics from the list above that best represent the quality goals agreed upon with the PO/stakeholders (Items 29, 30). Ensure these metrics are being actively tracked using the appropriate tools (Firebase, SonarQube, Jira). Establish a Reporting Cadence: Determine how frequently to share these metrics. Monthly or Quarterly is often appropriate. Avoid overwhelming stakeholders with too frequent updates. Align with existing reporting cycles if possible. Choose the Communication Channel: Sprint Reviews/Demos: Include a brief "Quality & Health" section. Regular Status Reports: Add a concise summary of the key quality metrics. Dedicated Quality Update (Less Common): A brief occasional email or meeting if significant changes or milestones occur. Present Metrics Clearly: Visualize: Use simple charts or graphs (e.g., trend lines for crash-free rate, gauge chart for coverage). Screenshots from Firebase or SonarQube can be effective if kept simple. Explain in Business Terms: Translate the metric into its impact. Instead of: "Maintainability Rating is A." Say: "Our code quality rating remains 'A', indicating the codebase is healthy and efficient for adding new features." Instead of: "Coverage is 82%." Say: "Our automated test coverage is strong at 82%, which helps us prevent bugs and release changes confidently." Show Trends: Highlight improvements or stability over time. If a metric temporarily dips, explain the reason and the plan to address it. Compare to Goals: Explicitly state whether you are meeting the agreed-upon NFR targets. Facilitate Discussion: Allow time for the PO and stakeholders to ask questions. Use the metrics as a basis for discussions about future priorities (e.g., "Given our stable crash rate, we can focus more on feature X next quarter," or "We need to dedicate some capacity to improving performance, as our app start time target is being missed."). Gather Feedback: Ask stakeholders if the reported metrics are understandable and useful. Adjust the metrics reported or the presentation format based on their feedback. By regularly sharing understandable quality metrics and connecting them to business value and user experience, you can ensure that the PO and stakeholders recognize and appreciate the team's efforts in maintaining a high-quality, sustainable product. 👍

Response Time: 95% of API responses should be < 300ms under normal load. Throughput: System must support at least 1000 concurrent users with no degradation. Scalability: Must support horizontal scaling of microservices and frontend pods.
Uptime: 99.9% monthly uptime (excluding planned maintenance). Disaster Recovery: RPO ≤ 15 minutes, RTO ≤ 1 hour. Failover: Automatic failover for critical services (DB, API Gateway).

Authentication: All endpoints require OAuth2/JWT authentication. Authorization: RBAC enforced for all APIs. Data Protection: Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit. Vulnerability Scanning: SAST and DAST run on every release.
Code Quality: All code must pass SonarQube quality gates. Documentation: All APIs and services must have up-to-date documentation. Modularity: Microservices must be independently deployable.
Monitoring: All services must expose metrics for Datadog/Prometheus. Logging: Centralized structured logging for all services. Alerting: Automated alerts for error rates, latency, and resource usage.
Auto-scaling: GKE pods auto-scale based on CPU/memory and queue depth. Caching: Redis used for session/data caching to reduce DB load.
Audit Logging: All user and admin actions logged for audit. Data Retention: Comply with GDPR/CCPA for user data.
Database Backups: Automated daily backups with 7-day retention. File Storage: Cloud Storage objects versioned and backed up.
API Standards: RESTful APIs with OpenAPI/Swagger documentation. Integration: Support for third-party payment, email, and auth providers.

Response Time & Throughput: Use APM tools (Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus) to monitor API latency and throughput. Set up dashboards and alerts for 95th percentile response times. Run regular load tests (k6, JMeter) to verify system can handle target concurrency. Scalability: Monitor pod/node auto-scaling events in GKE. Use metrics like CPU, memory, and queue depth to trigger scaling.

Uptime: Use uptime monitoring (Pingdom, UptimeRobot, Datadog Synthetics) for endpoints. Set up alerting for downtime or failed health checks. Disaster Recovery & Failover: Regularly test backup restores and failover procedures. Monitor backup job status and replication health.

Authentication & Authorization: Monitor failed/suspicious login attempts and RBAC violations in logs. Use security dashboards in Auth0 and API Gateway. Data Protection: Verify encryption settings for databases and storage. Use vulnerability scanners (SonarQube, OWASP ZAP) in CI/CD.

Code Quality: Enforce SonarQube quality gates in CI/CD. Review code coverage and static analysis reports. Documentation: Use tools like Swagger/OpenAPI for API docs. Periodically review and update documentation.

Monitoring & Logging: Ensure all services export metrics to Datadog/Prometheus. Use centralized logging (ELK, Datadog Logs) and set up log-based alerts. Alerting: Define alert thresholds for error rates, latency, and resource usage.
Auto-scaling: Monitor scaling events and resource utilization in GKE. Test scaling by simulating load. Caching: Monitor Redis hit/miss rates and latency.

Audit Logging: Regularly review audit logs for sensitive actions. Set up alerts for suspicious or unauthorized activities. Data Retention: Schedule and verify data deletion jobs for compliance (GDPR/CCPA).
Database Backups: Monitor backup job status and retention. Periodically perform restore drills. File Storage: Verify object versioning and backup policies in Cloud Storage.

API Standards: Use contract testing (e.g., Pact) to verify API compatibility. Validate OpenAPI/Swagger docs in CI. Integration: Monitor third-party API health and error rates. Set up fallback/alerting for integration failures.

This comprehensive guide walks you through building a production-ready e-commerce recommendation system using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology. The system combines the power of large language models with dynamic information retrieval to create intelligent, context-aware recommendations that drive engagement and conversions.
documents.s: Building Intelligent E-commerce Recommendations with RAG

Before starting, ensure you have: Development Environment: Python 3.8+, Node.js 16+, Docker API Access: OpenAI, Anthropic, or local LLM setup Databases: PostgreSQL, Redis access Vector Database: Qdrant, Pinecone, or Weaviate account Basic Knowledge: Python, machine learning concepts, web APIs

Throughout this guide, we'll build a complete e-commerce recommendation system with: Product Catalog: Electronics, clothing, books, and more User Behavior Tracking: Views, purchases, searches, reviews Real-time Recommendations: Personalized product suggestions Analytics Dashboard: Performance metrics and insights Ready to build the future of e-commerce recommendations? Let's start with the Introduction & Architecture!

This section covers building robust data pipelines and generating high-quality vector embeddings that capture the semantic essence of products and user behavior. Vector embeddings are the foundation that enables our recommendation system to understand relationships between products, users, and their preferences at a semantic level.

Our data pipeline follows the Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pattern, specifically designed for vector embedding generation: ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Raw Data │ │ Processing │ │ Vector │ │ Sources │───▶│ Pipeline │───▶│ Storage │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ├─ Product Catalog ├─ Data Cleaning ├─ Product Vectors│ ├─ User Profiles ├─ Feature Extraction ├─ User Vectors │ ├─ Interaction Logs ├─ Embedding Generation├─ Query Vectors │ ├─ Reviews/Ratings ├─ Quality Validation ├─ Metadata Index │ └─ Search Queries └─ Batch Processing └─ Search Index │

# processors/product_processor.py import pandas as pd import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict, Any import re import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class ProductDataProcessor: def __init__(self): self.stop_words = self._load_stop_words() self.category_keywords = self._load_category_keywords() def clean_product_data(self, products_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: """Clean and standardize product data""" logger.info(f"Cleaning {len(products_df)} products") # Remove duplicates products_df = products_df.drop_duplicates(subset=['id']) # Standardize text fields products_df['title'] = products_df['title'].apply(self._clean_text) products_df['description'] = products_df['description'].apply(self._clean_text) # Normalize prices products_df['price'] = pd.to_numeric(products_df['price'], errors='coerce') products_df = products_df.dropna(subset=['price']) # Fill missing values products_df['description'] = products_df['description'].fillna('') products_df['brand'] = products_df['brand'].fillna('Unknown') products_df['rating'] = products_df['rating'].fillna(0.0) products_df['review_count'] = products_df['review_count'].fillna(0) # Calculate derived features products_df['title_length'] = products_df['title'].str.len() products_df['description_length'] = products_df['description'].str.len() products_df['price_category'] = pd.cut( products_df['price'], bins=[0, 25, 100, 500, np.inf], labels=['budget', 'mid-range', 'premium', 'luxury'] ) logger.info(f"Cleaned data: {len(products_df)} products remaining") return products_df def extract_product_features(self, product: Product) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Extract meaningful features from product data""" features = { # Basic features 'title': product.title, 'description': product.description, 'category': product.category.value, 'subcategory': product.subcategory or '', 'brand': product.brand or '', # Numeric features 'price': product.price, 'rating': product.rating or 0.0, 'review_count': product.review_count, 'popularity_score': product.popularity_score, # Text processing 'combined_text': self._create_combined_text(product), 'keywords': product.keywords, 'search_terms': product.search_terms, # Categorical features 'price_range': self._categorize_price(product.price), 'rating_tier': self._categorize_rating(product.rating or 0.0), 'popularity_tier': self._categorize_popularity(product.popularity_score), # Availability features 'is_available': product.is_available, 'stock_level': self._categorize_stock(product.stock_quantity), } # Add attribute-based features features.update(self._process_attributes(product.attributes)) return features def _clean_text(self, text: str) -> str: """Clean and normalize text data""" if pd.isna(text) or not isinstance(text, str): return "" # Convert to lowercase text = text.lower() # Remove special characters but keep alphanumeric and spaces text = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9\s]', ' ', text) # Remove extra whitespaces text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip() return text def _create_combined_text(self, product: Product) -> str: """Create combined text for embedding generation""" components = [ product.title, product.description, product.brand or '', product.category.value, product.subcategory or '', ' '.join(product.keywords), ' '.join(product.search_terms) ] # Filter out empty components components = [comp for comp in components if comp and comp.strip()] return ' '.join(components)

# models/user.py from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any from datetime import datetime from enum import Enum class UserDemographic(BaseModel): age_range: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Age range (e.g., '25-34')") gender: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="User gender") location: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="User location") income_range: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Income bracket") class UserPreferences(BaseModel): preferred_categories: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list) preferred_brands: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list) price_sensitivity: float = Field(default=0.5, ge=0, le=1) quality_preference: float = Field(default=0.5, ge=0, le=1) style_preferences: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list) class InteractionType(str, Enum): VIEW = "view" CLICK = "click" ADD_TO_CART = "add_to_cart" PURCHASE = "purchase" REVIEW = "review" SEARCH = "search" WISHLIST = "wishlist" class UserInteraction(BaseModel): id: str user_id: str product_id: Optional[str] = None interaction_type: InteractionType timestamp: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow) session_id: str # Context data page_url: Optional[str] = None referrer: Optional[str] = None device_type: Optional[str] = None search_query: Optional[str] = None # Interaction specifics duration: Optional[float] = None # Time spent (seconds) scroll_depth: Optional[float] = None # Page scroll percentage quantity: Optional[int] = None price_paid: Optional[float] = None

# processors/user_processor.py import pandas as pd import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict from datetime import datetime from collections import defaultdict import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class UserBehaviorProcessor: def __init__(self): self.interaction_weights = { InteractionType.VIEW: 1.0, InteractionType.CLICK: 2.0, InteractionType.ADD_TO_CART: 5.0, InteractionType.PURCHASE: 10.0, InteractionType.REVIEW: 8.0, InteractionType.SEARCH: 3.0, InteractionType.WISHLIST: 4.0, } def process_user_interactions(self, interactions_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: """Process and enrich user interaction data""" logger.info(f"Processing {len(interactions_df)} user interactions") # Convert timestamp to datetime interactions_df['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(interactions_df['timestamp']) # Add temporal features interactions_df['hour'] = interactions_df['timestamp'].dt.hour interactions_df['day_of_week'] = interactions_df['timestamp'].dt.dayofweek interactions_df['is_weekend'] = interactions_df['day_of_week'].isin([5, 6]) # Calculate interaction weights interactions_df['interaction_weight'] = interactions_df['interaction_type'].map( lambda x: self.interaction_weights.get(InteractionType(x), 1.0) ) # Add session-based features interactions_df = self._add_session_features(interactions_df) return interactions_df def create_user_profiles(self, users_df: pd.DataFrame, interactions_df: pd.DataFrame) -> Dict[str, Dict]: """Create comprehensive user profiles from interaction data""" user_profiles = {} for user_id in users_df['id'].unique(): user_interactions = interactions_df[interactions_df['user_id'] == user_id] profile = { 'user_id': user_id, 'behavioral_features': self._extract_behavioral_features(user_interactions), 'preference_features': self._extract_preference_features(user_interactions), 'temporal_features': self._extract_temporal_features(user_interactions), 'engagement_features': self._extract_engagement_features(user_interactions), } user_profiles[user_id] = profile logger.info(f"Created profiles for {len(user_profiles)} users") return user_profiles

# embeddings/embedding_generator.py import numpy as np import torch from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import logging from abc import ABC, abstractmethod import asyncio import openai logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class BaseEmbeddingGenerator(ABC): """Abstract base class for embedding generators""" @abstractmethod async def generate_embeddings(self, texts: List[str]) -> np.ndarray: pass @abstractmethod def get_embedding_dimension(self) -> int: pass class SentenceTransformerEmbedding(BaseEmbeddingGenerator): """Local sentence transformer embedding generator""" def __init__(self, model_name: str = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"): self.model_name = model_name self.model = SentenceTransformer(model_name) self.device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu") self.model.to(self.device) logger.info(f"Loaded SentenceTransformer model: {model_name}") async def generate_embeddings(self, texts: List[str]) -> np.ndarray: """Generate embeddings for a list of texts""" if not texts: return np.array([]) # Process in batches to manage memory batch_size = 32 all_embeddings = [] for i in range(0, len(texts), batch_size): batch = texts[i:i + batch_size] embeddings = self.model.encode( batch, convert_to_numpy=True, show_progress_bar=False, batch_size=batch_size ) all_embeddings.append(embeddings) return np.vstack(all_embeddings) def get_embedding_dimension(self) -> int: return self.model.get_sentence_embedding_dimension() class OpenAIEmbedding(BaseEmbeddingGenerator): """OpenAI API embedding generator""" def __init__(self, model_name: str = "text-embedding-ada-002", api_key: Optional[str] = None): self.model_name = model_name openai.api_key = api_key or os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") self.dimensions = { "text-embedding-ada-002": 1536, "text-embedding-3-small": 1536, "text-embedding-3-large": 3072, } logger.info(f"Initialized OpenAI embedding model: {model_name}") async def generate_embeddings(self, texts: List[str]) -> np.ndarray: """Generate embeddings using OpenAI API""" if not texts: return np.array([]) batch_size = 100 all_embeddings = [] for i in range(0, len(texts), batch_size): batch = texts[i:i + batch_size] try: response = await openai.Embedding.acreate( model=self.model_name, input=batch ) batch_embeddings = [data.embedding for data in response.data] all_embeddings.extend(batch_embeddings) await asyncio.sleep(0.1) # Rate limiting except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Error generating embeddings: {e}") zero_embedding = [0.0] * self.get_embedding_dimension() all_embeddings.extend([zero_embedding] * len(batch)) return np.array(all_embeddings) def get_embedding_dimension(self) -> int: return self.dimensions.get(self.model_name, 1536)

class ProductEmbeddingGenerator: """Specialized embedding generator for products""" def __init__(self, embedding_generator: BaseEmbeddingGenerator): self.embedding_generator = embedding_generator self.dimension = embedding_generator.get_embedding_dimension() async def generate_product_embeddings(self, products: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]: """Generate embeddings for products""" logger.info(f"Generating embeddings for {len(products)} products") # Prepare texts for embedding product_texts = [] product_ids = [] for product in products: text = self._create_product_text(product) product_texts.append(text) product_ids.append(product['id']) # Generate embeddings embeddings = await self.embedding_generator.generate_embeddings(product_texts) # Create mapping product_embeddings = {} for product_id, embedding in zip(product_ids, embeddings): product_embeddings[product_id] = embedding return product_embeddings def _create_product_text(self, product: Dict[str, Any]) -> str: """Create text representation of product for embedding""" components = [] # Title (highest weight) if product.get('title'): components.append(f"Title: {product['title']}") # Category and subcategory if product.get('category'): components.append(f"Category: {product['category']}") if product.get('subcategory'): components.append(f"Subcategory: {product['subcategory']}") # Brand if product.get('brand'): components.append(f"Brand: {product['brand']}") # Description if product.get('description'): description = product['description'][:500] # Truncate long descriptions components.append(f"Description: {description}") # Price range if product.get('price_range'): components.append(f"Price range: {product['price_range']}") # Keywords and tags if product.get('keywords'): components.append(f"Keywords: {', '.join(product['keywords'])}") return ' '.join(components)

# validation/embedding_validator.py import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict, Any from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity from sklearn.decomposition import PCA import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class EmbeddingQualityValidator: """Validate the quality of generated embeddings""" def __init__(self): self.similarity_threshold = 0.7 self.diversity_threshold = 0.3 def validate_product_embeddings( self, product_embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray], products: List[Dict[str, Any]] ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Comprehensive validation of product embeddings""" logger.info("Validating product embeddings...") results = { 'total_products': len(product_embeddings), 'embedding_dimension': len(next(iter(product_embeddings.values()))), 'quality_metrics': {}, 'recommendations': [] } # Create product lookup product_lookup = {p['id']: p for p in products} # Test semantic similarity similarity_results = self._test_semantic_similarity(product_embeddings, product_lookup) results['quality_metrics']['semantic_similarity'] = similarity_results # Test category clustering clustering_results = self._test_category_clustering(product_embeddings, product_lookup) results['quality_metrics']['category_clustering'] = clustering_results # Test embedding diversity diversity_results = self._test_embedding_diversity(product_embeddings) results['quality_metrics']['diversity'] = diversity_results # Generate recommendations results['recommendations'] = self._generate_quality_recommendations(results['quality_metrics']) overall_score = self._calculate_overall_score(results['quality_metrics']) logger.info(f"Validation complete. Overall quality score: {overall_score:.3f}") return results def _test_semantic_similarity( self, embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray], products: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] ) -> Dict[str, float]: """Test if semantically similar products have similar embeddings""" # Sample products for testing sample_size = min(100, len(embeddings)) sampled_ids = list(embeddings.keys())[:sample_size] similarity_scores = [] for i, product_id_1 in enumerate(sampled_ids): for product_id_2 in sampled_ids[i+1:]: # Calculate embedding similarity emb_sim = cosine_similarity( embeddings[product_id_1].reshape(1, -1), embeddings[product_id_2].reshape(1, -1) )[0, 0] # Calculate semantic similarity semantic_sim = self._calculate_semantic_similarity( products[product_id_1], products[product_id_2] ) similarity_scores.append({ 'embedding_similarity': emb_sim, 'semantic_similarity': semantic_sim }) # Calculate correlation emb_sims = [s['embedding_similarity'] for s in similarity_scores] sem_sims = [s['semantic_similarity'] for s in similarity_scores] correlation = np.corrcoef(emb_sims, sem_sims)[0, 1] if len(emb_sims) > 1 else 0 return { 'correlation': correlation, 'avg_embedding_similarity': np.mean(emb_sims), 'avg_semantic_similarity': np.mean(sem_sims), 'sample_size': len(similarity_scores) } def _calculate_semantic_similarity(self, product1: Dict[str, Any], product2: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate semantic similarity between two products""" similarity = 0.0 # Category similarity (highest weight) if product1.get('category') == product2.get('category'): similarity += 0.4 # Subcategory similarity if product1.get('subcategory') == product2.get('subcategory'): similarity += 0.2 # Brand similarity if product1.get('brand') == product2.get('brand'): similarity += 0.2 # Price range similarity if product1.get('price_range') == product2.get('price_range'): similarity += 0.1 # Title similarity (simple word overlap) title1_words = set(product1.get('title', '').lower().split()) title2_words = set(product2.get('title', '').lower().split()) if title1_words and title2_words: word_overlap = len(title1_words & title2_words) / len(title1_words | title2_words) similarity += 0.1 * word_overlap return similarity

# storage/vector_storage.py import numpy as np from typing import Dict, List, Any import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class VectorStorage: """Handles storage and retrieval of vector embeddings""" def __init__(self, vector_db_client): self.client = vector_db_client async def store_product_embeddings( self, collection_name: str, product_embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray], product_metadata: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] ) -> bool: """Store product embeddings with metadata""" try: vectors_data = [] for product_id, embedding in product_embeddings.items(): vector_data = { 'id': product_id, 'vector': embedding, 'payload': product_metadata.get(product_id, {}) } vectors_data.append(vector_data) # Batch insert success = await self.client.upsert_vectors(collection_name, vectors_data) if success: logger.info(f"Successfully stored {len(vectors_data)} product embeddings") else: logger.error("Failed to store product embeddings") return success except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Error storing embeddings: {e}") return False async def store_user_embeddings( self, collection_name: str, user_embeddings: Dict[str, np.ndarray], user_metadata: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] ) -> bool: """Store user embeddings with metadata""" try: vectors_data = [] for user_id, embedding in user_embeddings.items(): vector_data = { 'id': user_id, 'vector': embedding, 'payload': user_metadata.get(user_id, {}) } vectors_data.append(vector_data) success = await self.client.upsert_vectors(collection_name, vectors_data) if success: logger.info(f"Successfully stored {len(vectors_data)} user embeddings") return success except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Error storing user embeddings: {e}") return False

# pipeline/embedding_pipeline.py import asyncio from typing import List, Dict, Any import logging from datetime import datetime logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class EmbeddingPipeline: """Orchestrates the embedding generation pipeline""" def __init__(self, product_processor: ProductDataProcessor, user_processor: UserBehaviorProcessor, embedding_generator: BaseEmbeddingGenerator, vector_storage: VectorStorage): self.product_processor = product_processor self.user_processor = user_processor self.embedding_generator = embedding_generator self.vector_storage = vector_storage async def run_product_pipeline(self, products_data: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool: """Run complete product embedding pipeline""" try: logger.info("Starting product embedding pipeline") # Step 1: Clean and process product data logger.info("Processing product data...") processed_products = [] for product_data in products_data: features = self.product_processor.extract_product_features(product_data) processed_products.append(features) # Step 2: Generate embeddings logger.info("Generating product embeddings...") product_embeddings = await self._generate_product_embeddings(processed_products) # Step 3: Validate embeddings logger.info("Validating embeddings...") validation_results = self._validate_embeddings(product_embeddings, processed_products) # Step 4: Store embeddings logger.info("Storing embeddings...") metadata = {p['id']: p for p in processed_products} success = await self.vector_storage.store_product_embeddings( 'products', product_embeddings, metadata ) if success: logger.info("Product pipeline completed successfully") return success except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Product pipeline failed: {e}") return False async def run_user_pipeline(self, user_profiles: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool: """Run complete user embedding pipeline""" try: logger.info("Starting user embedding pipeline") # Generate user embeddings user_embeddings = await self._generate_user_embeddings(user_profiles) # Store embeddings success = await self.vector_storage.store_user_embeddings( 'users', user_embeddings, user_profiles ) return success except Exception as e: logger.error(f"User pipeline failed: {e}") return False async def _generate_product_embeddings(self, products: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]: """Generate embeddings for products""" product_texts = [] product_ids = [] for product in products: text = self._create_product_text(product) product_texts.append(text) product_ids.append(product['id']) embeddings = await self.embedding_generator.generate_embeddings(product_texts) return { product_id: embedding for product_id, embedding in zip(product_ids, embeddings) }

# monitoring/pipeline_metrics.py import time from typing import Dict, Any import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class PipelineMetrics: """Collect and track pipeline performance metrics""" def __init__(self): self.metrics = { 'processing_times': {}, 'embedding_quality': {}, 'throughput': {}, 'error_rates': {} } def track_processing_time(self, stage: str, duration: float): """Track processing time for pipeline stages""" if stage not in self.metrics['processing_times']: self.metrics['processing_times'][stage] = [] self.metrics['processing_times'][stage].append(duration) logger.info(f"{stage} completed in {duration:.2f}s") def track_embedding_quality(self, quality_metrics: Dict[str, Any]): """Track embedding quality metrics""" self.metrics['embedding_quality'] = quality_metrics logger.info(f"Embedding quality: {quality_metrics}") def get_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Get summary of all metrics""" summary = {} # Average processing times for stage, times in self.metrics['processing_times'].items(): summary[f'{stage}_avg_time'] = sum(times) / len(times) if times else 0 # Latest quality metrics summary['quality_metrics'] = self.metrics['embedding_quality'] return summary

# generation/llm_client.py import openai import anthropic from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional, Union import logging import asyncio from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from dataclasses import dataclass logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) @dataclass class GenerationRequest: """Request structure for content generation""" prompt: str max_tokens: int = 1000 temperature: float = 0.7 user_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None format_type: str = "text" # text, json, markdown @dataclass class GenerationResponse: """Response structure for generated content""" content: str model_used: str tokens_used: int generation_time: float quality_score: Optional[float] = None class BaseLLMProvider(ABC): """Abstract base class for LLM providers""" @abstractmethod async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: pass @abstractmethod def is_available(self) -> bool: pass class OpenAIProvider(BaseLLMProvider): """OpenAI GPT provider""" def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str = "gpt-4"): self.client = openai.AsyncOpenAI(api_key=api_key) self.model = model self.available = True async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: """Generate content using OpenAI API""" try: import time start_time = time.time() messages = [ {"role": "system", "content": self._create_system_prompt(request)}, {"role": "user", "content": request.prompt} ] response = await self.client.chat.completions.create( model=self.model, messages=messages, max_tokens=request.max_tokens, temperature=request.temperature ) generation_time = time.time() - start_time return GenerationResponse( content=response.choices[0].message.content, model_used=self.model, tokens_used=response.usage.total_tokens, generation_time=generation_time ) except Exception as e: logger.error(f"OpenAI generation failed: {e}") self.available = False raise def is_available(self) -> bool: return self.available def _create_system_prompt(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> str: """Create system prompt based on context""" base_prompt = """You are an expert e-commerce recommendation assistant. Your task is to create personalized, helpful product recommendations and explanations.""" if request.user_context: context_info = [] if request.user_context.get('preferred_categories'): context_info.append(f"User prefers: {', '.join(request.user_context['preferred_categories'])}") if request.user_context.get('budget_range'): context_info.append(f"Budget: ${request.user_context['budget_range']}") if context_info: base_prompt += f"

User Context: {'; '.join(context_info)}" if request.format_type == "json": base_prompt += "

Please respond in valid JSON format." elif request.format_type == "markdown": base_prompt += "

Please format your response using Markdown." return base_prompt class AnthropicProvider(BaseLLMProvider): """Anthropic Claude provider""" def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str = "claude-3-sonnet-20240229"): self.client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic(api_key=api_key) self.model = model self.available = True async def generate(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> GenerationResponse: """Generate content using Anthropic API""" try: import time start_time = time.time() system_prompt = self._create_system_prompt(request) response = await self.client.messages.create( model=self.model, max_tokens=request.max_tokens, temperature=request.temperature, system=system_prompt, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": request.prompt}] ) generation_time = time.time() - start_time return GenerationResponse( content=response.content[0].text, model_used=self.model, tokens_used=response.usage.input_tokens + response.usage.output_tokens, generation_time=generation_time ) except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Anthropic generation failed: {e}") self.available = False raise def is_available(self) -> bool: return self.available def _create_system_prompt(self, request: GenerationRequest) -> str: """Create system prompt for Claude""" return """You are Claude, an AI assistant specialized in e-commerce recommendations. You provide thoughtful, accurate product recommendations with clear explanations. Product: {product_name} Product Details: {product_details} User Profile: - Interests: {user_interests} - Experience level: {experience_level} - Usage scenario: {usage_scenario} - Budget considerations: {budget_info} Write a compelling 2-3 sentence summary that: 1. Mentions value in their budget context Keep it engaging and personal.""", required_vars=['product_name', 'product_details'], optional_vars=['user_interests', 'experience_level', 'usage_scenario', 'budget_info'] ) } def generate_prompt(self, template_name: str, variables: Dict[str, Any]) -> str: """Generate a prompt from template and variables""" if template_name not in self.templates: raise ValueError(f"Template '{template_name}' not found") template = self.templates[template_name] # Check required variables missing_vars = [var for var in template.required_vars if var not in variables] if missing_vars: raise ValueError(f"Missing required variables: {missing_vars}") # Set default values for optional variables prompt_vars = variables.copy() if template.optional_vars: for var in template.optional_vars: if var not in prompt_vars: prompt_vars[var] = "Not specified" # Generate prompt try: prompt = template.template.format(**prompt_vars) return prompt except KeyError as e: raise ValueError(f"Variable substitution failed: {e}") def get_template_info(self, template_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Get information about a template""" if template_name not in self.templates: raise ValueError(f"Template '{template_name}' not found") template = self.templates[template_name] return { 'required_vars': template.required_vars, 'optional_vars': template.optional_vars or [], 'format_type': template.format_type }

# monitoring/vertex_ai_monitor.py import time from typing import Dict, Any import logging from dataclasses import dataclass from datetime import datetime, timedelta @dataclass class UsageMetrics: """Track Vertex AI usage metrics""" total_requests: int = 0 total_tokens: int = 0 total_cost: float = 0.0 average_response_time: float = 0.0 error_count: int = 0 class VertexAIMonitor: """Monitor Vertex AI usage and costs""" def __init__(self): self.metrics = UsageMetrics() self.request_history = [] # Pricing (as of 2025 - check latest pricing) self.pricing = { "gemini-1.5-pro": { "input_tokens_per_1k": 0.0035, "output_tokens_per_1k": 0.0105 } } def track_request(self, model_name: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, response_time: float, success: bool): """Track individual request metrics""" # Calculate cost pricing = self.pricing.get(model_name, self.pricing["gemini-1.5-pro"]) input_cost = (input_tokens / 1000) * pricing["input_tokens_per_1k"] output_cost = (output_tokens / 1000) * pricing["output_tokens_per_1k"] total_cost = input_cost + output_cost # Update metrics self.metrics.total_requests += 1 self.metrics.total_tokens += input_tokens + output_tokens self.metrics.total_cost += total_cost # Update average response time total_time = self.metrics.average_response_time * (self.metrics.total_requests - 1) self.metrics.average_response_time = (total_time + response_time) / self.metrics.total_requests if not success: self.metrics.error_count += 1 # Modern e-commerce platforms generate billions of interactions daily, creating vast amounts of unstructured data including product descriptions, user reviews, browsing patterns, and purchase histories. Traditional recommendation systems, while effective, often struggle to understand the nuanced context and semantic relationships within this data. Enter Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) - a revolutionary approach that combines the power of large language models with dynamic information retrieval to create more intelligent, context-aware recommendation systems. This comprehensive guide will walk you through building a sophisticated e-commerce recommendation system using RAG technology, covering everything from architectural design to production deployment.

Traditional collaborative filtering and content-based systems analyze patterns and similarities but often miss the subtle nuances of user intent. RAG systems can: Understand natural language queries: "Show me comfortable running shoes for winter marathons" Process complex product relationships: Understanding that "wireless earbuds with noise cancellation" relates to "productivity" and "commuting" Capture seasonal and temporal context: Recommending products based on current trends and seasonal relevance

RAG enables unprecedented personalization by: Dynamic content generation: Creating personalized product descriptions and recommendations Multi-modal understanding: Processing text, images, and user behavior simultaneously Real-time adaptation: Adjusting recommendations based on immediate context and user feedback

Unlike static models, RAG systems continuously improve by: Incorporating fresh data: New products, reviews, and trends are immediately available Learning from interactions: User feedback directly improves future recommendations Adapting to market changes: Seasonal trends, new categories, and emerging products

The entry point for all recommendation requests, responsible for: interface QueryProcessor { // Parse and understand user intent parseUserQuery(query: string): ParsedQuery; // Extract contextual information extractContext(userId: string, sessionData: SessionContext): UserContext; // Generate search parameters generateSearchParams(query: ParsedQuery, context: UserContext): SearchParams; } interface ParsedQuery { intent: 'browse' | 'search' | 'compare' | 'recommendation'; categories: string[]; filters: ProductFilter[]; sentiment: 'positive' | 'neutral' | 'negative'; urgency: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; } interface UserContext { userId: string; demographics: UserDemographics; purchaseHistory: Purchase[]; browsingBehavior: BrowsingSession[]; preferences: UserPreferences; currentSession: SessionContext; } Key Responsibilities: Natural language query understanding Intent classification and entity extraction Context enrichment with user data Query optimization for downstream components

The core of our RAG system, implementing hybrid search strategies: interface RetrievalEngine { // Semantic search using vector embeddings semanticSearch(query: string, filters: SearchFilters): Promise<Product[]>; // Traditional keyword-based search keywordSearch(query: string, filters: SearchFilters): Promise<Product[]>; // Hybrid search combining both approaches hybridSearch(params: SearchParams): Promise<SearchResult[]>; // Collaborative filtering recommendations collaborativeFilter(userId: string, context: UserContext): Promise<Product[]>; } interface SearchResult { product: Product; relevanceScore: number; searchType: 'semantic' | 'keyword' | 'collaborative'; explanation: string; } Search Strategies: Semantic Search: Vector similarity using embeddings Keyword Search: Traditional full-text search with BM25 Collaborative Filtering: User-based and item-based recommendations Hybrid Ranking: Combining multiple signals for optimal results

class CacheManager { private readonly cacheLayers = { // L1: In-memory cache for hot data memory: new Map<string, CacheEntry>(), // L2: Redis for session data redis: new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL), // L3: Database for persistent data database: new Database() }; async get(key: string): Promise<any> { // Check L1 cache first if (this.cacheLayers.memory.has(key)) { return this.cacheLayers.memory.get(key).value; } // Check L2 cache const redisValue = await this.cacheLayers.redis.get(key); if (redisValue) { // Promote to L1 this.cacheLayers.memory.set(key, { value: JSON.parse(redisValue), timestamp: Date.now() }); return JSON.parse(redisValue); } // Fallback to database return await this.cacheLayers.database.get(key); } }

This section focuses on building a robust retrieval system that efficiently finds relevant products based on user queries, preferences, and context. The retrieval system is the core component that bridges user intent with relevant products using vector similarity search.

Our retrieval system uses a multi-stage approach to ensure both relevance and performance: ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ User Query │ │ Query │ │ Retrieval │ │ + Context │───▶│ Processing │───▶│ Engine │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ├─ Search Query ├─ Query Expansion ├─ Vector Search │ ├─ User Profile ├─ Intent Detection ├─ Hybrid Filtering│ ├─ Session Context ├─ Embedding Gen. ├─ Re-ranking │ ├─ Behavioral Data ├─ Filter Extraction ├─ Diversity │ └─ Product Context └─ Query Enhancement └─ Post-processing │

# retrieval/vector_db.py from qdrant_client import QdrantClient from qdrant_client.models import Distance, VectorParams, PointStruct from qdrant_client.models import Filter, FieldCondition, Range, MatchValue import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class QdrantVectorDB: """Qdrant vector database implementation for product retrieval""" def __init__(self, host: str = "localhost", port: int = 6333): self.client = QdrantClient(host=host, port=port) self.collections = {} async def setup_collection(self, collection_name: str, vector_size: int, distance: Distance = Distance.COSINE) -> bool: """Setup a new collection for vector storage""" try: # Check if collection exists collections = self.client.get_collections() existing_names = [c.name for c in collections.collections] if collection_name not in existing_names: self.client.create_collection( collection_name=collection_name, vectors_config=VectorParams(size=vector_size, distance=distance) ) logger.info(f"Created collection: {collection_name}") else: logger.info(f"Collection already exists: {collection_name}") self.collections[collection_name] = { 'vector_size': vector_size, 'distance': distance } return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to setup collection {collection_name}: {e}") return False async def upsert_vectors(self, collection_name: str, vectors_data: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool: """Insert or update vectors in the collection""" try: points = [] for data in vectors_data: point = PointStruct( id=data['id'], vector=data['vector'].tolist() if isinstance(data['vector'], np.ndarray) else data['vector'], payload=data['payload'] ) points.append(point) # Batch upsert batch_size = 100 for i in range(0, len(points), batch_size): batch = points[i:i + batch_size] self.client.upsert( collection_name=collection_name, points=batch ) logger.info(f"Upserted {len(points)} vectors to {collection_name}") return True except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Failed to upsert vectors: {e}") return False async def search_vectors(self, collection_name: str, query_vector: np.ndarray, limit: int = 10, filters: Optional[Filter] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Search for similar vectors""" try: results = self.client.search( collection_name=collection_name, query_vector=query_vector.tolist() if isinstance(query_vector, np.ndarray) else query_vector, query_filter=filters, limit=limit, with_payload=True, with_vectors=False ) search_results = [] for result in results: search_results.append({ 'id': result.id, 'score': result.score, 'payload': result.payload }) return search_results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Search failed: {e}") return [] def create_filter(self, filter_conditions: Dict[str, Any]) -> Filter: """Create Qdrant filter from conditions""" conditions = [] for field, value in filter_conditions.items(): if isinstance(value, list): # Multiple values - use should condition should_conditions = [ FieldCondition(key=field, match=MatchValue(value=v)) for v in value ] conditions.extend(should_conditions) elif isinstance(value, dict) and 'range' in value: # Range condition range_filter = value['range'] conditions.append( FieldCondition( key=field, range=Range( gte=range_filter.get('gte'), lte=range_filter.get('lte') ) ) ) else: # Exact match conditions.append( FieldCondition(key=field, match=MatchValue(value=value)) ) return Filter(must=conditions) if conditions else None

# retrieval/query_processor.py import re import spacy from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional, Set import logging from datetime import datetime logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class QueryProcessor: """Advanced query processing for e-commerce search""" def __init__(self): # Load spaCy model for NLP processing try: self.nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm") except OSError: logger.warning("spaCy model not found. Install with: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm") self.nlp = None # Product categories and attributes self.categories = { 'electronics': ['phone', 'laptop', 'computer', 'tablet', 'camera', 'headphones'], 'clothing': ['shirt', 'pants', 'dress', 'shoes', 'jacket', 'jeans'], 'home': ['furniture', 'decor', 'kitchen', 'bedroom', 'bathroom'], 'books': ['novel', 'textbook', 'fiction', 'non-fiction', 'cookbook'], 'sports': ['fitness', 'outdoor', 'gym', 'running', 'cycling'] } # Price keywords self.price_keywords = { 'cheap': {'range': {'lte': 50}}, 'affordable': {'range': {'lte': 100}}, 'budget': {'range': {'lte': 75}}, 'expensive': {'range': {'gte': 500}}, 'premium': {'range': {'gte': 300}}, 'luxury': {'range': {'gte': 1000}} } # Brand extraction patterns self.brand_patterns = [ r'\b(apple|samsung|nike|adidas|sony|microsoft|google)\b', r'\b(amazon|dell|hp|lenovo|asus|lg)\b' ] def process_query(self, query: str, user_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Process user query and extract structured information""" logger.info(f"Processing query: {query}") # Basic preprocessing query_lower = query.lower().strip() # Extract components processed_query = { 'original_query': query, 'cleaned_query': self._clean_query(query_lower), 'intent': self._detect_intent(query_lower), 'entities': self._extract_entities(query_lower), 'filters': self._extract_filters(query_lower), 'keywords': self._extract_keywords(query_lower), 'embedding_text': self._create_embedding_text(query_lower, user_context), 'query_expansion': self._expand_query(query_lower), 'priority_terms': self._identify_priority_terms(query_lower) } logger.info(f"Processed query structure: {processed_query}") return processed_query def _clean_query(self, query: str) -> str: """Clean and normalize the query""" # Remove special characters but keep important ones query = re.sub(r'[^\w\s\-\$\.]', ' ', query) # Normalize whitespace query = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', query) # Remove common stop words that don't add value stop_words = {'a', 'an', 'the', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'for', 'with'} words = query.split() words = [word for word in words if word not in stop_words] return ' '.join(words) def _detect_intent(self, query: str) -> str: """Detect user intent from query""" # Define intent patterns intent_patterns = { 'specific_product': [r'\b(buy|purchase|order)\b', r'\b(specific|exact)\b'], 'browse_category': [r'\b(show|browse|look|find)\b.*\b(category|type)\b'], 'compare_products': [r'\b(compare|vs|versus|difference)\b'], 'price_search': [r'\b(cheap|expensive|price|cost|budget)\b'], 'brand_search': [r'\b(brand|manufacturer|make)\b'], 'feature_search': [r'\b(with|having|feature|specification)\b'], 'general_search': [r'.*'] # Default fallback } for intent, patterns in intent_patterns.items(): if any(re.search(pattern, query) for pattern in patterns): return intent return 'general_search' def _extract_entities(self, query: str) -> Dict[str, List[str]]: """Extract named entities from the query""" entities = { 'products': [], 'brands': [], 'categories': [], 'attributes': [], 'price_terms': [] } # Extract brands for pattern in self.brand_patterns: matches = re.findall(pattern, query, re.IGNORECASE) entities['brands'].extend(matches) # Extract categories for category, keywords in self.categories.items(): if any(keyword in query for keyword in keywords): entities['categories'].append(category) entities['products'].extend([kw for kw in keywords if kw in query]) # Extract price terms for price_term in self.price_keywords.keys(): if price_term in query: entities['price_terms'].append(price_term) # Use spaCy for additional entity extraction if available if self.nlp: doc = self.nlp(query) for ent in doc.ents: if ent.label_ in ['PRODUCT', 'ORG']: entities['brands'].append(ent.text) return entities def _extract_filters(self, query: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """Extract filter conditions from query""" filters = {} # Price filters for price_term, condition in self.price_keywords.items(): if price_term in query: filters['price'] = condition break # Extract specific price mentions price_match = re.search(r'\$?(\d+(?:\.\d{2})?)', query) if price_match: price = float(price_match.group(1)) if 'under' in query or 'below' in query: filters['price'] = {'range': {'lte': price}} elif 'over' in query or 'above' in query: filters['price'] = {'range': {'gte': price}} else: # Approximate range around the mentioned price filters['price'] = {'range': {'gte': price * 0.8, 'lte': price * 1.2}} # Category filters entities = self._extract_entities(query) if entities['categories']: filters['category'] = entities['categories'] # Brand filters if entities['brands']: filters['brand'] = entities['brands'] # Availability filters if any(term in query for term in ['available', 'in stock', 'ready']): filters['is_available'] = True # Rating filters if 'high rated' in query or 'top rated' in query: filters['rating'] = {'range': {'gte': 4.0}} elif 'highly rated' in query: filters['rating'] = {'range': {'gte': 4.5}} return filters def _extract_keywords(self, query: str) -> List[str]: """Extract important keywords for search""" # Basic keyword extraction words = query.split() # Remove common words stop_words = {'for', 'with', 'and', 'or', 'but', 'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'from'} keywords = [word for word in words if word not in stop_words and len(word) > 2] # Add entity-based keywords entities = self._extract_entities(query) keywords.extend(entities['products']) keywords.extend(entities['brands']) return list(set(keywords)) # Remove duplicates def _create_embedding_text(self, query: str, user_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> str: """Create optimized text for embedding generation""" text_components = [query] # Add user context if available if user_context: if user_context.get('preferred_categories'): text_components.append(f"Categories: {', '.join(user_context['preferred_categories'])}") if user_context.get('preferred_brands'): text_components.append(f"Brands: {', '.join(user_context['preferred_brands'])}") if user_context.get('recent_searches'): recent = user_context['recent_searches'][:3] # Last 3 searches text_components.append(f"Recent interests: {', '.join(recent)}") return ' '.join(text_components) def _expand_query(self, query: str) -> List[str]: """Expand query with synonyms and related terms""" # Simple synonym expansion synonyms = { 'phone': ['smartphone', 'mobile', 'cellphone'], 'laptop': ['notebook', 'computer', 'pc'], 'cheap': ['affordable', 'budget', 'inexpensive'], 'expensive': ['premium', 'luxury', 'high-end'], 'good': ['quality', 'excellent', 'top', 'best'] } expanded_terms = [query] words = query.split() for word in words: if word in synonyms: expanded_terms.extend(synonyms[word]) return expanded_terms def _identify_priority_terms(self, query: str) -> List[str]: """Identify high-priority terms that should have higher weight""" priority_patterns = [ r'\b(best|top|premium|quality)\b', r'\b(need|want|looking for)\b', r'\b(brand new|latest|newest)\b' ] priority_terms = [] for pattern in priority_patterns: matches = re.findall(pattern, query) priority_terms.extend(matches) return priority_terms

# retrieval/retrieval_engine.py import numpy as np from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import logging from dataclasses import dataclass import asyncio logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) @dataclass class RetrievalResult: """Structure for retrieval results""" product_id: str score: float payload: Dict[str, Any] retrieval_method: str ranking_factors: Dict[str, float] class RetrievalEngine: """Advanced retrieval engine with multiple search strategies""" def __init__(self, vector_db: QdrantVectorDB, embedding_generator, query_processor: QueryProcessor): self.vector_db = vector_db self.embedding_generator = embedding_generator self.query_processor = query_processor # Retrieval weights self.retrieval_weights = { 'semantic_similarity': 0.6, 'category_match': 0.2, 'brand_match': 0.1, 'price_relevance': 0.05, 'popularity': 0.05 } async def search(self, query: str, user_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, limit: int = 20, include_filters: bool = True) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Main search interface""" logger.info(f"Searching for: {query}") # Process query processed_query = self.query_processor.process_query(query, user_context) # Multiple retrieval strategies results = await self._multi_stage_retrieval(processed_query, user_context, limit) # Re-rank results ranked_results = self._rerank_results(results, processed_query, user_context) # Apply diversity diverse_results = self._apply_diversity(ranked_results[:limit * 2]) return diverse_results[:limit] async def _multi_stage_retrieval(self, processed_query: Dict[str, Any], user_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], limit: int) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Multi-stage retrieval with different strategies""" all_results = [] # Stage 1: Semantic vector search semantic_results = await self._semantic_search(processed_query, limit) all_results.extend(semantic_results) # Stage 2: Filtered search (if filters exist) if processed_query['filters']: filtered_results = await self._filtered_search(processed_query, limit) all_results.extend(filtered_results) # Stage 3: User preference-based search if user_context: preference_results = await self._preference_search(processed_query, user_context, limit) all_results.extend(preference_results) # Deduplicate results seen_ids = set() unique_results = [] for result in all_results: if result.product_id not in seen_ids: unique_results.append(result) seen_ids.add(result.product_id) return unique_results async def _semantic_search(self, processed_query: Dict[str, Any], limit: int) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Semantic similarity search using vector embeddings""" try: # Generate query embedding query_text = processed_query['embedding_text'] query_embedding = await self.embedding_generator.generate_embeddings([query_text]) if len(query_embedding) == 0: return [] # Search in vector database search_results = await self.vector_db.search_vectors( collection_name='products', query_vector=query_embedding[0], limit=limit * 2 # Get more results for re-ranking ) # Convert to RetrievalResult objects results = [] for result in search_results: retrieval_result = RetrievalResult( product_id=result['id'], score=result['score'], payload=result['payload'], retrieval_method='semantic', ranking_factors={'semantic_similarity': result['score']} ) results.append(retrieval_result) logger.info(f"Semantic search returned {len(results)} results") return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Semantic search failed: {e}") return [] async def _filtered_search(self, processed_query: Dict[str, Any], limit: int) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Search with specific filters""" try: filters = self.vector_db.create_filter(processed_query['filters']) # Generate query embedding query_text = processed_query['embedding_text'] query_embedding = await self.embedding_generator.generate_embeddings([query_text]) if len(query_embedding) == 0: return [] # Search with filters search_results = await self.vector_db.search_vectors( collection_name='products', query_vector=query_embedding[0], limit=limit, filters=filters ) # Convert to RetrievalResult objects results = [] for result in search_results: ranking_factors = { 'semantic_similarity': result['score'], 'filter_match': 1.0 # Perfect filter match } retrieval_result = RetrievalResult( product_id=result['id'], score=result['score'], payload=result['payload'], retrieval_method='filtered', ranking_factors=ranking_factors ) results.append(retrieval_result) logger.info(f"Filtered search returned {len(results)} results") return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Filtered search failed: {e}") return [] async def _preference_search(self, processed_query: Dict[str, Any], user_context: Dict[str, Any], limit: int) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Search based on user preferences""" try: # Create preference-enhanced query preference_filters = {} if user_context.get('preferred_categories'): preference_filters['category'] = user_context['preferred_categories'] if user_context.get('preferred_brands'): preference_filters['brand'] = user_context['preferred_brands'] if user_context.get('price_range'): preference_filters['price'] = user_context['price_range'] if not preference_filters: return [] filters = self.vector_db.create_filter(preference_filters) # Generate query embedding query_text = processed_query['embedding_text'] query_embedding = await self.embedding_generator.generate_embeddings([query_text]) if len(query_embedding) == 0: return [] # Search with preference filters search_results = await self.vector_db.search_vectors( collection_name='products', query_vector=query_embedding[0], limit=limit, filters=filters ) # Convert to RetrievalResult objects results = [] for result in search_results: ranking_factors = { 'semantic_similarity': result['score'], 'preference_match': 0.8 # High preference match } retrieval_result = RetrievalResult( product_id=result['id'], score=result['score'], payload=result['payload'], retrieval_method='preference', ranking_factors=ranking_factors ) results.append(retrieval_result) logger.info(f"Preference search returned {len(results)} results") return results except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Preference search failed: {e}") return [] def _rerank_results(self, results: List[RetrievalResult], processed_query: Dict[str, Any], user_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Re-rank results using multiple factors""" logger.info(f"Re-ranking {len(results)} results") for result in results: # Calculate composite score composite_score = 0.0 # Semantic similarity semantic_score = result.ranking_factors.get('semantic_similarity', 0.0) composite_score += semantic_score * self.retrieval_weights['semantic_similarity'] # Category match category_score = self._calculate_category_score(result, processed_query) composite_score += category_score * self.retrieval_weights['category_match'] result.ranking_factors['category_match'] = category_score # Brand match brand_score = self._calculate_brand_score(result, processed_query) composite_score += brand_score * self.retrieval_weights['brand_match'] result.ranking_factors['brand_match'] = brand_score # Price relevance price_score = self._calculate_price_score(result, processed_query) composite_score += price_score * self.retrieval_weights['price_relevance'] result.ranking_factors['price_relevance'] = price_score # Popularity score popularity_score = self._calculate_popularity_score(result) composite_score += popularity_score * self.retrieval_weights['popularity'] result.ranking_factors['popularity'] = popularity_score # User context boost if user_context: context_score = self._calculate_context_score(result, user_context) composite_score += context_score * 0.1 result.ranking_factors['context_match'] = context_score result.score = composite_score # Sort by composite score ranked_results = sorted(results, key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True) logger.info("Re-ranking completed") return ranked_results def _calculate_category_score(self, result: RetrievalResult, processed_query: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate category match score""" query_categories = processed_query['entities'].get('categories', []) if not query_categories: return 0.0 product_category = result.payload.get('category', '') if product_category in query_categories: return 1.0 # Partial match for subcategories product_subcategory = result.payload.get('subcategory', '') if any(cat in product_subcategory.lower() for cat in query_categories): return 0.5 return 0.0 def _calculate_brand_score(self, result: RetrievalResult, processed_query: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate brand match score""" query_brands = processed_query['entities'].get('brands', []) if not query_brands: return 0.0 product_brand = result.payload.get('brand', '').lower() for brand in query_brands: if brand.lower() in product_brand: return 1.0 return 0.0 def _calculate_price_score(self, result: RetrievalResult, processed_query: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate price relevance score""" price_filters = processed_query['filters'].get('price') if not price_filters: return 0.5 # Neutral score product_price = result.payload.get('price', 0) if 'range' in price_filters: price_range = price_filters['range'] min_price = price_range.get('gte', 0) max_price = price_range.get('lte', float('inf')) if min_price <= product_price <= max_price: return 1.0 else: # Calculate how far outside the range if product_price < min_price: ratio = product_price / min_price elif product_price > max_price: ratio = max_price / product_price else: ratio = 1.0 return max(0.0, ratio) return 0.5 def _calculate_popularity_score(self, result: RetrievalResult) -> float: """Calculate product popularity score""" # Normalize popularity metrics review_count = result.payload.get('review_count', 0) rating = result.payload.get('rating', 0.0) popularity = result.payload.get('popularity_score', 0.0) # Combine metrics review_score = min(1.0, review_count / 100) # Normalize to 0-1 rating_score = rating / 5.0 if rating > 0 else 0 popularity_score = min(1.0, popularity / 100) # Normalize to 0-1 return (review_score + rating_score + popularity_score) / 3 def _calculate_context_score(self, result: RetrievalResult, user_context: Dict[str, Any]) -> float: """Calculate user context match score""" score = 0.0 # Preferred categories preferred_categories = user_context.get('preferred_categories', []) product_category = result.payload.get('category', '') if product_category in preferred_categories: score += 0.5 # Preferred brands preferred_brands = user_context.get('preferred_brands', []) product_brand = result.payload.get('brand', '') if product_brand in preferred_brands: score += 0.3 # Price range preference preferred_price_range = user_context.get('price_range') if preferred_price_range: product_price = result.payload.get('price', 0) min_price = preferred_price_range.get('min', 0) max_price = preferred_price_range.get('max', float('inf')) if min_price <= product_price <= max_price: score += 0.2 return min(1.0, score) def _apply_diversity(self, results: List[RetrievalResult]) -> List[RetrievalResult]: """Apply diversity to results to avoid showing too similar products""" if len(results) <= 5: return results diverse_results = [results[0]] # Always include top result for result in results[1:]: # Check if result is diverse enough is_diverse = True for existing_result in diverse_results: # Check category diversity if (result.payload.get('category') == existing_result.payload.get('category') and result.payload.get('subcategory') == existing_result.payload.get('subcategory')): # Check if from same brand if result.payload.get('brand') == existing_result.payload.get('brand'): is_diverse = False break if is_diverse: diverse_results.append(result) # Limit diversity checking to avoid performance issues if len(diverse_results) >= 10: break # Fill remaining slots with best remaining results remaining_slots = len(results) - len(diverse_results) if remaining_slots > 0: remaining_results = [r for r in results if r not in diverse_results] diverse_results.extend(remaining_results[:remaining_slots]) logger.info(f"Applied diversity: {len(diverse_results)} results") return diverse_results

# retrieval/cache_manager.py import redis import json import hashlib from typing import Dict, Any, Optional, List import logging import pickle logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) class RetrievalCache: """Cache for retrieval results to improve performance""" def __init__(self, redis_client: redis.Redis): self.redis = redis_client self.cache_ttl = 3600 # 1 hour self.query_cache_ttl = 1800 # 30 minutes def _create_cache_key(self, query: str, filters: Dict[str, Any], user_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str: """Create a unique cache key for the query""" key_data = { 'query': query, 'filters': filters, 'user_id': user_id } key_string = json.dumps(key_data, sort_keys=True) key_hash = hashlib.md5(key_string.encode()).hexdigest() return f"retrieval_cache:{key_hash}" async def get_cached_results(self, query: str, filters: Dict[str, Any], user_id: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[List[RetrievalResult]]: """Get cached retrieval results""" try: cache_key = self._create_cache_key(query, filters, user_id) cached_data = self.redis.get(cache_key) if cached_data: results_data = pickle.loads(cached_data) logger.info(f"Cache hit for query: {query}") return results_data return None except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Cache retrieval error: {e}") return None async def cache_results(self, query: str, filters: Dict[str, Any], results: List[RetrievalResult], user_id: Optional[str] = None): """Cache retrieval results""" try: cache_key = self._create_cache_key(query, filters, user_id) results_data = pickle.dumps(results) self.redis.setex(cache_key, self.cache_ttl, results_data) logger.info(f"Cached results for query: {query}") except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Cache storage error: {e}")

# api/search_api.py from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional import logging logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) app = FastAPI(title="RAG E-commerce Search API") class SearchRequest(BaseModel): query: str = Field(..., description="Search query") limit: int = Field(default=20, ge=1, le=100, description="Number of results") filters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = Field(default=None, description="Search filters") user_id: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="User ID for personalization") class SearchResponse(BaseModel): query: str results: List[Dict[str, Any]] total_results: int search_time: float filters_applied: Dict[str, Any] # Global retrieval engine instance retrieval_engine: Optional[RetrievalEngine] = None def get_retrieval_engine() -> RetrievalEngine: """Dependency to get retrieval engine""" if retrieval_engine is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Retrieval engine not initialized") return retrieval_engine @app.post("/search", response_model=SearchResponse) async def search_products( request: SearchRequest, engine: RetrievalEngine = Depends(get_retrieval_engine) ) -> SearchResponse: """Search for products using the RAG retrieval system""" try: import time start_time = time.time() # Get user context if user_id provided user_context = None if request.user_id: user_context = await get_user_context(request.user_id) # Perform search results = await engine.search( query=request.query, user_context=user_context, limit=request.limit, include_filters=True ) search_time = time.time() - start_time # Format results formatted_results = [] for result in results: formatted_result = { 'product_id': result.product_id, 'score': result.score, 'product_data': result.payload, 'retrieval_method': result.retrieval_method, 'ranking_factors': result.ranking_factors } formatted_results.append(formatted_result) return SearchResponse( query=request.query, results=formatted_results, total_results=len(formatted_results), search_time=search_time, filters_applied=request.filters or {} ) except Exception as e: logger.error(f"Search error: {e}") raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)) async def get_user_context(user_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]: """Get user context for personalization""" # This would typically fetch from user service or database # Placeholder implementation return { 'preferred_categories': ['electronics', 'books'], 'preferred_brands': ['apple', 'samsung'], 'price_range': {'min': 0, 'max': 1000}, 'recent_searches': ['laptop', 'phone case', 'wireless headphones'] } @app.get("/health") async def health_check(): """Health check endpoint""" return {"status": "healthy", "service": "rag-search-api"}
